reviews.discipline: AI/ML evaluation methodology, benchmarking, split design, and reproducibility for scientific machine learning
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD in machine learning evaluation and benchmarking, 15 years. Published on data leakage, train/test split design (temporal, scaffold, and similarity-constrained splits), predictor calibration, and reproducibility failures in scientific ML. Routine reviewer for ML-for-biology venues; my usual job is to determine whether a reported number could have been produced by the procedure its authors describe.

findings.title: There is no evaluation of any kind in this project; the "Computational Benchmark" is a bar chart of the platform's own hardcoded literals
findings.evidence_location: app.js:1048-1103 (renderBenchmarkChart, comment at :1048 reads "Chart.js Benchmark Simulation"); app.js:1053-1055 (labels/ceiData/dgData mapped straight off AF3_CANDIDATES); app.js:124-135 (AF3_CANDIDATES literals); index.html:316-319 (chart titled "TOP 10 Candidate Computational Benchmark (CEI vs Binding Affinity)"); app.js:869-895 (renderLeaderboardTable); index.html:296-312 ("AlphaFold3 Leaderboard Ranking")
findings.what_is_wrong: renderBenchmarkChart() reads AF3_CANDIDATES[].cei and Math.abs(AF3_CANDIDATES[].dg) — both hardcoded literals declared 900 lines earlier at app.js:125-134 — and draws them as bars. Nothing is computed, compared, or held out. I grepped the entire repository (README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css) with word-boundary patterns for: baseline, held-out, holdout, test set, validation, cross-validation, k-fold, ablation, error bar, confidence interval, p-value, sample size, scrambled, control, bootstrap, significance, Bonferroni, FDR, AUROC, enrichment, RMSD, TM-score, DockQ, ECE, calibration, PoseBusters, CASP, CAMEO. Every one returns zero hits. (Raw case-insensitive substring counts are nonzero only because "ECE" matches "rECEptor", "ROC" matches "pROCess", "ITC" matches "swITCh", and "control" matches the Three.js OrbitControls variable; word-boundary greps return nothing.) The leaderboard is worse than merely self-referential: its Rank column is not a monotone function of ANY displayed metric. Ranks 1-10 give pLDDT [93.2, 94.0, 96.1, 95.4, 92.1, 94.8, 92.8, 93.6, 91.9, 90.7], dG [-17.9, -16.8, -15.1, -14.2, -14.8, -13.5, -12.6, -13.0, -11.8, -12.1], CEI [98.4, 95.2, 92.1, 93.8, 90.5, 89.0, 87.6, 85.4, 83.9, 82.5]. None is sorted. Rank 3 (CEI 92.1) is placed above rank 4 (CEI 93.8); dG has three inversions (rank 4 vs 5, 7 vs 8, 9 vs 10). No composite of the three columns reproduces the ordering either, and none is stated. Additionally, "CEI" (Cognitive Enhancement Index) is displayed as a headline 0-100 score with no definition anywhere in the repository — no formula, no units, no derivation, no reference.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader — a collaborator, an investor, a graduate student, an IRB or IACUC reviewer sizing up a follow-on animal study — sees a page titled "Computational Benchmark" and a "Leaderboard Ranking" and reasonably infers that ten designs were scored by some procedure and compared against something. Nothing was. The ranking cannot even be regenerated from the numbers printed next to it, so a reader who tries to check the work discovers only that the ordering has no rule. Every downstream prioritization decision ("pursue rank #1 first") is arbitrary. Because CEI is undefined and carries the largest visual weight (r = 0.939 with |dG|, i.e. it adds no information beyond dG anyway), the chart's apparent two-metric agreement is an artifact of the two columns having been written by the same hand.
findings.ground_truth: A benchmark requires, minimally: (i) a task with a ground-truth label the method did not see; (ii) at least one baseline; (iii) a held-out evaluation set constructed to prevent leakage; (iv) a dispersion estimate. For structure prediction the field-standard instruments are CASP (blind, targets sequestered pre-release; Simpkin et al., Proteins 2023, 91:1616-1635, DOI 10.1002/prot.26593, which defines the evaluation-unit decomposition and the GDT/lDDT/TM scoring conventions) and CAMEO (continuous weekly blind evaluation against PDB pre-release; Robin et al., Proteins 2021, 89:1977-1986, DOI 10.1002/prot.26213). For docking/pose tasks, RMSD alone is explicitly insufficient and must be paired with physical-validity checks (Buttenschoen, Morris & Deane, Chem. Sci. 2024, 15:3130-3139, DOI 10.1039/D3SC04185A). For ADMET endpoints, TDC supplies pre-split public leaderboards with defined metrics (Huang et al., arXiv:2102.09548). A leaderboard's sort key must be a stated, computable function of published columns.
findings.required_fix: Delete the words "Benchmark" and "Leaderboard" from index.html:296 and index.html:316, or make them true. To make them true: (1) define CEI explicitly as a formula over measurable inputs, or remove the column; (2) sort the table by a single named, published scoring function and add a unit test asserting the table is sorted by it; (3) add a genuine comparison — run every one of the 25 sequences plus a matched set of baselines (a scrambled-sequence control per design, a known-binder positive control per target such as BDNF for TrkB and donepezil for AChE) through the same pipeline and report the resulting score distributions side by side; (4) evaluate any predictive component on a held-out set with a similarity-constrained split and report a dispersion estimate. If none of this is going to be done, relabel the page "Design Concept Catalogue" and remove all numeric scores.

findings.title: The pLDDT curves, PAE heatmap, and 3D "confidence spectrum" are closed-form cosmetic functions of residue index and ASCII code, presented under the label "AlphaFold3" and "REAL"
findings.evidence_location: app.js:791 (`let score = 93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5;`); app.js:792-793 (dead clamps); app.js:802 (dataset label "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score"); app.js:850 (`let error = Math.abs(i - j) * 0.4 + (sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length) % 4) * 0.3;`); app.js:707 (comment "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION"); app.js:715-717 (`radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8`); app.js:747-750 (sphere colour by residue letter); index.html:371, 377, 383, 388-391, 397; README.md:108-110
findings.what_is_wrong:
Three separate panels are labelled as AlphaFold3 outputs and none contains any structure prediction.

(a) pLDDT (app.js:791). score = 93 + 4·sin(0.4·i) + 0.5·(ord(residue) mod 5). I evaluated this over all 25 sequences (876 residues): the reachable range is exactly [89.0, 99.0]. Consequences: the clamp `if (score > 100) score = 98.6` (app.js:792) is unreachable (max 99.0) and the clamp `if (score < 70) score = 76` (app.js:793) is unreachable (min 89.0) — both are dead code, which is direct evidence the author never inspected the function's range. The legend at index.html:388-391 advertises four bands; only two can ever be drawn (7.6% of residues fall in 89.0-90.0, 92.4% above 90), so "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" are structurally unreachable. The positional term is a fixed sinusoid of period 2π/0.4 = 15.71 residues, so *every* candidate's confidence profile shows the identical 15.7-residue ripple. The sequence term is ASCII mod 5, which aliases the 20 amino acids into 5 arbitrary lexical buckets: {A,F,K,P}, {G,L,Q,V}, {C,H,M,R,W}, {D,I,N,S}, {E,T,Y}. Proline and alanine are assigned identical confidence contributions; glycine and leucine likewise. This is not an approximation of AlphaFold behaviour, it is the ASCII table.

(b) PAE (app.js:850). error = 0.4·|i−j| + 0.3·(ord(seq[i mod len]) mod 4). This is a linear ramp off the diagonal by construction, so it can never exhibit the block structure that is the entire diagnostic content of a PAE map. index.html:397 labels the axis "0 - 30 Å"; the grid is capped at 45 (app.js:844), so the maximum attainable value is 44·0.4 + 0.9 = 18.5 Å, and for the actual sequences (28-45 aa) it is 11.7-18.5 Å. The top 38% of the advertised range is unreachable for every candidate.

(c) 3D viewer (app.js:707-761). The tube is a helix whose radius is 6 + 0.8·(ASCII mod 5) and whose angular sweep flips between 4π and 6π on `charCode % 3 === 0`. No backbone geometry, no bond lengths, no Ramachandran constraint. Worse, the residue spheres (app.js:747-750) are coloured by letter identity — G/S green, P/D amber, everything else cyan — while index.html:377 titles the panel "Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)" and README.md:108 says "residue-specific pLDDT color spectrum (Very High >90 Cyan, High 70-90 Green, Low 50-70 Amber)." I checked the two panels against each other: of 446 spheres drawn across the 25 modals, 104 (23.3%) are painted "High" or "Low" confidence while the pLDDT curve drawn six inches to their right, from the same sequence, assigns those exact residues ≥90. Two panels in the same modal, generated from the same input, contradict each other.

(d) The per-drug card pLDDT (e.g. app.js:146, "AF3 pLDDT = 96.2 / 100") does not match the mean of the curve the modal plots for that drug (93.93 for id 1). Mean absolute discrepancy across all 25 is 1.05 pLDDT units, max 2.69 (id 3: card 97.0 vs drawn 94.31).
findings.why_it_matters: pLDDT and PAE are the two quantities the structural-biology community uses to decide whether a predicted model is trustworthy enough to act on. Rendering an ASCII-derived sinusoid under the axis label "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" and a distance-from-diagonal ramp under "Predicted Aligned Error (0-30 Å)" is not a placeholder — a viewer with domain training reads those panels as evidence and will conclude the designs are confidently folded. The dead clamps and the unreachable legend bands prove no one ever validated the generator's output distribution, and the 23.3% internal contradiction between the colour map and the confidence curve means the platform disagrees with itself about its own headline claim. Anyone who copies a FASTA to AlphaFold Server (the workflow the app actively encourages at index.html:362-363) and gets a real pLDDT of 45 for a 31-residue disulfide-rich peptide will find the platform's displayed 95.1 was never a prediction at all.
findings.ground_truth: pLDDT is a per-residue estimate of local distance difference test, produced by a trained head of the structure module and calibrated against experimental structures; PAE[i][j] is the expected positional error at residue i when the prediction and truth are aligned on residue j, and its off-diagonal block structure is what distinguishes confidently-packed domains from independently-mobile ones (Abramson et al., Nature 2024, 630:493-500, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w). Neither is a function of the amino-acid alphabet's ASCII encoding. Real AF3 output ships as an mmCIF with per-atom B-factor-slot pLDDT plus a confidences JSON containing the full PAE matrix, pTM and ipTM; those files are the artifact. Where a display is a mock-up, the field's convention is to say so on the figure, and confidence-band legends must reflect the reachable range of the data plotted.
findings.required_fix: Do one of two things, not a compromise. Either (1) actually run each sequence through AlphaFold Server or a local AF3/Boltz/Chai deployment, commit the returned mmCIF and confidences JSON per candidate under a `structures/` directory, and have renderModalPlddtChart() and renderModalPaeHeatmap() read the real arrays from those files — deleting app.js:791 and app.js:850 outright; or (2) if the panels stay synthetic, rename the dataset label at app.js:802 to "Illustrative placeholder — not a prediction", change index.html:371/377/383/397 and README.md:108-110 to remove every occurrence of "AlphaFold3", "Real", and "pLDDT", delete the comment at app.js:707, remove the four-band legend at index.html:388-391, and stamp a visible watermark on all three canvases. Independently of which path is taken: delete the unreachable clamps at app.js:792-793, fix the PAE axis label to the reachable range, and make the sphere colours a function of the plotted pLDDT array rather than the residue letter.

findings.title: Identical input sequences are assigned different ΔG, Kd, and pLDDT and different targets — proof the reported metrics are not the output of any deterministic pipeline
findings.evidence_location: app.js:153 vs app.js:247 (sequence KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG); app.js:173 vs app.js:371 (CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH); app.js:195 vs app.js:319 (SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC); app.js:205 vs app.js:361 (VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH); affinity strings at app.js:156/250, 176/374, 198/322, 208/364; app.js:381 (sequence field containing "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate")
findings.what_is_wrong:
I parsed all 25 sequence fields and grouped them. Four sequences appear twice, and in every case the two copies carry different reported metrics:

1. KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG — id 2 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2): ΔG −16.2, Kd 2.1 nM, pLDDT 94.8. id 11 (BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1): ΔG −17.5, Kd 0.65 nM, pLDDT 94.3.
2. CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH — id 4: ΔG −16.9, Kd 1.2 nM, pLDDT 95.1, target "Frizzled-8 CRD". id 23: ΔG −16.1, Kd 2.8 nM, pLDDT 93.8, target "ZO-1 & Occludin Complex".
3. SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC — id 6: ΔG −16.5, Kd 1.8 nM, pLDDT 93.2, target "α7 nAChR ECD". id 18: ΔG −15.7, Kd 3.8 nM, pLDDT 92.8, target "TLR4/MD-2".
4. VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH — id 7: ΔG −17.2, Kd 0.85 nM, pLDDT 95.8, target "TrkB Ig-like D5". id 22: ΔG −15.8, Kd 3.6 nM, pLDDT 94.1, target "EAAT2/GLT-1 transporter".

pLDDT is a property of a single-chain prediction. The same sequence submitted to the same model with the same settings returns the same pLDDT; the model does not know which target the designer had in mind. Four pairs differ by 0.4-1.7 units. That is not achievable by any pipeline, seeded or not.

Separately, the ΔG and Kd columns are mutually inconsistent. Using ΔG = RT·ln(Kd) with R = 1.9872×10⁻³ kcal/mol/K and T = 298.15 K (RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol), the reported Kd values imply ΔG values 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol less negative than the reported ΔG, for all 25 without exception (mean residual −4.74, SD 0.55). Example: id 1 reports ΔG −18.4 with Kd 0.32 nM; 0.32 nM implies ΔG = −12.95. The residual is not constant (SD 0.55 over a 1.9 kcal/mol spread), so this is not even a single mislabelled unit convention or a fixed reference-state offset — the two columns were written independently.

Finally, two "FASTA" strings are not sequences at all: ids 4 and 23 contain the character B, which is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx and is rejected by AlphaFold Server; id 24's sequence field (app.js:381) holds the literal English string "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate". Both are nonetheless assigned pLDDT (95.1, 93.8, 92.4) and ΔG values, and both are fed to the FASTA-copy button at app.js:660-671.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the finding that cannot be argued with. Any scoring function, deterministic or stochastic, is a function of its input. Here the same input yields four different output triples, and the difference tracks the *narrative* the designer wanted (the one described as an AChE gorge clamper scores better on AChE than the one described as a hippocampal peptidomimetic) rather than anything in the sequence. The four duplicate pairs are, unintentionally, exactly the off-target decoy control a binder platform is supposed to run — and the platform passes both arms with equally spectacular scores. One 31-residue peptide is asserted to bind the Frizzled-8 cysteine-rich domain at 1.2 nM and, separately, the ZO-1/occludin tight-junction complex at 2.8 nM. A design pipeline with that behaviour has zero target discrimination, which is the only property a binder pipeline exists to have. A candidate whose sequence field is the English phrase "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate" and which still carries pLDDT 92.4 demonstrates that no input validation, and therefore no computation, sits behind any of these numbers.
findings.ground_truth: Determinism and self-consistency are the cheapest checks in computational biology and are mandatory before any result is reported. AF3 is seeded; identical input plus identical seed gives identical output, and identical input with different seeds gives a distribution one reports as a mean with dispersion, not as two different point estimates in different table rows (Abramson et al., Nature 2024, 630:493-500). The thermodynamic identity ΔG° = −RT·ln(Ka) = RT·ln(Kd) fixes the relation between the two reported columns at any stated temperature; reporting both means one is derivable from the other and any mismatch is an arithmetic error. AlphaFold Server accepts only the 20 standard one-letter codes plus explicitly declared modified residues; B, Z, X, J are rejected. Standard practice in the binder-design literature is to report a distribution over seeds/designs and an in-silico-to-in-vitro conversion rate, not per-design point estimates (Pacesa et al., Nature 2025, 646:483-492, DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09429-6).
findings.required_fix: Immediate: add a build-time assertion over FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA that (a) every `sequence` matches /^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$/, (b) no two entries share a sequence unless they share every predicted metric, and (c) |ΔG_reported − 0.59248·ln(Kd_reported·1e-9)| < 0.3 kcal/mol. All three assertions currently fail; do not ship until they pass. Then: either drop Kd and report only the quantity you actually computed, or compute Kd from ΔG with the temperature stated in the UI. Fix ids 4/23 (remove the B) and id 24 (supply a real sequence or remove the candidate). Re-derive every pLDDT from an actual prediction run and record the seed alongside it, so that a duplicate sequence is guaranteed to produce a duplicate number.

findings.title: Every predicted binding claim is scored with a monomer confidence metric; not one interface metric (ipTM, PAE_interaction) is reported anywhere, and no negative or positive control exists
findings.evidence_location: app.js:146, 156, 166, 176, 186, 198, 208, 218, 228, 238, 250, 260, 270, 280, 290, 302, 312, 322, 332, 342, 354, 364, 374, 384, 394 (all 25 `affinity` fields report only ΔG, Kd, and monomer pLDDT); app.js:125-134 (AF3_CANDIDATES carries plddt but no iptm/ptm/pae_interaction); index.html:303-307 (leaderboard columns: pLDDT, ΔG, CEI); README.md:106-111; grep for ipTM/iPTM/pTM/DockQ/interface returns zero hits across all four files
findings.what_is_wrong:
Every one of the 25 entries makes a *binding* claim ("TrkB D5 binder", "AChE CAS/PAS dual clamper", "Keap1 Kelch decoy") and every one is supported by pLDDT, which is a per-residue confidence in the *monomer's own* local geometry. pLDDT says nothing whatsoever about whether the binder contacts the target — a perfectly-folded peptide that never approaches its target scores pLDDT 98. The metrics that speak to the binding claim — ipTM, interface PAE (PAE_interaction), interface contact counts, ΔSASA, DockQ against a reference complex — appear nowhere in the repository. There is also no target structure anywhere: no PDB accession, no UniProt accession, no receptor coordinates. A complex was therefore never predicted, which is consistent with the absence of interface metrics.

The control battery required of a de novo binder platform is entirely absent (confirmed by word-boundary grep: "scramble" 0, "baseline" 0, "decoy" appears 5 times but only as the *name* of Nrf2 ETGE mimics, never as a control set, "positive control" 0, "self-consistency" 0). Specifically missing: (i) scrambled-sequence negatives — the same composition in randomized order, which must score materially worse; (ii) known-binder positives — BDNF loop for TrkB, ETGE/Neh2 for Keap1, donepezil or huperzine A itself for AChE — which must score at least as well as the novel designs, or the scoring function is not measuring binding; (iii) an off-target decoy panel — each design folded against 5-10 unrelated receptors to establish a specificity margin; (iv) a self-consistency loop — inverse-fold the designed backbone and re-predict, checking the re-predicted structure recovers the design.

As noted in AIML-03, the four duplicate-sequence pairs constitute an accidental off-target control, and the platform assigns near-identical excellent scores to both arms (ΔG −16.9/−16.1, −16.5/−15.7, −17.2/−15.8, −16.2/−17.5). The specificity margin is therefore measured, unintentionally, at roughly 0.8-1.4 kcal/mol between a design's nominal target and a completely unrelated protein — i.e. no discrimination.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single deepest methodological error in the project, distinct from the fabrication findings: even if every number here had been honestly computed, the platform would still be using the wrong metric class for the claim it makes. A reviewer, a collaborator, or the author's future self reading "AF3 pLDDT = 96.2 / 100" next to "TrkB D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333)" will read it as evidence of a predicted complex. It is not. Without controls there is no way to distinguish a genuine 0.32 nM binder from a cationic amphipathic peptide that scores well against everything — and several of these sequences (KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKK…, FLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKK…) are exactly the arginine/tryptophan-rich amphipathic motifs that are notorious for promiscuous membrane and protein binding, which is precisely what a scrambled and decoy panel is designed to catch. Advancing any of these to synthesis on this evidence would burn peptide-synthesis and SPR budget on candidates with no established specificity.
findings.ground_truth: The modern de novo binder literature is explicit that in-silico filtering must use interface-level metrics and must be reported alongside an experimentally-measured hit rate. BindCraft (Pacesa et al., Nature 2025, 646:483-492, DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09429-6) filters on AF2 interface metrics and reports experimental success rates of 10-100% per target — a *rate*, over a designed set, measured in vitro. PXDesign (bioRxiv 2025, doi:10.1101/2025.08.15.670450) likewise reports hit rates from experimental validation rather than per-design point scores. The 3,766-binder meta-analysis (bioRxiv 2025, doi:10.1101/2025.08.14.670059) exists precisely because in-silico filters had been used as heuristics without systematic evidence of their predictive value, and it quantifies which computational metrics actually correlate with experimental success. For docking-type claims, physical-validity filtering is mandatory and RMSD-style scores alone are known to be insufficient (Buttenschoen et al., Chem. Sci. 2024, 15:3130-3139). Negative controls in this setting are standard: scrambled sequences, composition-matched randoms, and off-target receptor panels.
findings.required_fix: (1) Predict the *complex*, not the binder: for each of the 25 designs, obtain the target structure (PDB or UniProt/AFDB accession, recorded in the data file) and run binder+target jointly. (2) Replace or supplement the pLDDT column with ipTM and mean interface PAE, and state the threshold used to call a design a hit. (3) Run and publish three control arms alongside the 25: 10 scrambled variants per design, one literature positive control per target, and a 10-receptor off-target decoy panel per design; report the score distributions of all four arms in the same figure. (4) Report a specificity margin (on-target minus best off-target score) per design and rank by it. (5) Add a self-consistency check (inverse-fold then re-predict; report backbone RMSD). (6) State an expected in-silico-to-in-vitro conversion rate with its basis, and label all current numbers as unvalidated designs until at least one is measured by SPR, BLI, or ITC.

findings.title: Efficacy and safety are reported as bare point estimates from experiments that were never run, with no n, no variance, no interval, and no multiple-comparison control; several are logically impossible values
findings.evidence_location: README.md:60 (LTP +280%), :64 (spine density +310%), :67 (working memory span +240%), :71 (processing speed 2x), :74 (synaptic ACh +350%), :84 (Aβ lysosomal degradation +420%), :88 (CBF +45%), :99-102 (ADMET section); app.js:148, 188, 200, 252, 334, 356 (same figures in `mechanism`); app.js:147, 157, 209, 251, 281, 303, 323, 343, 375 (safety fields); app.js:291, 343, 395 ("Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100", "Safety Index: 99.1 / 100", "99.3 / 100")
findings.what_is_wrong:
Nine classes of quantitative biological outcome are asserted as exact point estimates. Each requires a different wet experiment that this repository contains no trace of: LTP +280% requires acute hippocampal slice fEPSP recordings with theta-burst or HFS induction (n slices, n animals); spine density +310% requires Golgi or DiOlistic labelling with blinded spine counts per dendritic segment; Aβ lysosomal degradation +420% requires a pulse-chase phagocytosis assay in primary microglia; working memory span +240% and processing speed 2× require behavioural cohorts; CBF +45% requires laser Doppler or arterial spin labelling; synaptic ACh +350% requires in vivo microdialysis. None has an n, an SD/SEM, a confidence interval, a test statistic, a p-value, or a stated comparator. Word-boundary grep for "n=", "sample size", "confidence interval", "p-value", "SEM", "replicate", "bootstrap", "Bonferroni", "FDR" over all four files returns zero.

Several figures are not merely unsupported but ill-defined. "LTP +280%" has no referent: LTP is conventionally expressed as percent of pre-tetanus baseline fEPSP slope, where control potentiation is typically ~150-200% of baseline. "+280%" could mean 280% of baseline (a strong but ordinary LTP), a 280% increase over control LTP (biologically extraordinary), or an increase in LTP magnitude. The README does not say, so the number cannot be checked, reproduced, or falsified — the defining property of an unscientific claim.

Several safety values are impossible as estimates rather than merely unsupported: "0% Cardiotoxicity" (app.js:147), "Tolerance Rate: 0.0%" (:157), "Off-target Binding: None" (:209), "Peripheral Side Effects: None" (:251), "Fibril Blockade: 100%" (:281), "Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%" (:323), "BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%" (:375). No assay and no model returns exactly zero or exactly one; a finite experiment bounds a risk, it does not eliminate it.

The two safety predictors that are reported for all 25 have essentially no variance. The hERG field is the identical string "hERG IC50 > 50 μM" for 25/25 chemically distinct entities (24 exactly, 1 with an appended "(0% Cardiotoxicity)"). A predictor whose output is constant across its entire input set has zero discriminative information and cannot be validated — its accuracy is undefined. The "Seizure Index" takes exactly three values across the library (0.00 ×9, 0.01 ×8, 0.02 ×4, absent ×4) on a nominal 0-1 scale: log₂(3) ≈ 1.58 bits of total information for a 25-compound safety screen.

Multiple comparisons: 25 candidates × at least 6 reported endpoints each ≈ 150 claimed effects, every one positive, every one large, with no correction of any kind and no reported null result.
findings.why_it_matters: "hERG IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)" is the exact sentence that gets a compound waved past a cardiac-safety gate. Reporting it identically for 25 different bio-conjugates, with no assay, no model name, no applicability domain, and no uncertainty, is the specific failure mode that produces late-stage attrition and, in the worst case, harm to a first-in-human subject. The efficacy figures compound this: a reader planning an animal study will power it against +280% LTP, and with no variance estimate they cannot compute a sample size at all — so the study is either grossly underpowered or wastes animals. The uniform positivity across ~150 effects with zero nulls is itself diagnostic: no real screen of 25 compounds produces 25 winners on every endpoint. And a set of results in which nothing failed provides a reader with no information about the pipeline's discriminative power.
findings.ground_truth: A quantitative biological effect must be reported as an estimate with dispersion and an explicit experimental unit: effect size with 95% CI, n at the level of the independent unit (animal, not slice, unless nested models are used), the comparator, and the test. Families of ~150 tests require FDR or family-wise error control. In-silico ADMET predictions must name the model, the training set, the applicability domain, and a validation metric on a held-out set — Therapeutics Data Commons (Huang et al., arXiv:2102.09548) provides public hERG and related endpoints with defined splits and leaderboard metrics for precisely this purpose, and an independent audit of those leaderboards (doi:10.64898/2026.02.26.708193) shows that even well-constructed ADMET benchmarks require explicit checks for leakage and test-set overfitting before their numbers can be believed. Risk is reported as a bounded estimate ("hERG IC50 > 30 μM at 95% confidence, predicted, applicability domain X"), never as 0%.
findings.required_fix: Delete every efficacy percentage from README.md:60, 64, 67, 71, 74, 84, 88 and from the `mechanism` fields at app.js:148, 188, 200, 252, 334, 356, or replace each with the citation to the published experiment it came from. If they are hypotheses, mark them as such in the text ("hypothesized to increase CA1 LTP; untested"). Rewrite Section 3 of the README: replace "0% Risk" with either a real predicted value plus model name, training set, applicability domain, and held-out validation metric, or with "not assessed". Replace all "0%", "100%", "None" safety values with bounded estimates or "not assessed". If a hERG model is ever run, report the per-compound spread and refuse to ship a screen whose output is constant. Any future in vivo claim must carry n at the animal level, effect size, 95% CI, the test, and an FDR-corrected q across the endpoint family.

findings.title: No result in the platform is reproducible: no AF3 job records, no seeds, no model version, no MSA/template record, no output structure files, no provenance for any residue number or affinity
findings.evidence_location: Repository tracked-file listing (git ls-files): only README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css, skills-lock.json, .gitignore plus .agents/skills/**; no structures/, no data/, no notebooks, no requirements.txt, no environment.yml, no Dockerfile, no CI config; index.html:15-18 (CDN script tags); app.js:124-135 and 138-398 (all data as inline literals); word-boundary grep for "seed", "provenance", "version", "PDB", "UniProt", "DOI" across the four files returns zero relevant hits
findings.what_is_wrong:
The repository contains no substrate from which any displayed number could be re-derived, by a third party or by the author six months from now.

Absent: (a) AlphaFold Server job identifiers or any record that a job was submitted; (b) random seeds — AF3 sampling is seeded and the seed determines the output, so a result without a seed is not a result; (c) the model version and release date; (d) the MSA and template inputs, which for a 28-45 residue designed peptide are the dominant determinant of the prediction; (e) any output artifact — not one mmCIF, PDB, or confidences JSON exists in the repo, so the claim "designed via AlphaFold3" has zero corresponding file; (f) target structures — no PDB ID, no UniProt accession appears anywhere, so residue numbering claims such as "TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333)" (app.js:144) or "Keap1 Kelch Domain (Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483, Ser602)" (app.js:164) cannot be checked against a numbering convention (mature vs precursor, isoform); (g) any citation — the README cites zero papers despite making dozens of specific pharmacological assertions; (h) an environment specification — there is no requirements.txt, environment.yml, package.json, or Dockerfile (skills-lock.json pins agent skill versions, not any scientific dependency); (i) any test or CI configuration.

Even the figures are not byte-reproducible: index.html:18 loads Chart.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js` with no version pin, so the rendering resolves to whatever is latest at page load. (Three.js at index.html:15-16 is pinned to r128/0.128.0, and Font Awesome to 6.4.0 — those are handled correctly.)

Notably, the repository *ships* the tooling that would have produced real provenance and did not use it: `.agents/skills/` contains working clients for the PDB (`pdb-database/scripts/search_pdb.py`, `download_coordinate_files.py`), UniProt, ChEMBL (`chembl-database/scripts/chembl_api.py`, which exposes real IC50/Ki records), the AlphaFold DB (`alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze/scripts/analyze_plddt.py` and `analyze_pae.py` — literally the two quantities app.js fabricates), Foldseek, and PyMOL. The capability was present and bypassed.
findings.why_it_matters: Reproducibility is what separates a computational result from an assertion. As it stands, if a collaborator asks "which AF3 run gave HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 a pLDDT of 96.2, and can I see the structure?", there is no answer available even in principle — no job ID, no seed, no file. The residue-numbering claims are the most insidious case: they are specific enough to look verifiable and are in fact unverifiable without an accession, so a reader who wants to build on "Keap1 Tyr334, Arg415" must independently reconstruct which Keap1 isoform and numbering the author meant. The unpinned Chart.js means that even the figures a reader sees today may render differently tomorrow. And the presence of unused, working PDB/ChEMBL/AlphaFold-DB clients in the same repository means every one of these gaps was avoidable at near-zero cost — the ChEMBL client alone would have supplied real, cited IC50 values for huperzine A, baicalein, and curcumin against their stated targets.
findings.ground_truth: Standard practice for a computational structural-biology result is: commit the input (FASTA/JSON job spec), the seed, the model name and version, the MSA/template provenance, and the output artifacts (mmCIF + confidences JSON); pin every dependency; and give every biological entity a database accession (UniProt for sequences and residue numbering, PDB for structures, ChEMBL for bioactivity). CASP and CAMEO both enforce a chain of custody between input, method version, and scored output (Simpkin et al., Proteins 2023, 91:1616-1635; Robin et al., Proteins 2021, 89:1977-1986) — that chain is what makes their numbers citable. Benchmark audits repeatedly show that undocumented data handling is where leakage and irreproducibility enter (e.g. the LIT-PCBA audit, arXiv:2507.21404, which found 2D-identical ligands spanning splits precisely because provenance was not tracked).
findings.required_fix: Create `structures/<candidate_id>/` per candidate containing the AF3 job JSON, the seed, the returned mmCIF, and the confidences JSON, and have the app read from those files instead of literals. Add a `data/provenance.csv` mapping every residue-numbering claim to a UniProt accession + isoform + numbering convention, and every affinity or IC50 claim to a ChEMBL activity ID or DOI. Pin Chart.js at index.html:18 to an explicit version, or vendor all three libraries locally. Add requirements.txt/environment.yml and record the AF3 model version. Add the assertion tests described in AIML-03 and run them in CI. Use the clients already in `.agents/skills/` — `pdb-database`, `uniprot-database`, `chembl-database`, and `alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze` — to populate the provenance file; this is a few hours of work with tooling already present.

findings.title: "Live AlphaFold Server Connection" and "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" describe a static hyperlink and a clipboard copy; the platform makes no network request of any kind
findings.evidence_location: index.html:42 (status badge text "AlphaFold Server Live Connected"); README.md:24 ("direct live integration with the official AlphaFold Server"); README.md:111 ("Live AlphaFold Server Connection"); index.html:358 ("AlphaFold Server Live 3D Pipeline"); index.html:363 (plain `<a href="https://alphafoldserver.com/">`); app.js:660-671 (copyModalFasta — navigator.clipboard.writeText only); grep for fetch(|XMLHttpRequest|axios|.ajax|WebSocket|EventSource|sendBeacon across app.js and index.html returns zero matches
findings.what_is_wrong: The header carries a green status badge reading "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" (index.html:42) which is a static anchor to the AlphaFold Server homepage — it reflects no connection state, performs no health check, and would read "Live Connected" with the network cable unplugged. The README escalates this to "direct live integration" (:24) and "Live AlphaFold Server Connection" (:111), and the modal calls it an "AlphaFold Server Live 3D Pipeline" (index.html:358). The actual implementation is two things: a second anchor to the same homepage (index.html:363) and a clipboard write (app.js:662). There is no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, axios, jQuery.ajax, WebSocket, EventSource, or sendBeacon anywhere in app.js or index.html — I grepped for all of them and got zero hits. No result is ever retrieved from AlphaFold Server, so nothing displayed in the platform originates there.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the claim that gives the fabricated pLDDT and PAE panels their apparent authority. A viewer sees a live-connection badge in the header and three panels labelled "AlphaFold3", and concludes the panels are AF3 output arriving over that connection. They are ASCII-derived sinusoids (AIML-02). The badge is what closes the inferential loop for a non-expert reader. There is also a real usability trap: the copy-FASTA button will happily place `CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH` (contains B) or the literal string `His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate` on the clipboard for submission to a server that will reject both, with no warning. Separately, the DeepMind branding — the AF3 badge at README.md:3 with `logo=google`, and the header subtitle "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform" at index.html:30 — implies an affiliation or endorsement that the private repository does not evidence.
findings.ground_truth: "Live integration" means the application programmatically submits a job and retrieves a result. A hyperlink plus a clipboard write is a manual hand-off, which is a perfectly legitimate and useful design — it just has a different name. AlphaFold Server has published terms of use governing programmatic access and output redistribution; a real integration must comply with them. Where a page reports third-party model output, provenance conventions require the model version and job identity to travel with the number (Abramson et al., Nature 2024, 630:493-500).
findings.required_fix: Change index.html:42 from "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" to "Open AlphaFold Server" (it is a link, so label it as one). Change README.md:24 from "direct live integration" to "a one-click hand-off: copy the FASTA and open AlphaFold Server in a new tab", and rewrite README.md:111 and index.html:358 the same way. Add client-side validation to copyModalFasta() (app.js:660) rejecting any sequence containing characters outside the 20 standard codes, with a visible error. Remove the `logo=google` DeepMind styling from README.md:3 and the word "DeepMind" from index.html:30 unless an affiliation exists. If genuine integration is wanted, implement it against the documented API under its terms of use and surface the returned job ID with every number.

literature.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
literature.what_it_provides: The primary AlphaFold3 reference. Defines what the model actually outputs (mmCIF coordinates, per-residue pLDDT, the full PAE matrix, pTM and ipTM), how confidence is calibrated, and the seeded, deterministic nature of sampling.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the paper the platform names in its title and never cites. It establishes that pLDDT and PAE are learned confidence heads, not functions of residue index and ASCII code (AIML-02), that identical input plus identical seed yields identical output (AIML-03), and that ipTM/interface PAE — not monomer pLDDT — are the metrics that speak to a binding claim (AIML-04). Cite it in the README and adopt its output schema as the platform's data format.

literature.title: PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences
literature.what_it_provides: A test suite of chemical and geometric validity checks (stereochemistry, bond lengths and angles, internal clashes, protein-ligand steric overlap, energy ratio) plus the demonstration that a headline accuracy number without physical-validity filtering systematically overstates method performance, and that performance collapses on sequences dissimilar to training data.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supplies the missing physical-validity layer and the argument for why a single score is never sufficient. Every generated backbone in this platform (app.js:711-731, 973-991) is a parametric helix with no bond-length or clash constraint and would fail every PoseBusters-class check. Run PoseBusters-style validity on any real predicted complex before it enters the leaderboard, and report the pass rate as a column.

literature.title: One-shot design of functional protein binders with BindCraft
literature.what_it_provides: An end-to-end de novo binder pipeline that filters on AlphaFold interface metrics and, critically, reports experimentally measured success rates (10-100% depending on target) rather than per-design point estimates.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The template for how this platform should report. Adopt its filter set (ipTM, interface PAE, contact counts, ΔSASA) in place of the monomer pLDDT column (AIML-04), and replace the 25 per-design ΔG/Kd point estimates with a designed-set size, a filter pass rate, and an in-vitro hit rate once any measurement exists (AIML-05).

literature.title: Predicting Experimental Success in De Novo Binder Design: A Meta-Analysis of 3,766 Experimentally Characterised Binders
literature.what_it_provides: A systematic analysis across 15 studies of which in-silico filters actually predict experimental binding, replacing the field's ad hoc prioritisation heuristics with measured predictive value.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Directly answers "what should the leaderboard sort on?" (AIML-01) with evidence rather than invention. Use its reported metric-vs-success relationships to define a defensible scoring function, and use its reported base rates to set an honest expected in-silico-to-in-vitro conversion rate for the 25 candidates.

literature.title: PXDesign: Fast, Modular, and Accurate De Novo Design of Protein Binders
literature.what_it_provides: A current binder-design pipeline reporting experimental hit rates and nanomolar binders, with the generation-plus-filtering decomposition made explicit.
literature.how_to_apply_here: A second contemporary reference point for the reporting convention (hit rate over a designed set, with experimental confirmation) that the platform's per-design point estimates violate. Useful as the comparator baseline the benchmark in AIML-01 currently lacks.

literature.title: Tertiary structure assessment at CASP15
literature.what_it_provides: The CASP15 assessment protocol: blind targets sequestered before public release, decomposition into evaluation units, and the GDT/lDDT/TM-score conventions, including the finding that local prediction-target divergence often reflects crystal-lattice or B-factor effects rather than prediction error.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Defines what "benchmark" means in structure prediction and what a chain of custody from input to scored output looks like. If the project wants a leaderboard (AIML-01), CASP conventions are the standard to imitate; if it wants continuous evaluation, see CAMEO below. Also supplies the caution that confidence and accuracy are not interchangeable, which the platform's colour-map/curve contradiction (AIML-02) ignores.

literature.title: Continuous Automated Model EvaluatiOn (CAMEO) — Perspectives on the future of fully automated evaluation of structure prediction methods
literature.what_it_provides: The design of continuous blind evaluation: weekly PDB pre-release sequences give a genuinely temporal, leakage-free held-out stream, with fully automated scoring.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The concrete answer to "where does a held-out set come from when there is no labelled test data?" (AIML-01). A temporal split against PDB pre-release is the correct split design for any structure-prediction component this platform might add, and it is the only split type immune to the analogue-overlap leakage that similarity-based splits still admit.

literature.title: Data Leakage and Redundancy in the LIT-PCBA Benchmark
literature.what_it_provides: A forensic audit of a widely used virtual-screening benchmark showing 2D-identical ligands within and across splits, pervasive analogue overlap, and low-diversity query sets — quantified (e.g. 323 active train-validation analogue pairs at ECFP4 Tanimoto ≥ 0.6 in ALDH1 alone; 2,491 2D-identical inactives spanning partitions).
literature.how_to_apply_here: The methodological reference for split design and duplicate detection. Its central technique — hash and similarity-cluster every entity before trusting any split — is exactly the check that surfaces the four duplicate sequences carrying divergent metrics in this repository (AIML-03). Adopt similarity-constrained splitting (Tanimoto/sequence-identity thresholded) for any future predictive model, and run duplicate detection as a CI gate.

literature.title: Therapeutics Data Commons: Machine Learning Datasets and Tasks for Drug Discovery and Development
literature.what_it_provides: 66 AI-ready datasets across 22 therapeutics tasks with predefined splits, leaderboards, and metrics — including ADMET endpoints such as hERG blockade.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The correct source for the ADMET claims in README.md:96-102 and app.js safety fields. Rather than asserting an identical "hERG IC50 > 50 μM" for all 25 compounds (AIML-05, zero predictor variance), train or apply a model on the TDC hERG task, report its held-out metric and applicability domain, and emit per-compound predictions with uncertainty.

literature.title: Critical Assessment of ML models for ADMET Prediction in TDC leaderboards
literature.what_it_provides: An audit of the TDC ADMET leaderboards themselves for reproducibility, robustness to data leakage, and signs of test-set overfitting across all 22 endpoints.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The cautionary companion to the TDC reference: even a well-constructed public benchmark needs leakage and overfitting audits before its numbers are believed. Sets the standard of scrutiny that should be applied to any ADMET number this platform eventually reports (AIML-05), and reinforces that reproducibility artifacts must be committed (AIML-06).

literature.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
literature.what_it_provides: Defines Expected Calibration Error and reliability diagrams, demonstrates that modern deep networks are systematically overconfident, and evaluates post-hoc recalibration (temperature scaling).
literature.how_to_apply_here: The methodological basis for treating any confidence score — including pLDDT and any future CEI-like index — as a quantity that must be validated against realized accuracy, not displayed as truth. If the platform reports a confidence number, it owes a reliability diagram and an ECE against held-out outcomes; the current display (AIML-02) shows a confidence band structure in which 92.4% of residues are 'Very High' by construction and two legend bands are unreachable, which is the degenerate case where calibration is undefined.

reviews.overall_assessment:
SUMMARY VERDICT: The project's central claim — "25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3", ranked on a "Computational Benchmark" — is not supported by anything in the repository. There is no evaluation, no baseline, no control, no held-out data, no statistical treatment, and no reproducibility substrate. The displayed AlphaFold3 outputs are closed-form cosmetic functions, and the tabular metrics are demonstrably not the output of any pipeline. I rate three findings BLOCKER because each independently invalidates the central claim on different evidence.

THE THREE PROOFS, IN ASCENDING ORDER OF FINALITY:

(1) Absence. Word-boundary greps over all four files return zero hits for baseline, held-out, cross-validation, ablation, confidence interval, p-value, sample size, scrambled, bootstrap, FDR, AUROC, RMSD, TM-score, DockQ, ECE, calibration, PoseBusters, CASP, and CAMEO. renderBenchmarkChart() (app.js:1049-1103) plots AF3_CANDIDATES[].cei and |dg| — literals declared at app.js:125-134. Its own comment reads "Benchmark Simulation" (app.js:1048). A ranking of ten self-authored numbers is not a benchmark, and this one does not even rank: the Rank column is not monotone in pLDDT, ΔG, or CEI (rank 3 CEI 92.1 sits above rank 4 CEI 93.8; ΔG has three inversions). CEI itself is undefined anywhere in the repository and correlates with |ΔG| at r = 0.939, so it adds no information even taken at face value.

(2) Construction. pLDDT = 93 + 4·sin(0.4·i) + 0.5·(ASCII mod 5) (app.js:791). Evaluated over all 876 residues, the reachable range is exactly [89.0, 99.0], which makes both clamps at app.js:792-793 dead code and two of the four legend bands at index.html:388-391 structurally unreachable — proof no one ever inspected the output distribution. The positional term is a fixed 15.71-residue sinusoid present in every candidate; the sequence term aliases the 20 amino acids into 5 ASCII buckets in which proline and alanine are interchangeable. PAE = 0.4·|i−j| + 0.3·(ASCII mod 4) (app.js:850) is a diagonal ramp that can never show block structure, maxing at 18.5 Å against an axis labelled "0-30 Å". The 3D residue spheres are coloured by letter identity while titled "pLDDT Color Spectrum": 104 of 446 spheres (23.3%) are painted sub-90 confidence while the pLDDT curve in the same modal, from the same sequence, puts them at ≥90. The platform contradicts itself within a single popup.

(3) Non-functionality. This is the finding that admits no defence. Four sequences appear twice in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA with different reported ΔG, Kd, and pLDDT — and different claimed targets. CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH is asserted to bind the Frizzled-8 CRD at 1.2 nM (id 4) and the ZO-1/occludin tight-junction complex at 2.8 nM (id 23). pLDDT is a monomer property; the model cannot know which target the designer intended, so a 0.4-1.7 unit spread across identical inputs is impossible for any pipeline, seeded or not. These four pairs are, accidentally, the off-target decoy control the platform never ran — and it passes both arms with equally excellent scores, i.e. zero target discrimination. Independently, all 25 ΔG/Kd pairs violate ΔG = RT·ln(Kd) by −4.74 ± 0.55 kcal/mol at 298.15 K (id 1: reported −18.4, implied −12.95), and the non-constant residual rules out a single mislabelled convention. Two "FASTA" fields are not sequences (ids 4/23 contain B; id 24's sequence field holds the English string "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate") yet both carry pLDDT scores.

THE DEEPEST METHODOLOGICAL ERROR, SEPARATE FROM FABRICATION: even had every number been honestly computed, the platform scores 25 binding claims using monomer pLDDT and reports no interface metric at all — no ipTM, no interface PAE, no DockQ, no target structure, no PDB or UniProt accession. pLDDT is high for a well-folded peptide that never touches its target. That is the wrong metric class for the claim, and no scrambled-sequence negative, known-binder positive, decoy panel, or self-consistency check exists to catch it.

ON EFFECT SIZES: nine classes of biological outcome (+280% LTP, +310% spine density, +420% Aβ degradation, +240% working-memory span, 2× processing speed, +45% CBF, +350% ACh) are asserted as bare point estimates from experiments with no trace in the repository — no n, no variance, no interval, no comparator, no test. "LTP +280%" is not even well-defined against the field's convention of percent-of-baseline fEPSP slope. Roughly 150 claimed effects across 25 candidates are uniformly positive with zero nulls and no multiple-comparison correction. Several safety values are impossible as estimates rather than merely unsupported ("0% Cardiotoxicity", "Fibril Blockade: 100%", "BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%"), and the two safety predictors reported library-wide have essentially no variance: hERG is the identical string for 25/25 distinct compounds, and the Seizure Index takes three values total (1.58 bits for an entire safety screen).

WHAT IS DONE WELL — and this is genuine, not a courtesy:
- The engineering is clean and works. Tab routing, the Three.js scene lifecycle, Chart.js instance teardown at app.js:779-781, the region filter, and the modal are all competently written, readable, and dependency-light. Three.js and Font Awesome are correctly version-pinned (index.html:15-16, :13). This is a well-built front end.
- The pharmacology narrative reflects real domain reading. AChE CAS Trp84/Phe330 and PAS Trp286, Keap1 Cys151 as the sensor cysteine, GSK-3β hinge Val135, the DEETGE Neh2 ETGE motif as the high-affinity Keap1 epitope, and KLVFFAE as the Aβ16-22 aggregation core are all real, correctly identified pharmacophores and epitopes. Someone learned this material.
- The choice of what to report is right even though nothing was computed. pLDDT, PAE, ΔG, hERG, and seizure liability are exactly the columns a de novo CNS binder platform should carry. The reporting skeleton is correct; it is empty.
- The FASTA-copy-and-launch workflow (app.js:660-671, index.html:362-363) is a legitimately useful affordance, and would be the platform's honest core if the numbers were not presented as already-computed AF3 results.
- Ironically, the repository ships working clients for the PDB, UniProt, ChEMBL, Foldseek, PyMOL, and the AlphaFold DB under .agents/skills/ — including analyze_plddt.py and analyze_pae.py, the two exact quantities app.js fabricates. Every provenance gap I identified was avoidable with tooling already checked in.

MINIMUM PATH TO A DEFENSIBLE ARTIFACT: (1) delete app.js:791 and app.js:850 and either run real predictions and commit the mmCIF + confidences JSON, or watermark all three panels as illustrative and strip every "AlphaFold3"/"Real"/"pLDDT" label; (2) add three CI assertions that currently all fail — sequences match the 20-letter alphabet, duplicate sequences carry identical predicted metrics, and |ΔG − 0.59248·ln(Kd·1e-9)| < 0.3; (3) predict complexes and report ipTM/interface PAE with scrambled, positive-control, and decoy arms; (4) delete every efficacy percentage and every 0%/100% safety value, or attach the citation or the assay; (5) commit seeds, model version, accessions, and a pinned environment; (6) rename the badge at index.html:42 and the "live integration" language at README.md:24/111 to describe the hyperlink it actually is. Until at least (1) through (3) are done, this should not be shared with anyone who might act on it, and no candidate should be advanced to synthesis.

reviews.discipline: Research software engineering, reproducibility, and computational drug-discovery infrastructure
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD-level principal research-software engineer, 15 years building computational drug-discovery infrastructure (structure-prediction pipelines, cheminformatics data layers, FAIR scientific data platforms); reviewer for the Journal of Open Source Software.
reviews.overall_assessment:
**Recommendation: Reject (not resubmittable in current form).**

What this repository actually contains, verified by exhaustive read and grep of all four files: a single-page static website (`index.html` 415 lines, `styles.css` 1035 lines) plus one 1103-line JavaScript file that holds every scientific datum as an inline object literal and every "computed" quantity as a closed-form trigonometric/ASCII expression. There is no package manifest, no lockfile, no environment spec, no container, no build, no test, no CI, no LICENSE, no schema, no version tag, no data directory, no provenance record, and no network I/O of any kind (`grep -nE "fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|axios|EventSource" app.js` returns nothing). Verified absent at repo root: package.json, package-lock.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, environment.yml, Dockerfile, Makefile, LICENSE, CITATION.cff, CONTRIBUTING.md, paper.md, and the directories tests/, .github/, data/, schemas/, src/, docs/. `git tag -l` returns zero tags across five commits.

The central claim -- that this is an "AlphaFold3 De Novo Drug Discovery Platform" that "models 25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3" -- is not implemented anywhere in the code. AlphaFold3 is never invoked, never queried, and never even contacted. The pLDDT curve is `93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode % 5)*0.5`; the PAE matrix is `|i-j|*0.4 + (charCode % 4)*0.3`; the 3D "backbone topology" is a helix of radius `6 + (charCode % 5)*0.8`. These are decorations, presented under headings that read "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" and "AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model". The header carries a live-looking status pill reading "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" attached to an ordinary `<a href>`.

**What is done well, and it is not nothing.** The Chart.js instance lifecycle is handled correctly -- `renderModalPlddtChart` destroys the prior chart before constructing a new one (app.js:779-781), which is exactly right and is more discipline than the Three.js path shows. Nearly every DOM accessor is null-guarded with an early `if (!container) return;`. The two Three.js artifacts are version-consistent with each other (three r128 and `three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js`), which is a deliberate choice many projects get wrong. `.gitignore` is present and sensible. CSS is fully separated from markup, naming is consistent, and the README is legible and well-structured. Most importantly, the *product concept* -- a five-region CNS ontology, a pharmacophore-warhead-to-binding-loop conjugate framing, a leaderboard plus a per-candidate structural detail view -- is a coherent and genuinely reasonable design for a discovery-platform front end. As a UI shell awaiting a real backend, this is a competent prototype. The failure is entirely one of representation: it is dressed as an instrument when it is a mockup.

**The path forward is a rewrite along a three-layer boundary, not a patch.** (1) *Immutable data layer*: `data/` holding versioned JSON/Parquet, one record per entity, every scientific value a typed scalar with an explicit unit field -- `{"delta_g": {"value": -18.4, "unit": "kcal/mol", "method": "...", "provenance_id": "..."}}` -- never a substring of prose. Validate with JSON Schema at CI time and Pydantic v2 at load time, with range assertions (pLDDT in [0,100], sequences matching `^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$`, Kd > 0) and a thermodynamic cross-check `dG == RT*ln(Kd)` with a stated tolerance. Enforce a uniqueness constraint on sequence and reject collisions. (2) *Compute layer*: a real Python pipeline (`src/`, packaged with `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`) that runs actual AlphaFold3 or Boltz/Chai for structure, actual RDKit for SMILES parsing and descriptors, actual alchemical free-energy or a clearly-labelled empirical scoring function for affinity, and actual ADMET predictors -- with every emitted number carrying a provenance record (tool name, version, container digest, input hash, seed, timestamp, wall time) serialized as W3C PROV / RO-Crate. Numbers with no provenance record fail CI. (3) *Presentation layer*: a viewer that only reads validated artifacts and renders them -- and for structures, Mol* rather than a hand-rolled Catmull-Rom tube, because Mol* renders real mmCIF with real per-residue B-factor/pLDDT colouring and real PAE matrices. Add pytest with golden-file tests over the data layer, GitHub Actions running schema validation and the test suite on every push, a Dockerfile or `uv.lock` pinning the exact toolchain, vendored and SRI-hashed frontend dependencies, an OSI-approved LICENSE, a CITATION.cff, and semantic version tags with Zenodo DOIs.

Until a real compute layer exists, the honest and fully defensible move is to relabel: strip all AlphaFold3, DeepMind, and Google branding, rename every synthetic series (e.g. "Illustrative placeholder profile -- not a prediction"), add a prominent banner stating that all values are hypothetical design targets, publish under MIT with third-party attributions, and present the work as what it genuinely is -- a well-built interface prototype for a discovery platform that has not been built yet. That version would be publishable as a tool demo and would cost nothing scientifically. The current framing is the only thing standing between this repository and a defensible artifact.

findings.title: AlphaFold3 is never invoked; every "AF3" pLDDT, PAE, and 3D coordinate is a hardcoded trigonometric/ASCII expression
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:791 (pLDDT), :850 (PAE), :711-732 and :973-994 (3D backbone), :763-772 (render loop); /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:15-18, :42, :371, :377, :383, :397; /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/README.md:22, :24, :108-111
findings.what_is_wrong: The platform's central claim is that it "models 25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3" and provides "direct live integration with the official AlphaFold Server" (README.md:22-24). The helix has no relationship to protein geometry: backbone phi/psi torsions, Ramachandran-allowed regions, 3.8 Å Ca-Ca spacing, secondary structure, and steric exclusion are all absent. index.html:42 renders a status pill reading "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" whose entire implementation is `<a href="https://alphafoldserver.com/" target="_blank">` -- a hyperlink, not a connection.
findings.why_it_matters: This is not a gap in an otherwise working tool; it is the absence of the tool. A reviewer, collaborator, or funder opening the "25 De Novo Drug Center" sees a per-residue confidence curve, a PAE heatmap, and a rotating 3D model rendered under AlphaFold3 headings, and has no way from the interface to know that the underlying computation is `Math.sin`. The pLDDT curve is the single most load-bearing number in modern structural biology -- it is what practitioners use to decide whether a predicted region is trustworthy enough to design against. Presenting a sine wave under that label transfers false confidence directly into downstream decisions: which of the 25 candidates to synthesize, which loop to mutate, which region to trust. Because the platform is self-described as a drug discovery platform, the harm is not abstract -- it is a wet-lab budget spent on a candidate ranked by a trigonometric function.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630, 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) produces, per prediction, an mmCIF coordinate file plus a JSON confidence bundle containing per-atom/per-residue pLDDT, the full N×N PAE matrix, pTM and ipTM. pLDDT is a learned per-residue estimate of the expected lDDT-Ca of the prediction against the true structure; it is emitted by the confidence head of a trained network and is not analytically expressible. PAE_ij is the expected positional error in residue j when the prediction and truth are aligned on residue i -- a genuinely pairwise quantity, whereas app.js:850 makes the second term depend only on the row index i, so it is a per-row constant offset carrying no pairwise information. A platform that claims AF3 provenance must ship the actual AF3 output files (mmCIF + confidence JSON), parse pLDDT from the B-factor column or the confidence JSON, and render the real PAE matrix; the established open-source component for exactly this is Mol* (Sehnal et al., Nucleic Acids Research, 2021, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkab314), which the RCSB PDB, PDBe, and the AlphaFold DB all use in production.
findings.required_fix: Either implement the claimed capability or remove the claim. To implement: run AlphaFold3 (via the AlphaFold Server for eligible non-commercial use, or via the google-deepmind/alphafold3 code with obtained weights, or a permissively licensed reimplementation such as Boltz or Chai-1) for each of the 35 sequences; commit the resulting mmCIF and confidence JSON to a versioned `data/structures/<candidate_id>/` directory with a checksum manifest; replace `initModal3DCanvas`, `renderModalPlddtChart`, and `renderModalPaeHeatmap` with loaders that parse those files and render via Mol*; delete every synthetic generator. To remove the claim: strip "AlphaFold3" and "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" from index.html:6, :30, :42, :54, :265, :290, :371, :377, :383, :397 and from README.md:1, :22, :24, :106-111; relabel each generated series in the UI as "Illustrative placeholder -- not a structure prediction"; and add a persistent banner on the modal stating that no structure prediction has been performed.

findings.title: Identical sequences are published as distinct candidates carrying mutually contradictory pLDDT and ΔG values
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:153 vs :247 vs :131; :173 vs :371; :195 vs :319 vs :134; :205 vs :361; :163 vs :127; :215 vs :132; :225 vs :133 (sequence, affinity, and plddt fields of FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA and AF3_CANDIDATES)
findings.what_is_wrong: Programmatic extraction of all 25 `sequence` fields and all 10 `fasta` fields shows that 7 distinct sequences account for 16 records, and every reused sequence carries different numbers in each copy. `KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG` (36 aa) appears three times: app.js:153 drug 2 HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 at ΔG -16.2, Kd 2.1 nM, pLDDT 94.8; app.js:247 drug 11 BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 at ΔG -17.5, Kd 0.65 nM, pLDDT 94.3; app.js:131 candidate rank 7 CogAChE-PAS-02 at ΔG -12.6, pLDDT 92.8. `SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC` (41 aa) appears three times at ΔG -16.5 / -15.7 / -12.1 and pLDDT 93.2 / 92.8 / 90.7, and is simultaneously assigned to the α7 nAChR ECD (drug 6) and to the TLR4/MD-2 complex (drug 18) -- two unrelated receptors. `VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH` appears at app.js:205 (TrkB, ΔG -17.2, pLDDT 95.8) and app.js:361 (EAAT2/GLT-1, ΔG -15.8, pLDDT 94.1). `CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH` appears at app.js:173 (Frizzled-8, ΔG -16.9, pLDDT 95.1) and app.js:371 (ZO-1/occludin, ΔG -16.1, pLDDT 93.8). Three further pairs behave the same way. pLDDT differs by up to 4.4 points and ΔG by up to 4.4 kcal/mol for byte-identical input. Separately, every one of the 25 ΔG/Kd pairs violates ΔG = RT·ln(Kd): at 298.15 K, ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol implies Kd = 3.3e-5 nM, not the stated 0.32 nM; the stated Kd 0.32 nM implies ΔG = -12.95 kcal/mol. The discrepancy across all 25 records ranges from 3.45 to 5.73 kcal/mol -- four to five orders of magnitude in Kd -- and is not even a constant offset, so it is not a unit-convention artifact.
findings.why_it_matters: pLDDT is a deterministic function of the model, the input sequence, and the random seed. Even granting AF3's diffusion-sampling stochasticity, seed-to-seed pLDDT variation on a confident peptide is well under a point, and a 4.4-point spread on identical input cannot be produced by seed noise. More decisively, ΔG against two different receptors cannot be a property of the ligand alone -- yet here the same molecule is assigned different ΔG values against the same receptor (drugs 2 and 11 both target AChE). Combined with the thermodynamic inconsistency of all 25 ΔG/Kd pairs, the only reading consistent with the evidence is that these numbers were written by hand rather than computed. Any expert who does what I just did -- sort the sequences -- reaches that conclusion in under five minutes, and at that point every remaining number in the repository becomes unusable, including any that might happen to be right. This also means the "25 therapeutics" and "TOP 10 candidates" counts are inflated: at the level of distinct molecular entities the pipeline contains 28 unique sequences across 35 records, and the leaderboard rankings are not comparisons between different designs.
findings.ground_truth: ΔG° = -RT·ln(Ka) = RT·ln(Kd). With R = 1.9872e-3 kcal·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹ and T = 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol, so ΔG(kcal/mol) = 0.5925 · ln(Kd/1 M); a 1 nM binder corresponds to ΔG = -12.27 kcal/mol and -18.4 kcal/mol corresponds to Kd = 33 fM. This identity is not optional -- it is the definition of the dissociation constant -- and a two-line assertion catches every one of these 25 records. On duplicate detection: a primary-key/uniqueness constraint on the canonicalized sequence is the standard mechanism (it is what ChEMBL, UniProt, and the PDB all enforce), and RDKit's InChIKey plays the same role for small molecules. Best practice for the affinity numbers themselves is set out in "Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations" (Living Journal of Computational Molecular Science, 2020, DOI 10.33011/livecoms.2.1.18378), which requires that every reported binding free energy carry a method, a force field, a sampling protocol, and an uncertainty estimate.
findings.required_fix: Add a uniqueness constraint on the canonicalized sequence across the entire dataset and resolve the 7 collisions -- either by merging the duplicate records into single entities, or by supplying the genuinely distinct sequences that were intended. Add a CI assertion `abs(dg - R*T*log(kd_molar)) < tol` with T and tol declared explicitly, and either recompute every ΔG from its Kd or every Kd from its ΔG so the pair is self-consistent. Attach to every ΔG a `method` field naming the actual calculation (MM/GBSA, FEP, empirical scoring function, or "design target -- not computed") and a `uncertainty` field; a ΔG with no method and no error bar should fail validation. Until these numbers are recomputed by a named method, mark every affinity and pLDDT value in the UI as a hypothetical design target rather than a computed result.

findings.title: No schema, type, unit, or range validation exists anywhere; scientific values are packed inside human-readable prose strings
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:146, :147 (and the 24 analogous affinity/safety fields through :395); :381 (drug 24 sequence); :60, :70 (SMILES fields); :173, :371, :130 (non-standard residue letter); :50 (curcumin SMILES); :562-563 (positional string parsing)
findings.what_is_wrong: There is no schema file, no type annotation, no validator, and no assertion in the repository (verified: `schemas/` absent, no `assert` in app.js). Every scientific quantity is embedded inside an English sentence. app.js:146 stores affinity as the single string `"ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol | Kd = 0.32 nM | AF3 pLDDT = 96.2 / 100"` and app.js:147 stores safety as `"hERG IC50 > 50 μM (0% Cardiotoxicity) | Seizure Index: 0.01 | Downregulation: < 3.5%"`. Three numbers with three different units, plus a categorical claim, plus an inequality operator, in one untyped string. The only consumer is positional splitting at app.js:562-563 (`drug.affinity.split('|')[0].trim()` / `[1].trim()`), which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')` on any record with fewer than two pipes -- a one-character edit away from a blank page. Four concrete corruptions already sit in the data and would be caught by any schema: (1) app.js:381 the `sequence` field of drug 24 AstroPafr-Block-A4 is `"His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"`, English prose, not a sequence -- yet it is passed to `initModal3DCanvas`, `renderModalPlddtChart` (producing residue labels `H1`, `i2`, `s3`, `-4`, `1`5), `renderModalPaeHeatmap`, and to the "Copy FASTA Sequence" button at index.html:362, which would paste it into the AlphaFold Server input box; (2) the non-standard residue letter `B` (the Asx ambiguity code, not a proteinogenic amino acid and not accepted as protein input by AlphaFold Server) appears in app.js:173, :371, and :130; (3) app.js:60 and :70 store `"C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)"` and `"C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)"` in fields named `smiles` -- molecular formulas, which are not SMILES; (4) app.js:50, the curcumin `smiles` value, ends `...C=C2)O)OCH3)O`, and bare `CH3` is not valid SMILES (H is only legal inside brackets), so this string fails to parse in RDKit or OpenBabel.
findings.why_it_matters: The direct question posed by the review -- could a typo in a ΔG ever be caught? -- has a definitive answer: no. Nothing reads these values as numbers, so `-18.4` becoming `-184` or `18.4` would render, pass unnoticed, and propagate into the drug cards and the leaderboard. The four corruptions above are the proof: they are already present, already shipped, and already rendered without complaint. The string-packing also makes the entire dataset programmatically unusable -- you cannot sort candidates by Kd, filter by pLDDT threshold, plot ΔG against molecular weight, join against ChEMBL, or run a unit check, because there are no numbers, only sentences. That is what "unusable programmatically" means concretely, and it is why the ΔG/Kd inconsistency in SWE-02 survived into a published artifact: no code path ever compared them. Worst of all is the drug-24 case, where a UI button offers to copy a non-sequence to the user's clipboard for submission to a real external structure-prediction service.
findings.ground_truth: Scientific data layers separate value, unit, and provenance into distinct typed fields -- `{"delta_g": {"value": -18.4, "unit": "kcal/mol", "method": "...", "uncertainty": 0.8}}` -- and validate them mechanically. The two standard mechanisms are JSON Schema (declarative, language-neutral, runs in CI) and Pydantic v2 (runtime, Python, with custom validators). The pattern is a core element of the FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al., Scientific Data 3:160018, 2016, DOI 10.1038/sdata.2016.18), specifically I1 ("formal, accessible, shared and broadly applicable language for knowledge representation") and R1 ("richly described with a plurality of accurate and relevant attributes"), and of "Best Practices for Scientific Computing" (PLoS Biology, 2014, DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745), which states the rule as: make the data machine-readable and check it automatically. Protein sequence validity is `^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$` for standard residues -- B, J, O, U, X, Z are ambiguity or non-standard codes that AlphaFold Server rejects. SMILES validity is checked by round-tripping through `rdkit.Chem.MolFromSmiles`, which returns None on failure.
findings.required_fix: Move all data out of app.js into `data/*.json` and write `schemas/*.schema.json` declaring every field. Replace each prose string with typed fields: `delta_g_kcal_per_mol` (number, maximum 0), `kd_nM` (number, exclusiveMinimum 0), `plddt` (number, 0-100), `herg_ic50_uM` (number plus a separate `operator` enum for `>`), `seizure_index` (number, 0-1). Constrain `sequence` with `"pattern": "^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$"` -- this rejects drug 24 and the three B-containing records immediately. Add a CI step that runs the JSON Schema validator, an RDKit round-trip over every SMILES field, and the ΔG/Kd consistency assertion from SWE-02, and fails the build on any error. Delete the positional `split('|')` parsing at app.js:562-563 in favour of reading the typed fields directly.

findings.title: Not reproducible or installable by anyone: no manifest, no environment, no tests, no CI, no version, and a run instruction that is an absolute path on the author's laptop
