findings.what_is_wrong: The complete documented installation and execution procedure is README.md:119-124: "Clone this repository or open the project folder. Open `index.html` directly in any web browser: `file:///Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html`". The sole run instruction is an absolute filesystem path inside one named user's home directory -- it is not portable to any other machine, and it discloses the author's OS username. There is no dependency manifest of any kind, so the three runtime dependencies (Three.js, OrbitControls, Chart.js) are undeclared and undiscoverable except by reading the HTML. There is no test suite and no test framework: `grep -rnE "describe\(|it\(|test\(|expect\(|assert" app.js` returns only two false positives from `split('|')`. There is no CI configuration -- `.github/` does not exist. There is no version identifier anywhere: no `version` field (no manifest to hold one), no git tag, no `__version__`, no CHANGELOG. There is no LICENSE file, no CITATION.cff, no CONTRIBUTING.md, and no code of conduct. Because `file://` origins block `fetch()` in Chrome and Safari, the stated launch method also forecloses the only architecturally correct fix for the data-layering problem -- loading data from external JSON -- so the current run instruction actively entrenches the inline-literal design.
findings.why_it_matters: Reproducibility is the property that a third party can obtain the same artifact and the same outputs from the same inputs. None of the necessary preconditions is present here. A reader cannot determine which Chart.js version produced the figures (see SWE-05), cannot pin an environment, cannot verify that the code still runs correctly after any change (no tests), cannot detect regressions (no CI), and cannot cite a specific state of the work (no version, no DOI). For JOSS specifically these are hard requirements, not preferences: the review checklist requires an OSI-approved license in the repository, installation instructions, example usage, functionality documentation, automated tests or a documented manual test procedure, and community guidelines. This submission satisfies zero of the six and would be desk-rejected before a reviewer was assigned. Independent of JOSS, the absence of tests around a codebase whose entire purpose is to display numeric scientific values means there is no mechanism -- none -- by which a wrong number becomes a failing build.
findings.ground_truth: "Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research" (PLoS Computational Biology, 2013, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285) states the applicable rules directly: record how every result was produced, avoid manual data manipulation, archive the exact versions of all external programs used, and version-control all custom scripts. The FAIR principles (DOI 10.1038/sdata.2016.18) add F1 (globally unique and persistent identifiers -- i.e. versioned releases with DOIs) and R1.1 (a clear and accessible data usage license). "Best Practices for Scientific Computing" (DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745) adds: plan for mistakes by adding assertions and unit tests, and use a build tool to automate workflows. The modern packaging of this is RO-Crate ("Packaging research artefacts with RO-Crate", Data Science, 2022, DOI 10.3233/DS-210053), which bundles data, code, and machine-readable provenance into one citable archive.
findings.required_fix: Add `package.json` with an exact-version `dependencies` block plus a committed lockfile, and a `"scripts": {"start": "npx serve ."}` entry so the documented launch is `npm start` opening `http://localhost:3000`, never a `file://` path. Delete the absolute path from README.md:123. Add an OSI-approved LICENSE (MIT is the natural fit given the MIT dependencies). Add `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` for the compute layer once it exists. Add a `tests/` directory with, at minimum: schema validation over every data record, the ΔG/Kd thermodynamic assertion, sequence-alphabet validation, SMILES round-trip validation, and a sequence-uniqueness check. Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running those tests plus a linter on every push and pull request. Add a Dockerfile pinning the full toolchain. Add CITATION.cff and CONTRIBUTING.md. Tag `v0.1.0` and mint a Zenodo DOI so the artifact is citable at a fixed state.

findings.title: Every drug-modal open leaks a WebGL context and installs a permanent, uncancellable requestAnimationFrame loop
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:688-691 (renderer construction), :763-772 (animation loop), :655-658 (closeDrugModal), :731-758 (geometry/material construction); `grep -n "dispose\|cancelAnimationFrame" app.js` returns zero matches
findings.why_it_matters: The symptom is deterministic and user-visible: the 3D model spins twice as fast after the second modal open, three times as fast after the third, and so on -- so the animation itself advertises the bug. Browsers cap concurrent WebGL contexts (Chrome at 16); past that limit the oldest context is force-lost and its canvas goes blank, so a user who inspects all 25 candidates in one session will find the 3D panel dead for the last nine, with `WARNING: Too many active WebGL contexts` in the console and no explanation in the UI. Frame time degrades linearly with the number of opens because N redundant draw calls execute per frame. Three.js documents explicitly that GPU-side resources are not reclaimed by JavaScript garbage collection and that `dispose()` must be called; abandoning geometries and materials leaks VRAM. On a page whose stated purpose is browsing 25 candidates in sequence, this is not a theoretical leak -- it is the primary usage pattern.
findings.ground_truth: The correct Three.js teardown, per the library's own "How to dispose of objects" guide, is: cancel the animation frame using the handle returned by `requestAnimationFrame`; traverse the scene calling `geometry.dispose()` and `material.dispose()` (and `texture.dispose()`) on every disposable; call `renderer.dispose()`; and, to release the context immediately rather than at GC's convenience, `renderer.forceContextLoss()` followed by dropping the reference to `renderer.domElement`. Modern Three.js also offers `renderer.setAnimationLoop(fn)` and `renderer.setAnimationLoop(null)`, which makes loop cancellation a single call and is the idiomatic replacement for hand-rolled rAF recursion. The correct structural fix is a single long-lived renderer reused across all modal opens, with only the scene contents swapped -- which eliminates the context-exhaustion class of bug entirely. Notably, the same file already gets the analogous Chart.js case right at app.js:779-781 (`if (modalPlddtChartInstance) { modalPlddtChartInstance.destroy(); }`); the Three.js path simply omits the equivalent.
findings.required_fix: Capture the frame handle: `modalRafId = requestAnimationFrame(animateModal3D);`. In `closeDrugModal`, add `cancelAnimationFrame(modalRafId); modalRafId = null;` then traverse `modalThreeScene` disposing every geometry and material, call `modalThreeRenderer.dispose()` and `modalThreeRenderer.forceContextLoss()`, set `modalThreeRenderer = null` (which also makes the existing guard at app.js:764 functional), and clear the container. Better: hoist the renderer to a module-level singleton created once and reused, and swap only `modalThreeMeshGroup` contents per candidate. Add a regression test that opens and closes the modal 30 times and asserts `renderer.info.memory.geometries` and `renderer.info.memory.textures` return to baseline.

findings.title: Unpinned Chart.js CDN dependency, a five-year-stale Three.js, and zero Subresource Integrity across all four third-party resources
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:11, :13, :15, :16, :18; `grep -c "integrity=" index.html` returns 0
findings.what_is_wrong: The page loads four third-party resources over the network and pins none of them safely. index.html:18 is `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js"></script>` -- no version constraint at all. jsDelivr resolves a bare package path to the current latest release: I verified the response header today is `x-jsd-version: 4.5.1` and the served banner reads `Chart.js v4.5.1 ... (c) 2025`. Nothing in the repository records that. When Chart.js 5.x ships, this URL silently begins serving it, and any breaking change to the `new Chart(ctx, {...})` config surface -- Chart.js has made exactly such changes at every major boundary, notably v2→v3 and v3→v4 -- will break both `renderModalPlddtChart` (app.js:797) and `renderBenchmarkChart` (app.js:1057) with no commit, no diff, and no CI signal. index.html:15 pins Three.js to `r128`, published 2021-04-23 per the npm registry; the current release is 0.185.1 (2026-07-01), so the project is 57 minor releases and over five years behind, on a library that has since removed the `examples/js/` UMD directory that index.html:16 depends on. index.html:13 pins Font Awesome 6.4.0, and index.html:11 loads Google Fonts. None of the four carries an `integrity=` attribute -- `grep -c "integrity=" index.html` returns 0 -- and none carries `crossorigin="anonymous"` on the script tags. Nothing is vendored: the repository contains no `vendor/`, `lib/`, or `node_modules/` (the latter is gitignored).
findings.why_it_matters: Two distinct failures. Reproducibility: it is impossible to reconstruct the environment that produced any figure in this repository, today or in five years, because the Chart.js version is not recorded anywhere and the CDN's notion of "latest" moves under the code. A reviewer re-running this page next year may see different rendering, or a blank canvas, and cannot diagnose why. This is precisely the failure mode Rule 6 of the Ten Simple Rules -- "always archive the exact versions of all external programs used" -- exists to prevent. Supply chain: without SRI, the browser executes whatever bytes the CDN returns. A compromise of cdnjs or jsDelivr, or a namespace hijack of the `chart.js` package, injects arbitrary JavaScript into a page that the author is inviting collaborators to open. The unpinned URL widens this further, since a malicious release is picked up automatically with no version bump for anyone to notice. And because the page requires network access at load, it cannot be run at all on an air-gapped or offline machine -- a routine constraint in pharmaceutical and clinical research environments, and a hard blocker for archival reproducibility.
findings.ground_truth: The W3C Subresource Integrity specification defines the `integrity` attribute so a browser can verify a fetched resource against a cryptographic digest and refuse to execute it on mismatch; both cdnjs and jsDelivr publish ready-made SRI hashes for every file they serve. For genuine long-term reproducibility, vendoring is stronger than SRI: commit the exact dependency files into the repository so the artifact has no runtime network dependency at all. Rule 6 of "Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research" (DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285) requires archiving exact versions of all external programs. Both Three.js (0.128.0) and Chart.js (4.5.1) are MIT-licensed per their npm registry metadata, as is Font Awesome's code (its icons are CC BY 4.0 and its brand icons carry additional restrictions), so vendoring is permitted provided the license texts travel with the copies.

findings.title: No LICENSE file, no AlphaFold3 citation, and DeepMind/Google branding plus a false "Live Connected" status claim that conflict with the AlphaFold Output Terms of Use
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/README.md:3-4, :22, :135; /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:30, :42, :410; repository root (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, COPYING all verified absent)
findings.what_is_wrong: Four distinct compliance defects. (1) No license: README.md:4 renders a badge reading `License-Private_Research` linking to the GitHub repo, but no LICENSE, LICENSE.md, or COPYING file exists at the root. A badge is not a license grant; with no license text the work is all-rights-reserved by default, meaning no recipient may legally copy, modify, or redistribute it -- and JOSS requires an OSI-approved license present in the repository as a hard submission criterion. (2) Google/DeepMind branding: README.md:3 renders `[![AlphaFold3](https://img.shields.io/badge/AlphaFold3-DeepMind_Server-00f2fe?style=for-the-badge&logo=google)]`, embedding the Google logo in a badge reading "AlphaFold3 | DeepMind Server"; index.html:30 sets the product subtitle to "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform", placing "DeepMind" in the masthead of a third-party product; index.html:410 states "Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling". (3) A false connection claim: index.html:42 renders a status pill reading "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" that is an ordinary hyperlink, with no connection of any kind (SWE-01). (4) No citation: `grep -i abramson` across all four files returns nothing -- the AlphaFold3 paper is never cited, in the README, the UI, or the code. Third-party MIT attributions for Three.js, Chart.js, and Font Awesome are likewise entirely absent.
findings.why_it_matters: The branding and the false status claim run directly into terms I retrieved and read in this session. The AlphaFold 3 Output Terms of Use (google-deepmind/alphafold3, OUTPUT_TERMS_OF_USE.md) prohibit use of Output "[t]o misinform, misrepresent or mislead", enumerating "misrepresenting your relationship with Google" and "misrepresenting the origin of" outputs. A page whose masthead reads "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology... Platform", whose README badge carries the Google logo, and whose header asserts "AlphaFold Server Live Connected", is a textbook instance of the conduct that clause names -- and it is aggravated, not mitigated, by the fact that no AlphaFold output is present at all, so nothing is being misrepresented *as* Google's except the platform's own synthetic sine waves. Section 6 of those Terms further requires that anyone distributing Output or disclosing findings from AlphaFold 3 cite Abramson et al.; this project claims AlphaFold3 findings throughout and cites nothing. Separately, the AlphaFold Server Output Terms prohibit use of Output "[i]n connection with any automated system that predicts the binding or interaction of the protein with ligands or peptides, including, but not limited to, Glide or AutoDock" -- language I retrieved verbatim as quoted in google-deepmind/alphafold3 issue #340. A platform that displays per-candidate ΔG and Kd values for peptide-receptor binding alongside AlphaFold Server integration would sit squarely inside that prohibition the moment real Server output entered the pipeline, so this must be resolved before the compute layer is built, not after. Finally, absent a LICENSE the repository cannot be shared, forked, or built upon by anyone, including collaborators the author intends to share it with.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold 3 Output Terms of Use (google-deepmind/alphafold3, OUTPUT_TERMS_OF_USE.md, retrieved this session): non-commercial use only, restricted to universities, nonprofits, research institutes, educational and journalism organizations, and government bodies; §2 prohibits use "[t]o misinform, misrepresent or mislead", including "misrepresenting your relationship with Google" and misrepresenting the origin of Output; §4 prohibits training biomolecular structure prediction models similar to AlphaFold 3; §5 requires "conspicuous notice that published or distributed Output is provided under and subject to these Terms"; §6 requires citing Abramson, J. et al. The Terms further state that "Output are for theoretical modeling only. These are not intended, validated, or approved for clinical use" and "are predictions with varying levels of confidence and should be interpreted carefully." The AlphaFold Server Terms add the automated-ligand/peptide-binding-system prohibition quoted above. Canonical citation: Abramson, J. et al., "Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3", Nature 630:493-500 (2024), DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w, PMID 38718835. Three.js 0.128.0 and Chart.js 4.5.1 are both MIT (verified via the npm registry); MIT requires the copyright notice and permission notice to accompany all copies.
findings.required_fix: Add a LICENSE file with the full text of an OSI-approved license (MIT recommended, matching the dependencies) and align the README badge to it; if the work is genuinely to remain proprietary, make the repository private and remove the JOSS framing. Remove "DeepMind" from index.html:30 and from the README.md:3 badge, and remove `logo=google` from that badge -- a third-party project must not present a vendor's name or logo as its own product identity. Replace the index.html:42 "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" pill with an accurate, non-status label such as "AlphaFold Server (external link)". Add the Abramson et al. citation with its DOI to the README and to any UI panel displaying structure-derived data, and add the §5 conspicuous notice if and when real Output is distributed. Add a THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES file carrying the MIT texts for Three.js and Chart.js and the Font Awesome license. Before building the compute layer, obtain written clarification from Google DeepMind on whether the intended peptide-binding-affinity workflow is permitted under the AlphaFold Server Terms, or route structure prediction through a permissively licensed alternative (Boltz, Chai-1) whose terms allow it.

findings.title: No architectural layering: 36% of the application script is scientific data literals, with unescaped innerHTML injection, two divergent region vocabularies, and no provenance field anywhere
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:6-398 (data literals inside the UI script); :467, :515, :565, :606, :873, :880 and 6 further innerHTML sinks; :90-121 vs :138-398 (region key vocabularies); :535 (onclick-attribute string matching); :562-563, :582 (presentation logic parsing data)
findings.what_is_wrong: app.js is the application's only script and lines 6-398 -- 393 of 1103 lines, 36% of the file -- are `NATURAL_PRODUCTS_DATA`, `BRAIN_REGIONS_DATA`, `AF3_CANDIDATES`, and `FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA` as inline object literals, interleaved with the DOM handlers that render them. There is no data layer, no compute layer, and no boundary between either and the view. Four concrete consequences are already visible. (i) Divergent vocabularies: `BRAIN_REGIONS_DATA` (app.js:90-121) keys the five regions as `hippocampus, pfc, "basal-forebrain", microglia, astrocytes`, while `FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA` (app.js:138-398) uses `hippocampus, pfc, basal, microglia, astrocyte` -- two of five keys differ, with no shared enum, no constant, and no validation to catch the drift, so the two datasets cannot be joined. (ii) Unescaped injection: 12 `innerHTML` assignments interpolate data straight into markup via template literals (app.js:467, :515, :565, :606, :873, :880 and others), with no escaping or sanitization. The data is static today, so this is not currently exploitable -- but the entire remediation path for this repository involves loading data from external JSON and, plausibly, accepting user-supplied sequences, at which point every one of these 12 sinks becomes a live XSS vector. (iii) Presentation logic is parsing data: app.js:562-563 splits the affinity prose on `|` by position, and app.js:582 does `drug.bindingSites.substring(0, 52)` followed by a literal `...` -- I verified this appends a false ellipsis to 13 of the 25 records whose bindingSites are already shorter than 52 characters (e.g. `"Trem2 Ig domain & Keap1 Kelch domain"`, 36 chars, renders as `"Trem2 Ig domain & Keap1 Kelch domain..."`), and truncates 10 others mid-token (`"...TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val3..."`). (iv) Control flow reads markup: app.js:535 determines the active filter by string-matching the literal text of a DOM `onclick` attribute (`btn.getAttribute('onclick').includes(...)`), which throws on any button lacking that attribute and couples routing to HTML formatting. Across all four datasets there is not one provenance field: no `method`, no `software_version`, no `date_computed`, no `seed`, no `input_hash`, no `uncertainty`, no `source_doi`.
findings.why_it_matters: The layering violation is why every other finding in this review was possible. Because there is no data layer, there is no schema; because there is no schema, nothing validated the ΔG/Kd pairs (SWE-02) or the non-sequence in drug 24 (SWE-03). Because there is no compute layer, the numbers have no origin, and because there is no provenance field, an expert cannot ask the only question that matters -- "how was -18.4 kcal/mol obtained?" -- and get an answer from the artifact. Practically, the current design means a domain scientist cannot correct a residue assignment without editing JavaScript and risking a syntax error that blanks the entire page; the data cannot be diffed meaningfully in review, cannot be validated in CI, cannot be exported, cannot be consumed by any other tool, and cannot be cited independently of the UI. The vocabulary drift and the false-ellipsis bug are the small, visible symptoms of the same missing boundary.
findings.ground_truth: The standard layering for a scientific platform is three strictly separated tiers. (1) An immutable, versioned data layer: `data/` holding JSON or Parquet, one record per entity, every value typed with an explicit unit, validated against a committed schema, addressed by content hash, and never edited in place -- corrections land as new versions. (2) A compute layer that reads the data layer and emits derived artifacts, each accompanied by a provenance record naming the tool, its version, the container digest, the input hash, the random seed, and the timestamp; W3C PROV-O (W3C Recommendation, 2013, https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/) is the standard vocabulary and RO-Crate (Data Science, 2022, DOI 10.3233/DS-210053) the standard packaging. (3) A presentation layer that only reads validated artifacts and renders them, containing no data, no domain constants, and no arithmetic. This is the structure behind FAIR principles I3 ("qualified references to other data") and R1.2 ("associated with detailed provenance") in Wilkinson et al. (DOI 10.1038/sdata.2016.18), and behind the modularity guidance in "Best Practices for Scientific Computing" (DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745).
findings.required_fix: Extract app.js:6-398 verbatim into `data/natural_products.json`, `data/brain_regions.json`, `data/candidates.json`, and `data/therapeutics.json`, each governed by a schema under `schemas/`. Define one canonical `region_id` enum in the schema and migrate both datasets to it, adding a CI check that every `region_id` in the therapeutics file resolves in the regions file. Add a required `provenance` object to every record -- `{method, software, software_version, container_digest, input_sha256, seed, computed_at, uncertainty}` -- and fail CI on any numeric field lacking one. Replace all 12 `innerHTML` template-literal sinks with `textContent` assignment or explicit DOM construction, or route every interpolation through an escaping helper. Delete the `substring(0, 52) + '...'` truncation at app.js:582 in favour of CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis`, which truncates correctly and never lies. Replace the onclick-attribute string matching at app.js:535 with `data-region` attributes read via `dataset`. Serve the page over HTTP (SWE-04) so `fetch()` of the data files is permitted.

findings.title: The synthetic confidence visualizations contradict their own legends and contradict each other, with unreachable clamps and a mislabelled PAE axis
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:791-794, :825-826, :747-749, :844, :850-851; /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:388-391, :397, :399
findings.what_is_wrong: Four internal inconsistencies, each verified numerically. (1) Unreachable branches and dead legend: the generator at app.js:791 has an exact analytic range of [89.0, 99.0] over all i and all uppercase letters (I enumerated it: `93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode%5)*0.5`, sin term in [-4,4], ASCII term in {0,0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0}). Both clamps that follow -- app.js:792 `if (score > 100) score = 98.6;` and app.js:793 `if (score < 70) score = 76;` -- are therefore unreachable dead code, and the legend bands at index.html:390-391 declaring "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" describe states the generator cannot produce. The y-axis is fixed to `min: 50` (app.js:825), so 78% of the plot area is permanently empty. (2) The two "pLDDT" views disagree about the same residue: the 3D sphere colouring at app.js:747-749 keys on amino-acid identity, not on any confidence value -- `if (char === 'G' || char === 'S') resColor = 0x10b981;` (green, legended "High 70-90") and `if (char === 'P' || char === 'D') resColor = 0xf59e0b;` (amber, legended "Low 50-70") -- while the chart assigns those same residues 89.0-98.5, i.e. "Very High". A proline in the modal is simultaneously drawn amber-for-low in the 3D panel and plotted above 90 in the chart directly beside it, under a heading (index.html:377) that calls the 3D colouring a "pLDDT Color Spectrum". (3) Mislabelled PAE axis and unreachable clamp: index.html:397 titles the heatmap "0 - 30 Å", but the maximum value the generator can emit is `(gridSize-1)*0.4 + 3*0.3`, which for the largest grid (45) is 18.5 Å and for a 28-residue sequence is 11.7 Å -- so the clamp at app.js:851 `if (error > 30) error = 30;` is likewise unreachable and the top 38% of the declared range is never used. (4) Silent truncation and aspect distortion: app.js:844 caps the matrix at `Math.min(sequence.length, 45)`, silently dropping residues 46+ for the 47-residue sequence at app.js:143 with no indication in the UI, and renders the square N×N matrix into a 540×220 canvas (index.html:399), giving cells a 2.45:1 aspect ratio so the diagonal of a PAE plot -- the feature practitioners read first -- is not at 45°.
findings.why_it_matters: Taken on their own these are cosmetic; taken together with SWE-01 they show that the synthetic outputs were never checked even for internal coherence, which is corroborating evidence that no one ever compared the rendered figures against what a real AlphaFold output looks like. The concrete misleading effect is specific: a viewer sees a pLDDT chart in which nothing ever drops below 89 and concludes the designs are uniformly high-confidence, when in fact the floor is a property of the constant `93` in the source. And a viewer who trusts the 3D panel's amber colouring will down-weight exactly the prolines and aspartates that the adjacent chart marks as most confident. Two panels in the same modal, under the same heading, give opposite answers about the same residue.
findings.ground_truth: Real AlphaFold pLDDT distributions for designed peptides span a wide range and characteristically drop at termini and in flexible linkers -- long poly-glycine-serine linkers of the kind present in these sequences (`GGGGS` repeats at app.js:183, :235, :287, :339, :391) reliably score low, typically 30-60, because they genuinely are disordered. A pLDDT profile that never falls below 89 across a GS-linkered bispecific construct is not a plausible AlphaFold output. The standard AlphaFold colour bands are pLDDT > 90 very high, 70-90 confident, 50-70 low, < 50 very low, and they are applied to the pLDDT value, never to residue identity. Real PAE matrices are plotted on a square canvas with equal axes, scaled to the model's actual maximum (commonly 0-31.75 Å for AlphaFold's binned output), showing the full N×N matrix with no truncation; the block structure off the diagonal is the diagnostic feature and is destroyed by both cropping and aspect distortion.
findings.required_fix: These panels should be deleted along with the synthetic generators under SWE-01 rather than repaired. If they are retained as acknowledged placeholders pending the real pipeline, then: delete the unreachable clamps at app.js:792-793 and :851; remove the "Low" and "Very Low" bands from the index.html:390-391 legend or set the y-axis to the actual data range; delete the residue-identity colouring at app.js:747-749 and colour the 3D spheres from the same array the chart plots, so the two panels cannot disagree; relabel the index.html:397 heatmap axis to the actual attainable range; remove the 45-residue cap at app.js:844 or display an explicit "showing residues 1-45 of N" note; and make the PAE canvas square so the diagonal renders at 45°. Retitle every panel to state plainly that the values are illustrative placeholders.

literature.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
literature.what_it_provides: The primary AlphaFold3 paper. Defines what an actual AF3 run produces: an mmCIF coordinate file plus a confidence bundle containing per-residue pLDDT, the full N x N PAE matrix, pTM and ipTM. Establishes that pLDDT is the output of a learned confidence head, not an analytic function of sequence.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the citation the AlphaFold 3 Output Terms Section 6 require and that the repository never makes. It is also the specification against which app.js:791 and app.js:850 must be replaced: parse pLDDT and PAE from real AF3 confidence JSON, and ship the mmCIF files in a versioned data/structures/ directory rather than generating helices from ASCII codes.

literature.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
literature.what_it_provides: The canonical statement of Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable data practice. Directly relevant clauses: F1 (globally unique persistent identifiers), I1 (formal shared knowledge representation, i.e. a schema), R1 (rich accurate attributes), R1.1 (clear accessible usage license), R1.2 (detailed provenance).
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supplies the requirements the repository fails on: I1 motivates extracting app.js:6-398 into schema-governed JSON with typed value/unit fields instead of prose strings; R1.1 is the missing LICENSE; R1.2 is the missing provenance object on every ΔG, Kd, and pLDDT; F1 is the missing version tag and DOI.

literature.title: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research
literature.what_it_provides: Ten operational rules, of which four map exactly onto defects here: Rule 1 (record how every result was produced), Rule 2 (avoid manual data manipulation), Rule 6 (archive the exact versions of all external programs used), Rule 8 (version-control all custom scripts).
literature.how_to_apply_here: Rule 6 is the direct authority for pinning the unpinned Chart.js CDN URL at index.html:18 and recording the exact dependency versions in a committed lockfile. Rule 1 is the authority for attaching a provenance record (tool, version, container digest, input hash, seed, timestamp) to every computed number. Rule 2 condemns the hand-written ΔG/Kd pairs that fail the thermodynamic identity.

literature.title: Best Practices for Scientific Computing
literature.what_it_provides: Consensus engineering practice for research code: plan for mistakes by adding assertions and unit tests, make the data machine-readable, modularize rather than duplicate, automate workflows with a build tool, and use version control on everything.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Justifies the missing tests/ and .github/ directories as substantive defects rather than nice-to-haves. The assertion guidance is the direct remedy for the review's central question -- a typo in a ΔG becomes catchable the moment a CI assertion enforces ΔG = RT ln(Kd) and a JSON Schema enforces pLDDT in [0,100] and sequences matching ^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$.

literature.title: Mol* Viewer: modern web app for 3D visualization and analysis of large biomolecular structures
literature.what_it_provides: The production-grade open-source web molecular viewer used by RCSB PDB, PDBe, and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. Parses mmCIF/PDB/BinaryCIF natively, renders cartoon/surface/ball-and-stick representations, and supports per-residue colouring by B-factor or pLDDT out of the box.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Replaces the hand-rolled Catmull-Rom tube at app.js:711-732 and app.js:973-994 entirely. Adopting Mol* simultaneously fixes the fabricated geometry (SWE-01), the amino-acid-identity colouring that contradicts the pLDDT chart (SWE-09), and the WebGL context leak (SWE-05), since Mol* manages renderer lifecycle and disposal internally rather than leaving it to ad hoc rAF recursion.

literature.title: Packaging research artefacts with RO-Crate
literature.what_it_provides: A lightweight, widely adopted specification for bundling data, code, and machine-readable provenance metadata into a single citable archive, built on schema.org and JSON-LD.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The concrete packaging format for the provenance requirement in SWE-08. Each AlphaFold3 prediction, each affinity calculation, and each ADMET prediction should be emitted as an RO-Crate carrying the input hash, tool version, container digest, seed, and timestamp, so that every number displayed in the UI traces back to a reproducible computation rather than to an inline literal.

literature.title: W3C PROV-O: The PROV Ontology (W3C Recommendation)
literature.what_it_provides: The W3C standard vocabulary for provenance: Entity, Activity, and Agent, with relations wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, and wasAttributedTo, expressed in OWL/RDF.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Gives the formal vocabulary for the provenance field that no record in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA or AF3_CANDIDATES currently has. A ΔG value becomes an Entity that wasGeneratedBy a named calculation Activity which used a specific structure Entity and was attributed to a specific software Agent at a specific version -- making the question 'where did -18.4 kcal/mol come from?' answerable mechanically instead of unanswerable.

literature.title: Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations [Article v1.0]
literature.id: DOI 10.33011/livecoms.2.1.18378 (Living Journal of Computational Molecular Science)
literature.what_it_provides: Community best-practice guidance for computing binding free energies: choice of method, force field, sampling protocol, convergence assessment, and mandatory uncertainty estimation, plus what must be reported alongside any ΔG.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Defines the minimum metadata every one of the 25 ΔG values at app.js:146-395 is missing. Once the compute layer exists, each affinity record must carry method, force field, sampling protocol, and a statistical uncertainty; a ΔG with no method and no error bar should fail schema validation. It also frames why the current values cannot be interpreted at all -- there is no way to know whether they were meant as docking scores, MM/GBSA estimates, or aspirational design targets.

reviews.discipline: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD structural biologist, 20 years in X-ray crystallography and single-particle cryo-EM; routine validation of deposited coordinates (MolProbity/wwPDB OneDep reports), service on PDB validation-related committees; working experience with AlphaFold2/3 confidence metrics and PoseBusters-style ligand-pose assessment.

findings.title: The "3D structure" is a parametric ASCII-driven helix, not a protein backbone; geometry is wrong by scale-free measures
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:707 (comment "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION"); app.js:711-729 (coordinate loop); app.js:715 radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8; app.js:716 pitch = (i - seqLength/2) * 0.6; app.js:717 angle = (i/seqLength) * Math.PI * (charCode % 3 === 0 ? 6 : 4); app.js:719-721 x=sin(angle)*r, y=pitch, z=cos(angle)*r; app.js:723-726 (C/P radial scaling ×1.3); app.js:973-991 (identical construction in update3DProteinStructure, radius = 7 + (charCode%4)*0.8, pitch ×0.5, angle ×π*5); index.html:377 "Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)"; README.md:108 "Real sequence-driven backbone topology parsing"
findings.what_is_wrong: The renderer produces no protein geometry of any kind. Each "residue" position is sin/cos of an index times a radius derived from the residue's ASCII code modulo 5 — a cyclic function of the alphabet, not of chemistry. Three independent, scale-free tests fail. (1) Virtual bond length: re-running app.js:711-729 in Python on the actual sequences gives consecutive point separations of 1.91-19.08 units (drug X1, L=47), 0.63-16.63 (X3), 2.14-16.22 (P1); coefficient of variation 0.56-0.82 and max/min ratios of 8-26x. Real Cα-Cα virtual bond length is 3.80-3.81 Å with sigma ~0.04 Å (CV ~1%), fixed by the planar trans peptide bond (omega ~180°); it does not vary with residue identity. Because CV and max/min are invariant to any unit scaling, no choice of Å-per-scene-unit rescues this. (2) The cause of the scatter is that `angle` at app.js:717 is recomputed from scratch at each i with a multiplier that flips between 4 and 6 depending on that residue's ASCII code mod 3 (E,H,K,N,Q,T,W,B,Z take 6; everything else 4). The angle is therefore non-monotonic — verified on X1: i=5(N) angle=2.005 rad, i=6(P) angle=1.604 rad. The chain jumps backwards and across the cylinder, producing the 19-unit "bonds". (3) Helical parameters: rise per residue is a constant 0.6 units (app.js:716) and radius is 6.0-9.2 units (11.96 with the C/P ×1.3 factor), giving radius/rise = 10.0-19.9. For an alpha-helix that ratio is 2.3/1.5 = 1.53 — the model is off by 6.5-13x, again scale-free. Residues per turn is L/2 or L/3, i.e. 13-24 for these designs (50 for the 100-mer at app.js:125) versus 3.6 for alpha-helix, 3.0 for 3-10, 4.4 for pi, and ~2 for beta-strand; the model's helical period scales with chain length, which is physically meaningless. Finally, the covalently attached natural-product warhead — the defining feature of a "bio-conjugate" — is never represented by a single atom, and the target receptor (TrkB, AChE, Keap1, ...) is never rendered, so no binding pose exists anywhere in the codebase despite ΔG and Kd being quoted for every entry.
findings.why_it_matters: The image on screen is the platform's primary evidence that these 25 molecules were structurally modelled. A reader — a collaborator, a reviewer, an investor, an IRB — sees a ribbon with pLDDT-coloured residue spheres and reasonably concludes a structure prediction was run and inspected. It was not. Any downstream decision that depends on the fold, the presentation of the warhead, the accessibility of the binding epitope, or the compatibility of the peptide with its stated receptor pocket is being made against a decorative sine wave. Because the comment at app.js:707 and the README explicitly assert the parsing is "real", this is an affirmative misrepresentation rather than an acknowledged placeholder.
findings.ground_truth: Protein backbone geometry is determined by covalent restraints (Engh & Huber 1991) plus the phi/psi torsions; Cα(i)-Cα(i+1) = 3.80 Å for trans peptides (~2.9 Å for the rare cis-Pro). Alpha-helix: 3.6 residues/turn, 1.5 Å rise/residue, 5.4 Å pitch, ~2.3 Å Cα radius, phi/psi ≈ (-57°, -47°), stabilised by i→i+4 N-H···O=C hydrogen bonds. Beta-strand: ~3.3-3.4 Å rise, phi/psi ≈ (-120°, +130°). Secondary structure is assigned from backbone H-bonding and geometry (DSSP), never from residue identity — the same residue adopts helix, strand or coil depending on context, which is precisely why sequence-to-structure is a hard prediction problem rather than a lookup. A structure of a covalent bio-conjugate must contain the warhead atoms and, to support any ΔG claim, the receptor.
findings.required_fix: Delete the synthetic geometry generator entirely (app.js:674-773 and app.js:959-1022) and the "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING" comment. findings.what_is_wrong: pLDDT is generated as 93 + 4·sin(0.4i) + 0.5·(ASCII mod 5). Its range over every possible input is [89.0, 99.0] (computed: min 93-4+0, max 93+4+2), so the clamps at app.js:792-793 (>100→98.6, <70→76) are unreachable dead code and no residue can ever fall below 89. The UI legend at index.html:390-391 advertises "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" bands that the generator cannot produce. The sin term has period 2π/0.4 = 15.71 residues, so every one of the 25 molecules displays the same waveform with a ±1.0 ASCII ripple — verified means: X1 93.92, X3 94.30, P1 94.29. PAE is 0.4·|i-j| plus a row-constant ASCII offset: it is a pure function of sequence separation, so it can never show the off-diagonal low-error blocks that are the entire diagnostic content of a PAE matrix (rigid inter-domain packing, well-defined interfaces). Its maximum attainable value on a 45×45 grid is 44·0.4+0.9 = 18.5 Å, yet the panel title claims a 0-30 Å scale. Separately, the residue spheres at app.js:747-749 are coloured by amino-acid letter — G/S mapped to the "High" band, P/D to the "Low" band — which asserts that residue identity determines local confidence.
findings.why_it_matters: pLDDT and PAE are the only quantities that tell a structural biologist which parts of a prediction may be trusted. Presenting synthetic curves under the label "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" inverts their function: every candidate is rendered as uniformly "Very High" confidence, which is exactly the signal a reader uses to decide the model is good enough to design experiments against. A flat 89-99 band with no low-confidence regions is also intrinsically implausible for short, Cys-rich, linker-containing designed peptides, which in practice show pLDDT collapsing to 30-60 across GGGGS linkers and termini. The colour rule is affirmatively wrong science: Gly and Pro are the two residues most associated with backbone flexibility and *low* local confidence, and Ser and Asp are unremarkable — the mapping is not merely arbitrary, it is close to inverted for Gly.
findings.ground_truth: pLDDT is the network's per-atom/per-residue estimate of the lDDT-Cα score (Mariani et al. 2013) — a prediction about that specific model's local accuracy, emitted by the confidence head and written to the B-factor column of the output mmCIF and to the accompanying confidences JSON. It is a property of the model, conditioned on the full input (sequence, MSA, ligands, stoichiometry), not of the amino-acid alphabet. PAE(i,j) is the expected positional error at residue j when the prediction and true structure are aligned on residue i; it is genuinely asymmetric, is emitted as a full N×N matrix (AF3 caps at 31.75 Å), and its block structure is what identifies domains and confident interfaces. The AF3 paper explicitly warns that geometry is rendered sharply regardless of confidence: "the local structure will be sharply defined (for example, side-chain bond geometry) even when the network is uncertain about the positions" — which is why the confidence arrays, not the rendered geometry, must be the source of colouring.
findings.required_fix: Load the predictor's actual outputs: parse pLDDT from the B-factor column of the output mmCIF (or from the `atom_plddts`/`pae` fields of AF3's `*_confidences.json`), and render the PAE panel directly from that N×N matrix with a proper 0-31.75 Å colourmap, real axis ticks, and no truncation at 45. Also surface pTM and ipTM, which are the correct global metrics for a multi-entity (peptide + covalent ligand + receptor) prediction. findings.title: AlphaFold 3 cannot model a covalently conjugated natural-product warhead in the way claimed, and no prediction was ever submitted
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/README.md:22,45 ("25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3"), README.md:111 ("Live AlphaFold Server Connection"); index.html:42 "AlphaFold Server Live Connected"; index.html:362-363 (a Copy button and a plain <a href> to alphafoldserver.com); app.js:660-671 copyModalFasta() writes drug.sequence only; app.js:142,152,162 etc. chemStruct fields naming Ginsenoside Rg1 C42H72O14, Huperzine A C15H18N2O, Curcumin C21H20O6 etc.; app.js:173 and app.js:371 sequences containing the non-standard letter 'B'. findings.what_is_wrong: Every one of the 25 entities is described as a small-molecule warhead covalently coupled to a peptide, i.e. exactly the case AF3 handles least freely. Three concrete gaps. (1) The public AlphaFold Server accepts ligands only from a fixed allow-list (CCD_ATP, ADP, AMP, GTP, GDP, FAD, NAD, NAP, NDP, HEM, HEC, PLM, OLA, MYR, CIT, CLA, CHL, BCL, BCB, plus ten common ions); arbitrary SMILES are rejected. None of ginsenoside Rg1/Rb1/Rg3, huperzine A, curcumin, asiatic acid, salvianolic acid B, ginkgolide B, bilobalide, ferulic acid or presenegenin is on that list, so not one of these conjugates can be submitted to the Server at all — and the only "integration" in the code is an anchor tag plus a clipboard copy of the bare peptide, which would model the peptide alone with the pharmacophore silently discarded. (2) The local AF3 code does accept SMILES, but its own documentation states: "If using SMILES, you cannot specify covalent bonds to other entities as these rely on specific atom names", and "Defining covalent bonds between or within polymer entities is not currently supported." A covalent conjugate therefore requires the author to write a full user-supplied CCD block (named atoms, bond orders, charges, leaving atoms, ideal coordinates) and an explicit bondedAtomPairs entry — non-trivial cheminformatics work that appears nowhere in this repository. (3) Input hygiene: the sequences at app.js:173 and app.js:371 contain 'B' (Asx, an ambiguity code, not an amino acid) and would be rejected by both the Server and the local parser. A related instance of unmodelled chemistry: drug #9 (app.js:225) is exactly GSK-3β residues 3-34 (verified against UniProt P49841, MSGRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG...), a genuinely sensible pseudosubstrate choice — but it only inhibits when Ser9 is phosphorylated, and no phosphoserine (CCD SEP) modification is specified anywhere. Finally, AF3 emits no free energy: there is no scoring function in AF3 that produces kcal/mol, so the ΔG and Kd values throughout cannot have come from the tool credited with producing them.
findings.why_it_matters: The central claim of the platform — 25 therapeutics "designed via AlphaFold3" — is not achievable with the described inputs and was demonstrably not attempted. A structural biologist or medicinal chemist reading the README will assume the conjugation geometry was modelled: whether the linker reaches, whether the warhead is presented toward the pocket, whether conjugation occludes the binding epitope. Those are the questions a bio-conjugate design lives or dies on, and none of them can even be posed without bondedAtomPairs plus a userCCD. Anyone attempting to reproduce this work would discover at the first submission that the Server refuses the ligand and the sequence, and would conclude the results were never generated.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold 3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024) predicts joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions and modified residues. Local code: ligands via CCD code, SMILES, or user-provided CCD; covalent linkage only via bondedAtomPairs, which requires named atoms and therefore a CCD/userCCD entity, not a SMILES; no covalent bonds within or between polymer entities. AlphaFold Server: restricted ligand/ion allow-list, restricted PTM list, no arbitrary SMILES, no user CCD. AF3 also has documented physical failure modes relevant here — "the model outputs do not always respect chirality" (4.4% chirality violations on the PoseBusters set), "a tendency of the model to occasionally produce overlapping (clashing) atoms", and "spurious structural order (hallucinations) in disordered regions" — all of which apply with force to short designed peptides. AF3 predicts a single static conformation, not an ensemble, and outputs no binding free energy.
findings.required_fix: Either (a) actually run local AF3 with, for each conjugate, a userCCD block defining the warhead (atom names, bonds, charges, leaving atoms, ideal geometry generated with RDKit or the CCD tooling), a bondedAtomPairs entry defining the conjugation bond to the named side-chain atom of the correct residue, the receptor as a second protein entity so a pose exists, and explicit SEP/other CCD modification codes where the mechanism requires them — then commit the resulting mmCIF and confidences JSON; or (b) drop "AlphaFold3" from every claim and relabel the entries as unmodelled design concepts. Fix the invalid 'B' residues at app.js:173 and app.js:371. Separately, replace all ΔG/Kd values with either output from a tool that actually computes them (FEP/MM-GBSA/docking, with the method and settings stated) or with nothing.

findings.what_is_wrong: Cysteine-rich designs are specified purely as one-letter strings with no disulfide topology. Eight cysteines admit 105 distinct fully-paired connectivities (7!! = 105); six admit 15; four admit 3 — and each is a different molecule with a different fold, not a different conformer of one molecule. Eleven of the designs have an odd cysteine count and therefore cannot be fully paired at all: at least one free thiol remains, which under oxidising extracellular or serum conditions drives disulfide scrambling, intermolecular dimerisation, and mixed disulfides with albumin Cys34 and glutathione. This is not a modelling nicety for these particular targets: the peptides are explicitly presented as CRD/Ig-domain and knottin-like binders (FZD8 CRD at app.js:174, TrkB Ig-like D5 at app.js:144), folds whose entire specificity derives from a defined cystine framework. Separately, app.js:152 states the huperzine A warhead is attached by "Cys-Lys Amide Coupling" to a 36-mer (app.js:153) containing no cysteine — the stated conjugation chemistry has no anchor in the stated sequence.
findings.why_it_matters: Without a specified cystine framework these are not defined chemical entities, and any predicted structure is a prediction about an arbitrary one of up to 105 possible molecules. In practice, a synthesis attempt on a 7- or 8-Cys peptide with unspecified pairing yields a heterogeneous mixture of oxidised isomers that cannot be resolved into the intended product; the odd-Cys designs additionally aggregate. Reporting a single pLDDT and a single Kd for such an entity implies a homogeneity that cannot exist, and would send a peptide-chemistry group down a months-long dead end. The X2 contradiction is worse in kind: the conjugation step described cannot be performed on the molecule described.
findings.ground_truth: A disulfide is a covalent bond with tight geometry — Sγ-Sγ ≈ 2.05 Å, Cβ-Sγ-Sγ ≈ 104°, χ3 (Cβ-Sγ-Sγ-Cβ) ≈ ±87° with a strong left-handed-spiral preference — and validation packages (MolProbity, wwPDB OneDep) flag deviations, non-bonded Cys pairs within bonding distance, and unpaired buried thiols. Cystine-stabilised scaffolds (knottins, EGF/Ig folds, Wnt/FZD CRD interfaces) are defined by their connectivity pattern, which must be stated as part of the sequence definition. In AF3, standard CYS residues can form disulfides implicitly, but the pairing is not user-controllable from a bare sequence and must be verified in the output; deliberate control requires explicit chemistry. In synthesis, defined pairing requires orthogonal protecting-group strategies (Trt/Acm/Mob/tBu) and staged oxidation, and the number of Cys must be even.
findings.required_fix: For every Cys-containing design, publish the intended disulfide connectivity explicitly (e.g. C1-C4, C2-C5, C3-C6) and the intended redox state of any deliberately free thiol. Make Cys count parity a hard validation rule: no design ships with an odd count unless the free thiol is the deliberate conjugation handle and is named as such. Verify the pairing in each predicted mmCIF by measuring Sγ-Sγ distances and χ3 angles and reporting them; flag any pair outside 2.0-2.1 Å / ±(75-105)°. Reconcile every chemStruct conjugation chemistry against the sequence — starting with app.js:152/153, where either a Cys must be introduced or the coupling chemistry restated. Choose orthogonal protection consistent with the declared pairing before any synthesis is proposed.

findings.title: No structure validation of any kind exists — no MolProbity/Ramachandran, no clashscore, no bond-geometry check, no PoseBusters ligand-pose check
findings.evidence_location: Absence verified by grep over /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/{README.md,app.js,index.html,styles.css}: 0 hits for each of molprobity, ramachandran, clashscore, posebusters, rdkit, openmm, .pdb, mmcif, .cif, B-factor, resolution. The only claimed quality metrics in the whole platform are the synthetic pLDDT (app.js:791) and the hardcoded strings at app.js:146,156,166,... and README.md:96-102.
findings.what_is_wrong: The platform presents itself as structural pharmacology output but contains no validation layer whatsoever — and cannot have one, since no coordinate file is ever produced or read. Absent are: backbone torsion validation (Ramachandran favoured/allowed/outlier percentages, Cβ deviations), all-atom steric validation (clashscore from reduced/probe-style H-atom contact analysis), covalent-geometry validation (bond-length and bond-angle Z-scores against Engh & Huber targets, peptide omega/planarity, cis-nonPro and twisted-peptide flags, chirality at Cα), rotamer outliers, and — most important for a ligand-conjugate platform — any physical-plausibility check on the ligand and its pose (internal energy, ring planarity, stereochemistry retention, protein-ligand steric overlap, ligand-in-pocket volume). Disulfide geometry validation is likewise absent (see SB-05).
findings.why_it_matters: These checks are the reason the field trusts any set of coordinates; they are mandatory in wwPDB deposition and are the first thing a reviewer runs on a predicted model. Their absence means nothing in this platform distinguishes a physically realisable molecule from one with inverted stereocentres, clashing atoms, or a warhead buried inside the peptide. This matters concretely for AF3 output specifically, because the AF3 authors report that their model "outputs do not always respect chirality" (4.4% chirality violations on the PoseBusters benchmark) and shows "a tendency ... to occasionally produce overlapping (clashing) atoms" — i.e. the very failure modes that only validation catches are known to occur at non-trivial rates in the tool being credited. Publishing predicted conjugate poses without PoseBusters-class checks is, since 2024, below the accepted standard of the field.
findings.ground_truth: MolProbity (Williams et al., Protein Science 27:293-315, 2018) is the community standard for all-atom validation and supplies clashscore, updated Ramachandran and rotamer criteria from a million quality-filtered residues, CaBLAM for low-resolution/cryo-EM backbone, and cis-nonPro/twisted-peptide flags; its clashscore is the metric the wwPDB tracks. wwPDB validation reports (Gore et al., Structure 25:1916-1927, 2017) codify the required checks for deposition. Engh & Huber (Acta Cryst A47:392-400, 1991) provide the target bond lengths and angles. PoseBusters (Buttenschoen, Morris & Deane, Chem. Sci. 15:3130-3139, 2024) is the standard physical-validity test suite for ligand poses — chemical validity, stereochemistry, internal geometry, and intra/intermolecular plausibility including protein-ligand clashes — and established that pose RMSD alone is not sufficient evidence of a usable prediction.
findings.required_fix: Add a validation stage that runs on every predicted mmCIF before any result is displayed: (1) MolProbity (or the phenix.molprobity CLI) for clashscore, Ramachandran favoured/outlier %, rotamer outliers, Cβ deviations, and cis/twisted peptides; (2) PoseBusters on every ligand pose in the conjugate and, where a receptor is modelled, on the protein-ligand pair; (3) explicit disulfide geometry measurement per SB-05; (4) a bond-length/angle Z-score summary against Engh & Huber. Surface these numbers in the UI next to pLDDT — a real validation panel is the honest replacement for the current confidence theatre — and gate publication on thresholds (e.g. clashscore < 10, Ramachandran outliers < 0.5%, zero PoseBusters failures), with any candidate that fails marked as such rather than hidden.

literature.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
literature.what_it_provides: The AF3 model itself, plus the authors' own limitations: chirality is not always respected (4.4% violations on the PoseBusters set), occasional overlapping/clashing atoms including whole-chain overlaps in homomers, hallucinated order in disordered regions mitigated by AF2 cross-distillation, prediction of a single static structure rather than solution dynamics, and the warning that 'the local structure will be sharply defined (for example, side-chain bond geometry) even when the network is uncertain about the positions'.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Establishes the ground truth for SB-03 (what AF3 is and outputs — notably no ΔG) and supplies the field's own justification for SB-06: the failure modes AF3 is documented to exhibit are precisely the ones that only post-hoc validation detects, so publishing predicted conjugate poses without validation is below standard.

literature.title: AlphaFold 3 input documentation (google-deepmind/alphafold3, docs/input.md)
literature.what_it_provides: The authoritative input contract: ligands by CCD code, SMILES, or user-provided CCD; bondedAtomPairs 'intended for modelling covalent ligands, and for defining multi-CCD ligands (e.g. glycans)'; and the two decisive restrictions — 'If using SMILES, you cannot specify covalent bonds to other entities as these rely on specific atom names' and 'Defining covalent bonds between or within polymer entities is not currently supported.'
literature.how_to_apply_here: Directly grounds SB-03: a covalent natural-product-to-peptide conjugate cannot be specified by SMILES alone; it requires a userCCD block with named atoms plus an explicit bondedAtomPairs entry, neither of which exists in this repository.

literature.title: PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences
literature.what_it_provides: An RDKit-based test suite for the physical validity of ligand poses — chemical and geometric consistency including stereochemistry, aromatic-ring planarity, standard bond lengths, and intra/intermolecular plausibility including protein-ligand clashes — and the finding that no deep-learning docking method beats classical docking once physical plausibility is scored alongside RMSD.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the missing check named in SB-06. Every conjugate pose (warhead + linker + peptide, and the receptor complex if predicted) must pass PoseBusters before any pose-derived claim is displayed; PoseBusters is also the benchmark on which AF3's 4.4% chirality-violation rate was measured.

literature.title: MolProbity: More and better reference data for improved all-atom structure validation
literature.what_it_provides: The community-standard all-atom validation suite: clashscore from explicit-H contact analysis, Ramachandran and rotamer criteria rebuilt from a million quality-filtered residues, CaBLAM Cα-CO virtual-angle analysis for low-resolution and cryo-EM backbone, and flags for rare cis-nonPro and twisted peptides.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Defines the exact validation stage absent per SB-06. Run MolProbity on every predicted mmCIF and surface clashscore, Ramachandran favoured/outlier %, rotamer outliers and Cβ deviations in the UI in place of the synthetic pLDDT panel.

literature.title: Validation of Structures in the Protein Data Bank
literature.what_it_provides: The wwPDB OneDep validation framework and the expert-task-force recommendations behind the standard validation report for X-ray, NMR and cryo-EM structures.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Provides the deposition-grade checklist a platform claiming 'structural pharmacology' should be measured against, and the template for the validation panel recommended in SB-06.

literature.title: lDDT: a local superposition-free score for comparing protein structures and models using distance difference tests
literature.what_it_provides: The definition of the local Distance Difference Test — the quantity that pLDDT predicts — including its superposition-free construction and its stereochemical-plausibility component.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Grounds SB-02: pLDDT is a per-residue estimate of lDDT-Cα for a specific predicted model, read from the mmCIF B-factor column or the confidences JSON. It is not a function of the amino-acid alphabet, which is what app.js:791 and the G/S/P/D colour rule at app.js:747-749 assume.

literature.title: Mol* Viewer: modern web app for 3D visualization and analysis of large biomolecular structures
literature.what_it_provides: The web-native molecular viewer used as the primary 3D viewer by both RCSB PDB and PDBe; streams and renders mmCIF/BinaryCIF, supports per-atom colouring from B-factor (hence pLDDT), ligand and polymer representations, and selection-based highlighting.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The recommended replacement for the synthetic Three.js tube in SB-01: load the predicted mmCIF, colour by the real pLDDT array, and render warhead and receptor so an actual binding pose is shown.

literature.title: 3Dmol.js: molecular visualization with WebGL
literature.what_it_provides: A lightweight, dependency-free JavaScript/WebGL molecular viewer with hardware-accelerated cartoon, stick and surface representations and PDB/mmCIF parsing, requiring no plugins.
literature.how_to_apply_here: A drop-in alternative to Mol* for this vanilla-JS, CDN-only codebase — it fits the existing architecture almost exactly and would replace app.js:674-773 and app.js:959-1022 with a real structure viewer at comparable code size.

literature.title: Accurate bond and angle parameters for X-ray protein structure refinement
literature.what_it_provides: The standard restraint targets for protein covalent geometry — bond lengths and angles derived from small-molecule crystal structures in the CSD, with force constants reflecting observed variability.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The reference against which the geometry in SB-01 fails and against which the bond-geometry Z-scores recommended in SB-06 should be computed. It is the basis for the fixed 3.80 Å Cα-Cα virtual bond length that the app.js:711-729 generator violates by up to 26-fold within a single chain.

reviews.overall_assessment:
Verdict: the structural component of this platform is not a weak implementation of structure prediction — it is a visual simulation of one, and the claims attached to it are not recoverable by incremental fixes.

What I verified, with numbers. The 3D "backbone" at app.js:711-729 (and its twin at app.js:973-991) places each residue at sin/cos of its index on a cylinder whose radius is 6 + (ASCII mod 5)·0.8. Re-running that code in Python on the actual sequences gives consecutive-point separations of 0.63-19.08 scene units, coefficient of variation 0.56-0.82, max/min ratios of 8-26x within a single chain. Real Cα-Cα is 3.80 Å with CV ~1%. Those are ratios, so no choice of Å-per-unit rescues them. The cause is that the angle at app.js:717 is recomputed per residue with a multiplier that flips 4↔6 on ASCII mod 3, making it non-monotonic (verified: i=5 → 2.005 rad, i=6 → 1.604 rad); the chain jumps backwards across the cylinder. Helical parameters are equally scale-free wrong: radius/rise = 10.0-19.9 versus 1.53 for an alpha-helix, and residues-per-turn is L/2 or L/3 — 13 to 50 depending only on chain length, against 3.6. Secondary structure is being assigned by character code where it is physically determined by phi/psi and backbone H-bonding, which is why the residue colouring (G/S → high confidence, P/D → low) is not just arbitrary but close to inverted for glycine. The pLDDT curve is 93 + 4·sin(0.4i) + 0.5·(ASCII mod 5), range [89.0, 99.0] over all possible inputs — the clamps at app.js:792-793 are unreachable and the legend's "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" bands can never render. The PAE matrix is 0.4·|i-j| plus a row constant: a pure function of sequence separation, structurally information-free, maxing at 18.5 Å under a panel labelled 0-30 Å. Nothing anywhere reads a coordinate or confidence file — zero grep hits for pdb, cif, mmcif, fetch(, XMLHttpRequest — so "Live AlphaFold Server Connection" is an anchor tag and a clipboard copy.

Three findings independently invalidate the central claim, and they are mutually reinforcing rather than redundant: the geometry is synthetic (SB-01), the confidence metrics are synthetic (SB-02), and the molecules as described cannot be submitted to AF3 in the first place (SB-03) — the AlphaFold Server takes ligands only from a ~19-code allow-list that contains none of these natural products, and the local code's own documentation states that SMILES ligands cannot carry covalent bonds to other entities. Two further findings are, to me, the most diagnostic: four sequences appear twice with different reported pLDDT and ΔG (SB-04), which is not a modelling error but a signature of hand-written numbers; and 103 cysteines across 25 designs, 11 with odd counts and up to 8 in one peptide, with no disulfide connectivity anywhere (SB-05) — an 8-Cys peptide with unspecified pairing is 105 different molecules, and drug X2's stated "Cys-Lys Amide Coupling" targets a cysteine its sequence does not contain. The absence of MolProbity, clashscore, bond-geometry and PoseBusters checks (SB-06) is real but secondary, because there are no coordinates to validate.

Credit where it is due, and it is not trivial. The underlying pharmacology is often genuinely well-informed: the AChE CAS (Trp84/Phe330) and PAS (Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341) assignments, the GSK-3β hinge contacts (Val135/Asp133), Keap1 Cys151 alkylation, the Nrf2 Neh2 ETGE motif rendered correctly as DEETGE, the Aβ16-35 segment KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM reproduced exactly, and GGGGS as the flexible linker are all correct and non-obvious. I checked drug #9's peptide against UniProt P49841 and it is exactly GSK-3β residues 3-34 — the autoinhibitory N-terminal pseudosubstrate, a genuinely sound design idea (though it only inhibits when Ser9 is phosphorylated, and no SEP modification is specified anywhere). The information architecture of the modal is also right: 3D model, per-residue confidence, PAE matrix side by side is exactly the panel a structural biologist wants. The code is clean, deterministic and runs. The problem is confined but total: every quantity in those panels is invented, and the comment at app.js:707 and README.md:108 assert the opposite in so many words.

Path forward. This is salvageable as an honest artifact with modest work and one hard decision. Strip the synthetic generators (app.js:674-773, 775-866, 959-1022) and the "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING" claim; relabel the 25 entries as design concepts; remove every ΔG, Kd and pLDDT number, since none has a generating process. Then, if real modelling is wanted, do the work AF3 actually requires: userCCD blocks for each warhead, bondedAtomPairs for the conjugation bond, the receptor as a second entity so a pose exists, explicit disulfide connectivity and even Cys counts, and a validation stage (MolProbity + PoseBusters) whose output is displayed rather than a confidence curve. Swapping Three.js for Mol* or 3Dmol.js is the smallest part of this — it fits the existing vanilla-JS architecture almost exactly. What cannot be kept is the current state: a private repository is a fine place for exploratory work, but the README as written would mislead any structural biologist who read it, and the "designed via AlphaFold3" claim should not leave this machine attached to these files.

reviews.discipline: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD in computational chemistry and biophysics, 18 years' experience; alchemical free-energy method development (FEP/TI, ABFE double-decoupling), MM-GB/PBSA end-state calculations, and docking scoring-function validation on CASF/D3R-style benchmarks.

findings.title: All 25 (ΔG, Kd) pairs violate ΔG° = RT ln Kd by 3.85–5.73 kcal/mol (2.8–4.2 orders of magnitude); zero pairs are self-consistent
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:146,156,166,176,186,198,208,218,228,238,250,260,270,280,290,302,312,322,332,342,354,364,374,384,394 (the `affinity:` string of every FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA record); split and rendered as separate badges at app.js:562-575 and app.js:636; restated in README.md:60-64,71,78,85,92
findings.what_is_wrong: Every drug record states a ΔG and a Kd side by side, e.g. app.js:146 `"ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol | Kd = 0.32 nM"`. These are not independent quantities — for a 1:1 equilibrium they are the same number in different units. I evaluated all 25 pairs with RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol (R = 1.98720e-3 kcal/mol/K, T = 298.15 K, c° = 1 M). Not one pair is consistent, and the error is systematic and one-signed. Worked examples: id 1 HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (app.js:146) states ΔG = -18.4 and Kd = 0.32 nM; -18.4 kcal/mol implies Kd = 3.26e-14 M (32.6 fM), while 0.32 nM implies ΔG = -12.95 kcal/mol — a 5.45 kcal/mol / 3.99 log10 contradiction. id 15 BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (app.js:290) states ΔG = -19.5 and Kd = 0.08 nM; -19.5 implies Kd = 5.09e-15 M (5.1 fM), 0.08 nM implies ΔG = -13.77 — a 5.73 kcal/mol / 4.20 log10 contradiction (the worst). id 24 AstroPafr-Block-A4 (app.js:384) is the mildest at 3.85 kcal/mol / 2.82 log10. Across all 25: mean discrepancy 4.73 kcal/mol, range 3.85–5.73; mean 3.47 orders of magnitude in Kd, range 2.82–4.20; number of pairs consistent within ±0.5 kcal/mol = 0/25. No unit slip explains it: reading Kd in nM rather than M would give ΔG values near -0.7 kcal/mol, not -18. Regressing the stated ΔG on the thermodynamically correct ΔG derived from the stated Kd gives ΔG_stated = 1.771 × ΔG_true + 4.682 with R² = 0.9939 and a maximum residual of 0.22 kcal/mol — i.e. the two columns are related by a near-perfect affine rescaling with a gain of 1.77, not by physics. Equivalently, the implied conversion slope is 1.0495 kcal/mol per ln unit instead of RT = 0.5925, corresponding to a 'temperature' of 528 K (255 °C), a condition at which liquid water does not exist at ambient pressure and no protein is folded.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader — or an automated downstream consumer of this dataset — cannot recover which number, if either, is intended. Every headline claim in the platform depends on the choice: the dashboard 'Peak Binding Energy' tile (index.html:74-75) advertises -19.5 kcal/mol, which is femtomolar, while the same candidate's own card advertises 0.08 nM, which is ordinary optimized-binder territory — a 4-order-of-magnitude difference in claimed potency. A medicinal chemist or investor reading the ΔG column would conclude these are the tightest peptide binders ever described; reading the Kd column they would conclude they are unremarkable. Presenting both, in the same string, as if they corroborate each other manufactures false confirmation from a single made-up number.
findings.ground_truth: For a 1:1 binding equilibrium the standard binding free energy is ΔG° = RT ln(Kd/c°) = -RT ln(Ka·c°), with the standard state c° = 1 M. At T = 298.15 K, RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol and RT·ln(10) = 1.3642 kcal/mol per decade in Kd. Reference points: Kd = 1 nM → ΔG° = -12.28; 1 pM → -16.37; 1 fM → -20.46 kcal/mol. ΔG and Kd are therefore a single degree of freedom, not two measurements; reporting both is only meaningful when one is explicitly the transform of the other (and when the standard state and temperature are stated).
findings.required_fix: Report exactly one primary quantity per candidate and derive the other in code rather than hardcoding it. Concretely: keep a single numeric field (e.g. `kd_M`), add `const RT = 0.0019872041 * 298.15;` and compute `dg = RT * Math.log(kd_M)` at render time in app.js (replacing the hand-written `affinity:` strings at app.js:146-394), and display the standard state and temperature next to the value ('ΔG°, 1 M standard state, 298.15 K'). Add a unit test asserting |ΔG - RT·ln(Kd)| < 0.01 kcal/mol for every record so the two columns can never drift again.

findings.title: The ΔG/Kd values are demonstrably not the output of any calculation: identical peptide sequences against the same target are assigned ΔG values differing by up to 4.9 kcal/mol, and a record that contains no sequence at all still carries an affinity
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:153+156 vs app.js:247+250 vs app.js:131 (sequence KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG); app.js:195+198 vs app.js:319+322 vs app.js:134; app.js:205+208 vs app.js:361+364; app.js:173+176 vs app.js:371+374; app.js:215+218 vs app.js:132; app.js:225+228 vs app.js:133; app.js:163+166 vs app.js:127; app.js:381+384
findings.what_is_wrong: I extracted every sequence in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA and AF3_CANDIDATES and grouped by exact string. Seven sequences are reused across two or three records, and every reuse carries a different ΔG. The decisive case is the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG: at app.js:153 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, bindingSites 'AChE CAS ... & PAS') it is ΔG = -16.2 / Kd = 2.1 nM; at app.js:247 (BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, bindingSites 'AChE Catalytic Gorge') the byte-identical sequence against the same protein is ΔG = -17.5 / Kd = 0.65 nM; at app.js:131 (CogAChE-PAS-02, target 'AChE PAS Gorge') the same sequence is ΔG = -12.6. That is a 4.9 kcal/mol spread — 3.6 orders of magnitude in Kd — for the same molecule binding the same protein. Free energy is a state function; the same complex cannot have three different ΔG values. Further instances: SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC → -16.5 (app.js:198, α7 nAChR), -15.7 (app.js:322, TLR4/MD-2), -12.1 (app.js:134, α7 nAChR) — 4.4 kcal/mol spread, and the same peptide is asserted to bind two structurally unrelated receptors. GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG → -16.0 (app.js:228) vs -11.8 (app.js:133), 4.2 kcal/mol. GCPWECDRRACPCYRGFWRERACPDCHSEAEFRLFRDVWANYCAC → -15.4 (app.js:218) vs -13.0 (app.js:132), 2.4 kcal/mol. VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH → -17.2 vs -15.8 (app.js:208, 364) for TrkB and for the EAAT2 transporter. Most conclusively, app.js:381 sets `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` — a label, not a sequence, containing hyphens and digits — and app.js:384 nonetheless assigns it ΔG = -15.2 kcal/mol, Kd = 4.8 nM and pLDDT = 92.4. Two of the sequences also contain 'B' (app.js:173, 371, 130), which is not a standard one-letter amino acid code and cannot be modelled by any structure or energy method.
findings.why_it_matters: This is not an accuracy problem that better methods would fix; it is proof that no method was run. If any docking, MM-GBSA, FEP, or ML scorer had produced these numbers, identical inputs would have produced identical outputs, and a string like 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' would have raised a parse error rather than a nanomolar Kd. The 25-drug table and the TOP-10 leaderboard are therefore a narrative artifact: the values track the marketing tier of each entry ('Dual', 'Super', 'Bispecific', 'Tri-Functional' entries get the most negative ΔG) rather than any property of the molecules. Anyone treating this repository as a screening result — synthesizing a peptide, filing IP, or citing the ranking — would be acting on numbers with no referent.
findings.ground_truth: Binding free energy is a thermodynamic state function of a defined (receptor, ligand, solvent, T, p, standard state) system. For a fixed ligand and fixed target it has one value, and any legitimate estimator is a deterministic or statistically convergent function of the input structures/sequences. Reproducibility on identical inputs is the minimum acceptance criterion for a scoring pipeline; benchmark suites such as CASF-2016 (Su et al. 2019) exist precisely to characterize the residual error of estimators that do satisfy this.
findings.required_fix: Delete all hardcoded ΔG/Kd strings from app.js:146-394 and app.js:125-134. Replace them either with (a) values produced by a checked-in, runnable pipeline whose inputs (target PDB/UniProt accession, prepared receptor, ligand definition), software version, and random seed are stored alongside each number, or (b) an explicit 'not computed' placeholder. Add a data-integrity test that hashes each sequence and asserts that identical (sequence, target) keys map to identical affinity values. Reject records whose `sequence` field is not a valid string over the 20 canonical one-letter codes (this alone catches app.js:173, 371, 381 and app.js:130).

findings.title: The stated ΔG magnitudes are at or beyond the empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding: 6 of 25 exceed biotin–streptavidin, presented as routine output for 28–47-residue de novo peptides
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:146,186,238,290,342,394 (ΔG = -18.4, -19.1, -18.7, -19.5, -18.9, -18.2); dashboard headline at /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:74-75 ('-19.5 kcal', 'Peak Binding Energy'); README.md:60,64,71,78,85,92
findings.what_is_wrong: Taken at face value (which is what the dashboard tile at index.html:74-75 and the leaderboard ΔG column at app.js:885 invite the reader to do), the stated free energies correspond to: -18.2 → 46 fM, -18.4 → 33 fM, -18.7 → 20 fM, -18.9 → 14 fM, -19.1 → 10 fM, -19.5 → 5.1 fM. Biotin–streptavidin, the canonical tightest non-covalent biological interaction, has Kd ≈ 4e-14 M → ΔG° = -18.28 kcal/mol (experimental value widely quoted as ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol). Six of the 25 candidates are therefore claimed to bind more tightly than biotin–streptavidin, and the flagship BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (app.js:290) at -19.5 kcal/mol is claimed to be ~8-fold tighter than biotin–streptavidin. The remaining 19 sit between -15.2 and -17.8, i.e. 7 pM to 90 fM — still tighter than essentially any reported de novo designed peptide. For calibration, the best affinity-matured de novo mini-protein binders from state-of-the-art structure-based design reach roughly 20 pM to 10 nM (Cao et al., Nature 2022), i.e. ΔG° of -14.6 to -10.9 kcal/mol; unoptimized first-round designs are typically µM–nM. There is no ligand-efficiency argument that rescues these: -19.5 kcal/mol over the ~295 heavy atoms of a 39-mer is LE ≈ 0.066 kcal/mol per heavy atom, which is not itself anomalous, but the total is, because the interface a 28–47-residue linear peptide can bury is small and largely unpreorganized (these are flexible chains, several with unpaired cysteines and GGGGS linkers, so a large conformational-entropy penalty applies before any interface term is counted).
