The claimed affinities are also asserted uniformly across six unrelated target classes (RTK ectodomains, an AChE gorge, a Kelch β-propeller, a Frizzled CRD, a pentameric LGIC ECD, a membrane transporter), which is itself implausible — achievable affinity is strongly target- and epitope-dependent.
findings.why_it_matters: Femtomolar affinity is effectively irreversible on any biological timescale; a compound with Kd = 5 fM would not dissociate from its target over the lifetime of the cell, which contradicts the platform's own claim of 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2%' and reversible allosteric tuning (README.md:100-102). It also makes the safety narrative incoherent: at 5 fM the drug would be quantitatively bound to every copy of the target at concentrations far below one molecule per cell (one molecule in a 1 pL cell is ~1.7 nM). Any reviewer, grant panel, or partner with binding-thermodynamics training will read the -18 to -19.5 kcal/mol column as an immediate red flag and discount the entire repository, including the parts that are sound.
findings.ground_truth: Kuntz et al. (PNAS 1999, 'The maximal affinity of ligands') established the empirical ceiling on binding free energy: affinity grows at ≈ -1.5 kcal/mol per non-hydrogen atom only for the first ~15 heavy atoms and then plateaus, with the tightest known complexes clustering near -18 kcal/mol. Biotin–streptavidin, Kd ≈ 4e-14 M (ΔG° ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol), is the standard benchmark for that ceiling (Jain & Cheng, PLoS ONE 2019, for the modern solution kinetics/thermodynamics characterization). Reported de novo designed protein/peptide binders reach 20 pM–10 nM after experimental optimization (Cao et al., Nature 2022). A pipeline that routinely outputs values beyond the biotin–streptavidin ceiling for short linear peptides is reporting an artifact, not a discovery.
findings.required_fix: Add a physical-plausibility guard to the data layer: flag or reject any candidate whose |ΔG| exceeds ~15 kcal/mol (Kd < ~10 pM) unless it is backed by an experimental measurement or a converged ABFE calculation with a reported uncertainty. Re-baseline all claimed potencies against an achievable range for the modality (for 28–47-residue linear peptides: high-nM to low-nM as a design target, pM only after affinity maturation with data). Replace the index.html:74-75 'Peak Binding Energy -19.5 kcal' tile, which currently advertises the least credible number in the dataset as the platform's headline result.

findings.title: AlphaFold3 does not compute binding free energy, and the repository contains no affinity-estimation code of any kind — yet every ΔG/Kd/CEI number is attributed to 'AF3'
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/README.md:22,24,45,106-111; /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:30,54,285,291,371,410; /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:124 (comment '--- AlphaFold3 Top 10 Candidates ---' over the hardcoded `dg` field), app.js:707 (comment 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION'), app.js:791, app.js:850, app.js:905, app.js:1071
findings.what_is_wrong: AlphaFold3 (Abramson et al., Nature 2024) predicts 3D coordinates for biomolecular complexes and emits confidence estimates — pLDDT (per-atom/per-residue local confidence, 0–100), PAE (pairwise predicted aligned error, in Å), pTM/ipTM, and clash/disorder metrics. It has no free-energy term, no thermodynamic ensemble, no solvation model, and no affinity head; its confidence scores are calibrated to structural accuracy, not to binding strength, and independent assessments report minimal correlation between AF3 ranking metrics and experimental affinity. Nothing in this repository bridges that gap. I grepped README.md, app.js, index.html and styles.css for `vina|smina|gnina|autodock|rosetta|openmm|gromacs|amber|namd|mmgbsa|mm-gbsa|mmpbsa|prodigy|boltz|diffdock|foldx|glide|alchemical|thermodynam|Math.log|Math.exp|boltzmann`: exactly one line matched, README.md:108, and it matched only because 'Amber' is used there as a UI colour name ('Low 50-70 Amber'). `git ls-files` confirms the tracked platform is README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css and skills-lock.json plus vendored `.agents/skills/` documentation; there is no .pdb, .cif, .mmcif, AF3 confidence JSON, trajectory, topology, or scoring script anywhere. The quantities the UI labels as AF3 output are literals or sine waves: `dg`/`cei`/`plddt` are hardcoded at app.js:125-134; the modal 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' is `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode % 5)*0.5` (app.js:791); the 'PAE' matrix is `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (charCode % 4)*0.3` (app.js:850); the 3D 'backbone' is a helix of radius `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` (app.js:715) fed to a Catmull-Rom tube. The 'Live AlphaFold Server Connection' (README.md:111, index.html:42, 363) is an `<a href>` to alphafoldserver.com plus a clipboard copy (app.js:660-671) — a link, not an integration; no request is ever made and no prediction is ever retrieved.
findings.why_it_matters: The platform's central claim — '25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3', ranked by ΔG on a leaderboard (index.html:295-312) — asserts a capability that neither AlphaFold3 nor this codebase possesses. The header badge 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' (index.html:42) and the footer 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling' (index.html:410) tell a non-expert that DeepMind's model produced these energies. It did not, and nothing did. This misattributes authorship of the numbers to a third party's tool and converts a static mock-up into an apparent computational result.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold3 outputs structure plus confidence (pLDDT, PAE, pTM/ipTM) — Abramson et al., Nature 2024 (PMID 38718835). It does not predict Kd, IC50, or ΔG_bind. Docking with AlphaFold models is additionally known to underperform docking to experimental structures (Karelina, Noh & Dror, eLife 2023). Affinity requires a separate, explicitly physical or explicitly trained layer: physics-based (ABFE/RBFE via OpenMM/GROMACS alchemical protocols; MM-GB/PBSA via gmx_MMPBSA), empirical (AutoDock Vina 1.2.0, smina, gnina CNN rescoring), interface-statistical (PRODIGY for protein–protein Kd; Rosetta InterfaceAnalyzer/ddG for interface energetics in Rosetta Energy Units, which are not kcal/mol), or learned (Boltz-2, the first open model to approach FEP-level correlation on small-molecule potency).
findings.required_fix: Stop attributing energies to AlphaFold3. Restrict AF3-derived claims to what AF3 actually returns, and only after a real prediction is run: store the returned mmCIF plus the confidence JSON per candidate and plot the real per-residue pLDDT and real PAE matrix instead of app.js:791 and app.js:850. Then add a genuine, separately-labelled affinity layer and state its expected accuracy in the UI — e.g. Vina/gnina for pose generation and coarse ranking (enrichment yes, quantitative ΔG no), gmx_MMPBSA for relative end-state ranking within a congeneric series (not absolute), PRODIGY for protein–protein Kd from a 3D complex (r ≈ 0.73, RMSE ≈ 1.89 kcal/mol on its benchmark), Boltz-2 for learned small-molecule potency, and OpenMM-based ABFE/RBFE as the only tier that legitimately produces kcal/mol with an error bar (~1–2 kcal/mol RMSE at best, and only for small molecules — ABFE for 30–50-mer flexible peptides is not a solved problem). Every displayed number must carry its provenance: method, version, and uncertainty.

findings.title: One-decimal ΔG values are reported with no uncertainty, no method, no temperature and no standard state — precision an order of magnitude finer than the best available methods can deliver
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:125-134 (`dg: -17.9` … `dg: -11.8`), app.js:146-394 (`ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol` … `ΔG = -15.2 kcal/mol`), app.js:905 (`ΔG: ${cand.dg} kcal/mol`), app.js:1071; /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:285,305; README.md:60-92
findings.what_is_wrong: Every energy is given to 0.1 kcal/mol with no ± interval, no method label, no temperature, no standard state, no replicate count, and no statement of whether the value is absolute or relative. The ΔG differences that drive the entire leaderboard ordering are of the same size as, or smaller than, the irreducible error of the best available methods: the gap between rank 4 (-14.2, app.js:128) and rank 5 (-14.8, app.js:129) is 0.6 kcal/mol, and rank 7 (-12.6) vs rank 8 (-13.0) is 0.4 kcal/mol. Even converged alchemical calculations cannot resolve those gaps reliably. Nothing in the codebase records where any value came from, so no reader can assess it.
findings.why_it_matters: A one-decimal number without an interval reads as a measurement. It licenses decisions the data cannot support — 'rank 4 beats rank 5', 'X5 is better than X1' — when the entire spread of the leaderboard (-11.8 to -17.9) is only ~6 kcal/mol and the honest error bar on any of the individual values would be 1–2 kcal/mol at best, or unbounded for docking scores. Ranking on unlabelled point estimates is the single most common way computational affinity work misleads experimentalists into synthesizing the wrong compound.
findings.ground_truth: Absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations — the gold standard — report RMSE against experiment historically in the 0.8–2.3 kcal/mol range depending on system, with ~1.1 kcal/mol achievable after zero-point shifting; note also that experimental reproducibility between independent assays is itself ~0.9 kcal/mol and can reach 2 kcal/mol. Empirical docking scoring functions are far worse: CASF-2016 (Su et al. 2019) evaluates 'scoring power' separately from 'docking power' precisely because correlation with measured affinity is the weakest of the four metrics; docking scores are useful for enrichment, not for kcal/mol. MM-GB/PBSA is explicitly intermediate between empirical scoring and rigorous alchemical perturbation in both accuracy and cost, is highly sensitive to the choice of solvation model and entropy treatment, and requires per-system calibration (Genheden & Ryde 2015) — it is a relative ranking tool within a congeneric series, not a quantitative predictor. PRODIGY, the best-performing simple protein–protein affinity predictor, reports Pearson r = 0.73 with RMSE = 1.89 kcal/mol on its benchmark. Against any of these, a bare '-18.4' is not a result.
findings.required_fix: Never display a free energy without (i) the method and version, (ii) an uncertainty (statistical SEM from replicates plus a stated model error), and (iii) T, p and standard state. Change the rendering at app.js:905 and app.js:636 to a form like 'ΔG° = -12.3 ± 1.5 kcal/mol (Vina score, not calibrated; 298 K, 1 M standard state)'. Where the estimator is a docking score, label it a score in arbitrary units and do not print 'kcal/mol'. Rank candidates by score bands or with confidence intervals shown, and suppress orderings whose gaps fall inside the stated error — do not present a strict 1–10 leaderboard (index.html:295-312) built on 0.4 kcal/mol differences.

findings.title: 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI)' is an invented score with no definition, no units and no computation, yet is the primary ranking axis and is plotted on the same axis as |ΔG|
findings.evidence_location: /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/app.js:125-134 (`cei: 98.4` … `cei: 82.5`), app.js:886 (rendered as a leaderboard column), app.js:1054,1063 (`'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI / 100)'`), app.js:1055,1071 (`Math.abs(c.dg)` plotted as a second series on the same chart); /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/index.html:306 ('CEI Score' table header), index.html:316 ('TOP 10 Candidate Computational Benchmark (CEI vs Binding Affinity)')
findings.what_is_wrong: 'Cognitive Enhancement Index' is not a defined scientific metric. It appears nowhere in the pharmacology, neuroscience, or cheminformatics literature as a standardized quantity, and the repository never defines it: there is no formula, no input variables, no units, no validation set, and no reference. The ten values are literals in app.js:125-134. They are strictly monotone with the assigned rank (r(CEI, rank) = -0.985) while ΔG is not (the `dg` sequence -17.9, -16.8, -15.1, -14.2, -14.8, -13.5, -12.6, -13.0, -11.8, -12.1 inverts at rank 4/5 and 7/8), which shows the leaderboard is ordered by CEI, i.e. by the undefined quantity, and that CEI was written first and ΔG fitted loosely around it (r(CEI, ΔG) = -0.94). The chart at app.js:1057-1078 then plots CEI (0–100, dimensionless) and |ΔG| (kcal/mol) as two bar series on a single shared y-axis, so a 98.4 'index' bar towers over a 17.9 kcal/mol bar with no axis distinction — a category error in the visualization on top of the category error in the metric. Separately, r(pLDDT, ΔG) = -0.38 across the ten candidates, i.e. even the internal narrative that high AF3 confidence tracks tight binding is not supported by the platform's own invented numbers.
findings.why_it_matters: The UI labels this a 'Computational Benchmark' (index.html:316) and gives it the top-ranked, gold-badge column position, so it reads as the platform's primary figure of merit. An undefined index presented as a benchmark score is unfalsifiable: no one can reproduce it, contest it, or compare a new candidate against it. Because it is the actual sort key, the entire 'TOP 10' framing rests on a number that means nothing — and plotting it against |ΔG| on a shared axis implies a validated relationship between a cognition outcome and a binding energy, which no in silico method can supply (target engagement does not predict cognitive efficacy, and no computational pipeline in existence outputs a cognition score).
findings.ground_truth: There is no accepted composite metric named 'Cognitive Enhancement Index'. Legitimate, defined composite scores in this space are things like ligand efficiency (LE = -ΔG/N_heavy_atoms), ligand-efficiency-dependent lipophilicity (LELP), QED, or CNS MPO — each with a published formula, input descriptors, and a validation cohort. Predicted cognitive benefit is not derivable from structure: it requires in vivo pharmacodynamic and behavioural endpoints, and even validated target engagement is a poor predictor of clinical cognitive outcome. Any composite score that is presented must publish its formula, its component weights, the data it was fitted to, and its out-of-sample performance.
findings.required_fix: Either remove CEI entirely (delete the `cei` field at app.js:125-134, the column at app.js:886 and index.html:306, and the first chart series at app.js:1062-1069), or define it explicitly: publish the formula, its inputs, their sources, the weighting rationale, and its validation, and rename it to something that does not claim a clinical cognitive outcome from in silico data. If any composite is retained, do not sort the leaderboard by it without showing the formula in the UI, and split the chart into two panels or two labelled axes so a dimensionless index is never drawn on the same scale as a kcal/mol quantity.

literature.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
literature.what_it_provides: The primary AlphaFold3 paper. Defines what the model actually outputs: 3D coordinates for protein/nucleic-acid/ligand/ion complexes plus confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE, pTM/ipTM). Contains no free-energy, affinity, or Kd prediction of any kind.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Cite as the authority for CT-04: every ΔG, Kd and CEI value labelled 'AF3' in app.js:125-134 and app.js:146-394 is outside AlphaFold3's output space. Use it to rewrite README.md:22-24 and index.html:30,410 so AF3 is credited only for structure and confidence, and only once a real prediction has been run and stored.

literature.title: The maximal affinity of ligands
literature.what_it_provides: The empirical ceiling on binding free energy: affinity increases at ≈ -1.5 kcal/mol per non-hydrogen atom only up to ~15 heavy atoms, then plateaus; the tightest complexes surveyed cluster near -18 kcal/mol.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Ground truth for CT-03. Provides the literature basis for a plausibility guard rejecting |ΔG| > ~15 kcal/mol claims for de novo peptides, and for flagging the six candidates (app.js:146,186,238,290,342,394) that are asserted to bind more tightly than the strongest known non-covalent complex.

literature.title: Detailed characterization of the solution kinetics and thermodynamics of biotin, biocytin and HABA binding to avidin and streptavidin
literature.what_it_provides: Modern quantitative characterization of the biotin–streptavidin interaction, the canonical tightest non-covalent biological complex (Kd on the order of 4e-14 M, ΔG° ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol).
literature.how_to_apply_here: The calibration point for CT-03. Used to show that ΔG = -19.5 kcal/mol (app.js:290) implies Kd = 5.1 fM, ~8× tighter than biotin–streptavidin, for a 39-residue flexible peptide conjugate.

literature.title: Design of protein-binding proteins from the target structure alone
literature.what_it_provides: State-of-the-art de novo binder design with experimentally measured affinities; optimized mini-protein binders reach roughly 20 pM to 10 nM (ΔG° ≈ -14.6 to -10.9 kcal/mol), with crystal structures confirming five designs.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The realistic affinity envelope for CT-03. Establishes what a credible de novo binder pipeline claims after experimental optimization, against which the platform's uniform -15.2 to -19.5 kcal/mol for unvalidated 28–47-mers is an outlier by 3–5 kcal/mol.

literature.title: Comparative Assessment of Scoring Functions: The CASF-2016 Update
literature.id: 10.1021/acs.jcim.8b00545 (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 59(2):895-913; Su, Yang, Du, Feng, Liu, Li, Wang)
literature.what_it_provides: The standard benchmark decoupling scoring from docking across 285 protein–ligand complexes and 25 scoring functions, evaluated on scoring, ranking, docking and screening power; finds docking power is the strongest metric and scoring power (correlation with measured affinity) the weakest.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Ground truth for CT-05. Justifies labelling any docking output as a score in arbitrary units rather than kcal/mol, and refusing to rank candidates on 0.4–0.6 kcal/mol gaps (app.js:128-132).

literature.title: The MM/PBSA and MM/GBSA methods to estimate ligand-binding affinities
literature.what_it_provides: Authoritative review placing MM/PBSA and MM/GBSA as intermediate between empirical scoring and rigorous alchemical perturbation in both accuracy and cost, with emphasis on the calibration, testing and validation required before the numbers mean anything.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supports CT-04 and CT-05: if the project adds an end-state rescoring tier, it must be presented as a relative ranking within a congeneric series with per-system calibration, never as an absolute kcal/mol affinity.

literature.title: gmx_MMPBSA: A New Tool to Perform End-State Free Energy Calculations with GROMACS
literature.what_it_provides: A maintained, runnable MMPBSA.py-derived tool for end-state free energy calculations from GROMACS trajectories: PB/GB/3D-RISM solvation, computational alanine scanning, entropy corrections, per-residue decomposition.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Concrete implementation for the remediation in CT-04 — the tier that would produce per-residue interaction decompositions consistent with the binding-site residue lists already annotated at app.js:144,154,164,174,184 etc., with the honest caveat from Genheden & Ryde attached.

literature.title: AutoDock Vina 1.2.0: New Docking Methods, Expanded Force Field, and Python Bindings
literature.what_it_provides: The current reference implementation of the most widely used open-source docking engine, with macrocycle and explicit-water support, the AD4.2 scoring function, multi-ligand docking, batch mode and Python bindings.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The minimum viable real scoring layer for CT-04. Runnable today on the targets already named in the repo; its output must be labelled a score (enrichment-useful, not quantitative), which is exactly the correction CT-05 requires.

literature.title: GNINA 1.0: molecular docking with deep learning
literature.what_it_provides: CNN-ensemble scoring/rescoring on top of the Vina/smina framework; outperforms Vina scoring on redocking and cross-docking when the pocket is defined.
literature.how_to_apply_here: A drop-in rescoring upgrade over bare Vina for the affinity layer proposed in CT-04, with the same caveat that CNN pose scores are not calibrated free energies.

literature.title: Contacts-based prediction of binding affinity in protein–protein complexes (PRODIGY)
literature.id: 10.7554/eLife.07454 (eLife 4:e07454; PMID 26193119; Vangone & Bonvin). Web server: Xue et al., Bioinformatics 32(23):3676
literature.what_it_provides: Interface-contact-based predictor of protein–protein binding affinity, reporting Pearson r = 0.73 and RMSE = 1.89 kcal/mol on its benchmark — with the explicit finding that experimental method and conformational change strongly affect achievable accuracy.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The correct tool class for this project's actual modality (peptide/protein binding to TrkB, Trem2, Keap1, FZD8, α7 nAChR ECD), and the source of an honest error bar: ~1.9 kcal/mol RMSE is the realistic uncertainty to display instead of the bare one-decimal values flagged in CT-05.

literature.title: Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction
literature.what_it_provides: Open structural-biology foundation model that jointly predicts structure and binding affinity; the first ML model reported to approach relative-FEP-level correlation on small-molecule potency benchmarks (OpenFE set, CASP16 affinity challenge) at ~1000× lower cost than FEP.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The honest modern answer to 'can a neural network give me an affinity number?' — yes, for small molecules, with published benchmark correlations that must be quoted alongside the prediction. Directly contrasts with CT-04: an affinity head is a separate, explicitly trained component that AlphaFold3 does not have.

literature.title: PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences
literature.what_it_provides: RDKit-based physical- and chemical-validity checks showing that deep-learning docking methods (DiffDock, EquiBind, TankBind, Uni-Mol and others) achieve strong RMSD numbers while producing stereochemically and geometrically invalid poses, and generalize poorly to novel sequences.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The required caveat if DiffDock-class generative docking is added under CT-04: RMSD-based success rates are not evidence of usable poses, and any pose feeding a downstream energy calculation must pass PoseBusters checks first. Also the general lesson for this repo — a plausible-looking 3D rendering is not a validated structure.

literature.title: How accurately can one predict drug binding modes using AlphaFold models?
literature.what_it_provides: Systematic assessment showing that docking to AlphaFold models yields ligand pose accuracy no better than docking to traditional homology models, and much worse than docking to experimental structures.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Bounds the whole 'AF3 → affinity' premise (CT-04). Even the legitimate pipeline — predict structure with AF3, then dock/score — inherits a substantial accuracy penalty relative to experimental structures, which must be stated in the UI rather than hidden behind a 'Very High confidence' pLDDT pill (index.html:278).

reviews.overall_assessment:
Verdict: the binding-thermodynamics layer of CognitionBioChem does not survive audit. It is not a pipeline with accuracy problems; it is a set of literals with no generator, and the physics it displays is internally contradictory.

The quantitative core of the audit is arithmetic and is not in dispute. Applying ΔG° = RT ln(Kd/c°) with RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol (298.15 K, c° = 1 M) to all 25 (ΔG, Kd) pairs in app.js:146-394 gives zero self-consistent pairs. The mean contradiction is 4.73 kcal/mol (range 3.85–5.73), equivalently 3.47 orders of magnitude in Kd (range 2.82–4.20). The two columns are related by ΔG_stated = 1.771 × ΔG_true + 4.682, R² = 0.994, max residual 0.22 kcal/mol — a clean affine rescaling with gain 1.77, i.e. one invented number and one arbitrary transform of it. The implied conversion factor of 1.0495 kcal/mol per ln unit corresponds to T = 528 K.

Three independent lines of evidence show no calculation was performed. (1) Byte-identical sequences carry different energies: KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears at app.js:153, app.js:247 and app.js:131 against AChE with ΔG = -16.2, -17.5 and -12.6 — a 4.9 kcal/mol spread for one molecule and one target, which is impossible for a state function. Six other sequences show the same pattern. (2) app.js:381 has `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` — a label, not a sequence — and app.js:384 still assigns it ΔG = -15.2 kcal/mol, Kd = 4.8 nM, pLDDT = 92.4. (3) Grepping all four files for every mainstream affinity tool (vina/smina/gnina/autodock/rosetta/openmm/gromacs/amber/mmpbsa/prodigy/boltz/diffdock/foldx/glide/alchemical) returns exactly one hit, README.md:108, and only because "Amber" is a UI colour name there. `git ls-files` confirms no structure files, no confidence JSON, no scripts.

The magnitudes are also implausible on their face. Six of 25 stated ΔG values exceed biotin–streptavidin (-18.28 kcal/mol at Kd = 4e-14 M), the canonical tightest non-covalent biological interaction, and the headline -19.5 kcal/mol (app.js:290, advertised at index.html:74-75) implies Kd = 5.1 fM for a 39-residue flexible peptide conjugate — roughly 8× tighter than biotin–streptavidin and ~3,900× tighter than the best experimentally-matured de novo mini-protein binders. This also contradicts the platform's own reversibility and tolerance claims at README.md:100-102.

On the two other assigned questions: AlphaFold3 emits coordinates plus pLDDT/PAE/pTM confidence and has no free-energy term whatsoever, so every ΔG attributed to it is a capability misrepresentation; and 'Cognitive Enhancement Index' is not a defined scientific metric — it appears nowhere in the literature, is never defined in the repo, is a hardcoded literal, and is nonetheless the actual sort key of the "TOP 10" leaderboard (r(CEI, rank) = -0.985 while ΔG is non-monotone with rank), plotted on the same y-axis as kcal/mol.

What is done well, and it is worth saying plainly. The structural-pharmacology annotation layer is largely real and non-trivial: the AChE CAS/PAS residue assignments, the Nrf2 ETGE motif encoded as DEETGE for a Keap1 Kelch decoy, the Keap1 Arg415/Arg483/Ser602 arginine triad, the GSK-3β Val135 hinge contact, and KLVFFAE as the Aβ16-22 aggregation core are all correct textbook structural pharmacology, and the decoy-peptide and bio-conjugate design concepts are legitimate and literature-grounded. The signalling cascades in index.html:205-259 are accurate. The engineering is clean, dependency-light vanilla JS with sensible separation of data and rendering, and the "copy FASTA → open AlphaFold Server" handoff (app.js:660-671, index.html:355-366) is a genuinely useful UX pattern — it is honest about being a handoff, unlike the "Live Connected" badge above it. The project's real problem is that a well-built presentation layer and a sound pharmacology narrative have been wrapped around a quantitative layer that was written rather than computed.

Minimum path to credibility: delete every hardcoded ΔG, Kd and CEI value; run one real AF3 prediction per candidate and plot the returned pLDDT and PAE instead of the sine wave at app.js:791 and the |i-j| ramp at app.js:850; add a single honest affinity tier (PRODIGY is the right first choice for this peptide/protein modality, r ≈ 0.73, RMSE ≈ 1.89 kcal/mol) and display its uncertainty next to every number; and add a unit test asserting |ΔG - RT ln Kd| < 0.01 kcal/mol. Until then the affinity data should be removed from the public surface rather than corrected in place, because in its current form it is indistinguishable from experimental results to any non-specialist reader.

reviews.discipline: Machine learning for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold-class models): model outputs, confidence calibration, de novo binder design evaluation, and inference infrastructure
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD in machine learning, 16 years post-PhD. Worked on protein structure prediction since AlphaFold1; trained and evaluated AlphaFold2/OpenFold reimplementations and AF3-class open models (Boltz, Chai, Protenix); regular reviewer for NeurIPS, ICML, and Nature Methods.
reviews.overall_assessment:
CognitionBioChem contains no AlphaFold3. It is a three-file static web page (README.md, index.html, app.js, styles.css) with no inference code, no model weights, no API client, no network request of any kind beyond four CDN asset loads and two ordinary `<a href>` hyperlinks to alphafoldserver.com, and no parsed AF3 artifact (no .cif, no confidences.json, no ranking_scores.csv). I verified this by enumerating every file in the repository and grepping for every AF3 output field name and every MSA/inference dependency; the result is zero matches. Every quantity the platform attributes to AlphaFold3 -- 35 pLDDT values, 25 dG values, 25 Kd values, 10 leaderboard rows, and every point of every pLDDT curve and PAE heatmap -- is either a string literal typed into an array or the output of a two-term trigonometric expression keyed on the ASCII codes of amino-acid letters. Those generators are trivially distinguishable from real AF3 output: the pLDDT generator is analytically confined to [89.0, 99.0], so across all 876 residues in the 25-drug set not one falls below 70, the "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" legend bands are mathematically unreachable, and the (GGGGS)x3 linkers that real AF3 would render at pLDDT 30-60 are rendered at 96-97. The PAE generator is exactly PAE(i,j) = 0.4|i-j| + f(i): the residual after removing the ramp takes only four discrete values {0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9}, so there are no domain blocks, no inter-chain block, and no contact structure at all. The 3D "backbone topology" is a fixed helix whose radius is set by ord(residue) % 5 and whose consecutive point spacing measures 0.63-16.63 units against a real, essentially invariant Ca(i)-Ca(i+1) distance of 3.80 +/- 0.04 A.

Beyond the fabrication, the science of the AF3 framing is wrong in a way an expert would catch immediately. pLDDT is a self-consistency estimate of local geometric confidence; it is not a measure of correctness and it is emphatically not a measure of binding. It is the single worst confidence metric to rank designed binders by, because idealized designed sequences are precisely the regime in which AF models are confidently wrong. The metrics that actually matter for a binder-design campaign -- ipTM, interface PAE, ranking_score, has_clash -- do not appear anywhere in the repository. Nor could they: every "AF3 job" here is a lone peptide string with no receptor chain and no ligand entity, so even a genuine AF3 run on these inputs could not produce a binding site, an interface metric, a dG, or a Kd. Two sequences contain the non-residue character 'B' and one is not a sequence at all ("His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"), yet the app happily generates a 37-residue "AlphaFold3 pLDDT profile" from its lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Finally, the availability story is legally as well as technically false: AF3 weights are request-only, non-commercial, and non-redistributable, and the AlphaFold Server terms specifically prohibit using the server or its outputs in an automated system that predicts binding of a protein with ligands or peptides -- which is exactly what this platform describes itself as.

Credit where it is due, and there is real credit. The front-end engineering is competent and idiomatic: clean tab routing, a proper Chart.js instance teardown before re-creation (app.js:779-781, a leak most people miss), a working resize handler, and a clean separation of data arrays from render functions. The information architecture -- 5 regions x 5 candidates, a leaderboard tab, a per-drug modal with 3D/pLDDT/PAE panels side by side -- is genuinely the right shape for a structure-prediction platform, and a real AF3 or Boltz-2 backend could be dropped behind these exact components. The domain vocabulary is largely drawn from real literature and used correctly at the level of naming: Huperzine A does engage AChE Trp84/Phe330 via cation-pi, Cys151 is the genuine Keap1 electrophile sensor, DEETGE is the real high-affinity Nrf2 Kelch-binding ETGE motif, KLVFF is the authentic Abeta16-20 self-recognition element, and GGGGS is a standard flexible linker. Whoever built this understands the field's language and can build a clean interface. What is missing is the entire computational substrate. My recommendation is not to patch the numbers but to either (a) wire in a permissively licensed AF3-class model that can legally be run locally and automated -- Boltz-2 (MIT), Chai-1 (Apache 2.0, code and weights), Protenix (Apache 2.0), or OpenFold3 (Apache 2.0) -- and surface the real ipTM/PAE/ranking_score it emits, or (b) relabel the entire artifact unambiguously as a UI mockup with synthetic placeholder data. The current state, in which fabricated numbers are labeled "AlphaFold3", "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING", and "Live Connected", is not a modeling error; it is a provenance failure, and it would be treated as such by any reviewer, collaborator, or investor who opened app.js.

findings.title: AlphaFold3 is entirely absent from the codebase; "Live AlphaFold Server Connected" is a plain hyperlink
findings.evidence_location: Whole repository (git ls-files: only README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css, skills-lock.json, .gitignore are project files); index.html:15-18 (only CDN loads: three.js r128, OrbitControls, chart.js); index.html:42 ("AlphaFold Server Live Connected" badge); index.html:363 ("Launch AlphaFold Server"); app.js:660-671 (copyModalFasta); README.md:24, README.md:111
findings.what_is_wrong: There is no AlphaFold3 inference, no model weights, no API client, and no parsed AF3 artifact anywhere in the repository. Grepping the entire project for `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `axios`, `api_key`, and `endpoint` returns zero matches in app.js; the only URLs in the project are four CDN asset loads (Google Fonts, FontAwesome, three.js, Chart.js) and two ordinary `<a href="https://alphafoldserver.com/">` links. Grepping for every AF3 output field name -- iptm, ptm, ranking_score, ranking_scores.csv, confidences.json, summary_confidences, has_clash, contact_probs, fraction_disordered, chain_pair_pae_min, atom_plddts -- and for every MSA dependency -- msa, a3m, jackhmmer, hmmer, uniref, mgnify, template -- returns zero matches across README.md, app.js, and index.html. There are no .cif, .pdb, .json, or .csv structure files on disk. The badge at index.html:42 that reads "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" is a static anchor tag; nothing is connected and nothing is live. The only "integration" is app.js:660-671, which copies a string to the clipboard for a human to paste manually into a browser.
findings.why_it_matters: The platform's single central claim -- README.md:22, "models 25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3" -- is false as a statement about this software. A reviewer, collaborator, funder, or acquirer who reads the README and the UI will believe structure prediction was performed; opening app.js reveals it was not. Every downstream artifact (the leaderboard, the 25 drug cards, the confidence plots) inherits this and is therefore unusable as evidence for anything. This is a provenance failure rather than an accuracy failure, which is worse: accuracy failures can be measured and corrected, provenance failures destroy trust in the entire artifact.
findings.ground_truth: A real AF3 run produces, per job, `<name>_model.cif`, `<name>_confidences.json`, `<name>_summary_confidences.json`, `<name>_data.json`, and a `ranking_scores.csv` across seeds/samples (google-deepmind/alphafold3, docs/output.md, retrieved this session). None of these files, and none of the fields they contain, exist in this repository. Running AF3 also requires the genetic-search stage (jackhmmer/nhmmer against UniRef90, MGnify, BFD/UniClust, and RNA databases) plus the model parameters; none of that machinery is referenced either.
findings.required_fix: Either (a) implement a real backend: add a server-side inference service that submits a properly specified job (protein chains + ligand entities) to a locally hosted AF3-class model, persists the returned model.cif / confidences.json / summary_confidences.json / ranking_scores.csv, and has the front-end read those files rather than hard-coded arrays; or (b) if no backend is intended, delete the "Live Connected" badge at index.html:42, delete the "Live AlphaFold Server Connection" bullet at README.md:111, and add a prominent banner to index.html and the top of README.md stating that the application is a user-interface prototype populated with synthetic placeholder data and that no structure prediction has been performed.

findings.title: All pLDDT and PAE values are closed-form fakes that are statistically distinguishable from real AlphaFold3 output
findings.evidence_location: app.js:791 (pLDDT generator), app.js:792-793 (dead clamps), app.js:802 (label "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score"), app.js:844 (gridSize truncation), app.js:850-851 (PAE generator and dead clamp); index.html:371, index.html:383, index.html:388-391 (legend), index.html:397; README.md:109-110
findings.what_is_wrong: The pLDDT curve is `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5)*0.5` (app.js:791). Over the 20 standard amino acids ord(aa)%5 spans 0..4, so the expression is analytically bounded to [93-4+0.0, 93+4+2.0] = [89.0, 99.0]. I reproduced the generator over all 25 drug sequences (876 residues): observed min 89.0, max 99.0, mean 94.11, and 0.0% of residues below 70. Consequences: (i) the clamps at app.js:792-793 are unreachable dead code; (ii) the legend at index.html:390-391 advertises "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" bands that can never be produced; (iii) there is no terminal droop -- the mean value at residue 1 is 95.50, *higher* than the global mean of 94.11, whereas real AF3 termini drop sharply; (iv) flexible linkers are invisible. HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 (app.js:183) has a GGGGS linker at index 9 and the generator returns [90.5, 89.7, 89.5, 90.0, 92.0] there; CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10 (app.js:125) has a 15-residue (GGGGS)x3 linker at indices 49-63 and the generator returns ~96-97. Real AF3 puts a Gly-Ser linker at pLDDT 30-60. The PAE matrix is `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (sequence.charCodeAt(i % len) % 4)*0.3` (app.js:850). Subtracting the 0.4|i-j| ramp leaves a residual that takes exactly four discrete values {0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9} and depends only on the row index i -- the matrix is exactly PAE = 0.4|i-j| + f(i). There are no domain blocks, no inter-chain block, and no contact structure. For a 45-residue chain the analytic maximum is 44*0.4+0.9 = 18.50 A, so the 30 A clamp at app.js:851 is dead code and the "0 - 30 Å" range advertised at index.html:397 and README.md:110 is never reached. Separately, app.js:844 caps the grid at `Math.min(len, 45)`, silently dropping residues 46-47 of HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (47 aa) with no indication in the UI. Finally, the two fabrications disagree with each other: the modal prints "AF3 pLDDT = 97.0 / 100" for HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 (app.js:166) while the chart rendered in the same popup has mean 94.31 (delta -2.69); deltas across the 25 drugs range from -2.69 to +1.69 in both directions.
findings.why_it_matters: These plots carry the labels "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" (app.js:802), "AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs" (index.html:371), and "Predicted Aligned Error 2D domain contact heatmap (0 - 30 Å)" (README.md:110). Any structural biologist reading them will interpret them as model output and will conclude the designs are uniformly high-confidence, well-ordered, single-domain constructs. All three conclusions are artifacts of the formula. The most damaging consequence is the inverted signal at the linkers: the (GGGGS)x3 spacers are the one part of these constructs where a real prediction would flag low confidence and a bright inter-domain PAE block, i.e. the exact information a designer needs to decide whether a bispecific construct will hold its two warheads in a defined relative orientation. The fake reports the opposite. The internal disagreement between the chart mean and the printed pLDDT string is a self-contained proof of fabrication that requires no external ground truth to establish.
findings.ground_truth: Real AF3 pLDDT is a per-atom predicted lDDT on a 0-100 scale, written to `atom_plddts` in confidences.json (google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/output.md). Empirically it has a characteristic signature: sharp droop over the first and last few residues, dips to 40-70 in loops and flexible linkers, near-90+ plateaus in secondary-structure elements, and values below 50 in genuinely disordered segments -- AF3 additionally reports `fraction_disordered` for exactly this reason. Real PAE (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) is a token x token estimate of the error in relative position and orientation between two tokens; for multi-domain or multi-chain systems it is visibly block-structured, with low intra-unit blocks (typically <5 A) and high off-diagonal cross-unit blocks (10-30 A) separated by sharp edges. It does not increase linearly with sequence separation, and its asymmetry reflects the choice of alignment frame, not a per-row constant.
findings.required_fix: Delete renderModalPlddtChart (app.js:775-832) and renderModalPaeHeatmap (app.js:834-866) as data sources. Replace them with parsers that read `atom_plddts` and `pae` out of a real `<job>_confidences.json` produced by an actual inference run, aggregate atom pLDDT to per-residue for display, and render the PAE at full token resolution with no 45-token cap. Until a real backend exists, either remove these two panels entirely or relabel them "Illustrative placeholder -- not model output" and remove the words "AlphaFold3" and "Real" from app.js:802, index.html:371, index.html:383, index.html:397, and README.md:109-110.

findings.title: pLDDT is misused as a binder-quality and affinity metric; the interface metrics that actually govern binder design (ipTM, interface PAE, ranking_score) are absent
findings.evidence_location: app.js:124-135 (AF3_CANDIDATES: plddt co-reported with dg and cei), app.js:146 and 25 further `affinity:` strings of the form "ΔG = ... | Kd = ... | AF3 pLDDT = ... / 100", app.js:903 ("pLDDT: ... (AF3 Confidence: Very High)"), index.html:296 ("AlphaFold3 Leaderboard Ranking"), index.html:303-306 (table columns Rank / AF3 pLDDT / ΔG / CEI); confirmed absent: grep for iptm|ptm|ranking_score|has_clash|chain_pair across README.md, app.js, index.html returns zero matches
findings.what_is_wrong: Three distinct errors are compounded. (1) pLDDT is presented as a design-quality score. It is not. pLDDT is the model's prediction of its own lDDT -- a self-consistency estimate of *local* geometric confidence. It measures neither correctness nor binding. A high pLDDT means the model would reproduce its own local environment under superposition; it says nothing about whether the peptide binds the named receptor, or binds anything. (2) pLDDT is packed into the same string as a dG in kcal/mol and a Kd in nM (app.js:146 and 24 others), implying they are commensurate outputs of one calculation. AF3 emits no free energy and no dissociation constant, and no combination of its outputs can be converted into one. The dG/Kd pairs are also internally inconsistent with each other: applying dG = RT ln(Kd) at 298.15 K (RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol), dG = -18.4 implies Kd = 0.033 pM, but the table states 0.32 nM -- a factor of ~9,800. Across all 25 drugs the stated Kd values are on average 10^3.47 too high, and a regression of log10(Kd) on dG gives r = 0.9969 with an implied RT of 1.056 kcal/mol, i.e. an implied temperature of 531 K. The numbers were produced by a wrong constant, not by a thermodynamic calculation. (3) The ranking is not what it claims. The tab is titled "AlphaFold3 Leaderboard Ranking" (index.html:296) but Spearman(rank, pLDDT) = -0.612 while Spearman(rank, CEI) = -0.988. The leaderboard is actually sorted by "CEI", a "Cognitive Enhancement Index" that appears only as a chart label (app.js:1063) and a column header (index.html:306) and is defined nowhere in the repository. Meanwhile ipTM, pTM, ranking_score, has_clash, and chain_pair_pae_min -- the metrics AF3 actually provides for judging an interface -- appear zero times.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the error that would most mislead a domain expert, because it is stated in fluent, correct-sounding vocabulary. A reader is invited to believe that pLDDT 96.2 means "this binder is better" and that pLDDT and dG are two views of one prediction. Neither is true, and acting on that belief is how binder-design campaigns fail: designed sequences are precisely the regime where AF confidence is least trustworthy, because idealized de novo sequences fold cleanly and confidently in the model whether or not they engage the target. Filtering or ranking designs on monomer pLDDT selects for designability, not for binding, and will pass through a set of well-folded non-binders at essentially the base rate. The field settled this question a decade into the deep-learning era and the answer is well documented.
findings.ground_truth: AF3's actual confidence outputs (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w; google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/output.md) are: per-atom pLDDT (0-100, `atom_plddts`) = local geometric confidence, does NOT measure global topology, inter-chain placement, or binding; PAE (token x token, in Å, `pae`) = expected error in the relative position/orientation of two tokens, the correct metric for domain and chain placement; pTM (0-1) = predicted TM-score of the whole complex, >0.5 means the overall fold may be right; ipTM (0-1) = predicted accuracy of the *relative placement of subunits*, the interface metric, with >0.8 confident, <0.6 a likely failure and 0.6-0.8 a gray zone; ranking_score (range [-100, 1.5]) = AF3's own model-selection score; plus has_clash, fraction_disordered, chain_pair_iptm, and chain_pair_pae_min. None of these is a binding free energy or a Kd. For designed binders specifically, Bennett et al. (Nat Commun 14:2625, 2023, PMID 37149653, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-38328-5) established that filtering with AlphaFold2's interface predicted-aligned-error (pAE_interaction) -- not monomer pLDDT -- raises experimental binder success rates roughly ten-fold. Karelina, Noh & Dror (eLife 12:RP89386, 2023) showed independently that high-confidence AlphaFold models do not translate into accurate ligand poses, reinforcing that model confidence and binding accuracy are separate axes.
findings.required_fix: Remove pLDDT from any ranking or quality role. Rank candidates on ipTM and interface PAE computed from a real prediction of the *complex* (binder chain + receptor chain), with ranking_score as the tiebreak, and display has_clash as a hard filter. Split the `affinity:` strings so that model confidence and thermodynamic quantities are never presented in the same field, and remove all dG and Kd values unless they are produced by an actual free-energy method (FEP/TI, MM-GBSA with a stated protocol, or an affinity-predicting model such as Boltz-2, which emits log10(IC50 in µM) rather than a kcal/mol dG) with the method, force field, and error bars cited. Either define CEI explicitly with its formula and inputs, or delete the column and the chart series; and rename index.html:296 to reflect whatever metric actually determines the sort order.

findings.title: The "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY" viewer renders a physically impossible helix whose geometry is set by ASCII codes, and its "pLDDT color spectrum" is keyed on residue letter, not confidence
findings.evidence_location: app.js:707 (comment), app.js:711-729 (geometry loop), app.js:715 (radius), app.js:717 (angle), app.js:723-727 (C/P scaling), app.js:742-755 (residue spheres), app.js:747-749 (color assignment), app.js:757-761 (fixed "pocket" sphere), app.js:973-991 and app.js:1012-1021 (same construction in the main viewer); index.html:377, README.md:108
findings.what_is_wrong: The comment at app.js:707 claims "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION" and index.html:377 labels the panel "Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)". The code does neither. Geometry: helix radius = `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` (app.js:715), i.e. 6.0-9.2 units, multiplied by 1.3 for Cys and Pro (app.js:723-727) up to 12.0; rise = 0.6 per residue; and the total turn count is `(i/seqLength) * PI * (charCode%3===0 ? 6 : 4)` (app.js:717), which fixes the number of turns at 2 or 3 regardless of chain length, so the pitch scales with length -- the inverse of how a real helix behaves. I measured the resulting virtual bond lengths: for HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (36 aa) consecutive point spacing runs 1.21 to 15.77 (mean 6.41); for HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 (28 aa) it runs 0.63 to 16.63 (mean 7.90). A real trans-peptide Ca(i)-Ca(i+1) distance is 3.80 +/- 0.04 A and is essentially invariant; a 15.8 A virtual bond is over four peptide bonds' worth of separation and a 0.63 A one is a steric impossibility. A real alpha-helix has radius 2.3 A, rise 1.5 A per residue, and 3.6 residues per turn -- none of which this reproduces. The determining variable throughout is `charCode % 5`, the ASCII code of the letter modulo 5, a quantity with no chemical meaning whatsoever (it makes Ala and Phe identical and Cys and Trp identical). Coloring: app.js:747-749 assigns cyan by default, green if the residue is G or S, and amber if it is P or D. The comments on those very lines read "// Very High (>90)", "// High", "// Low" -- so residue identity is being presented to the user as a confidence band. The code never reads any pLDDT value, and it directly contradicts the chart generated in the same modal at app.js:791, which places 92.4% of those same residues above 90 and would therefore color them all cyan. Binding site: app.js:757-761 (and app.js:1012-1021) place a fixed-radius wireframe sphere at the origin, identical for all 25 drugs and all 10 candidates, unrelated to any of the `bindingSites` residue strings.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the panel a viewer will trust most, because 3D structure reads as ground truth in a way a line chart does not, and it sits directly under a heading containing the words "Real" and "AlphaFold3". A user will believe they are looking at a predicted fold of the named construct, colored by predicted confidence, with a marked binding pocket. They are looking at none of those things: they are looking at the same helix 25 times, tinted by which letters happen to appear in the string, with a decorative sphere at the origin. Because the coloring is keyed on letter identity, Gly/Ser-rich linkers -- which really are low-confidence -- are colored "High" green while Pro and Asp anywhere in the chain, including in well-ordered turns, are colored "Low" amber. The visual is not merely uninformative; it points the reader's attention at the wrong residues.
findings.ground_truth: A real structure viewer parses coordinates, not letters. Backbone geometry is determined by the predicted Cartesian coordinates in the model .cif: Ca-Ca 3.80 +/- 0.04 A for trans peptides (~2.9 A for the rare cis-Pro), alpha-helix radius 2.3 A with 1.5 A rise and 3.6 residues/turn, beta-strand rise 3.3-3.4 A per residue. pLDDT coloring uses the per-atom `atom_plddts` array from confidences.json against the standard AlphaFold bands (>90 very high / 70-90 confident / 50-70 low / <50 very low). Binding-site annotation comes from the predicted complex -- residues within a distance cutoff of the partner chain or ligand -- not from a fixed sphere at the coordinate origin.
findings.required_fix: Delete the synthetic geometry in initModal3DCanvas (app.js:711-761) and update3DProteinStructure (app.js:973-1021). Replace with a real coordinate parser that loads the `<job>_model.cif` produced by an inference run and renders actual atom positions; use an established viewer (NGL, Mol*, or 3Dmol.js) rather than hand-rolling a Catmull-Rom tube. Color by `atom_plddts` against the four standard AlphaFold bands. Derive the binding-site highlight from residues in contact with the partner chain in the predicted complex. Until then, remove the word "REAL" from app.js:707, remove "Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)" from index.html:377 and the equivalent claim at README.md:108, and label the panel a decorative placeholder.

findings.title: The claimed AlphaFold3 jobs are under-specified: no receptor chain and no ligand entity, so no reported quantity is obtainable even from a genuine AF3 run
findings.evidence_location: app.js:138-398 (all 25 entries carry only a peptide `sequence` field), app.js:142 ("Ginsenoside Rg1 Dammarane-12,20-diol (C42H72O14) + C-20 Linker"), app.js:144 ("TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333)"), app.js:125-134 (AF3_CANDIDATES: `fasta` field only); README.md:45; index.html:290-291 ("FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)")
findings.what_is_wrong: Every one of the 25 therapeutics and 10 leaderboard candidates is described as a bio-conjugate of a natural-product warhead fused to a targeting peptide -- app.js:142 is explicit: "Ginsenoside Rg1 Dammarane-12,20-diol (C42H72O14) + C-20 Linker". But the only thing carried in the data structure and the only thing fed to the viewer, the pLDDT chart, and the PAE heatmap (app.js:648-652) is the bare peptide string. The small molecule is never expressed as a SMILES string or a CCD code, and there is no ligand entity of any kind. Equally important, the *target receptor* is never included either: `bindingSites` names TrkB D5 residues Asp298/Glu319/Tyr342/Val312/Leu333 (app.js:144) as free text, but no TrkB sequence, no UniProt accession, and no receptor chain appears anywhere. The claimed AF3 job is therefore a single unbound peptide in vacuum. Such a job cannot produce a binding site, an interface, an ipTM, an inter-chain PAE block, a dG, or a Kd -- these quantities are undefined for a monomer. This is not a matter of the numbers being wrong; the numbers are not computable from the stated input. It is also a straight inversion of AF3's actual contribution: joint prediction of protein-ligand and protein-protein complexes is the entire reason AF3 exists over AF2, and this platform uses none of it.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader who accepts the framing will believe that AF3 was asked "does this conjugate bind TrkB D5, and how well?" and answered. The question was never posed. Any decision made downstream -- which of the 25 to synthesize, which region to prioritize, whether the bispecific designs hold their two warheads in a defined geometry -- rests on an input specification that could not have addressed it. For the bispecific candidates in particular (X5, P5, B5, M5, A5, and CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10) the entire design question is the relative orientation of two binding modules across a linker, which is an inter-domain PAE / ipTM question about a complex. A monomer job is structurally incapable of answering it.
findings.ground_truth: An AF3 input JSON specifies a list of `sequences` entities: `proteinChain` (with sequence and copy count), `ligand` (by CCD code or SMILES), `dna`/`rna`, plus optional bonded-atom pairs for covalent conjugates, ions, and post-translational modifications (google-deepmind/alphafold3, input/output docs, retrieved this session). To evaluate a peptide-conjugate binder against TrkB you must supply at minimum: the TrkB D5 domain chain (UniProt Q16620, the Ig-like C2-type 2 domain), the designed peptide chain, and the natural-product warhead as a ligand entity with an explicit covalent linkage to the peptide. Only then does AF3 report `iptm`, `chain_pair_iptm`, `chain_pair_pae_min`, and a cross-chain PAE block -- the quantities that actually speak to binding. Absolute binding free energy is not an AF3 output at all and requires a separate method (alchemical FEP/TI, MM-GB/PBSA with a stated protocol, or an affinity model such as Boltz-2).
findings.required_fix: Redefine each candidate as a complete AF3 job specification rather than a bare string: a `target` field carrying the receptor UniProt accession and the exact domain sequence used, a `binder` field for the designed peptide, and a `ligand` field carrying the warhead as SMILES or CCD plus the covalent bond specification to the conjugation residue. Run prediction on the complex. Report ipTM, chain_pair_pae_min, has_clash, and the interface PAE block, and drop dG/Kd unless separately computed by a named free-energy method with stated error bars.

findings.title: Two sequences contain the non-residue character 'B' and one field is not a sequence at all, yet all three are fed to the pLDDT, PAE, and 3D generators without validation
findings.evidence_location: app.js:173 (HippoWnt-FzdAgonist-X4), app.js:371 (AstroZo1-Protect-A3), app.js:130 (CogWnt-Fzd-09 `fasta`) -- all containing 'B' at index 18 of "CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWG**B**LCPFRRACPDCH"; app.js:381 (AstroPafr-Block-A4, `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"`); consumed unvalidated at app.js:648-652, app.js:708-728, app.js:787-794, app.js:844-850
findings.what_is_wrong: I scanned all 25 modal sequences and all 10 leaderboard FASTA strings against the 20 standard one-letter codes. Three entries fail. 'B' appears at index 18 in app.js:173, app.js:371, and app.js:130; B is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx (Asn or Asp), not a residue, and is not an acceptable character in an AF3 `proteinChain` sequence. More seriously, app.js:381 sets `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` -- a prose description, not a sequence. The application does not validate any of these. It passes the prose string straight into initModal3DCanvas, renderModalPlddtChart, and renderModalPaeHeatmap, which treat it as a 37-residue chain and generate a complete "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" curve, a PAE heatmap, and a 3D backbone from the ASCII codes of its lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. The UI labels the result identically to the other 24. The modal for A4 additionally prints "AF3 pLDDT = 92.4 / 100" (app.js:384) for this non-sequence. There is no input validation anywhere in the codebase and no error path.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest available proof that no prediction ever ran: a real pipeline would have failed loudly on 'B' at the parser and could not have accepted "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate" at all. It also means the "Copy FASTA Sequence" button (app.js:660-671) hands users strings that will be rejected by AlphaFold Server, by any AF3-class local model, and by most FASTA tooling -- so the one manual workflow the app does support is broken for three of its entries. And because A4's fake curve is indistinguishable from the other 24, a user has no way to tell that one card is describing nothing at all.
findings.ground_truth: AF3's `proteinChain.sequence` accepts the 20 standard amino-acid one-letter codes; non-standard residues are expressed through the separate `modifications` field with CCD codes (e.g. MSE, SEP), not by ambiguity letters. B (Asx), Z (Glx), and J (Leu/Ile) are alignment-format ambiguity codes and are not valid model input. X (UNK) is handled specially and is not a substitute for specifying the actual residue.
findings.required_fix: Add a validation function that rejects any sequence containing characters outside ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY before it reaches the render path, and surface a visible error in the modal instead of drawing plots. Resolve the 'B' at index 18 of the FZD8/ZO-1 sequence to the intended D or N in app.js:130, app.js:173, and app.js:371. Replace app.js:381 with an actual peptide sequence for AstroPafr-Block-A4, or mark the card explicitly as having no peptide component and suppress its three structural panels.

findings.title: AlphaFold3 availability is misrepresented, the described workflow is prohibited by the AlphaFold Server terms, and DeepMind affiliation is implied
findings.evidence_location: README.md:3 (badge "AlphaFold3 - DeepMind_Server"), README.md:22-24, README.md:111 ("Live AlphaFold Server Connection"); index.html:30 ("DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform"), index.html:42, index.html:410 ("Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling"); repository directory name /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio
findings.what_is_wrong: The project presents AlphaFold3 as a freely available service it is plugged into, and presents itself as associated with DeepMind. Neither is accurate. On availability: the AF3 source at github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3 is Apache 2.0, but the code is inert without model parameters, and the parameters are governed by a separate AlphaFold 3 Model Parameters Terms of Use under which access is granted only to non-commercial organizations on request directly from Google, weights "must not" be published or shared outside the receiving organization, and use "in connection with any commercial activities, including research on behalf of commercial organizations" is forbidden. On the server route: AlphaFold Server is non-commercial-only, is subject to a daily job quota (launched at 10 requests/day, later raised to 20), exposes no API, supports only a restricted CCD-based ligand set rather than arbitrary SMILES, and its Prohibited Use Policy states that users must not use AlphaFold Server or its outputs "in connection with any automated system that predicts the binding or interaction of the protein with ligands or peptides, including, but not limited to, Glide or AutoDock." A platform whose stated purpose (README.md:22) is automated de novo bio-conjugate binder design against named receptors is squarely inside that prohibition. On affiliation: the shields.io badge at README.md:3 reads "AlphaFold3 | DeepMind_Server" with a Google logo, the page subtitle at index.html:30 reads "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform", the footer at index.html:410 reads "Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling", and the repository lives in a directory named DeepMind_Bio. Nothing in the project is from, endorsed by, or connected to Google DeepMind.
findings.why_it_matters: Three separate exposures. Scientifically, a reader is led to believe local automated AF3 inference at scale is a routine thing this project does, which sets a false expectation about how reproducible the work is -- nobody can rerun it, and not only because there is no code. Legally, if any commercial use is contemplated, the described workflow is not merely unimplemented but not permitted by the route named, and the Google-branded badge plus "DeepMind" in the product subtitle and the repo path constitutes an implied endorsement that is not authorized. Practically, it obscures the fact that a fully permissive path exists and is what a real build should use.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold 3: code Apache 2.0 (github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/LICENSE); model parameters under the separate AlphaFold 3 Model Parameters Terms of Use -- request-only, non-commercial organizations only, no redistribution outside the receiving organization, outputs may be published but may not be used to train competing structure-prediction models. AlphaFold Server: non-commercial only, daily quota (10 raised to 20 jobs/day), no API, restricted ligand set, and an explicit prohibition on use in automated protein-ligand/peptide binding-prediction systems. Permissively licensed AF3-class models that DO allow local automated and commercial inference: Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 (MIT, code and weights; Boltz-2 additionally predicts binding affinity as log10(IC50 in µM)); Chai-1 (Apache 2.0, code and weights, explicitly usable for drug discovery); Protenix (Apache 2.0, free for academic and commercial use); OpenFold3 (Apache 2.0, a reproduction of AF3 from the AlQuraishi Lab / OpenFold consortium, academic and commercial use).
findings.required_fix: Remove the DeepMind/Google-branded badge at README.md:3, remove "DeepMind" from the subtitle at index.html:30, remove the "Generated with AlphaFold3" footer at index.html:410, and rename the project directory away from DeepMind_Bio. Replace the claimed AF3 dependency with one of the permissively licensed models above -- Boltz-2 or Chai-1 are the closest fit here, since both can be run locally in an automated pipeline and Boltz-2 additionally emits an affinity estimate to replace the fabricated dG/Kd column -- and state the chosen model, its version, and its license in the README. If AF3 itself is genuinely wanted, add an explicit statement that weights must be requested from Google under non-commercial terms and that the AlphaFold Server route may not be used for automated binding prediction.

findings.title: Modal WebGL contexts and animation loops leak on every drug-card open, multiplying render calls and rotation speed
findings.evidence_location: app.js:674-773 (initModal3DCanvas), app.js:678 (`container.innerHTML = ''`), app.js:688-691 (new WebGLRenderer per open), app.js:763-772 (animateModal3D), app.js:655-658 (closeDrugModal)
findings.what_is_wrong: Each time a drug card is opened, initModal3DCanvas creates a fresh THREE.WebGLRenderer (app.js:688) and starts a new animateModal3D requestAnimationFrame loop (app.js:772). The previous renderer's canvas is discarded by `container.innerHTML = ''` (app.js:678) but `.dispose()` is never called, so its WebGL context is never released; likewise the previous geometries, materials, and textures are never disposed. Worse, the guard at app.js:764 is `if (!modalThreeRenderer) return;` against a module-scope variable that has just been *reassigned* to the new renderer -- so the stale loop does not exit. It sees the new renderer as truthy, applies `modalThreeMeshGroup.rotation.y += 0.006` to the *new* group, and calls render on the *new* scene. After k modal opens, k loops are alive, the model spins at k*0.006 rad/frame, and the scene is rendered k times per frame. closeDrugModal (app.js:655-658) only toggles a CSS class and cancels nothing.
findings.why_it_matters: Browsers cap live WebGL contexts (typically ~16 in Chrome); past that the oldest are force-lost and the viewer goes blank or throws. Since the platform's headline interaction is browsing 25 drug cards, a user doing exactly what the UI invites will hit the cap partway through and see the 3D panel fail, with visibly accelerating rotation beforehand. This is a real defect independent of the scientific issues, and it would persist verbatim after a correct viewer is wired in -- so it is worth fixing as part of that work rather than after.
findings.ground_truth: Standard Three.js lifecycle management: retain the handle returned by requestAnimationFrame and cancelAnimationFrame it on teardown; call renderer.dispose() and renderer.forceContextLoss(); traverse the scene calling geometry.dispose() and material.dispose(); or, preferably, create one renderer once and reuse it across modal opens, swapping only the scene contents.
findings.required_fix: Store the rAF id from app.js:765 in a module-scope variable and cancelAnimationFrame it at the top of both initModal3DCanvas and closeDrugModal. Before clearing the container at app.js:678, traverse modalThreeScene disposing geometries and materials, then call modalThreeRenderer.dispose() and forceContextLoss(). Better: construct the renderer once on first open and reuse it, replacing only modalThreeMeshGroup on subsequent opens.

literature.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
literature.what_it_provides: The primary AlphaFold3 paper. Defines the model's confidence outputs and their semantics: pLDDT (per-atom predicted lDDT, 0-100, local geometric confidence), PAE (token x token estimate of error in the relative position and orientation of two tokens, in Angstroms), pTM (0-1, predicted TM-score of the whole complex; >0.5 suggests the overall fold may be correct), and ipTM (0-1, accuracy of the relative placement of subunits; >0.8 confident, <0.6 likely failed, 0.6-0.8 a gray zone). Establishes that AF3 jointly predicts protein-ligand, protein-nucleic-acid, and protein-protein complexes -- the capability this platform names but never uses.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the ground truth against which every metric claim in the repository should be rewritten. Use it to justify replacing the pLDDT-based ranking (index.html:296-306, app.js:124-135) with ipTM plus interface PAE, and to justify deleting the dG/Kd fields (app.js:146 and 24 others) since AF3 outputs neither. The ipTM thresholds (>0.8 / 0.6-0.8 / <0.6) give the platform a defensible confidence banding to replace the fabricated one.

literature.title: AlphaFold 3 output specification (docs/output.md) and Model Parameters Terms of Use (WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md)
literature.what_it_provides: The exact output contract: per job, `<name>_model.cif`, `<name>_confidences.json` (containing `pae`, `atom_plddts`, `contact_probs`, `token_chain_ids`, `atom_chain_ids`), `<name>_summary_confidences.json` (containing `ptm`, `iptm`, `ranking_score` in [-100, 1.5], `fraction_disordered`, `has_clash`, `chain_pair_pae_min`, `chain_pair_iptm`, `chain_ptm`, `chain_iptm`), `<name>_data.json`, and `ranking_scores.csv`. Confirms pLDDT in AF3 is per-atom, not per-residue. The LICENSE is Apache 2.0 for code; the weights are governed by separate terms restricting access to non-commercial organizations on request from Google, forbidding redistribution outside the receiving organization and any commercial use.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Provides the exact absence proof for finding AIML-01 (none of these filenames or field names appear in the repository) and the file schema a real backend must parse for AIML-02 and AIML-04. The weights terms are the legal basis for AIML-07 and for recommending a permissively licensed alternative instead.

literature.title: Improving de novo protein binder design with deep learning
literature.what_it_provides: Bennett, Coventry, Goreshnik, Huang, Allen, Vafeados, Peng, Dauparas, Baek, Stewart, DiMaio, De Munck, Savvides, Baker. Establishes the standard evaluation protocol for de novo binder design: filtering candidates with AlphaFold2's interface predicted-aligned-error (pAE_interaction) rather than monomer confidence raises experimental success rates roughly ten-fold, and ProteinMPNN sequence design substantially improves efficiency over Rosetta. Documents realistic experimental hit rates for designed binders (single-digit percent even with good in silico filters).
literature.how_to_apply_here: Directly supports AIML-03: this is the field-standard evidence that interface PAE, not pLDDT, is the operative filter for designed binders. Also calibrates expectations -- the platform implies 25 of 25 designs succeed with sub-nanomolar Kd, whereas the literature baseline for AF-filtered de novo binders is a few percent hit rate. Any honest rewrite should adopt interface-PAE/ipTM filtering and report a candidate pool rather than 25 guaranteed successes.

literature.title: How accurately can one predict drug binding modes using AlphaFold models?
literature.what_it_provides: A rigorous assessment on GPCRs showing that ligand poses docked into AlphaFold2 models are not significantly more accurate than poses from traditional template-based homology models, and are much less accurate than poses docked into experimental structures -- even though the AF2 binding pockets themselves are near-experimental in accuracy. Demonstrates that high model confidence does not translate into accurate ligand placement.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supports AIML-03 and AIML-05: model confidence and binding accuracy are orthogonal axes. Cite this to justify removing any claim that a confident structure prediction implies a validated binding mode or a computable affinity for the natural-product warheads described at app.js:142 and throughout FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA.

literature.title: Boltz-1: Democratizing Biomolecular Interaction Modeling; and Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction
literature.id: 10.1101/2024.11.19.624167 (Boltz-1, Wohlwend, Corso, Passaro et al.) and 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707 (Boltz-2, Passaro, Corso, Wohlwend et al.); https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz
literature.what_it_provides: Open AF3-class biomolecular structure prediction under the MIT license for both code and weights, explicitly free for academic and commercial use. Boltz-2 additionally predicts binding affinity, reporting `affinity_pred_value` as log10(IC50) with IC50 in µM plus `affinity_probability_binary` in [0,1] for binder/non-binder discrimination.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The single best replacement for the fictional AF3 backend. Boltz-2 can be run locally and automated without licensing conflict (unlike AF3 weights or AlphaFold Server), it emits the real confidence fields needed to fix AIML-02 and AIML-03, and its affinity head gives a legitimate, citable quantity to put in place of the fabricated dG/Kd column -- reported in its native log10(IC50 µM) units, not converted into a spurious kcal/mol free energy.

literature.title: Chai-1: Decoding the molecular interactions of life
literature.what_it_provides: An AF3-class multimodal structure prediction model released under Apache 2.0 for both code and model weights, explicitly permitted for academic and commercial use including drug discovery. Supports protein, ligand, nucleic acid, and covalent-modification entities in a single job.
literature.how_to_apply_here: A second viable local backend, and the one to prefer if a permissive license covering weights as well as code is a hard requirement. Its job specification is the template for fixing AIML-05: supply the receptor chain, the designed peptide chain, and the natural-product warhead as an explicit ligand entity with a covalent bond, rather than a bare peptide string.

literature.title: Protenix (ByteDance) and OpenFold3 (AlQuraishi Lab / OpenFold consortium)
literature.what_it_provides: Two further open AF3 reproductions, both Apache 2.0 and free for academic and commercial use. Protenix reports outperforming AlphaFold3 across benchmark sets at matched training-data cutoff, model scale, and inference budget. OpenFold3 aims at a bitwise reproduction of AlphaFold3 and ships full training data and a trainable framework, making it the option to choose if fine-tuning on a proprietary binder set is ever wanted.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Completes the set of legally usable backends for AIML-07 and demonstrates concretely that the licensing obstacle the project implicitly works around does not require working around -- a fully open, commercially usable AF3-class model can be installed and run locally today. OpenFold3's trainability is the relevant option if the project later wants a model tuned on CNS peptide binders.

reviews.discipline: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD-level research integrity specialist and journal editor (20 years) handling data-fabrication allegations under COPE/ICMJE procedure; doctorate in biomedical science with working expertise in structural biology, ligand thermodynamics, and in-silico model credibility assessment (ASME V&V 40 / FDA CM&S framework).

findings.title: Values generated by hardcoded display formulas are labelled as AlphaFold3 model output; identical sequences are assigned different pLDDT, which is mathematically impossible for real predictions
findings.evidence_location: app.js:791 (`let score = 93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5;`); app.js:802 (`label: 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score',`); app.js:850 (`let error = Math.abs(i - j) * 0.4 + (sequence ? (sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length) % 4) * 0.3 : 1);`); app.js:707 (`// REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION`); app.js:673, 715, 731-732; index.html:371, 377, 383, 397; README.md:108-110; app.js:125-135 and app.js:146,156,166,176,186 (hardcoded `AF3 pLDDT = ...` strings)
findings.what_is_wrong: Three separate quantities that the UI and README present as AlphaFold3 output are deterministic display formulas with no model behind them. (a) The residue confidence curve plotted under the legend 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' is 93 + 4*sin(0.4i) + 0.5*(ASCII%5); its analytic range is [89.0, 99.0], so it can never enter the 'High (70-90)', 'Low (50-70)' or 'Very Low (<50)' bins that index.html:389-391 advertises. (b) The 'Predicted Aligned Error' matrix is |i-j|*0.4 + 0.3*(ASCII%4) — symmetric by construction and a monotone function of sequence separation, which real PAE matrices are not. (c) The '3D Structure' is a parametric helix of radius 6.0-9.2 with 0.6 rise per index; I measured its consecutive 'Cα' spacings at min 1.21, max 15.77, mean 6.41 arbitrary units (real Cα-Cα is 3.80 ± 0.04 Å, invariant) — a 1208% bond-length variation, i.e. not a protein backbone. Grep confirms zero `fetch`/XHR/WebSocket calls and zero data files anywhere in the tracked repository (`git ls-files` returns only README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css, skills-lock.json and the .agents/ skill bundle), so no AlphaFold3 run could have supplied any of it. Independent proof by identity: the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears three times and is assigned pLDDT 92.8 (AF3_CANDIDATES CogAChE-PAS-02, app.js:131), 94.8 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, app.js:156) and 94.3 (BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, app.js:250). pLDDT is a function of the input; the same monomer sequence cannot yield three different values beyond seed noise of well under 1 unit. I found four such duplicate pairs inside the 25-drug set and seven sequence identities between the 25 drugs and the AF3 top-10 table, every one of them carrying conflicting numbers.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the platform's central claim. A collaborator, reviewer, or investor reading 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' over a chart, or the code comment 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING', will reasonably conclude that AlphaFold3 was run and that the confidence profile reflects model uncertainty. It does not. A design prototype with placeholder data is entirely legitimate; this repository crosses the line because the placeholders are affirmatively labelled with the provenance they lack. Under ICMJE 'B. Scientific Misconduct', data fabrication is 'making up data or results'; presenting formula output under a model's name meets that description if the artefact is ever presented as a research result. Anyone who tried to reproduce these numbers by actually submitting the sequences to AlphaFold Server would get different values and would have grounds to allege fabrication.
