findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold 3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) has a confidence head that 'predict[s] a modified local distance difference test (pLDDT) and a predicted aligned error (PAE) matrix as in AF2, as well as a distance error matrix (PDE)', plus pTM/ipTM. These are learned per-token outputs of a diffusion model conditioned on an MSA and template stack; they are not analytic functions of residue index or ASCII code, they are not smooth sinusoids, and PAE is not symmetric. AF3 confidence values are effectively deterministic for a fixed sequence and seed. Real Cα-Cα virtual bond length is 3.80 Å (trans peptide), and an α-helix has a Cα radius of ~2.3 Å with 1.5 Å rise per residue and 3.6 residues/turn — none of which the generator reproduces.
findings.required_fix: Either (a) actually run the sequences (AlphaFold Server or a local AF3/Boltz/Chai deployment), commit the resulting mmCIF plus the per-residue pLDDT and PAE arrays as data files, and render those arrays; or (b) keep the synthetic curves but rename every label so no reader can mistake them: legend `'Illustrative confidence profile (synthetic — not an AlphaFold prediction)'`, panel headings 'Illustrative sequence-parameterised ribbon (not a predicted structure)' and 'Illustrative contact-separation map (not a PAE matrix)', delete the comments at app.js:673, 707 and the word 'Real' at index.html:108, 371, 375, 377 and README.md:108. Additionally, deduplicate the sequences or give identical sequences identical predicted values — the current contradictions are self-falsifying regardless of labelling.

findings.title: All 25 ΔG/Kd pairs are thermodynamically impossible; the pair was co-generated by a rule implying RT = 1.05 kcal/mol (T = 528 K) with a non-zero intercept, and AlphaFold3 emits no energetic quantity at all
findings.what_is_wrong: Every one of the 25 candidates reports a ΔG and a Kd side by side. At 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol and ΔG = RT·ln(Kd). Checking all 25: the stated ΔG is more negative than the stated Kd permits by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol, i.e. the stated Kd is 665x to 15,729x larger than the stated ΔG implies. Examples: HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 'ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol | Kd = 0.32 nM' — 0.32 nM corresponds to -12.95 kcal/mol, and -18.4 kcal/mol corresponds to 3.3e-14 M (0.033 pM), a 9,828-fold discrepancy. BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 'ΔG = -19.5 | Kd = 0.08 nM' is off by 15,729x. Regressing ΔG on ln(Kd) across all 25 gives ΔG = 4.682 + 1.0495·ln(Kd) with R² = 0.9939. The near-perfect fit proves the two columns were produced together by a single rule rather than measured or computed independently; the slope 1.0495 implies an 'effective RT' of 1.05 kcal/mol, i.e. T = 528 K (255 °C), and the +4.68 intercept means no temperature whatsoever reconciles them. Separately, the ΔG values themselves are outside the physical envelope: -19.5 kcal/mol implies Kd = 5 fM, tighter than the biotin-streptavidin complex (~10 fM, ΔG ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol), the tightest well-characterised non-covalent protein-ligand interaction known. All 25 candidates are claimed to sit at or beyond that limit. Finally, AF3 does not produce ΔG or Kd under any configuration, so the README's framing of these as products of an AlphaFold3 pipeline has no possible mechanism.
findings.why_it_matters: This is an independent, arithmetic falsification that does not depend on reading the rendering code at all: a reviewer with a calculator can demonstrate in one minute that the affinity table cannot be the output of any method. It converts a 'the labels are overclaimed' concern into a demonstrable internal contradiction. Ranking candidates (the 'Leaderboard', index.html:296) on numbers that are mutually inconsistent means the entire prioritisation is arbitrary — a downstream user selecting X5 over X3 for synthesis would be acting on noise. The 'Peak Binding Energy -19.5 kcal' headline stat (index.html:74-75) is the single most prominent number on the landing page.
findings.ground_truth: ΔG° = -RT·ln(Ka) = RT·ln(Kd) with R = 1.9872e-3 kcal·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹. At 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol; at 310 K (body temperature), RT = 0.6160 kcal/mol. 1 nM ⇒ ΔG = -12.28 kcal/mol at 298 K. Neither temperature nor any plausible standard-state convention produces the reported pairs. AlphaFold 3 (Abramson et al., Nature 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) outputs coordinates plus pLDDT, PAE, PDE, pTM and ipTM — no energetics. Binding free energy requires a separate method (FEP/TI, MM-GBSA/PBSA, or an empirical scoring function), each with its own error bars; even well-executed alchemical FEP typically carries ~1 kcal/mol RMSE, so a claimed value must always be accompanied by a method, a force field, a sampling protocol, and an uncertainty.
findings.required_fix: Delete the Kd column or derive it: `kd = Math.exp(dG / (R*T))` with T stated on the page. Report only one of the two as primary and mark the other 'derived'. If any ΔG is meant to be real, name the method, software version, force field, and per-value uncertainty (e.g. 'MM-GBSA, AMBER ff19SB/GAFF2, 100 ns, ΔG = -8.2 ± 1.9 kcal/mol, rescoring only — not a binding constant'). Cap claimed affinities at physically defensible values and state explicitly that scoring-function ΔG is not a measured Kd. Add a unit test that fails the build if |ΔG - RT·ln(Kd)| > 0.5 kcal/mol for any record.

findings.title: Absolute safety claims ('0% Risk', 'Peripheral Side Effects: None', 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%') are asserted for molecules intended for human cognition, with no ADMET model in the repository and a mechanism that is directionally wrong for these sequences
findings.evidence_location: README.md:98 (`All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening:`); README.md:99 (`**hERG Cardiotoxicity Risk**: **IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)**. Hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore **Tyr652/Phe656** residues.`); README.md:100-102; the 25 `safety:` strings at app.js:147, 157, 167, 177, 187, 199, 209, 219, 229, 239, 251, 261, 271, 281, 291, 303, 313, 323, 333, 343, 355, 365, 375, 385, 395 — including 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' (app.js:251), 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (app.js:323), 'Off-target Binding: None' (app.js:209), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (app.js:281), 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291); index.html:639 renders these under the heading '6. ADMET Safety Profile & Side Effects'
findings.what_is_wrong: Three distinct defects. (1) Provenance: README.md:98 asserts that screening was performed. There is no ADMET predictor, no hERG model, no immunogenicity tool, no descriptor calculation and no result file anywhere in the repository — the safety fields are literal strings in the same array as the drug names. (2) Expressibility: '0% Risk', 'None', '0.0%' and '100%' are not outputs any predictive method can produce. Every in-silico classifier returns a probability with a decision threshold and a validated applicability domain; a zero is a statement of certainty that no model licenses. (3) Direction: the stated mechanism — that hydrophobic linkers sterically prevent hERG binding — inverts the actual structure-activity relationship. I computed the physicochemistry of the sequences: HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 / BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 (KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG) carry a net charge of +9 at pH 7.4 with 13 Lys/Arg and 31% aromatic (W/F/Y) content; MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 is +7 with 28% aromatics. Cationic, aromatic-rich, amphipathic sequences are the canonical hERG-blocker pharmacophore and the canonical membrane-lytic/haemolytic peptide motif — the opposite of a safety argument. No haemolysis, no cytotoxicity, and no immunogenicity (MHC-II binding / ADA risk) assessment appears anywhere, despite 24 of 25 candidates being peptides.
findings.why_it_matters: These are nootropic candidates aimed at healthy human cognition, where the safety bar is higher than for oncology, not lower. A '0% cardiotoxicity' claim carried in a README with a DeepMind badge is precisely the kind of statement a non-specialist reader — an angel investor, a supplement formulator, a collaborator, a journalist — would take at face value. If this repository were shown as a pitch, it constitutes a specific, quantified, unsubstantiated safety representation about substances for human consumption. It is also the claim most likely to attract regulatory attention if the project ever moves toward an IND, an NDI notification, or a wellness product, and the most damaging if the underlying formula-generated provenance is later discovered.
findings.ground_truth: Tyr652 and Phe656 in the hERG (KCNH2) S6 inner cavity are correctly identified as the principal drug-binding residues (Mitcheson et al., 'A structural basis for drug-induced long QT syndrome', PNAS 2000, doi:10.1073/pnas.210244497, PMID 11005845) — but that paper establishes that binding is driven by aromatic/hydrophobic contact with those residues, typically for cationic amphiphiles. Hydrophobicity and a basic centre increase hERG liability; they do not shield against it. Regulatory hERG assessment is governed by ICH S7B/E14 and requires in-vitro patch clamp, not a computed descriptor. No validated in-silico ADMET model reports a zero-probability outcome; the FDA CM&S credibility framework (see literature) requires that any computational output used as evidence be accompanied by a stated context of use, model risk, and verification/validation evidence commensurate with that risk.
findings.required_fix: Delete every absolute safety statement. If a screen is genuinely wanted, run named tools and record their identity and version (e.g. ADMET-AI, pkCSM, SwissADME, ProtParam plus an MHC-II binding predictor such as NetMHCIIpan for the peptides) and report each result as a probability with the tool's own stated accuracy and applicability domain: `hERG blockade: P = 0.31 (ADMET-AI v1.x, classifier AUC 0.84 on ChEMBL hold-out; peptides are outside the model's small-molecule applicability domain — result not interpretable)`. Explicitly flag that essentially all published hERG and ADMET models are trained on small molecules and are out-of-domain for 30-45mer cationic peptides, so the correct honest output here is 'not assessable with available in-silico models'. Add the missing peptide-specific liabilities (haemolysis, membrane lysis, immunogenicity, protease stability, BBB penetration) as explicit open risks rather than omitting them.

findings.title: In-vivo efficacy and chronic-dosing outcomes (LTP +280%, ACh +350%, CBF +45%, working memory +240%, tolerance <4.2% at 30 days) are presented as platform results, though no computational method can produce them
findings.evidence_location: README.md:60 ('Neurogenesis & CA1 LTP (+280%)'); README.md:64 ('Dendritic spine density (+310%)'); README.md:67 ('Working memory span restoration (+240%)'); README.md:71 ('Information processing speed 2x'); README.md:74 ('Synaptic ACh +350%'); README.md:84 ('Aβ lysosomal degradation (+420%)'); README.md:88 ('Cerebral Blood Flow (CBF) +45%'); README.md:100 ('capped Emax (135%)'); README.md:102 ('**Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days**'); mirrored in app.js:148, 188, 200, 240, 252, 334, 356 and app.js:1063 ('Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI / 100)')
findings.what_is_wrong: The README frames the entire document as the output of an 'AlphaFold3 De Novo Drug Discovery Platform' and then reports two-and-three-significant-figure effect sizes for endpoints that are measured, not predicted: field-EPSP slope potentiation (LTP), Golgi/two-photon spine counting, microdialysis ACh, laser-Doppler or ASL-MRI cerebral blood flow, delayed-response behavioural testing, and lysosomal degradation kinetics. 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' is a chronic in-vivo pharmacodynamic endpoint requiring 30 days of repeat dosing in an animal model. No structure predictor, docking program, or ADMET tool outputs any of these. There is no methods section, no animal model, no assay, no n, no error bar, no statistical test, and no citation anywhere in the repository. The precision of the figures ('+280%', '<4.2%') is the signature of invented numbers: a real +280% LTP measurement would be reported as, e.g., '278 ± 34% of baseline, n = 8 slices, p = 0.003'.
findings.why_it_matters: These are the numbers that make the project look like it has results rather than a hypothesis. They are the sentences a reader will quote back — 'their lead candidate gives +310% spine density'. A journal would treat unsourced quantitative efficacy claims with no methods as a fabrication concern under ICMJE 'B. Scientific Misconduct'; an institution's research integrity office would open an inquiry on the 30-day tolerance figure alone, because it implies an animal study that did not occur. The same claims in a fundraising or partnering context are material misrepresentations.
findings.ground_truth: None of AlphaFold 3's outputs (coordinates, pLDDT, PAE, PDE, pTM, ipTM — Abramson et al., Nature 2024) bear on physiological efficacy. Effect sizes at these endpoints come from ex-vivo electrophysiology, in-vivo microdialysis, imaging, and behaviour. Reporting standards for any predictive-model claim in biomedicine require the model, data, evaluation split and metric to be specified (DOME recommendations, Walsh et al., Nat Methods 18:1122-1127, 2021, doi:10.1038/s41592-021-01205-4); reporting standards for any prediction intended to inform clinical decisions require the full TRIPOD+AI item set (Collins et al., BMJ 385:e078378, 2024, doi:10.1136/bmj-2023-078378). The current text satisfies neither because there is no model to report.
findings.required_fix: Move every efficacy percentage out of the results voice and into an explicitly hypothetical voice, with the experiment that would test it named. E.g. replace 'Neurogenesis & CA1 LTP (+280%)' with 'Design hypothesis: TrkB D5 engagement should enhance CA1 LTP. Untested. Proposed assay: field-EPSP slope in acute hippocampal slices, theta-burst induction, n ≥ 8, vs vehicle.' Add a 'Claim status' column to every candidate with values HYPOTHESIS / IN-SILICO / IN-VITRO / IN-VIVO, and set all 25 to HYPOTHESIS today. Delete 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' outright — there is no in-silico substitute for it.

findings.title: 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' and 'Generated with AlphaFold3' assert a computational integration and a provenance that do not exist in the code
findings.evidence_location: index.html:42 (` AlphaFold Server Live Connected`); index.html:69-70 ('AF3 Engine' / 'Live AlphaFold Integration' stat card); index.html:54 ('Modeling 25 De Novo therapeutics via **AlphaFold3 sequence-driven 3D structural topology parsing and live AlphaFold Server integration**'); index.html:410 (`Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling & Structural Pharmacology Algorithms.`); README.md:24 ('direct live integration with the official **AlphaFold Server**'); README.md:111 ('**Live AlphaFold Server Connection**'). Absence verified: `grep -rniE "fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|axios|WebSocket" README.md app.js index.html styles.css` returns nothing (exit 1)
findings.what_is_wrong: The header badge reads 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' and the dashboard advertises an 'AF3 Engine' with 'Live AlphaFold Integration'. The implementation is a plain `<a href>` hyperlink to alphafoldserver.com plus a clipboard copy (app.js:660-671). There is no HTTP client, no API key, no request, no response handling, no polling — I confirmed zero network primitives in the entire codebase. A 'Live Connected' status badge is a specific technical assertion about system state, and it is false. The footer goes further: 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling' attributes the page's contents to AlphaFold3, which per INTEG-01 never ran.
findings.why_it_matters: A status badge is the one UI element users trust as machine-verified rather than authored. Presenting a static hyperlink as a live connection misrepresents the system's capability to anyone evaluating the platform's technical maturity — which is exactly the audience a demo is built for. Combined with the footer provenance line, a viewer reasonably concludes that the pLDDT curves and ΔG values on screen came off an AlphaFold3 run. This is the mechanism by which an internal prototype becomes an external misrepresentation without anyone intending it.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold Server has no public programmatic API for third-party submission; the documented workflow is manual upload through the web UI. A truthful description of what this code does is: 'copies the sequence to your clipboard and opens AlphaFold Server in a new tab, where you can paste it and run the prediction yourself.' That workflow is genuinely useful and is the honest version of the claim.
findings.required_fix: Change index.html:42 to 'Open AlphaFold Server ↗' (no 'Live', no 'Connected'). Change the stat card at index.html:69-70 to 'Manual hand-off' / 'Copy FASTA → AlphaFold Server'. Change index.html:54 and README.md:24, 111 to 'one-click FASTA hand-off to AlphaFold Server (you run the prediction; results are not imported back into this page)'. Delete index.html:410 entirely, or replace with 'UI prototype. No AlphaFold3 prediction has been run; all displayed values are illustrative placeholders.'

findings.title: Google DeepMind branding, an AlphaFold3 shield badge with the Google logo, and the repository name imply an affiliation and endorsement that do not exist, while AlphaFold Server's terms restrict use

README.md:3 (`[![AlphaFold3](https://img.shields.io/badge/AlphaFold3-DeepMind_Server-00f2fe?style=for-the-badge&logo=google)](https://alphafoldserver.com/)`); index.html:30 (`

`); index.html:6 (`NeuroCognition BioChem - Advanced AlphaFold3 & Natural Products Platform`); index.html:410; README.md:4 ('License: Private Research'); repository working directory path `/Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio`; README.md:135 ('© 2026 Seung H. Jung - CognitionBioChem Intelligence')
findings.what_is_wrong: The README's first badge renders as a for-the-badge shield reading 'AlphaFold3 | DeepMind Server' carrying the Google logo, and the application header subtitle reads 'DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform' — a construction that parses as 'this is a DeepMind platform', not 'this platform uses AlphaFold'. The project directory is literally named DeepMind_Bio. Nowhere in README.md, index.html or app.js is there any disclaimer of affiliation (grep for 'disclaim|not affiliated' returns nothing across all four files). Separately, the README declares a 'Private Research' licence but does not state a use restriction inherited from the tool it advertises: AlphaFold Server output is licensed for non-commercial use only, and holders must not use it on behalf of a commercial organisation or in automated systems predicting protein-ligand interactions. A platform that describes itself as a 'drug discovery platform' generating ranked therapeutic candidates is squarely in the territory those terms restrict — a point the repository never engages with.
findings.why_it_matters: If this repository is made public, shown to an investor, or attached to a grant or partnering deck, the Google/DeepMind visual identity plus the absence of a disclaimer creates a false impression of institutional backing for the '0% Risk' safety claims and the candidate rankings. That is the compounding harm: the borrowed credibility attaches specifically to the numbers that are least supportable. It also exposes the author to a trademark/attribution complaint that is entirely avoidable, and — if the project ever commercialises — to a terms-of-use conflict on any AlphaFold Server output actually incorporated.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold is a Google DeepMind trademark. AlphaFold Server Output Terms of Use state the output is available free of charge for non-commercial use only, that only individuals and non-commercial organisations may use it, that users must not use the Server, Output or Derivatives on behalf of a commercial organisation or in connection with commercial activities including research on behalf of commercial organisations, and that Google reserves the right to require deletion of Output. The separate AlphaFold 3 model-parameter terms and prohibited-use policy impose further constraints on self-hosted use. Standard practice for third-party tools built on a vendor model is an explicit non-affiliation notice plus a citation of the model paper.
findings.required_fix: Replace the badge at README.md:3 with a neutral one (`![Uses AlphaFold Server](https://img.shields.io/badge/uses-AlphaFold_Server-blue)`, no Google logo, no 'DeepMind' in the label). Change index.html:30 to 'Structural Pharmacology & De Novo Design Prototype'. Rename the directory away from DeepMind_Bio. Add verbatim to README.md immediately under the title: 'This project is an independent effort and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or connected to Google DeepMind or Google LLC. AlphaFold is a trademark of Google DeepMind. No AlphaFold Server output is contained in this repository. If AlphaFold Server output is added in future, it will be used only under the AlphaFold Server Output Terms of Use, which permit non-commercial use only.' Add a proper citation of Abramson et al., Nature 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w.

findings.title: The candidate dataset is internally contradictory and partly not chemistry: identical sequences carry conflicting targets and numbers, three sequences contain the non-standard residue 'B', and one 'FASTA sequence' is an English phrase that the pLDDT chart happily plots
findings.evidence_location: app.js:173 and app.js:371 (identical `CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH` assigned to FZD8 CRD and to ZO-1/Occludin respectively); app.js:195 and app.js:319 (identical 41-mer assigned to α7 nAChR ECD and to TLR4/MD-2); app.js:205 and app.js:361 (identical 37-mer assigned to TrkB D5 and to EAAT2/GLT-1); app.js:153 and app.js:247 (identical 36-mer, AChE, different ΔG/Kd/pLDDT); app.js:130 (`CogWnt-Fzd-09` fasta also contains 'B'); app.js:381 (`sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"`); app.js:582 (`drug.bindingSites.substring(0, 52)` truncates every card's residue list mid-token); app.js:844 (`const gridSize = Math.min(sequence ? sequence.length : 30, 45);`)
findings.what_is_wrong: Four defects in the underlying data model. (1) Four sequence pairs are byte-identical yet are asserted to bind entirely unrelated proteins with different residue contacts, and are given different ΔG, Kd and pLDDT — e.g. CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH is simultaneously a 'Frizzled-8 CRD activator' (Phe72/Tyr125/Asp99/Arg104, ΔG -16.9, Kd 1.2 nM, pLDDT 95.1) and a 'ZO-1 tight junction protector' (Arg220/Asp310, ΔG -16.1, Kd 2.8 nM, pLDDT 93.8). One sequence cannot have two different pLDDTs and cannot plausibly be a selective binder of two unrelated folds. (2) That sequence contains 'B' at position 19. B is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx (Asn or Asp); it is not a residue, cannot be synthesised, and is rejected by AlphaFold Server input validation — so the advertised 'Copy FASTA → Launch AlphaFold Server' workflow (index.html:362-363) fails outright for three of the entries. (3) AstroPafr-Block-A4's 'sequence' field is the string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. It is rendered under the modal heading '2. Sequence Structure (FASTA Peptide / Bio-Conjugate Sequence)' (index.html:619) and then fed to the confidence chart, which plots 37 points labelled H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8 … and reports a mean 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT' of 94.08 for the ASCII codes of an English phrase. (4) The PAE canvas is 540x220 px for a square N×N matrix (2.45x aspect distortion) and grid size is silently capped at 45, so the 99-residue lead candidate is truncated without notice.
findings.why_it_matters: Defect (3) is the single most efficient demonstration that no model is behind the charts, and it is visible to any user who clicks the A4 card — this is how the project gets discovered rather than disclosed. Defect (1) means the 25-candidate 'pipeline' is not 25 distinct designs; the duplication with divergent annotations is the pattern integrity officers look for when assessing whether a dataset was assembled or invented. Defect (2) breaks the one genuinely honest feature the platform has. Collectively these make the dataset unusable as a design record even for the author's own purposes.
findings.ground_truth: FASTA sequences for structure prediction must use the 20 standard one-letter codes (optionally U/O for selenocysteine/pyrrolysine); B (Asx), Z (Glx), J (Xle) and X are ambiguity codes and are rejected or coerced by prediction pipelines. A PAE matrix is square N×N by definition and must be rendered with 1:1 aspect. A design record should carry one row per distinct construct, with a stable identifier, and distinct constructs should not share a sequence.
findings.required_fix: Add a validation function that runs on load and refuses to render any record whose `sequence` is not `/^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$/`; surface the failure in the UI rather than silently plotting it. Replace 'B' with the intended residue (N or D) and re-derive anything downstream. Give A4 a real sequence or mark it explicitly 'small-molecule conjugate — no peptide component; structural prediction not applicable' and suppress the 3D/pLDDT/PAE panels for it. Deduplicate: either merge the four duplicate pairs into single records with multiple annotated indications, or design genuinely distinct sequences. Make the PAE canvas square and remove the silent gridSize cap (or label 'showing residues 1-45 of N').

findings.title: Reference natural-product SMILES are wrong or unparseable, showing the curated reference layer was not retrieved from any chemical database
findings.evidence_location: app.js:10 (Huperzine A), app.js:20 (Ginsenoside Rg1), app.js:30 (Ginkgolide B), app.js:50 (Curcumin), app.js:60 (`smiles: "C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)"`), app.js:70 (`smiles: "C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)"`); rendered at app.js:477 under the label `SMILES Formulation:`; README.md:32-39
findings.what_is_wrong: I parsed all eight SMILES strings and compared heavy-atom counts against PubChem records I retrieved this session. Curcumin (app.js:50) ends in 'OCH3', which is not valid SMILES — a bare H is illegal in the organic subset, so no cheminformatics toolkit will parse the string at all. Huperzine A (app.js:10) encodes 14 carbons against the true C15H18N2O (PubChem CID 854026). Ginsenoside Rg1 (app.js:20) encodes 38 carbons against C42H72O14 (CID 441923). Ginkgolide B (app.js:30) encodes C18O8 against C20H24O10 (CID 11973122). Two of the eight fields (app.js:60, 70) contain a molecular formula plus a prose annotation rather than a SMILES at all, yet are displayed to the user under the heading 'SMILES Formulation'. Only Baicalein and Asiatic Acid match on atom count (and Baicalein's hydroxyl regiochemistry differs from PubChem CID 5281605, which places OH at 5,6,7 — worth a separate chemistry check). No stereochemistry is specified anywhere, despite six of the eight being stereochemically defined natural products where configuration determines target engagement.
findings.why_it_matters: The natural-product matrix is the part of the platform that could have been fully correct at zero cost, because all eight compounds have authoritative public records. That it is not correct tells a reviewer the reference data was written from memory rather than retrieved — which retroactively lowers confidence in every other unsourced number on the page, including the ones that cannot be checked against a database. Anyone who copies these SMILES into a docking run or a similarity search gets the wrong molecule and does not find out.
findings.ground_truth: Retrieved from PubChem this session: Huperzine A CID 854026, C15H18N2O, MW 242.32, `C/C=C/1\[C@@H]2CC3=C([C@]1(CC(=C2)C)N)C=CC(=O)N3`. Curcumin CID 969516, C21H20O6, MW 368.4, `COC1=C(C=CC(=C1)/C=C/C(=O)CC(=O)/C=C/C2=CC(=C(C=C2)O)OC)O`. Ginkgolide B CID 11973122, C20H24O10, MW 424.4. Ginsenoside Rg1 CID 441923, C42H72O14, MW 801.0. Baicalein CID 5281605, C15H10O5. Asiatic acid CID 119034, C30H48O5. Salvianolic acid B is C36H30O16 (the formula in app.js:70 is correct — it is simply not a SMILES).
findings.required_fix: Replace all eight SMILES with the isomeric SMILES retrieved from PubChem, and store the CID alongside each so the value is traceable: `{ smiles: "...", smiles_source: "PubChem", cid: 969516, retrieved: "2026-08-16" }`. Render the CID as a link next to the structure. Add a build-time validation step (RDKit `MolFromSmiles` non-null and formula match against the recorded CID) so an unparseable or mismatched SMILES fails CI. For Onjisaponin V and Salvianolic acid B, either supply the real SMILES or rename the field 'Molecular formula' so the label matches the content.

findings.title: 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI)' is plotted as a computational benchmark and used to rank candidates, but is defined nowhere
findings.evidence_location: app.js:1063 (`label: 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI / 100)',`); app.js:125-134 (hardcoded `cei:` values 82.5-98.4); app.js:886 (rendered as a leaderboard column); index.html:306 (`<th>CEI Score</th>`); index.html:316 ('TOP 10 Candidate Computational Benchmark (CEI vs Binding Affinity)'). Grep for 'cei|cognitive enhancement index' across all four files returns only these render/data sites — no formula, no units, no derivation, no citation
findings.what_is_wrong: A metric named 'Cognitive Enhancement Index', scored out of 100, is displayed as a leaderboard column and charted under the heading 'Computational Benchmark'. It has no definition in the repository: no inputs, no formula, no normalisation, no validation set, and no reference. The values also track the rank order almost perfectly (98.4 down to 82.5 for ranks 1-10), which suggests the score was written to match a pre-decided ranking rather than the ranking being derived from the score.
findings.why_it_matters: Calling something a 'benchmark' asserts that a defined, reproducible quantity was measured. An undefined composite score presented in a ranked table is unfalsifiable — a reader cannot check it, disagree with its weighting, or reproduce it, but will still use it to prioritise. It is a small item next to the pLDDT and ΔG problems, but it is the same failure mode and is trivially fixable.
findings.ground_truth: A composite index used for ranking must state its constituent variables, their weights, their normalisation, and the rationale for the weighting; if it is model-derived, DOME (Walsh et al., Nat Methods 2021) requires the data, optimisation and evaluation to be reported. If it is a judgement-based scorecard, that is legitimate — it simply has to be labelled as expert judgement rather than as a computational benchmark.
findings.required_fix: Either (a) define it explicitly on the page — e.g. 'CEI = 0.4·norm(|ΔG|) + 0.3·norm(pLDDT) + 0.3·(target-class weight); an author-assigned heuristic, not a validated metric' — with the code that computes it from the other fields rather than a hardcoded literal, or (b) rename the column 'Author priority (subjective)' and change the chart heading from 'Computational Benchmark' to 'Author prioritisation vs ΔG'.

literature.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
literature.what_it_provides: The definitive specification of what AlphaFold 3 does and does not output. I retrieved the abstract and searched the Europe PMC full text: the confidence head 'predict[s] a modified local distance difference test (pLDDT) and a predicted aligned error (PAE) matrix as in AF2, as well as a distance error matrix (PDE)', plus pTM/ipTM ranking scores. There is no energetic output of any kind — no ΔG, no Kd, no IC50, no ADMET.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the ground truth that settles INTEG-01 and INTEG-02. Cite it in the README and state plainly which of its outputs the project uses. It also fixes the pLDDT colour bins the UI advertises: the paper's own convention is pLDDT ≤50 / 50-70 / 70-90 / 90-100, so if the synthetic curve can never leave [89, 99] (app.js:791), the four-bin legend at index.html:388-391 must go or the data must change.

literature.title: DOME: recommendations for supervised machine learning validation in biology
literature.id: doi:10.1038/s41592-021-01205-4 (PMID 34316068, Nature Methods 18:1122-1127); see also the DOME Registry, doi:10.1093/gigascience/giae094 (PMID 39661723, 2024)
literature.what_it_provides: The community reporting standard for any ML-derived claim in biology, organised as Data, Optimization, Model, Evaluation. It exists precisely to make the question 'where did this number come from, and how would I check it?' answerable in a fixed format, and the 2024 Registry paper provides a machine-readable schema and public deposition route.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Adopt DOME as the disclosure skeleton for the platform. For every model-derived value the repository must be able to fill in the four sections; where it cannot (which is currently everywhere), the value is by definition not model-derived and must be labelled 'illustrative'. Depositing a DOME Registry entry once a real AF3 run exists would give the project an external, citable provenance record at near-zero cost.

literature.title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
literature.what_it_provides: The reporting standard governing any prediction intended to inform a clinical or health decision, including explicit items on data provenance, model specification, performance with uncertainty intervals, and — critically — a requirement to state the intended use and limitations rather than presenting point estimates bare.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The '0% Risk' hERG claim and the efficacy percentages (INTEG-03, INTEG-04) are health-decision-relevant predictions. TRIPOD+AI is the standard a reviewer would hold them to, and it makes the necessary remediation concrete: every predicted quantity needs an uncertainty interval and an applicability-domain statement, and 'zero risk' is not a reportable prediction under any item of the checklist.

literature.title: Assessing the Credibility of Computational Modeling and Simulation in Medical Device Submissions: Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff (built on ASME V&V 40-2018)
literature.id: FDA final guidance, issued 16 Nov 2023; Federal Register 17 Nov 2023, doc 2023-25470; docket FDA-2021-D-0980; fda.gov/media/154985/download
literature.what_it_provides: The regulatory framework for when computational output may be used as evidence: define the context of use, assess model risk (influence of the model on the decision × consequence of a wrong decision), then generate verification, validation and uncertainty-quantification evidence proportionate to that risk. It formalises the ASME V&V 40 credibility-factor approach.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the vocabulary that lets the project stay ambitious while becoming honest. Every value gets a stated context of use and a model-risk tier. Under this framework a value used only to lay out a UI is low-risk and needs almost no credibility evidence — but it must be *declared* as such. A value used to claim '0% cardiotoxicity' in a human-cognition candidate is high-risk and needs V&V evidence the project does not have, so the correct action is to withdraw the claim rather than caveat it. I confirmed the guidance via official FDA and Federal Register listings; direct full-text fetch was blocked by the hosts.

literature.title: ICMJE Recommendations for the Conduct, Reporting, Editing, and Publication of Scholarly Work in Medical Journals — section 'B. Scientific Misconduct, Expressions of Concern, and Retraction'
literature.id: icmje.org/recommendations — Publishing and Editorial Issues, section B (retrieved and read this session)
literature.what_it_provides: The operative definition an editor or integrity officer would apply: scientific misconduct includes 'data fabrication; data falsification including deceptive manipulation of images; purposeful failure to disclose relationships and activities; and plagiarism', with editor obligations to investigate, inform institutions and funders, and issue expressions of concern or retraction.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the standard that determines whether the current state is a legitimate prototype or an integrity problem, and the answer turns entirely on labelling. Formula-generated placeholders labelled as placeholders are not fabrication. The same values labelled 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' and 'All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening' would be assessed as fabricated data the moment the artefact is submitted, presented, or published. Fix the labels before the artefact leaves the author's machine and the exposure disappears entirely.

literature.title: COPE flowcharts: 'Fabricated data in a submitted manuscript' and 'Fabricated data in a published article'; COPE Core Practices
literature.what_it_provides: The step-by-step procedure journals actually follow on a fabrication allegation — request raw data and provenance from the author, involve the institution if the response is unsatisfactory, and escalate to expression of concern or retraction. Core Practices additionally require journals to have a data-integrity policy and post-publication correction mechanisms.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Read as a stress test: the first thing a journal would ask for is the raw AlphaFold3 output files behind the pLDDT and PAE figures. This repository cannot produce them, and `git ls-files` shows no data files exist. Building the provenance discipline recommended below means that request becomes trivially satisfiable. NOTE: I confirmed these pages exist on the official COPE domain via search (exact titles and canonical URLs returned), but publicationethics.org returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch, so I did not read the full text this session — hence verified:false.

literature.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
literature.what_it_provides: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable — in particular principle R1.2, that data must be associated with detailed provenance, and R1.1, that data carry a clear and accessible usage licence.
literature.how_to_apply_here: FAIR R1.2 is the direct justification for the mandatory per-value provenance field proposed in the remediation standard. It also covers the natural-product layer (INTEG-08): recording a PubChem CID and retrieval date next to every SMILES makes the reference data findable and reusable, and turns an unverifiable string into a traceable one.

literature.title: A structural basis for drug-induced long QT syndrome
literature.what_it_provides: The primary evidence identifying Tyr652 and Phe656 in the hERG S6 inner cavity as the residues that mediate high-affinity drug block, and establishing that aromatic/hydrophobic interaction with those residues is what confers hERG liability.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The README names the right residues but inverts their meaning (INTEG-03). This citation is the ground truth showing that hydrophobicity and aromatic content increase rather than prevent hERG binding — directly contradicting 'Hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656 residues' (README.md:99) for sequences I measured at net charge +9 with 31% W/F/Y content.

literature.title: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion
literature.what_it_provides: The current reference standard for what an honest de novo binder-design pipeline reports: a generative design stage, an in-silico filter with a stated metric and threshold, and — decisively — experimental success rates from the wet lab, including the failures.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the template for keeping the project's ambition while making it credible. Restructure the 25 candidates as 'designs generated, filtered by [named metric] at [threshold], N selected for synthesis, 0 tested to date' rather than as 25 validated therapeutics with affinities and safety profiles. Reporting a design funnel with an honest zero at the experimental stage reads as serious work; reporting 25 finished candidates with -19.5 kcal/mol affinities and 0% risk does not.

literature.title: Benchmarking AlphaFold-enabled molecular docking predictions for antibiotic discovery
literature.what_it_provides: Empirical demonstration that high-confidence AlphaFold structures do not translate into reliable ligand-binding predictions — docking against AF models gave poor agreement with experimental ligand-binding measurements, with no useful correlation between structural confidence and binding prediction accuracy.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Pre-empts the most likely defence of the current design, namely 'high pLDDT justifies the affinity numbers'. It does not: structural confidence and binding energetics are decoupled. Cite this in the README's limitations section to explain why pLDDT is reported separately from, and never used to license, any affinity claim.

reviews.overall_assessment:
## Verdict

CognitionBioChem is a genuinely well-built front end wrapped around a data layer that currently misrepresents its own origin. The distinction that matters is not ambition versus modesty — it is labelling. A design prototype whose numbers are placeholders is entirely legitimate and needs no apology. This repository sits on the wrong side of that line for one reason: the placeholders are affirmatively labelled with a provenance they do not have. The chart legend says `'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score'` (app.js:802) over `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode%5)*0.5` (app.js:791). The code comment says `REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING` (app.js:707) over a parametric helix whose consecutive Cα spacings I measured at 1.21–15.77 units against a real invariant of 3.80 Å. The README says `All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening` (README.md:98) when no screening tool exists in the repository. The header badge says `AlphaFold Server Live Connected` (index.html:42) when grep confirms zero network calls in the entire codebase.

Nothing here requires bad intent, and I do not infer any — this reads as a design mock-up whose captions were written aspirationally and never walked back. But the current artefact, if shown to a collaborator, journal, institution, or investor exactly as it stands, would be assessed under ICMJE section B as fabricated data, and the assessment would be correct. Two findings are independently fatal and both are checkable in minutes by a third party: identical sequences carrying different pLDDT values (mathematically impossible for a real prediction), and 25/25 ΔG–Kd pairs that fail ΔG = RT·ln(Kd) by 3.85–5.73 kcal/mol on a regression with R² = 0.994 and an implied temperature of 528 K.

**The good news is that the fix is small and does not cost the project anything it actually has.** No science needs to be retracted, because none was performed. The remediation is a labelling and data-model change, and the platform is *more* impressive afterwards, not less — a prototype that is rigorous about what it does not yet know is a stronger artefact than one that claims 0% cardiotoxicity.

## Credit where due

- **The architecture is right.** The five-layer model (natural product → pharmacophore → conjugate → brain region → signalling cascade) is a coherent and defensible way to organise a CNS design program. Someone thought about the biology.
- **The mechanistic prose is largely sound.** Keap1 Cys151 alkylation → Nrf2 nuclear translocation → ARE (app.js:54), GSK-3β Ser9 inhibitory phosphorylation → β-catenin stabilisation → Tau (app.js:44), TrkB Tyr515/816 → PI3K/Akt and Ras/ERK → CREB (app.js:24), Trem2/DAP12 in microglial phagocytosis (app.js:304): these are correct textbook pathways, correctly wired. hERG Tyr652/Phe656 is the right residue pair (the inference drawn from it is backwards, but the anatomy is right).
- **The FASTA hand-off is the one honest computational feature.** `copyModalFasta()` (app.js:660-671) plus the AlphaFold Server link is a real, useful, correctly-implemented workflow. It only needs to stop being described as a "live connection."
- **The code is clean.** Readable, consistently structured, no dead paths, sensible separation of data and render. The rendering engineering is not the problem.
- **The data model is one field away from being fully honest.** Every value already lives in a structured object. Adding a `provenance` key is a mechanical change.

## Claim ledger

Every assertion of a performed computation or measurement in README.md and index.html, marked **S**=supported, **U**=unsupported (no evidence either way), **C**=contradicted by the code.

**Contradicted by code (the reader is told something the code disproves):**
| Claim | Location | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" chart legend | app.js:802 | sine + ASCII formula, app.js:791 |
| "AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs" | index.html:371 | both synthetic; app.js:791, 850 |
| "Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)" | index.html:377 | parametric helix, non-physical Cα spacing; app.js:711-729 |
| "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION" | app.js:707 | reads charCodes to set a helix radius |
| "Real sequence-driven backbone topology parsing" | README.md:108 | same |
| "residue-specific pLDDT color spectrum (Very High >90 Cyan, High 70-90 Green, Low 50-70 Amber)" | README.md:108 | colour is set by residue *letter* (G/S→green, P/D→amber), not by any confidence value; app.js:747-749 |
| pLDDT legend bins "Low (50-70)", "Very Low (<50)" | index.html:390-391 | formula range is [89.0, 99.0]; unreachable |
| "2D PAE ... (0 - 30 Å)" | README.md:110, index.html:397 | max attainable is 14.9 Å for a 36-mer; symmetric by construction |
| "Live AlphaFold Server Connection" / "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" / "Live AlphaFold Integration" | README.md:111, index.html:42, 70 | zero network calls in repository |
| "Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling" | index.html:410 | AF3 never ran |
| "All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening" | README.md:98 | no ADMET code, no result files |
| 25× "AF3 pLDDT = NN.N / 100" | app.js:146…394 | same sequence given three different values |
| 25× "ΔG = … \| Kd = …" | app.js:146…394 | thermodynamically impossible, all 25 |
| "-19.5 kcal — Peak Binding Energy" hero stat | index.html:74-75 | implies Kd = 5 fM, tighter than biotin–streptavidin |
| "Interactive 3-column drug hub featuring real FASTA sequence 3D WebGL structural viewers" | index.html:108 | "real" is false; 3 sequences contain non-standard 'B', 1 is an English phrase |

**Unsupported (asserted with no evidence; not disproved by code, but no method could produce them):**
"hERG IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)" (README.md:99) · "Seizure Index = 0.01–0.02" (README.md:100) · "Low Immunogenicity" (README.md:101) · "Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days" (README.md:102) · "capped Emax (135%)" (README.md:100) · "LTP (+280%)" (README.md:60) · "Dendritic spine density (+310%)" (README.md:64) · "Working memory span restoration (+240%)" (README.md:67) · "Information processing speed 2x" (README.md:71) · "Synaptic ACh +350%" (README.md:74) · "Aβ lysosomal degradation (+420%)" (README.md:84) · "CBF +45%" (README.md:88) · all 25 `safety:` strings · "CEI Score" / "Computational Benchmark" (index.html:306, 316) · all per-drug `bindingSites` residue lists (no docking, no structure, no citation) · "state-of-the-art ... platform" (README.md:22).

**Supported:** the FASTA copy-to-clipboard and AlphaFold Server launch (app.js:660-671, index.html:362-363) — real and correctly implemented · "built using pure Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js WebGL, and Chart.js" (README.md:117) — accurate · the qualitative signalling-cascade descriptions (app.js:14, 24, 44, 54, 64, 74, 84; index.html:206-258) — consistent with published pathway biology, though uncited · "8 major natural compound classes" and their target assignments (README.md:32-39) — broadly correct as literature summary, though the SMILES encoding them is not (INTEG-08) · "5 brain regions", "25 candidates" — counted and correct.

**Score: 0 of 15 computational-provenance claims supported; 15 contradicted; ~16 further quantitative claims unsupported.**

## Risk surface if this repository goes public or is shown as described

- **To a journal or preprint server.** A reviewer who opens app.js finds line 791 within a minute. The manuscript is desk-rejected and the editor is obliged under ICMJE section B to consider notifying the author's institution. The fabricated-data determination would rest on the labels, not the numbers.
- **To an institution.** "Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days" (README.md:102) implies a 30-day repeat-dose animal study. An integrity officer reading that claim next to a repository containing no protocol, no IACUC reference, and no data would open an inquiry on that single line.
- **To an investor or partner.** Quantified affinity and safety representations ("0% Cardiotoxicity", "Kd = 0.08 nM", "Safety Index 99.1/100") presented under Google DeepMind visual identity are material representations. Their falsity is demonstrable from the repository itself. This is the highest-consequence exposure and the easiest to trigger, because a deck is exactly what this artefact is shaped like.
- **To Google DeepMind.** README.md:3 renders a `for-the-badge` shield reading "AlphaFold3 | DeepMind Server" with the Google logo; index.html:30 reads "DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform"; the directory is named `DeepMind_Bio`. No disclaimer of affiliation exists anywhere (grep-confirmed). AlphaFold Server output is licensed non-commercial-only and may not be used on behalf of commercial organisations — a "drug discovery platform" ranking therapeutic candidates engages those terms directly.
- **To a member of the public.** These are nootropics for healthy human cognition. "hERG IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)" is the exact sentence that gets screenshotted out of context. Four of the peptides are strongly cationic amphipathic sequences (net +9, 31% aromatic) — the canonical membrane-lytic and hERG-blocker profile — so the safety claim is not merely unsupported, it points the wrong way.
- **To the author.** This is real, thoughtful work. The single most valuable thing about the finding list is that fixing it costs a labelling pass and a data-model field, and there is no wet-lab result to retract. That window closes the moment the repository is shared.

## Remediation standard — full honesty with no loss of ambition

**1. Mandatory provenance field on every value.** No number renders without one. Replace flat strings with typed objects:

```js
{ value: -18.4, unit: "kcal/mol", quantity: "dG_bind",
  provenance: "illustrative",   // enum, required
  source: null, tool: null, tool_version: null,
  computed_at: null, input_hash: null, artifact: null,
  note: "Placeholder for UI layout. Not a prediction." }
```

Enum, exhaustive:
- `measured` — wet-lab. Requires assay, n, replicates, date, lab.
- `computed` — a specific tool run. Requires `tool`, `tool_version`, `input_hash`, `computed_at`, and `artifact` (a committed output file). No artifact, no `computed`.
- `literature` — published. Requires DOI or PMID and the value exactly as reported.
- `database` — public record. Requires database, accession (e.g. PubChem CID 969516), retrieval date.
- `derived` — arithmetic on other tracked values. Requires the formula and the parent value ids. (Kd derived from ΔG belongs here.)
- `illustrative` — invented for layout. Carries no scientific meaning. **Not a defect — the honest default.**

**2. Render-time enforcement.** One `renderValue(v)` function; it throws in dev and renders `—` in prod if `v.provenance` is absent. Each value gets a visible inline badge: `COMPUTED` (green, links to the artifact) · `LIT` (blue, links to DOI) · `DB` (grey, links to accession) · `DERIVED` (grey) · `MEASURED` (green) · `ILLUSTRATIVE` (amber, tooltip "Placeholder — not a prediction"). Amber must be visually loud, not a footnote.

**3. Provenance propagates into chart labels.** A dataset built from illustrative values inherits the label:
```js
label: 'Illustrative confidence profile — synthetic curve, NOT an AlphaFold prediction'
```
Never `'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score'` over synthetic data. Same for the 3D panel ("Illustrative sequence-parameterised ribbon — not a predicted structure") and the heatmap ("Illustrative contact-separation map — not a PAE matrix").

**4. Page-level banner while any illustrative value is on screen**, auto-counted, not hand-written:
> ⚠ **Illustrative data.** 143 of 147 values on this page are placeholders generated by display formulas in `app.js`. No AlphaFold 3 prediction, docking calculation, or ADMET screen has been run. Do not cite, quote, or act on these numbers.

**5. Exact README disclosure — place immediately under the title, above the badges:**
> ## ⚠ Status: design prototype — no AlphaFold 3 run has been performed
>
> CognitionBioChem is a user-interface and data-model prototype for a structural-pharmacology platform. The 25 bio-conjugate candidates are **hypothesised designs, not validated therapeutics**. Every numeric value currently displayed — pLDDT, PAE, ΔG, Kd, hERG IC50, seizure index, tolerance rate, and all efficacy percentages — is an **illustrative placeholder produced by a display formula in `app.js`**, not the output of AlphaFold 3, of any docking or free-energy method, or of any ADMET predictor. The 3D viewer draws a parametric helix from the ASCII codes of the sequence characters; it is **not a predicted structure**. The pLDDT curve is `93 + 4·sin(0.4i) + 0.5·(charCode mod 5)`; the PAE matrix is `0.4·|i−j| + 0.3·(charCode mod 4)`.
>
> Nothing in this repository should be used to support any scientific, clinical, investment, or regulatory decision. No safety claim made here has been tested by any method, computational or experimental.
>
> This project is independent and is **not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or connected to Google DeepMind or Google LLC**. AlphaFold is a trademark of Google DeepMind. No AlphaFold Server output is contained in this repository; if any is added, it will be used only under the AlphaFold Server Output Terms of Use (non-commercial use only). AlphaFold 3: Abramson et al., *Nature* **630**, 493–500 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w.

**6. Delete rather than caveat, in three places.** Absolute values (`0%`, `None`, `100%`, `99.5/100`) — no label rescues them; no method emits them. The 30-day tolerance figure — no in-silico substitute exists. The `Live Connected` badge — replace with "Open AlphaFold Server ↗".

**7. CI gates (the discipline that keeps it honest after the fix).** Fail the build if: any value object lacks `provenance`; any `provenance: "computed"` lacks a committed `artifact`; a label containing AlphaFold/pLDDT/PAE/ΔG/Kd/IC50 is attached to a value whose provenance is not `computed`/`measured`; `|ΔG − RT·ln(Kd)| > 0.5 kcal/mol` for any record; any `sequence` fails `/^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$/`; any SMILES fails RDKit parsing or mismatches its recorded PubChem CID formula.

**8. The upgrade path that keeps the ambition.** Nothing above caps the project. Run the 25 sequences through AlphaFold Server, commit the mmCIF files and the per-residue pLDDT/PAE arrays under `data/af3/`, flip those values to `provenance: "computed"` with `artifact` paths, and the amber badges turn green one at a time. Fix the eight SMILES from PubChem CIDs — that is an afternoon and flips the whole natural-product layer to `database`. Restructure the 25 as a design funnel in the RFdiffusion reporting style ("N designs generated → filtered on ipTM ≥ 0.8 → M selected for synthesis → 0 tested to date"). An honest zero at the experimental stage reads as serious work. Twenty-five finished candidates with −19.5 kcal/mol affinities and 0% risk does not.

The ambition is fine. The engineering is fine. Only the captions are wrong — and captions are cheap to fix while the repository is still private.

reviews.discipline: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD in DMPK with 16 years in industry, focused on CNS drug delivery; has taken CNS biologics and therapeutic peptides from lead optimization through IND-enabling preclinical development, including BBB-shuttle bispecifics, intrathecal programs, and microdialysis-based Kp,uu,brain determination.
reviews.overall_assessment:
This platform contains no delivery science whatsoever, and that absence is fatal to its central claim. I read all four files in full and confirmed by word-boundary grep across README.md, app.js, index.html and styles.css that the strings dose, dosing, route, administration, intravenous, subcutaneous, intrathecal, infusion, half-life, plasma, serum, CSF, exposure, permeability, Papp, Kp, Kp,uu, efflux, P-gp, MDR1, transcytosis, TfR, transferrin, protease, peptidase, proteolysis, aggregation, solubility, hemolysis, excipient and anti-drug antibody appear ZERO times. The only apparent hits are substring artifacts: "clearance" is always glutamate/lysosomal/autophagic clearance, "blood" is always "blood-brain barrier" or "cerebral blood flow", "vial" comes from the FontAwesome class "fa-flask-vial", and "PK"/"Vd"/"ADA"/"oral" match inside amino-acid strings and inside "querySelectorAll". Meanwhile the word "therapeutic" appears 14 times, and index.html:326 calls the page a "25 De Novo Targeted Therapeutics Precision Center". A molecule with a binding affinity and no route, no dose, no dosing interval, no formulation and no PK/PD model is a docking hypothesis, not a therapeutic.

I computed the actual physicochemistry of all 25 peptides from their sequences (script and numbers in the findings). They are 26-47 residue, 2.9-5.4 kDa, strongly hydrophilic polypeptides (median MW 4094 Da, median GRAVY -0.92, median ~80 hydrogen-bond donors, |net charge at pH 7.4| up to 8.9). This is roughly ten times the empirical CNS molecular-weight ceiling and an order of magnitude over the H-bond-donor limit, with no BBB transport moiety of any kind attached. For calibration I retrieved real numbers: unmodified therapeutic IgG brain uptake is 0.028-0.07 %ID/g in mouse and brain IgG is <0.01% of the plasma concentration in primate (Pardridge 2023). Nothing in these 25 designs does better than an IgG at crossing, and several are worse-suited because a 4 kDa polycation is also a substrate for renal filtration, glomerular charge trapping, glycosaminoglycan sequestration and serum peptidases.

Three specific safety errors compound this. First, four candidates (X2/B1, M4, X5) are textbook cationic amphipathic alpha-helices: I computed Eisenberg hydrophobic moments of 0.88-0.89 at net charge +4.8 to +8.9, which exceeds LL-37 (0.78) and pexiganan (0.75) computed on the identical scale and window. These are membranolytic pharmacophores, and the platform labels them "hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Cardiotoxicity)" and "Tolerance Rate: 0.0%" with no hemolysis or infusion-reaction assessment anywhere. Second, candidate 14 (app.js:277) and AF3 candidate 5 (app.js:129) contain Abeta(16-35) verbatim -- I verified the exact residue mapping against UniProt P05067 -- and it is proposed as a systemically administered anti-fibril agent in an Alzheimer's context with "Fibril Blockade: 100%". Third, brain-region targeting is asserted without any targeting mechanism and is provably arbitrary: four pairs of byte-identical peptide sequences are assigned to different brain regions with different Kd and different pLDDT (e.g. app.js:153 vs 247, the same 36-mer sent to hippocampal CA1 and to the nucleus basalis of Meynert).

Credit where it is due, and it is not nothing. The five-region / cell-type framing is anatomically coherent and the target set (TrkB, TrkA, Keap1-Nrf2, TREM2, EAAT2, alpha7 nAChR, FZD8, AChE PAS/CAS) is a defensible, literature-grounded CNS target list, not a random one. The natural-product pharmacophore section names real compounds with mostly real target assignments and real signaling cascades. The decision to store sequences as first-class data and expose a genuine "Copy FASTA -> Launch AlphaFold Server" affordance is honest engineering: it does not fabricate a PDB file, it hands the user the real input and points at the real server. The pairing of a binding free energy with a dissociation constant is at least the right pair of quantities to report, even though the reported values are internally inconsistent by three to four orders of magnitude (dG = -18.4 kcal/mol implies Kd ~ 0.03 pM at 298 K, not the 0.32 nM stated at app.js:146). And using region-specific cell types rather than "the brain" as the target compartment shows the right instinct, even though the delivery mechanism to realize it is entirely absent.

My recommendation is not to abandon the project but to stop calling these "therapeutics". They are binder hypotheses. Reframed as "25 de novo binder designs requiring a delivery vehicle", with an honest, uncertainty-bearing DMPK panel attached (predicted Kp,uu,brain with credible intervals, fu,plasma, fu,brain, MDCK-MDR1 efflux ratio, predicted serum t1/2, aggregation and hemolysis flags), and with an explicit delivery strategy per candidate chosen from the real state of the art (TfR1 receptor-mediated transcytosis a la ATV:TfR or Brainshuttle/trontinemab, CD98hc, intrathecal/ICV, focused-ultrasound BBB opening, or TfR1-retargeted AAV), the platform would go from misleading to genuinely useful. The scientific content to do this is available and I have cited the primary sources below.

findings.title: No route of administration, dose, dosing frequency, formulation, or PK/PD model exists anywhere in the platform, yet all 25 molecules are labelled "therapeutics"
findings.evidence_location: README.md:43-92 ("25 targeted bio-conjugate therapeutics"), README.md:96-102 (ADMET section), index.html:326 ("25 De Novo Targeted Therapeutics Precision Center"), index.html:39, app.js:138-398 (FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA, all 25 records), app.js:606-643 (openDrugModal renders six numbered fields: chem struct, sequence, binding sites, target tissue, affinity, ADMET -- none of them pharmacokinetic)
findings.what_is_wrong: I ran a case-insensitive, word-boundary grep for the full DMPK vocabulary across all four project files (README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css). The following strings occur ZERO times: dose, doses, dosing, dosage, route, administered, administration, intravenous, subcutaneous, intrathecal, intranasal, infusion, injection, bolus, half-life, bioavailability, exposure, plasma, serum, CSF, cerebrospinal, microdialysis, Kp, Kp,uu, efflux, P-gp, MDR1, MDCK, BCRP, transcytosis, permeability, Papp, protease, peptidase, proteolysis, stability, aggregation, solubility, excipient, lyophil, hemolysis, anti-drug antibody. Every apparent hit is a substring artifact that I verified individually: "clearance" is always glutamate, lysosomal or autophagic clearance (README.md:89; app.js:64,65,112,333,359); "blood" is always "blood-brain barrier" or "cerebral blood flow" (app.js:34,116,118,119,349,356,373,376); "vial" comes from the FontAwesome class fa-flask-vial (index.html:35,89,117); "PK", "Vd", "ADA" and "oral" match inside amino-acid sequences and inside the JS identifier querySelectorAll. The per-drug modal (app.js:606-643) exposes exactly six numbered fields, and none of them is a route, a dose, a schedule, a vehicle, or an exposure. The word "therapeutic" appears 14 times across README.md, app.js and index.html.
findings.why_it_matters: A binding affinity without a delivery plan is not a drug candidate and cannot be triaged, prioritized, resourced or advanced. Any reader -- a collaborator, an investor, a grant reviewer, a student -- who takes README.md:45 ("We engineered 25 targeted bio-conjugate therapeutics") at face value will believe that a preclinical package exists. The consequence is concrete: the leaderboard at app.js:869-895 ranks candidates on pLDDT, dG and a "Cognitive Enhancement Index", so any decision made from this platform allocates effort purely on predicted potency, which is the single least predictive parameter for CNS success. In my experience the modal failure of CNS programs is not affinity, it is exposure at the target compartment; a platform that omits exposure entirely will systematically rank the wrong molecules first.
findings.ground_truth: The free-drug hypothesis is the accepted foundation of CNS pharmacology: pharmacological response is driven by the unbound concentration at the target site, not by affinity and not by total tissue concentration. A survey of DMPK leadership at 18 major pharmaceutical companies (Loryan et al., Pharm Res 2022;39:1321-1341, PMID 35411506) found 93% share a common cross-disciplinary understanding of Kp,uu,brain and 79% describe its adoption as "game-changing" for their CNS portfolios. A minimally credible candidate record must therefore carry, at absolute minimum: intended route; a dose or dose range with units; a dosing interval; the vehicle/formulation; predicted or measured fu,plasma and fu,brain; a predicted Kp,uu,brain; and a target-engagement calculation linking dose to unbound brain concentration versus Kd.
findings.required_fix: Add a mandatory seventh field to every record in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA (app.js:138-398) and to the modal renderer (app.js:606-643), named "Delivery & Exposure", containing five sub-fields: (1) intended route -- IV, SC, intrathecal, ICV, or intranasal; (2) a dose/dose-interval estimate with units, or the literal string "NOT ESTIMATED"; (3) a predicted Kp,uu,brain with an explicit credible interval; (4) predicted fu,plasma and predicted serum t1/2; (5) the resulting unbound-brain-concentration-versus-Kd target-engagement ratio. Where a value has not been computed, render "NOT ESTIMATED -- no delivery assessment performed" rather than omitting the field, so the gap is visible rather than invisible. Simultaneously, until a delivery strategy exists, change every occurrence of "therapeutic" and "drug" to "binder design" or "candidate binder" in README.md, index.html and app.js, and add a standing disclaimer to the README executive overview stating that no route, dose, formulation or PK/PD assessment has been performed.

findings.title: All 25 candidates are 2.9-5.4 kDa hydrophilic polypeptides with no BBB transport moiety; their computed physicochemistry places CNS parenchymal exposure at or below that of an unmodified IgG, which is 0.028-0.07 %ID/g
findings.evidence_location: app.js:143,153,163,173,183,195,205,215,225,235,247,257,267,277,287,299,309,319,329,339,351,361,371,381,391 (the 25 sequence fields); README.md:22 ("models 25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics ... across 5 specific brain regions"); app.js:145,155,165 etc. (targets fields all begin "CNS -> Brain -> ...")
findings.what_is_wrong: I parsed all 25 sequences directly out of app.js and computed their properties (average residue masses, EMBOSS pKa set for charge and pI, Kyte-Doolittle for GRAVY, backbone NH plus side-chain donors for H-bond donor count). Results: length 26-47 residues (median 35); MW 2877-5436 Da (median 4094 Da); net charge at pH 7.4 spanning -7.20 to +8.93; isoelectric point 3.44-10.95; GRAVY -1.12 to +0.26 with a median of -0.92, i.e. 24 of 25 are net hydrophilic; hydrogen-bond donors 52-106 (median 80). Selected rows -- HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (app.js:143): 47 aa, 5340 Da, q -0.54, GRAVY -0.94, 106 HBD. HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (app.js:153): 36 aa, 4943 Da, q +8.93, pI 10.95, GRAVY -1.09, 36.1% Arg+Lys. MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 (app.js:329): 32 aa, 4314 Da, q +6.93, 34.4% Arg+Lys. HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 (app.js:163): 28 aa, 3508 Da, q -7.20, pI 3.44. Not one of the 25 carries a receptor-mediated-transcytosis shuttle, a TfR1 or CD98hc binder, an Fc, a glucose- or LAT1-transporter ligand, or any other BBB-crossing element; the conjugated "warheads" are natural products (ginsenosides, salvianolic acid B, curcumin) which are themselves notoriously poor CNS penetrants. The platform nevertheless states a parenchymal, cell-type-resolved destination for every one of them ("CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1/CA3 Pyramidal Neurons & DG SGZ Neural Stem Cells)", app.js:145).
findings.why_it_matters: The central claim of the platform -- 25 therapeutics acting on five named brain regions -- requires the molecules to reach brain parenchyma. On the computed physicochemistry they will not, absent a delivery vehicle that does not exist in these designs. I ran the dose arithmetic for HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 using the platform's own claimed Kd of 2.1 nM (app.js:156), targeting 3xKd unbound brain concentration for ~75% occupancy, with Vd 0.1 L/kg, fu,plasma 0.05 and the predicted 27-min serum half-life: the required continuous-infusion dose for a 70 kg human is 16 g/day at Kp,uu 0.01 and 161 g/day at Kp,uu 0.001 (IgG-like). Under deliberately, implausibly generous assumptions (t1/2 4 h, Vd 0.3 L/kg, fu 0.5, Kp,uu 0.05 -- better than most successful CNS small molecules) it falls to 0.11 g/day. The dose requirement therefore swings by more than three orders of magnitude across parameters the platform never estimates and gives the reader no way to estimate. That is the harm: not that the answer is definitely "impossible", but that the platform presents these as finished therapeutics while withholding the one calculation that determines whether they are feasible or absurd.
findings.ground_truth: Empirical CNS penetration limits for passive transcellular diffusion sit near 400-500 Da with roughly 8-10 hydrogen-bond donors; all 25 candidates exceed the MW ceiling by ~6-13x and the donor limit by ~5-13x. For large molecules the measured reality is stark: unmodified therapeutic IgG brain uptake is 0.07 %ID/g for the murine precursor of bapineuzumab and 0.028 %ID/g for mAb158 in mouse, and IgG in primate brain is <0.01% of the plasma concentration (Pardridge, Front Drug Deliv 2023;3:1227816, PMID 37583474, DOI 10.3389/fddev.2023.1227816). Pardridge (Pharmaceuticals 2020;13:394, PMID 33207605) states that 98% of small-molecule drugs and ~100% of biologic drugs do not cross the BBB. Engineered receptor-mediated transcytosis is what changes this: the Denali Fc-based transport vehicle binding the apical domain of human TfR1 produced "substantially improved CNS uptake and sustained pharmacodynamic responses" in hTfR-knockin mice and cynomolgus monkeys (Kariolis et al., Sci Transl Med 2020;12:eaay1359, PMID 32461332); Roche's Brainshuttle fusion trontinemab achieved a modelled 4-18-fold increase in brain exposure over gantenerumab in non-human primates at half the dose (Grimm et al., mAbs 2023;15:2261509, PMID 37823690); anti-CD98hc antibodies showed robust brain accumulation and a significant Abeta pharmacodynamic response (Zuchero et al., Neuron 2016;89:70-82, PMID 26687840). Alternative routes that bypass the BBB entirely -- intrathecal/ICV -- are the established path for CNS oligonucleotides and enzymes; focused-ultrasound BBB opening is now clinically demonstrated with an antibody payload (Rezai et al., N Engl J Med 2024;390:55-62, PMID 38169490); and TfR1-retargeted AAV capsids give 40-50x greater CNS expression than AAV9 in human-TfR1 knockin mice (Huang et al., Science 2024;384:1220-1227, PMID 38753766).
findings.required_fix: Two changes. (a) Stop asserting parenchymal destinations that the molecules cannot reach: revise every "targets" field in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA (app.js:145,155,165,...) to state the intended target compartment together with the delivery mechanism required to reach it, e.g. "Hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons -- REQUIRES a BBB delivery vehicle; none present in this design". (b) Attach an explicit delivery strategy per candidate, chosen from the real state of the art and named in the record: TfR1 receptor-mediated transcytosis (ATV:TfR-style Fc fusion, or Brainshuttle-style monovalent scFab), CD98hc RMT, intrathecal or ICV administration, focused-ultrasound-assisted delivery, or TfR1-retargeted AAV for a genetically encodable payload. For each, state the expected fold-enhancement over unmodified molecule with a citation. Add a computed properties panel to every card showing length, MW, net charge at pH 7.4, pI, GRAVY and HBD count -- these take ten lines of JavaScript and immediately expose to the reader why a shuttle is mandatory.

findings.title: Four candidates are cationic amphipathic alpha-helices with hydrophobic moments exceeding LL-37 and pexiganan; the platform declares them "0% Cardiotoxicity" and "Tolerance Rate: 0.0%" and never assesses hemolysis or infusion reactions
findings.evidence_location: app.js:153 and app.js:247 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 and BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, identical 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG); app.js:329 (MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4, FLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG); app.js:183 (HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5); app.js:131 (AF3 candidate CogAChE-PAS-02, same motif); safety strings at app.js:157 ("hERG IC50 > 50 uM | Seizure Index: 0.02 | Tolerance Rate: 0.0%"), app.js:251 ("Peripheral Side Effects: None"), app.js:333 ("Seizure Index: 0.00 | Lysosomal Clearance: +420%"); README.md:99 ("hERG Cardiotoxicity Risk: IC50 > 50 uM (0% Risk). Hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding")
findings.what_is_wrong: I computed the Eisenberg consensus-scale hydrophobic moment over a sliding 18-residue, 100-degree-per-residue window for all 25 sequences, and calibrated against known membranolytic peptides on the identical scale and window. Results: X2/B1 muH = 0.89 at net charge +8.93 (36.1% Arg+Lys); M4 muH = 0.88 at +6.93 (34.4% Arg+Lys); X5 muH = 0.88 at +4.79 (27.3% Arg+Lys). Calibration on the same code: melittin (bee venom, hemolytic) 0.55; the (KLAKLAK)2 lytic peptide 0.69; pexiganan/MSI-78 0.75; LL-37 core 0.78; an idealized Leu/Lys amphipathic helix 0.63; polyalanine control 0.00. The four candidates therefore sit above every membranolytic reference I tested. The maximally amphipathic window in X2/B1 is KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFE -- a Trp/Phe-rich hydrophobic face opposed to an Arg/Lys polar face, which is the canonical pore-forming architecture. Against this, the platform asserts "0% Cardiotoxicity" and "Peripheral Side Effects: None" and the README (line 99) offers the affirmatively wrong mechanistic rationale that "hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656" -- hydrophobicity in a cationic amphipath is the driver of membrane interaction, not a shield against it. There is no hemolysis assay, no HC50, no mast-cell degranulation or MRGPRX2 assessment, no infusion-reaction risk statement, and no complement-activation-related pseudoallergy consideration anywhere in the codebase.
findings.why_it_matters: Hemolysis and infusion reactions are the historical killers of this exact molecular class and they occur at concentrations in the range these designs would require. Typical HC50 (50% hemolysis) for cationic amphipathic alpha-helical peptides is roughly 5-100 uM. My dose arithmetic for X2/B1 (Vd 0.1 L/kg, fu 0.05, predicted t1/2 27 min, 3xKd target occupancy) gives a required total plasma concentration of 12.6 uM at Kp,uu 0.01 and 126 uM at Kp,uu 0.001 -- squarely inside and then far above the hemolytic window. A reader who trusts "Seizure Index: 0.01, Peripheral Side Effects: None, Tolerance Rate: 0.0%" would conclude that the principal safety liability of the molecule has been evaluated and cleared. It has not been evaluated at all, and the one liability that actually dominates this chemotype is the one liability the safety string does not mention. Stating a numeric "0%" risk for an unassessed hazard is worse than silence: it converts an absence of data into a false negative.
findings.ground_truth: Membrane-lytic activity of alpha-helical peptides is governed by the combination of cationic charge and hydrophobic moment. Wieprecht et al. (Biochemistry 1997;36:6124-6132, PMID 9166783, DOI 10.1021/bi9619987) showed with magainin-2 amide analogues holding hydrophobic moment, charge and hydrophilic angle constant that increasing hydrophobicity drives permeabilization of zwitterionic PC-rich (i.e. mammalian) membranes and that "the antibacterial and hemolytic activity of the peptides increases with enhanced hydrophobicity", with a strong correlation between the hemolytic effect and PC-vesicle permeabilization. Maturana et al. (Colloids Surf B Biointerfaces 2017;153:152-159, PMID 28236791, DOI 10.1016/j.colsurfb.2017.02.003) showed with designed analogues differing in hydrophobic moment and net charge that affinity for zwitterionic rather than anionic membranes is what converts an antimicrobial into a hemolytic peptide. The correct developability panel for a cationic amphipath is: human erythrocyte HC50, a therapeutic index (HC50 divided by required plasma concentration), mammalian cell LDH release, MRGPRX2/mast-cell degranulation, and complement activation.
findings.required_fix: First, delete the fabricated numeric safety strings for these four candidates and every other candidate (app.js:147,157,167,177,187,199,209,219,229,239,251,261,271,281,291,303,313,323,333,343,355,365,375,385,395) and replace with "NOT ASSESSED". Second, add a computed-liability flag to each card: display net charge at pH 7.4, %Arg+Lys, and the Eisenberg hydrophobic moment, and raise an explicit "CATIONIC AMPHIPATHIC -- MEMBRANOLYTIC / HEMOLYSIS RISK" warning whenever muH > 0.5 and net charge > +3. Third, correct README.md:99, which currently states a mechanistically backwards rationale; replace with an honest statement that hERG liability has not been assessed and that hemolysis, not hERG, is the leading cardiovascular/haematological concern for cationic amphipathic peptides. Fourth, if these four candidates are to be retained, specify the required de-risking experiments: human RBC HC50, therapeutic index versus the required plasma Cmax, and MRGPRX2 activation.

findings.title: Two candidates contain the amyloid-beta(16-35) core sequence verbatim and are proposed as systemically delivered anti-fibril agents with "Fibril Blockade: 100%" and no aggregation, seeding, immunogenicity or ARIA assessment
findings.evidence_location: app.js:277 (BasalAChE-Abeta-B4, sequence "KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPW"); app.js:281 (safety string "hERG IC50 > 50 uM | Seizure Index: 0.01 | Fibril Blockade: 100%"); app.js:282 (mechanism claim); app.js:129 (AF3_CANDIDATES rank 5, CogAbeta-Clearer-08, fasta "KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPWECDRRACPCYRGFWR", listed with pLDDT 92.1 and CEI 90.5); README.md:77 ("BasalAChE-Abeta-B4: Salvianolic Acid B + Abeta Disruptor (KLVFFAED). Toxic Abeta-AChE seed blockade."); app.js:279 (target "Basal Forebrain (Cholinergic Septal Nuclei & Projection Tracts)")
findings.what_is_wrong: I retrieved the canonical human APP sequence from UniProt P05067 and mapped the fragment computationally. The string KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM at app.js:277 and app.js:129 is an exact, contiguous match to Abeta residues 16-35 -- it begins at Lys16 with the KLVFF central hydrophobic cluster (Abeta 16-20) and runs through GAIIGLM (Abeta 29-35), i.e. it spans both hydrophobic segments that drive Abeta beta-sheet nucleation and fibril elongation.
