findings.why_it_matters: Rg1 and Ginkgolide B are the declared warheads for four of the twenty-five candidates (HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 at app.js:141-148, AstroZo1-Protect-A3 at app.js:369-376, and via Rg3 BasalNgf-TrkA-B3 at app.js:265-272 and BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 at app.js:285-292). Any property computed from these SMILES — mass, formula, logP, docking pose — describes a molecule that does not exist in Panax ginseng or Ginkgo biloba. The internal contradiction is itself diagnostic: the correct formulas were typed into the prose fields by hand while the SMILES were generated separately and never reconciled, which means no single automated pass ever validated formula against structure. A collaborator who trusts the prose and a collaborator who trusts the SMILES will build on two different molecules.
findings.ground_truth: Ginsenoside Rg1: PubChem CID 441923, C42H72O14, MW 801.0, InChIKey YURJSTAIMNSZAE-HHNZYBFYSA-N; 6-O-beta-D-glucopyranosyl-20-O-beta-D-glucopyranosyl-protopanaxatriol, i.e. both sugars O-linked, on a dammarane skeleton bearing the C4,4-gem-dimethyl. Ginkgolide B: PubChem CID 11973122, C20H24O10, MW 424.4, InChIKey SQOJOAFXDQDRGF-ZMVGXLHTSA-N; a hexacyclic cage bearing three lactones, one tert-butyl and three hydroxyls. Ginsenoside Rg3: C42H72O13, MW 785.0. Presenegenin: PubChem CID 21594224, C30H46O7, MW 518.7.
findings.required_fix: Replace both SMILES with the PubChem isomeric SMILES and correct the Rg3 and presenegenin formulas. Then delete the hand-typed formula strings from the `chemStruct` prose fields entirely and render them from RDKit CalcMolFormula on the validated structure, so the formula shown to the user is derived from the structure rather than asserted in parallel with it. This class of contradiction cannot recur once the formula has a single source of truth.

findings.title: Every structure in the platform is stereochemically flat, so each saponin/terpenoid record denotes millions of distinct molecules rather than one
findings.evidence_location: app.js:20, app.js:30, app.js:40, app.js:80 (all four parseable SMILES); capability advertised at index.html:118
findings.what_is_wrong:
Not one of the eight structure fields carries a single stereodescriptor. There are no '@'/'@@' tetrahedral tags and no '/' or '\\' bond-direction tags anywhere in NATURAL_PRODUCTS_DATA. I quantified this with RDKit FindPotentialStereo on each parseable string and compared against the PubChem reference:

  Ginsenoside Rg1 — reference has 21 defined stereo elements; app.js has 0 specified and 22 unspecified => the string denotes 2^22 = 4,194,304 stereoisomers.
  Ginkgolide B   — reference has 11 defined; app.js has 0 specified, 12 unspecified => 2^12 = 4,096 stereoisomers.
  Asiatic acid   — reference has 12 defined; app.js has 0 specified, 12 unspecified => 2^12 = 4,096 stereoisomers.
  Baicalein      — achiral, so no loss here.
  Curcumin       — even after repairing the OCH3 typo, both (1E,6E) descriptors are absent => 2^2 = 4 geometric isomers.
  Huperzine A, Salvianolic acid B, Onjisaponin V — unparseable, so stereochemistry is moot (references carry 3 and 5 defined elements respectively).

This is a systematic omission across the whole dataset, not an isolated slip.

It is also a directly contradicted claim. index.html:118 advertises the natural-products tab as providing 'Detailed SMILES formulation, pharmacophoric moieties, receptor binding residue coordinates, and stereochemistry'. There is no stereochemistry anywhere in the file.
findings.why_it_matters:
For a pentacyclic triterpenoid or a dammarane saponin, stereochemistry is not decoration — it is the molecule. Asiatic acid is specifically 2-alpha,3-beta,23-trihydroxyurs-12-en-28-oic acid; the 2-alpha,3-beta relative configuration on the A ring determines the hydrogen-bonding geometry of the diol, and a 2-beta,3-alpha diastereomer is a different compound with different target engagement. Of the 4,096 stereoisomers the app.js asiatic acid string denotes, exactly one is asiatic acid; 4,095 are not, and most are not natural products at all. For Rg1 the ratio is one in 4.2 million.

Every downstream claim in the platform is 3D: 'in-depth analysis of cation-pi anchoring, hydrophobic cage insertion' (index.html:92), binding-residue contact lists (app.js:12, 22, 32, 42, 52, 62, 72, 82), and binding free energies to one decimal place (app.js:146 etc.). None of these are defined for a flat graph. You cannot dock, cannot compute a shape or pharmacophore overlay, cannot assign a binding pose, and cannot compute a DeltaG for an undefined stereoisomer — the answer differs between diastereomers by orders of magnitude in affinity. A platform that calls itself 'structural pharmacology' while carrying no stereochemistry has no structural layer at all.
findings.ground_truth: Isomeric SMILES with full stereochemistry, retrieved from PubChem this session: Ginsenoside Rg1 (CID 441923) CC(=CCC[C@@](C)([C@H]1CC[C@@]2([C@@H]1[C@@H](C[C@H]3[C@]2(C[C@@H]([C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@@H](C4(C)C)O)C)O[C@H]5[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O5)CO)O)O)O)C)O)C)O[C@H]6[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O6)CO)O)O)O)C. Ginkgolide B (CID 11973122) C[C@@H]1C(=O)O[C@@H]2[C@]1([C@@]34C(=O)O[C@H]5[C@]3([C@@H]2O)[C@@]6([C@@H](C5)C(C)(C)C)[C@H](C(=O)O[C@H]6O4)O)O. Asiatic acid (CID 119034) C[C@@H]1CC[C@@]2(CC[C@@]3(C(=CC[C@H]4[C@]3(CC[C@@H]5[C@@]4(C[C@H]([C@@H]([C@@]5(C)CO)O)O)C)C)[C@@H]2[C@H]1C)C)C(=O)O. Curcumin (CID 969516) COC1=C(C=CC(=C1)/C=C/C(=O)CC(=O)/C=C/C2=CC(=C(C=C2)O)OC)O.
findings.required_fix: Adopt isomeric SMILES from PubChem for all eight compounds and make stereochemical completeness a hard schema constraint: in the validation gate, run RDKit FindPotentialStereo on every structure and fail the build if any element returns Unspecified. Store and assert the full 27-character InChIKey (not just the 14-character skeleton block), since the second block is exactly what encodes stereochemistry — the reference asiatic acid key is JXSVIVRDWWRQRT-UYDOISQJSA-N while the flat app.js string gives JXSVIVRDWWRQRT-UHFFFAOYSA-N, and comparing only the first block would have masked this. Until stereochemistry is present, remove the claim at index.html:118 and every DeltaG and binding-pose assertion derived from these structures.

findings.title: Two candidates are the amyloidogenic core of Abeta, Abeta(16-35) verbatim, presented as an anti-amyloid therapeutic with '100% fibril blockade'
findings.evidence_location: app.js:277 (BasalAChE-Abeta-B4, sequence field), app.js:281 (safety field claiming 'Fibril Blockade: 100%'), app.js:282 (mechanism); app.js:129 (AF3_CANDIDATES rank 5, CogAbeta-Clearer-08); README.md:77
findings.what_is_wrong:
The sequence at app.js:277 is 'KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPW'. I matched its N-terminal segment against human Abeta1-42 (DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA) and the first 20 residues, KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM, are human Abeta(16-35) verbatim — not a fragment inspired by Abeta, but a contiguous exact copy. The same 20-mer opens AF3 candidate rank 5 at app.js:129.

That 20-mer is the aggregation engine of Abeta. It contains the KLVFF self-recognition motif (Abeta16-20), which is the nucleation element that drives beta-sheet association, together with the GAIIGLM hydrophobic stretch (Abeta29-35) that forms the second beta-strand of the cross-beta fibril core. Peptides spanning this region are the standard positive controls for spontaneous fibrillogenesis in ThT assays; they self-assemble in buffer without a template.

The platform presents this as an amyloid inhibitor. app.js:282 states it 'disrupts toxic hydrogen-bonded Abeta-AChE amyloid fibril seeding along cholinergic axonal tracts', app.js:281 asserts 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' and 'Seizure Index: 0.01', and README.md:77 labels it an 'Abeta Disruptor' delivering 'toxic Abeta-AChE seed blockade'. The declared route (app.js:279) is the basal forebrain cholinergic septal nuclei — i.e. direct CNS exposure. The genuine KLVFF-derived inhibitor literature works precisely by breaking this property: the recognition motif is kept short (KLVFF, LPFFD) and is deliberately N-methylated, D-amino-acid substituted, or capped so that it binds Abeta without extending the sheet. Appending the full GAIIGLM hydrophobic core does the opposite — it restores the self-assembly competence that inhibitor design exists to remove.
findings.why_it_matters:
This inverts the sign of the pharmacology. The molecule described is not an anti-amyloid agent; it is a seed. Delivering Abeta(16-35) into brain parenchyma is the standard method for accelerating amyloid deposition in seeding experiments, not for clearing it. The asserted '100% fibril blockade' and 'Seizure Index: 0.01' are the exact opposite of the expected behaviour and are stated with no supporting computation anywhere in the codebase.

The integrity risk is what elevates this above an ordinary design error. The repository is presented as a drug-discovery pipeline with quantitative safety numbers, and this entry carries the same confident formatting as every other. A reader without the Abeta sequence memorised has nothing in the document that would flag it — the sequence is displayed to the user at app.js:620 as a 'FASTA Peptide / Bio-Conjugate Sequence', and index.html:362-363 offers a one-click 'Copy FASTA Sequence' button next to a 'Launch AlphaFold Server' link, actively encouraging downstream use. If any of these sequences were ever ordered from a peptide vendor on the strength of the safety table, the stated safety profile would have been actively misleading about a known neurotoxic and aggregation-competent species.
findings.ground_truth: Human amyloid-beta 1-42 (UniProt P05067, APP770 residues 672-713): DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA. Residues 16-35 = KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM. KLVFF (Abeta16-20) is the central hydrophobic cluster and self-recognition element; GAIIGLM (Abeta29-35) forms the second strand of the U-shaped cross-beta protofilament. Established beta-sheet-breaker designs (iAbeta5/LPFFD, N-methylated KLVFF analogues, D-peptide variants) truncate to the recognition motif and chemically block the hydrogen-bonding face precisely to prevent the conjugate from nucleating fibrils itself.
findings.required_fix: Remove Abeta(16-35) from both records immediately. If a KLVFF-based recognition element is genuinely intended, truncate to the five-residue KLVFF motif and apply an explicit anti-aggregation modification (backbone N-methylation of alternating residues, or D-amino-acid substitution), state that modification in the chemStruct field, and delete the 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' and 'Seizure Index' assertions until an actual ThT kinetics or aggregation-propensity computation exists to support them. Add an automated screen over every sequence in the dataset that flags exact substring matches against known amyloidogenic segments (Abeta, alpha-synuclein NAC, IAPP, tau PHF6/PHF6*) and against an aggregation predictor such as TANGO/WALTZ/AGGRESCAN, and fail the build on any hit.

findings.title: The central 'natural-product warhead fused to a peptide' design premise is sterically impossible for the AChE-targeted candidates, measured against the crystal structures
findings.evidence_location: README.md:45 (the design premise); app.js:152 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, 'Huperzine A Pyridone Core + Cys-Lys Amide Coupling'), app.js:154 (claims simultaneous CAS and PAS occupancy), app.js:246-248 (BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1), app.js:194 (PfcACh-PAM-P1), app.js:286-288 (BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5); README.md:61, 74, 78
findings.what_is_wrong:
README.md:45 states the method: 'We engineered 25 targeted bio-conjugate therapeutics by fusing minimal natural product pharmacophore warheads with AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides.' For the acetylcholinesterase subset this is geometrically impossible, and the crystal structures say so quantitatively. I downloaded PDB 1VOT (TcAChE complexed with (-)-huperzine A, Raves et al. 1997) and PDB 4EY7 (human AChE with donepezil) from RCSB and measured directly:

  - Huperzine A sits at the base of the gorge, 4.78 A from the Trp84 side-chain centroid and 6.51 A from the catalytic Ser200. It is 12.58 A below the Trp279 peripheral anionic site.
  - It is enclosed by 26 protein residues within 6 A. It is fully buried, with no solvent-exposed face available for a linker.
  - The gorge axis, Trp84 (CAS) to Trp279 (PAS) side-chain centroids, is 16.12 A; Ser200 to Trp279 is 15.07 A.
  - The Tyr121/Phe330 bottleneck has a closest side-chain heavy-atom approach of 5.32 A. Subtracting two carbon van der Waals radii (1.70 A each) leaves a free aperture of roughly 1.9 A.
  - For calibration, donepezil — the canonical dual CAS/PAS binder — has a maximum intramolecular extent of 15.48 A in 4EY7. Spanning this gorge consumes an entire ~15 A small molecule.

A ~1.9 A aperture admits essentially nothing wider than a single extended aliphatic chain. The peptides attached to these warheads are 36-41 residues (app.js:153, 195, 247). An alpha-helix of 36 residues is ~54 A long and ~10-12 A in diameter including side chains; fully extended it is ~126 A. Neither can traverse a 16 A channel with a 1.9 A constriction, and there is no exit for the peptide because the warhead is buried under 26 residues.

The second half of the premise fails too. 'Minimal pharmacophore warhead' presupposes that huperzine A's pyridone is separable. Raves et al. specifically found 'surprisingly few strong direct interactions with protein residues to explain its high affinity' and attributed affinity to distributed hydrophobic contacts between the intact rigid tricycle and the aromatic residues lining the gorge. The binding energy is a property of the whole cage, not of an excisable pyridone. Excising the pyridone and amide-coupling it to a peptide (app.js:152, 'Huperzine A Pyridone Core (C15H18N2O) + Cys-Lys Amide Coupling') both discards the contacts that produce the affinity and consumes the ring nitrogen and the exocyclic amine that make the remaining contacts. Note also that the formula given for the 'pyridone core' fragment, C15H18N2O, is the formula of intact huperzine A — the record simultaneously claims a minimal fragment and quotes the whole molecule's formula.

app.js:154 makes the impossibility explicit by asserting the conjugate occupies 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)' simultaneously, and app.js:252 claims it 'completely blocks acetylcholine degradation' while elevating synaptic ACh by 350%.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the platform's stated method, applied to at least five of the twenty-five candidates and to the #1 and #7 ranked AF3 candidates (app.js:125, 131). If the paradigm is geometrically impossible for its flagship application, the ranked leaderboard and the DeltaG values attached to it are not weak estimates — they are describing binding events that cannot occur. An expert who takes README.md:45 at face value would conclude that a workable conjugation strategy had been identified for a target class where the buried-ligand problem is precisely the known, hard, unsolved obstacle. Genuine dual-site AChE inhibitors solve it the only way the geometry allows: a single small molecule long enough to span the gorge, tethered through a slim aliphatic or aromatic linker, never a polypeptide.
findings.ground_truth: Raves ML, Harel M, Pang YP, Silman I, Kozikowski AP, Sussman JL. Structure of acetylcholinesterase complexed with the nootropic alkaloid, (-)-huperzine A. Nat Struct Biol 1997;4(1):57-63 (PMID 8989325, DOI 10.1038/nsb0197-57) — establishes that huperzine A binds at the gorge base with affinity distributed over hydrophobic contacts with the aromatic gorge lining rather than a few separable strong interactions. Coordinates: PDB 1VOT (TcAChE + huperzine A) and PDB 4EY7 (human AChE + donepezil), both measured in this session. Measured geometry: CAS-PAS separation 16.1 A, Tyr121/Phe330 bottleneck free aperture ~1.9 A, huperzine A enclosed by 26 residues within 6 A, donepezil maximum extent 15.5 A. The design idiom that actually works for CAS+PAS dual occupancy is a small-molecule bivalent ligand (tacrine-donepezil hybrids, bis-tacrines) with a slim polymethylene tether sized to the ~15 A span.
findings.required_fix: Retract the peptide-conjugation strategy for all AChE-gorge-directed candidates (app.js:151-158, 193-200, 245-252, 285-292) and for AF3 candidates ranked 1 and 7. If dual CAS/PAS engagement is the goal, redesign as a small-molecule bivalent ligand: keep huperzine A intact as the CAS-binding unit, attach a slim linker of the length the measured 16 A span requires, and cap it with an aromatic PAS binder. Before asserting any binding mode, dock the actual proposed structure into 1VOT or 4EY7 and report the pose, the clash census, and the buried surface area — a single docking run against the real coordinates would have caught this. More generally, add a steric feasibility gate to the pipeline: for every conjugate, check whether the warhead's binding site is solvent-accessible in the target structure, and reject designs whose linker must pass through a buried channel.

findings.title: Every conjugate is a 3.5-6.1 kDa polycationic peptide that cannot reach the CNS, while the uniformly asserted hERG-based safety profile assesses the wrong liability entirely
findings.what_is_wrong:
I computed the mass of every conjugate from its sequence using standard average residue masses plus water, and added the true PubChem mass of each declared warhead less water per conjugation bond. Results for the 22 of 25 records with a parseable sequence:

  Conjugate MW range 3,538 - 6,137 Da, median 4,804 Da.
  22 of 22 exceed the Ro5 500 Da limit. 22 of 22 exceed 1,000 Da. 22 of 22 exceed 3,000 Da.
  Largest: PfcGluN2A-LTP-P3 6,137 Da (45-mer + salvianolic acid B) and HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 6,123 Da (47-mer + Rg1 801 Da).
  Net formal charge at pH 7.4 reaches +9 (app.js:153 and app.js:247, KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG).
  17 of 22 carry two or more free cysteines and 14 of 22 carry four or more, with no disulfide connectivity specified anywhere — an unconstrained 8-cysteine 47-mer (app.js:143) has 105 possible disulfide pairings and will scramble.
  Three records have no computable mass at all: app.js:173 and app.js:371 contain 'B', the Asx ambiguity code and not a standard residue (also at app.js:130 in AF3 candidate rank 6, which the UI offers for submission to AlphaFold Server); app.js:381 contains the literal placeholder 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' in the sequence field.

These numbers are 8-13x above the passive BBB permeation ceiling. The CNS MPO framework (Wager et al.) places desirable CNS agents at MW below ~360 Da with TPSA under ~90 A^2 and HBD at or below 3; peptides of this size have TPSA in the many hundreds of A^2 and dozens of backbone HBDs. Yet every record asserts a specific CNS parenchymal compartment ('CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1/CA3 Pyramidal Neurons & DG SGZ Neural Stem Cells)', app.js:145) and quantitative pharmacodynamics (LTP +280%, app.js:148). No BBB transport mechanism — receptor-mediated transcytosis, a shuttle peptide, an efflux assessment — appears anywhere in the repository.

The safety section is worse than absent; it assesses the wrong liability. Grep shows all 25 safety fields carry the identical string 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM', and README.md:99 explains it as 'Hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656'. A value identical across 25 chemically distinct entities is a constant, not a prediction. And hERG is not the liability here: hERG block is a small-molecule lipophilic-amine problem, and a 5 kDa polycation was never going to enter the channel inner cavity. The actual liability is the one the sequences are built from. I computed Eisenberg consensus hydrophobic moment on a 100-degree helical wheel for the recurring scaffold KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:153, app.js:247, and AF3 rank 7 at app.js:131): <muH> = 0.615 at net charge +9. Melittin, the reference bee-venom lytic peptide, scores <muH> = 0.353 at +5; magainin 2 scores 0.455 at +3. The design scores substantially higher on both axes than the canonical membrane-lytic peptides. The related 32-mer at app.js:329, labelled an 'LC3 motif', scores 0.578 at +7. Cationic amphipathic helices in this regime are hemolytic and cytolytic; that is the toxicity that needed assessing, and it is not mentioned anywhere. Instead app.js:239 asserts 'Systemic Toxicity: Negligible' and app.js:291 a 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100'.
findings.why_it_matters: This invalidates the pipeline as a therapeutics pipeline rather than merely weakening it. None of the 25 molecules can reach the compartment its own record names, so every efficacy number in the file describes an exposure that cannot occur. Simultaneously, the safety table directs a reader's attention to a liability these molecules do not have while remaining silent on the one they demonstrably do — and the numbers are asserted with two-significant-figure precision ('Seizure Index: 0.01', 'Inflammatory Cytokine Suppression: 98%', 'Downregulation: < 3.5%') that implies computation. Grep confirms no ADMET calculation of any kind exists in the codebase. A reader — particularly a non-medicinal-chemist evaluating this as a portfolio or a funding case — would conclude that 25 CNS-penetrant candidates had cleared cardiotoxicity screening. The opposite is true on both counts.
findings.ground_truth: Wager TT, Hou X, Verhoest PR, Villalobos A. Moving beyond rules: the development of a central nervous system multiparameter optimization (CNS MPO) approach to enable alignment of druglike properties. ACS Chem Neurosci 2010;1(6):435-449 (PMID 22778837, DOI 10.1021/cn100008c), and the follow-up validation, ACS Chem Neurosci 2016;7(6):767-775 (PMID 26991242, DOI 10.1021/acschemneuro.6b00029): CNS desirability is driven by MW, TPSA, HBD, ClogP, ClogD and basic pKa; 74% of marketed CNS drugs score >=4 of 6, and the marketed CNS set sits far below 1 kDa. Peptides of 3-6 kDa with net charge up to +9 have essentially zero passive BBB permeability and require an active transcytosis mechanism. On the toxicity side, net cationic charge >= +4 combined with Eisenberg <muH> above ~0.35 is the canonical membrane-lytic pharmacophore shared by melittin (<muH> 0.353, +5) and magainin 2 (<muH> 0.455, +3), both measured here for calibration.
findings.required_fix: Delete every asserted ADMET number in app.js:147-395 and README.md:96-102 — they are constants, not predictions — and replace them with values actually computed and labelled with the method and version that produced them. Compute, per candidate: MW, TPSA, HBD/HBA and cLogP/cLogD from the real structure via RDKit; a CNS MPO desirability score; net charge and Eisenberg hydrophobic moment with an explicit hemolysis/cytolysis flag for any sequence exceeding the melittin reference; predicted immunogenicity (MHC-II binding); and plasma/protease stability. Fix the three malformed sequences (remove 'B' at app.js:130/173/371, replace the placeholder at app.js:381) and specify disulfide connectivity for every multi-cysteine design. Then either state an explicit BBB delivery mechanism with supporting evidence, or restate the target compartment honestly as peripheral. Replace the hERG claim with a liability assessment appropriate to polycationic amphipathic peptides.

findings.title: No assay-interference assessment anywhere, though four of eight compounds are canonical interference scaffolds and curcumin is the textbook PAINS/IMPS case
findings.evidence_location: app.js:48-55 (curcumin record), app.js:38-45 (baicalein), app.js:68-75 (salvianolic acid B), app.js:78-85 (asiatic acid); design use at app.js:161-168, 296-304, 336-344; README.md:36; absence confirmed by grep for 'PAINS|aggregat|interference|redox|Michael|thiol' across all four platform files (zero hits)
findings.what_is_wrong:
Four of the eight compounds are recognised assay-interference liabilities, and the repository contains no interference discussion, no PAINS filter, no aggregation check and no counter-screen recommendation. Grep over README.md, app.js, index.html and styles.css returns zero hits for PAINS, aggregation, interference, redox, Michael acceptor or thiol reactivity.

Curcumin is the strongest case in the modern medicinal chemistry literature. Nelson et al. (J Med Chem 2017) classify it as both a PAINS and an IMPS (invalid metabolic panacea) candidate and conclude it is 'an unstable, reactive, nonbioavailable compound and, therefore, a highly improbable lead', noting that more than 120 clinical trials have run and that no double-blinded placebo-controlled trial of curcumin has succeeded. The mechanistic basis is exactly what the platform relies on: the bis-alpha,beta-unsaturated 1,3-diketone is a promiscuous Michael acceptor, it undergoes rapid hydrolytic degradation above pH 7, it redox-cycles, it is fluorescent and interferes with fluorescence-based readouts, it chelates metals, and it aggregates. The platform reports these liabilities as the mechanism of action: app.js:54 and README.md:36 present 'Keap1 Cys151 Alkylation' as the therapeutic mechanism. Covalent alkylation of a reactive cysteine by a promiscuous Michael acceptor is exactly the reactivity that makes curcumin non-selective — Cys151 is one of many thiols it will hit. Presenting non-selective thiol reactivity as targeted pharmacology, with no cysteine-selectivity data and no thiol-reactivity counter-screen, is the specific reasoning error the PAINS literature exists to correct. Curcumin is nevertheless deployed as a warhead in three candidates (app.js:162, 298, 338).

Baicalein (or rather the 6,7,8-triol actually encoded, per MEDCHEM-02) is a polyphenol with an ortho-triol: catechol and pyrogallol motifs auto-oxidise at physiological pH to generate quinones and hydrogen peroxide, which inactivate enzymes non-specifically — a particularly acute concern for the claimed 12/15-LOX iron target and for the cysteine-containing GSK-3beta. Salvianolic acid B carries four catechol rings by the platform's own description (app.js:75) and has cLogP and polyphenol character consistent with colloidal aggregation. Asiatic acid computes to cLogP 5.03 with MW 489 by RDKit here — squarely in the physicochemical regime the Aggregation Advisor flags as aggregation-prone.

None of this appears. The compounds are presented with clean, specific residue-level binding claims (app.js:42, 52, 72, 82) as though selectivity were established.
findings.why_it_matters: The entire Section 1 pharmacophore matrix rests on literature target assignments for compounds whose reported activities are, for a substantial fraction, artefacts of the assay format rather than genuine target engagement. Building 25 conjugate designs on those warheads propagates the artefact into the design layer: if curcumin's Keap1 engagement is non-selective thiol alkylation, a curcumin-peptide conjugate inherits the non-selectivity and gains nothing. A medicinal chemist reading README.md:36 would see a well-known IMPS presented as a validated Nrf2 mechanism with no caveat, and would immediately discount the credibility of the whole matrix — which is unfortunate, because parts of the pharmacology narrative are qualitatively sound (see the overall assessment). Honest treatment of the interference liability would cost the document nothing and would substantially raise its credibility with the audience it is aimed at.
findings.ground_truth: Nelson KM, Dahlin JL, Bisson J, Graham J, Pauli GF, Walters MA. The Essential Medicinal Chemistry of Curcumin. J Med Chem 2017;60(5):1620-1637 (PMID 28074653, DOI 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b00975), with the follow-up Curcumin May (Not) Defy Science, ACS Med Chem Lett 2017;8(5):467-470 (PMID 28523093, DOI 10.1021/acsmedchemlett.7b00139). Baell JB, Holloway GA. New substructure filters for removal of pan assay interference compounds (PAINS) from screening libraries and for their exclusion in bioassays. J Med Chem 2010;53(7):2719-2740 (PMID 20131845, DOI 10.1021/jm901137j) — the source of the PAINS substructure alerts, implemented in RDKit as FilterCatalogParams.FilterCatalogs.PAINS_A/B/C. Irwin JJ, Duan D, Torosyan H, Doak AK, Ziebart KT, Sterling T, Tumanian G, Shoichet BK. An Aggregation Advisor for Ligand Discovery. J Med Chem 2015;58(17):7076-7087 (PMID 26295373, DOI 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5b01105) — colloidal aggregation is the dominant mechanism of artifactual protein inhibition; the advisor tool predicts aggregation from lipophilicity, affinity and similarity to ~12,000 known aggregators.
findings.required_fix: Run RDKit's PAINS_A/B/C filter catalogue over all eight structures once they parse, and surface every alert in the UI alongside the compound rather than in a footnote. Add an explicit interference-liability field to each natural-product record covering Michael-acceptor reactivity, redox cycling, metal chelation, assay fluorescence, aggregation propensity (cross-checked against the Aggregation Advisor) and chemical stability at pH 7.4. For curcumin specifically, cite Nelson et al. 2017 in the record and either drop it as a warhead or state explicitly what selectivity evidence supports the Keap1 Cys151 claim over the many other reactive thiols in the proteome. Where a target claim rests on a reported activity, require the standard counter-screens (detergent control for aggregation, thiol-reactivity counter-screen, orthogonal non-fluorescent readout) to be cited or flag the claim as unvalidated.

findings.title: AChE binding-site residue lists are chimeras of Torpedo and human numbering; no single ortholog has the residue set claimed
findings.evidence_location: app.js:12, app.js:15, app.js:72, app.js:154, app.js:248, app.js:278, app.js:288; README.md:32, README.md:38
findings.what_is_wrong:
The AChE residue numbers throughout the platform mix two organisms' conventions, sometimes inside a single string. I verified the actual residue identities by parsing CA records from the two crystal structures.

PDB 1VOT (Torpedo californica AChE): residue 70 = TYR, 72 = ASP, 84 = TRP, 121 = TYR, 279 = TRP, 330 = PHE, 334 = TYR, 200 = SER, 440 = HIS.
PDB 4EY7 (human AChE): residue 72 = TYR, 74 = ASP, 86 = TRP, 121 = GLY, 124 = TYR, 286 = TRP, 330 = VAL, 337 = TYR, 338 = PHE, 341 = TYR, 203 = SER, 447 = HIS.

So Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121/Trp279 are Torpedo numbering, and Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341 are human numbering. app.js:154 states 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)' — Torpedo CAS concatenated with human PAS in one field. app.js:248 does the same: 'AChE Catalytic Gorge (Trp84, Phe330, Trp286, Tyr341)'. app.js:288 pairs them explicitly as 'CAS/PAS (Trp84/Trp286)'. README.md:32 mixes them in a single sentence: 'CAS: Trp84, Phe330 & PAS (Trp286)'.

There is no acetylcholinesterase for which any of these lists is correct. In human AChE, residue 121 is glycine and residue 330 is valine, so 'Phe330, Tyr121' is simply wrong. In Torpedo AChE, residue 286 is not tryptophan and 341 is not tyrosine, so 'Trp286, Tyr341' is wrong. Separately, app.js:12 describes the Trp84 interaction as a 'CAS Salt Bridge'; Trp84 is a tryptophan with no ionisable side chain and cannot form a salt bridge. The same file correctly identifies the interaction as cation-pi at app.js:15 and README.md:32, so the file contradicts itself on the interaction type as well as the numbering.
findings.why_it_matters: Residue numbers are the interface between this document and any structural work someone does downstream. Anyone loading a human AChE structure and looking for Phe330 finds a valine; anyone loading Torpedo and looking for Trp286 finds the wrong residue. Because the two systems are offset by only 2-8 residues in this region, the errors are quiet — a modeller may select a nearby residue and believe the mapping worked. The correspondences are well established and unambiguous, so this is straightforwardly fixable, but as written the binding-site definitions cannot be used and the 'CAS Salt Bridge' error signals that the interaction types were not checked either.
findings.ground_truth: Verified from coordinate files this session. Torpedo californica AChE (PDB 1VOT): CAS Trp84, Tyr130, Phe330, Phe331; catalytic triad Ser200/His440/Glu327; PAS Tyr70, Asp72, Tyr121, Trp279, Tyr334. Human AChE (PDB 4EY7): CAS Trp86, Tyr133, Tyr337, Phe338; catalytic triad Ser203/His447/Glu334; PAS Tyr72, Asp74, Tyr124, Trp286, Tyr341. Equivalences: Torpedo Trp84 = human Trp86; Phe330 = Tyr337; Trp279 = Trp286; Tyr70 = Tyr72; Tyr121 = Tyr124; Asp72 = Asp74. Trp84/Trp86 engages quaternary ammonium and protonated amines by cation-pi interaction, not a salt bridge (Raves et al. 1997, PMID 8989325).
findings.required_fix: Pick one numbering convention — human AChE (UniProt P22303, mature-protein numbering as in PDB 4EY7) is the right choice for a therapeutics platform — and convert every residue reference in app.js:12, 15, 72, 154, 248, 278, 288 and README.md:32, 38 to it. Add an explicit 'numbering: UniProt P22303 / PDB 4EY7' annotation to each binding-site field so the convention is never ambiguous again, and validate residue identities programmatically against the reference structure at build time. Correct 'CAS Salt Bridge' at app.js:12 to 'cation-pi'.

findings.title: No chemistry layer exists: no structure validation, canonicalization, InChIKey, database cross-reference, or computed property anywhere in the codebase
findings.evidence_location: Entire codebase. app.js:477 is the only consumer of the `smiles` field; grep across README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css for rdkit|inchi|pubchem|chembl|canonical|pains|openbabel|logp|tpsa|lipinski returns zero hits in the platform files
findings.what_is_wrong:
The repository presents itself as a cheminformatics platform but contains no cheminformatics. Chemical structures exist only as display strings: app.js:477 interpolates `${data.smiles}` into innerHTML inside a div labelled 'SMILES Formulation'. There is no parser, no canonicalizer, no identifier, no cross-reference and no computed descriptor. Every chemical property presented to the user — molecular formulas in the chemStruct fields, DeltaG values, Kd values, ADMET numbers — is a hand-typed literal in the data structure, not a computed quantity. This is the root cause that permitted MEDCHEM-01 through MEDCHEM-04 and MEDCHEM-08: with no validation pass, a token typo, a missing ring closure, two formula strings, a wrong isomer, two wrong constitutions and universally absent stereochemistry all reached a published repository undetected.

The absence is verifiable rather than inferred: the grep above returns hits only in unrelated directories (memory/SPEC_draft.md, research/memory_systems/surveys.json) and never in the four platform files.

This is worth stating separately from the individual errors because fixing the errors one at a time leaves the mechanism that produced them intact.
findings.why_it_matters: Without a validation layer, every future edit can reintroduce the same class of defect silently, and there is no way for a reader to distinguish a computed value from a typed one — which is the core epistemic problem with the document. Adding the layer is cheap: I installed RDKit into a fresh venv and validated all eight structures against PubChem in a few minutes of wall-clock time in this session, which is the same work the project would need to do once and then run in CI. The gap between what the platform claims ('AI-driven drug discovery platform', README.md:22) and what it implements (a static data-display page) is bridged almost entirely by this one missing component.
findings.ground_truth: Bento AP, Hersey A, Felix E, Landrum G, Gaulton A, Atkinson F, Bellis LJ, De Veij M, Leach AR. An open source chemical structure curation pipeline using RDKit. J Cheminform 2020;12(1):51 (PMID 33431044, DOI 10.1186/s13321-020-00456-1) — the reference implementation, comprising a Checker that tests structure validity and flags serious errors, a Standardizer that normalises to defined conventions, and a GetParent component; used to standardise the ~2 million compounds in ChEMBL and freely available on GitHub and via ChEMBL Beaker. RDKit (https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit) provides MolFromSmiles, MolToSmiles canonicalization, MolToInchiKey, CalcMolFormula, FindPotentialStereo, the Descriptors module and the PAINS FilterCatalog. PubChem PUG-REST and the ChEMBL API provide identity verification by name, InChIKey or connectivity SMILES.
findings.required_fix: Introduce a chemistry module with a build-time gate that, for every compound record, (1) parses the SMILES with RDKit and fails on None; (2) runs the ChEMBL structure_pipeline Checker and Standardizer; (3) computes the full 27-character InChIKey and asserts it against a stored PubChem/ChEMBL reference, failing on mismatch — this single check catches MEDCHEM-02 and MEDCHEM-03; (4) asserts zero Unspecified elements from FindPotentialStereo — this catches MEDCHEM-04; (5) runs the PAINS_A/B/C FilterCatalog and surfaces alerts — this catches MEDCHEM-08; (6) computes MW, formula, TPSA, cLogP, HBD/HBA, rotatable bonds and CNS MPO, and renders those computed values in the UI in place of the hand-typed strings. Store PubChem CID and ChEMBL ID as required fields on every record. Mark every remaining asserted value in the UI with a provenance tag distinguishing computed from literature-cited from estimated, so the reader can tell them apart.

findings.title: Onjisaponin V is conflated with DISS, a structurally unrelated compound, and its formula does not match the reference record
findings.evidence_location: app.js:58 (name 'Onjisaponin V / DISS'), app.js:59 (class), app.js:60 (formula in SMILES field); README.md:37; presenegenin formula at app.js:182 and app.js:328
findings.what_is_wrong:
app.js:58 names a single record 'Onjisaponin V / DISS' and app.js:59 gives its class as 'Triterpenoid Saponin & Oligosaccharide Ester', treating the two names as synonyms for one substance. They are different compounds from different structural classes. DISS is 3,6'-disinapoyl sucrose (PubChem CID 131752949), C34H42O19, MW 754.7 — a disaccharide bis-cinnamate ester with no triterpene at all. Onjisaponin V is a presenegenin-based triterpenoid saponin. Both occur in Polygala tenuifolia, which is presumably the source of the confusion, but they share neither a skeleton nor a mechanism. The record then assigns one merged set of targets and mechanisms (app.js:61-65) to the pair.

Separately, the formula placed in the SMILES field at app.js:60, C58H92O27, does not match the PubChem record for onjisaponin V (CID 177827987, C82H122O41, MW 1763.8). I note that onjisaponin nomenclature is inconsistent across sources, so I hold this specific formula discrepancy at lower confidence than the DISS conflation.

The derived aglycone formula is also wrong and is stated twice: app.js:182 and app.js:328 give 'Presenegenin Aglycone (C30H46O6)' where PubChem CID 21594224 gives presenegenin as C30H46O7, MW 518.7 — one oxygen short.
findings.why_it_matters: The conflated record drives two candidate designs (HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 at app.js:181-188 and MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 at app.js:327-334), both of which declare a presenegenin aglycone warhead with an incorrect formula. A reader trying to source or synthesise the warhead would order against the wrong formula, and a reader trying to trace the AMPK/autophagy mechanism claimed at app.js:64 would find it attributed in the literature to one of these two compounds and not the other. This is the least consequential of the findings and is straightforward to correct, but it compounds the general pattern that no chemical identifier in this repository was checked against a reference database.
findings.ground_truth: 3,6'-Disinapoyl sucrose (DISS): PubChem CID 131752949, C34H42O19, MW 754.7, InChIKey FHIJMQWMMZEFBL-KQQUZDAGSA-N — a sucrose ester of two sinapic acid units, not a saponin. Onjisaponin V: PubChem CID 177827987, C82H122O41, MW 1763.8, InChIKey MYKOTWPDDUNUJG-VNBMPPIYSA-N — a presenegenin-type oleanane triterpenoid saponin. Presenegenin (the aglycone): PubChem CID 21594224, C30H46O7, MW 518.7, InChIKey VGTALXLMFZXQSK-XIZCRSLYSA-N.
findings.required_fix: Split app.js:57-66 into two separate records with their own structures, classes, targets and mechanisms, and cite the specific literature supporting each mechanism to whichever compound it was actually demonstrated for. Correct the presenegenin formula to C30H46O7 at app.js:182 and app.js:328. Attach PubChem CIDs to all three compounds and resolve the onjisaponin V formula against a primary isolation paper, since database and literature formulas for the onjisaponin series are not fully consistent.

literature.title: The Essential Medicinal Chemistry of Curcumin
literature.what_it_provides: The definitive assessment of curcumin as simultaneously a PAINS and an IMPS (invalid metabolic panacea) candidate. Documents that curcumin is unstable above pH 7, reactive as a promiscuous Michael acceptor, redox-active, fluorescent, metal-chelating, aggregation-prone and essentially non-bioavailable orally, and records that despite >120 clinical trials no double-blinded placebo-controlled trial has succeeded. Concludes it is 'a highly improbable lead'.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Directly governs the curcumin record at app.js:48-55 and README.md:36, and the three candidates that use curcumin as a warhead (app.js:162, 298, 338). The platform presents 'Keap1 Cys151 Alkylation' as targeted pharmacology; this paper establishes that the alkylation is non-selective Michael reactivity and is the mechanism of curcumin's assay promiscuity, not of a selective therapeutic effect. Cite it in the record and either drop curcumin as a warhead or supply cysteine-selectivity data and a thiol-reactivity counter-screen.

literature.title: New substructure filters for removal of pan assay interference compounds (PAINS) from screening libraries and for their exclusion in bioassays
literature.what_it_provides: The original PAINS substructure alert set that identifies frequent-hitter scaffolds not caught by conventional reactive-compound filters, and the argument that such compounds are increasingly prevalent in the literature as apparent leads when they are not. Implemented directly in RDKit as FilterCatalogParams.FilterCatalogs.PAINS_A/B/C.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Older than the 10-year window but load-bearing as the ground truth for MEDCHEM-08. Provides the runnable filter to add to the validation gate specified in MEDCHEM-10: once the eight structures parse, running the RDKit PAINS catalogue over them gives an automated, reproducible interference flag per compound to surface in the UI. The curcuminoid and catechol/pyrogallol polyphenol scaffolds in this dataset are exactly what the alert set targets.

literature.title: Structure of acetylcholinesterase complexed with the nootropic alkaloid, (-)-huperzine A
literature.id: PMID:8989325 / DOI:10.1038/nsb0197-57 (Nat Struct Biol 4(1):57-63); coordinates PDB 1VOT
literature.what_it_provides: The 2.5 A crystal structure of the huperzine A-AChE complex, showing an unexpected binding orientation with 'surprisingly few strong direct interactions with protein residues to explain its high affinity', and demonstrating through SAR on structural analogues that the affinity arises from distributed hydrophobic contacts between the intact rigid tricycle and the aromatic residues lining the active-site gorge.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The ground truth for MEDCHEM-06 and MEDCHEM-09. It refutes the 'minimal pharmacophore warhead' premise at README.md:45 and app.js:152 — huperzine A's affinity is not localised in an excisable pyridone. The deposited coordinates are what I measured to obtain the gorge geometry (CAS-PAS 16.1 A, Tyr121/Phe330 free aperture ~1.9 A, ligand enclosed by 26 residues) and the authoritative Torpedo residue numbering. Any redesign should dock the actual proposed conjugate into 1VOT or 4EY7 and report the pose and clash census before asserting a binding mode.

literature.title: An open source chemical structure curation pipeline using RDKit
literature.what_it_provides: The ChEMBL structure curation pipeline: a Checker that tests chemical validity and flags serious structural errors, a Standardizer that normalises structures to defined conventions, and a GetParent component that strips salts and solvents. Used to standardise the ~2 million compounds in ChEMBL; freely available on GitHub and through ChEMBL Beaker webservices.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The reference implementation for the missing chemistry layer in MEDCHEM-10, and the single change that would have prevented MEDCHEM-01 through MEDCHEM-04. Running the Checker over NATURAL_PRODUCTS_DATA would immediately flag the four unparseable strings; adding an InChIKey assertion against PubChem would have caught the baicalein isomer swap and the Rg1/Ginkgolide B constitution errors, which molecular-formula checking alone cannot detect.

literature.title: An Aggregation Advisor for Ligand Discovery
literature.what_it_provides: Establishes colloidal aggregation as the dominant mechanism of artifactual protein inhibition and provides a predictive tool (advisor.bkslab.org) that scores aggregation likelihood from lipophilicity, affinity and similarity to a database of >12,000 known aggregators. Reports that 5.1% of ligands active in the 0.1-10 uM range in the medicinal chemistry literature resemble known aggregators, versus only 0.73% of drug-like commercial compounds — i.e. aggregators are strongly enriched in the published literature.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supports MEDCHEM-08 for the polyphenol and lipophilic-triterpenoid members of the set. Asiatic acid computes here to cLogP 5.03 at MW 489, and salvianolic acid B is a four-catechol polyphenol — both in the physicochemical regime the advisor flags. Run each validated structure through the advisor and record the score in the interference-liability field; require a detergent-control counter-screen before accepting any reported potency for these compounds.

literature.title: Moving beyond rules: the development of a central nervous system multiparameter optimization (CNS MPO) approach to enable alignment of druglike properties
literature.what_it_provides: The CNS MPO desirability algorithm built on six physicochemical parameters (ClogP, ClogD7.4, MW, TPSA, HBD, most basic pKa), validated against 119 marketed CNS drugs, 108 Pfizer CNS candidates and 11,303 diversity compounds. 74% of marketed CNS drugs score >=4 of 6, and higher scores track with favourable permeability, lower P-gp efflux, metabolic stability and safety.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The quantitative standard against which the 3,538-6,137 Da polycationic conjugates of MEDCHEM-07 fail by roughly an order of magnitude on MW alone, before TPSA and HBD are considered. Implement CNS MPO scoring in the validation gate and display the score per candidate; this replaces the asserted-constant ADMET table at app.js:147-395 with a computed, reproducible, method-labelled number.

literature.title: Central Nervous System Multiparameter Optimization Desirability: Application in Drug Discovery
literature.what_it_provides: Prospective validation of CNS MPO on a second wave of candidates designed after the tool's implementation, showing improved ADME alignment, better BBB penetration, residence in lower-risk safety space (low ClogP, high TPSA), fewer compounds sent to exploratory toxicology, and improved survival through regulatory toxicology into first-in-human.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Demonstrates that prospective multiparameter scoring, rather than post hoc assertion, is what moves CNS candidates forward — the exact discipline missing from Section 3 of the README. Use it to justify replacing the uniform 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' constant with a computed desirability profile plus liability flags appropriate to the actual modality.

literature.title: Curcumin May (Not) Defy Science
literature.what_it_provides: The authors' response to community pushback on the 2017 J Med Chem review, reinforcing and clarifying the evidentiary basis for classifying curcumin as an improbable lead.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Useful as the companion citation when documenting the curcumin liability in the compound record, since it addresses the counterarguments a reader is most likely to raise.

literature.title: RDKit: Open-source cheminformatics toolkit
literature.id: https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit (version 2026.3.5, installed and used in this session)
literature.what_it_provides: SMILES parsing and canonicalization, InChI/InChIKey generation, molecular formula and exact/average mass, FindPotentialStereo for stereochemical completeness auditing, the Descriptors module (MolLogP, TPSA, HBD/HBA, rotatable bonds), SMARTS substructure matching, and the PAINS FilterCatalog.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the tool I used to produce every structural claim in this review, and it is the concrete implementation vehicle for the validation gate in MEDCHEM-10. The entire audit — parsing all eight strings, computing formulas and InChIKeys, counting unspecified stereo elements, and diffing against PubChem references — took a few minutes in a fresh venv, which is the full cost of the missing chemistry layer.

literature.title: PDB 4EY7: Crystal structure of recombinant human acetylcholinesterase in complex with donepezil
literature.id: PDB:4EY7 (RCSB; coordinate file downloaded and parsed in this session)
literature.what_it_provides: Human AChE coordinates giving the authoritative human residue numbering (Trp86, Tyr72, Tyr124, Trp286, Tyr337, Phe338, Tyr341, Ser203, His447) and a bound dual-site inhibitor whose maximum intramolecular extent I measured at 15.48 A.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Ground truth for MEDCHEM-09 (it is what shows that human residue 121 is Gly and 330 is Val, falsifying the mixed residue lists at app.js:154 and app.js:248) and the calibration point for MEDCHEM-06: donepezil demonstrates that spanning the CAS-PAS gorge consumes an entire ~15 A small molecule, which is the design idiom a bivalent AChE inhibitor must use instead of a 36-mer peptide.

reviews.overall_assessment:
Verdict: the chemistry layer of this platform does not exist, and the structures that stand in for it are wrong often enough that the Section 1 pharmacophore matrix cannot be used by anyone for any purpose without being rebuilt from primary database records.

The single most compressive finding is that no chemical structure in this repository was ever passed through a parser. Four of the eight SMILES strings fail to parse in RDKit 2026.3.5 (curcumin contains the shorthand token "OCH3"; huperzine A has an unclosed ring-closure label; onjisaponin V and salvianolic acid B have molecular formulas with English glosses sitting in the SMILES field). Of the four that do parse, one is the wrong constitutional isomer (the compound labelled baicalein is 6,7,8-trihydroxyflavone, PubChem CID 14372623, missing exactly the C5-OH on which both its claimed mechanisms depend) and two are constitutionally wrong molecules whose formulas contradict formulas asserted elsewhere in the same file (Rg1 parses to C38H64O14 with no dammarane gem-dimethyl and a C-glycosidic rather than O-glycosidic sugar, while app.js:142 states the correct C42H72O14; ginkgolide B parses to C18H22O8 with one lactone and eight rings, while app.js:370 correctly calls it a six-ring tri-lactone, C20H24O10). Not one structure carries any stereochemistry, so the Rg1 record denotes 2^22 = 4,194,304 distinct molecules and the ginkgolide B and asiatic acid records 4,096 each — while index.html:118 advertises "stereochemistry" as a feature. All of these defects share one cause: the `smiles` field is read exactly once in the entire codebase, at app.js:477, where it is interpolated into innerHTML as text. A single InChIKey assertion against PubChem in CI would have caught six of the eight problems, and it took me a few minutes in a fresh venv to run.

Beyond the structures, three design-level conclusions are firm. First, the stated method — "fusing minimal natural product pharmacophore warheads with AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides" (README.md:45) — is geometrically impossible for its flagship application. Measured from 1VOT: huperzine A sits 4.8 A from Trp84 and 12.6 A below the PAS, enclosed by 26 residues within 6 A, in a gorge whose Tyr121/Phe330 bottleneck leaves ~1.9 A of free aperture after van der Waals. There is no solvent-exposed face for a linker and no channel a 36-mer peptide could traverse; donepezil, the reference dual-site binder, needs its entire 15.5 A length just to span the gorge. Second, none of the 25 conjugates can reach the CNS compartment its own record names: computed masses run 3,538-6,137 Da with net charge to +9, every one of the 22 computable entries violating Ro5 and bRo5 by 7-12x, with no BBB transport mechanism proposed anywhere. Meanwhile the safety table asserts an identical "hERG IC50 > 50 uM" across all 25 chemically distinct entities — a constant, not a prediction, and aimed at the wrong liability, since the recurring KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG scaffold scores an Eisenberg hydrophobic moment of 0.615 at +9 charge, well above melittin (0.353, +5) and magainin 2 (0.455, +3) on the canonical membrane-lytic axes. Third, and the finding I would raise first in any review meeting: two candidates (app.js:277 and app.js:129) open with KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM, which is human Abeta(16-35) verbatim — the KLVFF nucleation motif plus the GAIIGLM cross-beta core — presented as an "Abeta Disruptor" with "Fibril Blockade: 100%" and destined for direct basal-forebrain exposure. That is an amyloid seed labelled as an amyloid inhibitor, and the sign of the pharmacology is inverted. Genuine KLVFF-derived inhibitors work by truncating to the recognition motif and N-methylating or D-substituting it precisely so the conjugate cannot extend the sheet.

There is real credit to record, and it is worth being specific about it. The asiatic acid SMILES at app.js:80 is exactly correct at the constitutional level — it matches PubChem CID 119034's connectivity SMILES character for character, with the right formula C30H48O5 — so at least one structure was sourced properly. Ten of the thirteen molecular formulas hand-typed into the `chemStruct` prose fields are right (Rg1, Rb1, ginkgolide B, bilobalide, ferulic acid, curcumin, baicalein, salvianolic acid B, asiatic acid, huperzine A); only Rg3, presenegenin and onjisaponin V are wrong. Several qualitative pharmacology assignments are genuinely well chosen and match the primary literature: huperzine A engaging the AChE catalytic anionic site via cation-pi at Trp84 is correct per Raves et al. 1997 (and the file gets "cation-pi" right at app.js:15 even while mislabelling it a "salt bridge" at app.js:12); Keap1 Cys151 as the sensor cysteine for electrophilic Nrf2 activators is correct; the ETGE motif as the Keap1 Kelch-binding element and KLVFF as the Abeta self-recognition motif are both real, well-chosen design starting points. The signaling cascade diagrams in index.html:205-259 (TrkB→PI3K/Akt→CREB, Keap1/Nrf2→ARE, GSK-3beta→Wnt/beta-catenin) are textbook-accurate. The underlying domain reading is not naive; what is missing is any mechanism connecting that reading to verified chemical objects.

What would make this credible. The remediation is well defined and mostly mechanical. Replace all eight structures with PubChem isomeric SMILES and add a build-time gate that parses with RDKit, runs the ChEMBL structure_pipeline Checker/Standardizer, asserts the full 27-character InChIKey against a stored reference (not the 14-character skeleton — the flat asiatic acid string matches on the first block and differs only on the second), fails on any Unspecified stereo element, runs the PAINS_A/B/C catalogue, and computes MW/TPSA/cLogP/HBD/CNS MPO for display in place of the typed literals. Store PubChem CID and ChEMBL ID as required fields. Then delete every asserted DeltaG, Kd, pLDDT and ADMET number that no computation produced, and re-derive only those you can actually compute. Retract the peptide-conjugation strategy for the AChE-gorge targets in favour of small-molecule bivalent ligands sized to the measured 16 A span, remove Abeta(16-35) from both records, fix the three malformed sequences (the non-standard 'B' at app.js:130/173/371 and the literal placeholder at app.js:381), specify disulfide connectivity for the 17 multi-cysteine designs, and standardise all AChE residue numbering on human P22303. Add an honest interference-liability field per compound citing Nelson et al. 2017 for curcumin. Done properly, this becomes a modest but genuine natural-product pharmacophore resource. As it currently stands, the claim on README.md:22 to be an "AI-driven drug discovery platform" is not supported by anything in the repository, and I would advise strongly against circulating the FASTA sequences or the safety table to anyone who might act on them.

reviews.discipline: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD in molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology, 17 years post-PhD, running a laboratory on neurotrophin (BDNF/TrkB, NGF/TrkA) signalling, basal forebrain cholinergic systems, and microglial neuroinflammation. Routine hands-on work with hippocampal slice LTP, dendritic spine morphometry, AChE enzymology, and microglial phagocytosis assays; regular reviewer for neuroscience and neuropharmacology journals.
reviews.overall_assessment:
This is not a drug-discovery platform; it is a static web page whose 25 "therapeutics" are hand-written strings. I verified every residue-level claim against the actual UniProt sequences (human AChE P22303, Torpedo AChE P04058, NTRK2 Q16620, KEAP1 Q14145, TREM2 Q9NZC2, CHRNA7 P36544, CHRM1 P11229, GSK3B P49841, FZD8 Q9H461, SLC1A2 P43004, BDNF P23560, NGF P01138, WNT3A P56704, APP P05067, NFE2L2 Q16236) and every "designed" peptide against the protein it is attributed to.

Two findings are dispositive. First, none of the nine "binding-loop peptides" that the platform says were harvested from BDNF, NGF, Wnt3a, TREM2, or the alpha-7 nAChR actually occurs in those proteins — exact and core-substring searches return zero hits in every case (app.js:143, 173, 195, 267, 299). Second, four peptide sequences are byte-identical but are assigned to unrelated targets with different reported dG and Kd (e.g. the same 37-mer is a "TrkB Ig-like D5 binder, Kd 0.85 nM" at app.js:205-208 and an "EAAT2/GLT-1 transporter binder, Kd 3.6 nM" at app.js:361-364). Together these prove that no target-specific design, docking, or scoring was performed for any of the 25 candidates. Everything downstream — the dG values, the Kd values, the pLDDT numbers, the ADMET table, the "leaderboard" — is decoration on strings that have no relationship to their nominal targets.

The residue-level biology is a mix of correct textbook facts and errors that an expert would catch immediately. The AChE binding sites are a species chimera: "Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121" are Torpedo californica numbering (I confirmed all three against P04058) spliced into the same string as the human PAS residues "Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341" (confirmed against P22303), so app.js:154 describes one enzyme in two incompatible coordinate systems. The pharmacology is inverted in places that matter clinically: a 36-mer polycationic peptide is claimed to clamp both the AChE catalytic anionic site and the peripheral anionic site, which is sterically impossible for a peptide in a ~20 Angstrom-deep, narrow gorge, and the platform then claims "complete" ACh-degradation blockade with "+350% synaptic ACh," "Seizure Index 0.01," and "Peripheral Side Effects: None" — that combination is the pharmacology of organophosphate cholinergic crisis, not of a nootropic. Two candidates are labelled "PAM" while the residues listed for them are the orthosteric agonist sites (alpha-7 Tyr188/Trp149/Tyr195; M1 Tyr381), and the genuine alpha-7 type-II PAM site is an intrasubunit transmembrane cavity a linear peptide cannot reach. The M1/M2 microglial dichotomy that organises an entire fifth of the pipeline was formally deprecated by the field a decade ago. The efficacy numbers (+280% LTP, +310% spine density, +420% phagocytosis) are not physiologically interpretable quantities and, taken literally, describe pathology rather than enhancement.

Credit where it is due, and there is real credit. The Keap1 Kelch-domain residue set (Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483, Ser602) is exactly right — these are the canonical Nrf2-ETGE hot-spot residues from the 2FLU structure, and I confirmed all four identities. Keap1 Cys151 is correctly identified as a BTB-domain electrophile sensor. The GSK-3beta pocket (Val135, Asp133, Lys85) is correct and canonical. The alpha-7 aromatic-box residues are correct in mature numbering, and the M1 residues Tyr381/Trp164 are real residues — the error is what they are labelled as, not what they are. The "Abeta disruptor" peptide KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM is genuinely Abeta16-35, the correct self-recognition element. "TrkB Ig-like D5 domain" is correct nomenclature and correctly localises to residues 295-365. Asp298 is genuinely an aspartate inside d5. And the strategic ideas — dual-site AChE inhibitors that also block PAS-driven Abeta fibrillogenesis, Keap1-Nrf2 PPI decoys, TREM2 agonism, EAAT2 upregulation — are all real, active, defensible programmes in the field. The problem is not the ambition; it is that the execution consists of plausible-sounding strings with fabricated numbers attached, published under language ("state-of-the-art," "real sequence-driven," "AlphaFold3-designed," "rigorous computational safety screening") that asserts work which was not done.

Ironically, the repository already contains the exact tooling needed to have caught almost all of this: .agents/skills/ ships UniProt, PDB, ChEMBL, AlphaFold-DB, and PubMed skills. Not one residue or sequence in the platform was checked against them. My recommendation is that the platform must not be presented as a drug-discovery result. It should either be relabelled unambiguously as a UI mock-up with synthetic placeholder data, or rebuilt so that every residue is pulled from UniProt/PDB at load time and every affinity comes from an actual computation with a stated method.

findings.title: The "binding-loop peptides" do not occur in the proteins they are attributed to — every claimed natural-sequence provenance is false
findings.evidence_location: app.js:143 (X1 sequence, "BDNF Loop-5" per README.md:60); app.js:267 (B3, "NGF Loop-1" per README.md:76); app.js:299 (M1, "Trem2 Peptide" per README.md:81); app.js:195 (P1, "alpha-7 nAChR ECD Peptide" per README.md:67); app.js:173 and app.js:371 (X4/A3, "Wnt3a Loop" per README.md:63); app.js:163 (X3, "Nrf2 ETGE" per README.md:62)
findings.what_is_wrong: I searched each peptide, and its interior core substring, against the actual UniProt sequence of the protein it is credited to. Zero matches in every case. "BDNF Loop-5" CVDRENPVEWVRAC does not appear anywhere in human BDNF (P23560; mature chain HSDPARRGELSVCDSISEWVTAADKKTAVDMSGGTVTVLEKVPVSKGQLKQYFYETKCNPMGYTKEGCRGIDKRHWNSQCRTTQSYVRALTMDSKKRIGWRFIRIDTSCVCTLTIKRGR) — and neurotrophins have four beta-hairpin loops (L1-L4), so "Loop-5" is not a structure that exists. "NGF Loop-1" EPKHVNCDRENP is absent from NGF (P01138). "Trem2 Peptide" GRLVGHPWECDR is absent from TREM2 (Q9NZC2). "alpha-7 nAChR ECD Peptide" SEAEFRLFRDVW is absent from CHRNA7 (P36544). Two peptides are degraded copies of real motifs rather than absent: the "Wnt3a Loop" CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWG is a corrupted version of the genuine WNT3A segment CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP at position 203 (L->M, EVK->STK, plus an illegal residue B), and the "Nrf2 ETGE" DEETGEFLFQLP is a mangled version of the real Nrf2 Neh2 sequence DEETGEFLPIQP at residues 77-88 of NFE2L2 (Q16236) — first eight residues correct, tail scrambled. The cysteine spacing of the recurring "TrkB" peptides (…CPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH, app.js:205) is EGF-like-repeat architecture, which is not found anywhere in TrkB — TrkB-d5 is an Ig-like C2-set domain with no such cysteine ladder.
findings.why_it_matters: The entire premise of Section 2 of the README is that the 25 candidates were built by "fusing minimal natural product pharmacophore warheads with AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides" derived from the endogenous ligands. If the loops are not from the ligands, there is no rational basis for any of the binding claims, and a reader with a real target-validation budget could spend months and a five- to six-figure peptide-synthesis and SPR campaign chasing sequences that have no relationship to the receptors named. A pharmacologist skimming the README would reasonably assume "BDNF Loop-5" and "NGF Loop-1" are literature-sourced epitopes; both are inventions.
findings.ground_truth: Neurotrophin receptor-binding determinants are known experimentally. BDNF/NT-4 engage TrkB through the membrane-proximal Ig-like domain d5 (Ultsch et al., PDB 1WWB, J Mol Biol 1999; Banfield et al., NT-4/5:TrkB-d5 complex, PDB 1HCF, Structure 2001), and the epitope is discontinuous — formed by beta-hairpin loops L1/L2/L4 and the N-terminal segment across both protomers of the disulfide-linked cystine-knot dimer. It cannot be reduced to one linear 14-mer. Wnt engages the Frizzled CRD principally through a palmitoleoyl lipid on a serine at the tip of the Wnt "thumb" inserting into a hydrophobic CRD groove, plus an "index finger" contact (Janda et al., Science 2012, PDB 4F0A) — a synthetic peptide cannot reproduce a covalently lipidated interface. The genuine Nrf2 Keap1-binding motif is the DxETGE beta-hairpin at Nrf2 77-88 (Lo et al., EMBO J 2006, PDB 2FLU).
findings.required_fix: Delete every claimed natural-sequence provenance that cannot be reproduced by an exact substring search against the cited UniProt accession, or replace each peptide with the genuine segment plus its UniProt accession and residue range (e.g. "Nrf2 76-88, Q16236, LDEETGEFLPIQ"). Add an automated CI check that, for every entry declaring a source protein, fetches that UniProt sequence and asserts the substring is present; fail the build otherwise. The .agents/skills/uniprot-database and ncbi-sequence-fetch skills already in this repo do exactly this.

findings.title: Four peptide sequences are byte-identical but assigned to unrelated targets with different binding energies, proving no per-target computation was performed
findings.evidence_location: app.js:153 vs app.js:247 (same 36-mer, AChE, dG -16.2/Kd 2.1 nM vs dG -17.5/Kd 0.65 nM); app.js:205-208 vs app.js:361-364 (same 37-mer: "TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Thr315, Glu319)", Kd 0.85 nM vs "Astrocytic Glutamate Transporter EAAT2/GLT-1 (Thr368, Lys490)", Kd 3.6 nM); app.js:195-198 vs app.js:319-322 (same 41-mer: "alpha-7 nAChR ECD (Tyr188, Trp149, Tyr195)", Kd 1.8 nM vs "TLR4/MD-2 Complex (Arg264, Lys341, Glu439)", Kd 3.8 nM); app.js:173-176 vs app.js:371-374 (same 31-mer: "Frizzled-8 CRD", Kd 1.2 nM vs "ZO-1/Occludin Complex", Kd 2.8 nM)
findings.what_is_wrong: I extracted all 25 sequences programmatically and grouped them. Four sequences each appear twice. Two of the duplicates are assigned to the SAME target (AChE) yet carry different dG and Kd — an identical molecule against an identical enzyme cannot have two affinities. The other three duplicates are assigned to structurally and functionally unrelated targets: a receptor tyrosine kinase Ig domain versus a SLC1-family membrane transporter; a Cys-loop receptor extracellular domain versus a TLR4/MD-2 leucine-rich-repeat complex; a Frizzled cysteine-rich domain versus an intracellular MAGUK scaffold (ZO-1) that a secreted peptide could not physically reach. Each pairing carries a different, precisely stated nanomolar Kd.
findings.why_it_matters: This is internal proof that no docking, no free-energy calculation, and no target-specific structure prediction was ever run. The numbers in the affinity fields — which drive the leaderboard (app.js:869-895), the benchmark bar chart (app.js:1049-1103), and the README's headline "-19.5 kcal/mol Peak Binding Energy" — are literary, not computational. Any collaborator or investor reading the pipeline as a triaged candidate list is being shown a ranking with no underlying measurement.
findings.ground_truth: A binding free energy is a property of a specific complex. For a single ligand and a single receptor at fixed conditions there is exactly one dG and one Kd, related by dG = RT ln(Kd); at 298 K, RT = 0.592 kcal/mol, so Kd = 2.1 nM corresponds to dG = -11.8 kcal/mol and Kd = 0.65 nM to dG = -12.4 kcal/mol — neither matches the -16.2 and -17.5 stated, and the stated pair is not even self-consistent with the stated Kd pair. Cross-reactivity of a single peptide against unrelated folds at low-nanomolar affinity is essentially unprecedented and, if real, would be reported as a serious selectivity liability rather than as five separate optimised drugs.
findings.required_fix: Make every sequence unique per target, or, if reuse is intentional, state it explicitly and report one measured/computed affinity per (ligand, target) pair from a named method (e.g. Rosetta ddG, MM-GBSA, FoldX, or an experimental SPR value) with the software version and inputs. Add a uniqueness assertion over the sequence field and a consistency assertion that dG and Kd satisfy dG = RT ln(Kd) within stated error.

findings.title: AChE binding sites mix Torpedo californica and human residue numbering inside the same string
findings.evidence_location: app.js:154 ("AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)"); app.js:248 ("AChE Catalytic Gorge (Trp84, Phe330, Trp286, Tyr341)"); app.js:288 ("AChE CAS/PAS (Trp84/Trp286)"); app.js:12 and app.js:15 (Huperzine A: "Trp84, Phe330 (CAS Salt Bridge) … Trp279 (PAS)"); app.js:72 (Salvianolic acid B: "AChE PAS Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341"); README.md:32 ("CAS: Trp84, Phe330 … PAS (Trp286)"); README.md:38
findings.what_is_wrong: I tested each residue against both sequences. In human AChE (UniProt P22303, mature numbering, signal peptide 1-31 removed), position 84 is Glu, 330 is Val, 121 is Gly, and 279 is Gln — none of the claimed residues exists. In Torpedo californica AChE (P04058, mature numbering, signal 1-21 removed), positions 84/330/121/279 are exactly Trp/Phe/Tyr/Trp. So "Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121, Trp279" is Torpedo numbering. Meanwhile "Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341" and Asp74 are correct human residues (all verified against P22303). app.js:154 therefore describes the catalytic anionic site of an electric-ray enzyme and the peripheral anionic site of the human enzyme as if they were one protein, and app.js:12 compounds the error by pairing Torpedo Trp279 with the human Trp286 elsewhere in the same file — these are the same residue in two species, listed as if they were two distinct sites. A secondary error: app.js:12 labels the Trp84/Phe330 interaction a "CAS Salt Bridge," but app.js:15 correctly calls the same interaction cation-pi. Aromatic residues cannot form salt bridges; the gorge has no anionic site in the classical sense (this was the central finding of the 1991 Torpedo structure).
findings.why_it_matters: A reader designing a mutagenesis experiment, a docking grid, or a selectivity assay against human AChE would build W84A/F330A constructs that do not exist, or centre a docking box on the wrong coordinates. Species numbering confusion in the AChE literature is a classic, well-documented trap, and publishing a "human AChE" target sheet in Torpedo numbering propagates it. Because five of the 25 candidates (X2, B1, B4, B5, and the bispecific CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10) are AChE-directed, the error contaminates a fifth of the pipeline.
findings.ground_truth: Human AChE (P22303) mature numbering: catalytic triad Ser203/Glu334/His447; CAS/acyl pocket aromatics Trp86 (the cation-pi anchor for the quaternary ammonium), Tyr337, Tyr124, Phe295/Phe297; PAS at the gorge mouth Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr124, Asp74, Tyr341. The Torpedo equivalents are Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121, Trp279, Tyr70, Asp72, Tyr334. Note that Torpedo Phe330 maps to human Tyr337, not to a phenylalanine, so a naive renumbering would still be wrong. The gorge aromatics, not an anionic site, bind the quaternary ammonium (Sussman et al., Science 1991, PMID 1678899). Huperzine A binding is resolved in PDB 1VOT (Raves et al., Nat Struct Biol 1997), in Torpedo numbering.
findings.required_fix: Pick one convention, state it explicitly ("human AChE, UniProt P22303, mature numbering"), and convert consistently: Trp84->Trp86, Phe330->Tyr337, Tyr121->Tyr124, Trp279->Trp286. Correct "CAS Salt Bridge" to "cation-pi" at app.js:12. Where a structure is cited in Torpedo numbering (e.g. 1VOT), give both, e.g. "Trp86 (human; Trp84 in Torpedo, PDB 1VOT)".

findings.title: A 36-mer polycationic peptide cannot clamp both the AChE CAS and PAS, and the claimed "complete blockade with zero seizure risk" inverts cholinergic toxicology
findings.evidence_location: app.js:153-158 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG, "Dual-clamps the AChE gorge entrance (PAS) and catalytic site (CAS)"); app.js:247-252 (BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, same 36-mer, "Completely blocks acetylcholine degradation … elevating synaptic ACh levels by +350%", safety "Seizure Index: 0.01 | Peripheral Side Effects: None"); README.md:61 and README.md:74; README.md:100 ("Seizure & Excitotoxicity Risk: Negligible")
findings.what_is_wrong: Two separate errors. (i) Steric: the AChE active-site gorge is roughly 20 Angstroms deep, narrow, and lined with aromatics, with a bottleneck of a few Angstroms; the catalytic serine sits near its base. A 36-residue peptide with a formal charge of about +9 and four tryptophans cannot thread that gorge to contact Trp86/Tyr337 while simultaneously occupying the PAS at the mouth. The definitive precedent is fasciculin-2, a 61-residue three-finger toxin that inhibits AChE almost completely by capping the PAS and occluding the gorge entrance — it does not, and cannot, reach the catalytic site (PDB 1FSS, Bourne et al., Structure 1995). A peptide of this class is a PAS blocker, full stop. (ii) Pharmacological: "complete" blockade of ACh degradation with "+350% synaptic ACh," "no peripheral side effects," and a seizure index of 0.01 is not an achievable safety profile — it is the described mechanism of organophosphate and carbamate poisoning. Near-total AChE inhibition produces cholinergic crisis: status epilepticus, bronchorrhoea, bradycardia, and respiratory failure. The platform asserts maximal target engagement and zero on-target toxicity simultaneously, which is a contradiction in terms for this target.
findings.why_it_matters: AChE is the single most safety-constrained target in the cholinergic pharmacopoeia, and the therapeutic index is defined by submaximal, titrated inhibition. A document that presents "complete blockade" as a design goal and pairs it with a fabricated near-zero seizure index would, if acted on, drive dose escalation toward the exact toxicity the field spends its effort avoiding. This is the finding with the clearest path to physical harm if the platform were ever used to inform dosing or candidate selection.
findings.ground_truth: Clinically, cholinesterase inhibition in Alzheimer's disease is deliberately submaximal and plateaus: donepezil showed a red-blood-cell AChE inhibition plateau of 76-84% at plasma concentrations above 50 ng/mL, with efficacy correlated to that inhibition and dose limited by cholinergic adverse events (Rogers & Friedhoff, Dementia 1996, PMID 8915035). On-target dose-limiting effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, bradycardia and syncope; supratherapeutic inhibition causes seizures. Separately, the PAS is a legitimate and valuable target in its own right: PAS ligands block AChE-catalysed acceleration of Abeta fibril assembly (Inestrosa et al., Neuron 1996, PMID 8608006), which is exactly the secondary mechanism the platform claims — so the PAS half of the design is sound and should be kept.
findings.required_fix: Reclassify X2, B1, B4 and B5 as PAS-directed ligands only, and delete the CAS engagement claim for all peptide-only constructs (a small-molecule warhead conjugated on a linker could plausibly reach the CAS, but that requires an explicit linker-length calculation, not an assertion). Replace "completely blocks" and "+350% ACh" with a target inhibition range consistent with a therapeutic index (e.g. 40-80% enzyme inhibition) and remove the fabricated seizure indices entirely until a real convulsant-liability assessment exists. Add an explicit on-target cholinergic-toxicity section citing the organophosphate precedent.

findings.title: TrkB d5 domain is correctly identified but four of six named binding residues are the wrong amino acids, and the "BDNF Loop-5 dimerizer" concept ignores the reproducibility record of TrkB agonist pharmacology
findings.evidence_location: app.js:144 ("TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333)"); app.js:22 and README.md:33 ("TrkB Asp298, Glu319"); app.js:184 ("TrkB D5 (Asp298, Glu319)"); app.js:206 ("TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Thr315, Glu319)"); app.js:25 ("induce receptor dimerization"); README.md:60; app.js:126 ("CogBDNF-Mimic-04", "TrkB Dimerization Interface")
findings.what_is_wrong: The domain assignment is right and deserves credit: UniProt Q16620 annotates Ig-like C2-type 2 (the d5 domain, in the standard d1-d5 Trk nomenclature) at residues 295-365, so residues 298-342 do fall inside it. But the residue identities mostly do not check out. Against Q16620 full-length numbering: 298 is Asp (correct), 342 is Tyr (correct), but 319 is Tyr not Glu, 315 is Leu not Thr, 312 is Lys not Val, and 333 is Lys not Leu. Two of six correct is what random guessing constrained to the right domain would give. I also tested mature numbering (signal peptide 1-31 removed, offset +31): zero of six match, so the errors are not a numbering-convention artefact. Separately, "Glu319" is asserted as a BDNF-contact residue in four places, but there is no experimental BDNF-TrkB complex structure to derive it from — a PDB full-text search returns 1WWB (apo human TrkB ligand-binding domain), 1HCF (NT-4/5 bound to TrkB-d5), 5MO9 (TrkB LBD with an antibody Fab), and kinase-domain entries, but no BDNF-TrkB complex.
findings.why_it_matters: Anyone attempting to validate the design would order D298A/E319A TrkB constructs; E319A is not a mutation of the residue the platform thinks it is targeting, and the resulting negative result would be uninterpretable. More broadly, presenting a linear peptide as a "TrkB dimerizer" without engaging the field's reproducibility history is misleading to a non-specialist reader: several widely used "small-molecule TrkB agonists" failed to activate TrkB in rigorous multiplexed assays, and the field now regards claimed TrkB agonism as requiring unusually strong controls.
findings.ground_truth: Human TrkB (NTRK2, Q16620): LRRNT 32-61, LRR1 92-113, LRR2 116-137, LRRCT 148-196, Ig-like C2-type 1 (d4) 197-282, Ig-like C2-type 2 (d5) 295-365, kinase 538-807. d5 is the principal neurotrophin-binding domain (Ultsch et al., PDB 1WWB, J Mol Biol 1999; Banfield et al., NT-4/5:TrkB-d5, PDB 1HCF, Structure 2001). Boltaev et al.
