(Sci Signal 2017, PMID 28831019) developed complementary quantitative assays of TrkB phosphorylation, downstream signalling and gene expression and could not reproduce receptor activation by the reported small-molecule TrkB agonists, concluding that results obtained with these compounds must be interpreted with caution. Zagrebelsky & Korte (Neural Regen Res 2024, PMID 37488840) review the current TrkB-agonist landscape and note that agonist antibodies — which are bivalent and can genuinely crosslink the receptor — are the more credible modality, while questioning whether any TrkB agonist reverses pathology per se.
findings.required_fix: Replace the invented residue list with contacts read directly from PDB 1HCF (NT-4/5:TrkB-d5) and state the source and numbering convention, or drop the residue list and say only "TrkB d5 (Q16620, residues 295-365)". Remove the claim that a monovalent linear peptide induces TrkB dimerisation, or support it with a stated bivalent architecture and a dimerisation assay design. Add an explicit caveat citing Boltaev et al. 2017 wherever TrkB agonism is claimed.

findings.title: Two candidates are labelled positive allosteric modulators while the residues listed for them are the orthosteric agonist sites, and the real alpha-7 PAM site is inaccessible to a peptide
findings.evidence_location: app.js:193-200 (PfcACh-PAM-P1: "alpha-7 nAChR Extracellular Domain (ECD) (Tyr188, Trp149, Tyr195)" with mechanism "Allosterically potentiates cortical basal acetylcholine responsiveness"); app.js:255-262 (BasalM1-PAM-B2: "M1 Muscarinic Acetylcholine Receptor (M1 mAChR) (Tyr381, Trp164)" with mechanism "Potentiates Gq/11 coupling"); README.md:67 and README.md:75; app.js:78 ("M1 PAM" in tri-functional B5)
findings.what_is_wrong: The residues are real — I verified Tyr188, Trp149 and Tyr195 against CHRNA7 (P36544) mature numbering and Tyr381/Trp164 against CHRM1 (P11229) — but they are the wrong kind of site for the stated mechanism. Trp149 (loop B) and Tyr188/Tyr195 (loop C) are the canonical aromatic box of the alpha-7 ORTHOSTERIC acetylcholine binding site; a ligand occupying them is an agonist or competitive antagonist, definitionally not a PAM. Likewise M1 Tyr381 is part of the orthosteric tyrosine lid (with Tyr106, Tyr404, Tyr408, Asp105), not the allosteric vestibule. A second, independent problem: the best-characterised alpha-7 type-II PAM site is an intrasubunit cavity in the transmembrane domain, buried in the lipid bilayer — a 41-residue hydrophilic peptide cannot reach it. And PAM activity requires modulating the agonist-induced gating equilibrium without occupying the agonist site, which a peptide sitting in the aromatic box would preclude by construction.
findings.why_it_matters: PAM versus orthosteric agonist is the single most consequential distinction in cholinergic drug design for cognition: PAMs preserve the temporal and spatial pattern of endogenous ACh release and avoid the receptor desensitisation and peripheral cholinergic toxicity that sank orthosteric alpha-7 and M1 agonist programmes. A document that labels an orthosteric-site binder a PAM, and then asserts "Receptor Desensitization: Low" (app.js:199) as a consequence, gets the safety rationale exactly backwards — orthosteric alpha-7 agonism causes rapid, profound desensitisation.
findings.ground_truth: For alpha-7, PNU-120596 potentiates without altering the orthosteric agonist binding site; the modulation is transduced through a network of gating-interface and transmembrane residues (Marotta, Lester & Dougherty, Chem Biol 2015, PMID 26211363). Docking and MD analyses place type-II PAMs including PNU-120596 in an intrasubunit transmembrane cavity, with M1-Ser223 and M3-Ile281 as key contacts, and type-I PAMs at an ECD or ECD-TMD junction site (Targowska-Duda et al., J Biomol Struct Dyn 2018, PMID 29363414). For muscarinic receptors, the common allosteric site is the extracellular vestibule above the orthosteric pocket, structurally defined for M2 with LY2119620 (PDB 4MQT, Nature 2013) and for M1/M4 orthosteric architecture in PDB 5CXV (Thal et al., Nature 2016).
findings.required_fix: Either relabel P1 and B2 as orthosteric ligands and rewrite their mechanism and desensitisation claims accordingly, or keep the PAM label and replace the residue lists with genuine allosteric-site residues (alpha-7 intrasubunit TMD cavity; M1 extracellular vestibule) — and in that case explain how a peptide reaches an intramembrane cavity, which for alpha-7 it cannot. Remove "Receptor Desensitization: Low" until it is supported by a stated assay.

findings.title: Efficacy magnitudes (+280% LTP, +310% spine density, +350% ACh, +420% phagocytosis) are dimensionally undefined and, read literally, describe pathology rather than cognitive enhancement
findings.evidence_location: app.js:148 ("Long-Term Potentiation (LTP +280%)"); app.js:188 ("increasing dendritic spine density by +310%"); app.js:252 ("elevating synaptic ACh levels by +350%"); app.js:334 ("Lysosomal Clearance: +420%"); app.js:200 ("restoring working memory span by +240%"); app.js:240 ("doubling cortical information processing speed"); README.md:60, 64, 67, 74, 84
findings.what_is_wrong: None of these numbers is a well-formed quantity. LTP is conventionally reported as fEPSP slope or amplitude as a percentage OF baseline (e.g. 150-200% of baseline after theta-burst stimulation in CA1), so "+280%" is ambiguous between "180% of baseline" and "380% of baseline"; the latter exceeds what CA1 Schaffer-collateral synapses can express. Worse, more LTP is not monotonically better: potentiation saturates, and saturated hippocampal LTP impairs rather than improves learning, because there is no residual dynamic range left to encode new information. "Spine density +310%" is physically implausible — CA1 pyramidal basal and apical oblique dendrites carry roughly 1-3 spines per micrometre; a 4.1-fold increase implies 4-12 spines per micrometre, beyond the geometric packing limit of the dendritic shaft, and pathological spine overproduction is a feature of fragile X and related synaptopathies, not of enhanced cognition. "Working memory span +240%" is not a defined psychometric operation on a span score. All of these are stated with no assay, no species, no n, no baseline, no variance, and no statistic.
findings.why_it_matters: These figures are the platform's headline efficacy claims and appear in the README's public-facing summary. Presented without units or method they read as spectacular preclinical data; interpreted correctly by a slice electrophysiologist or a spine morphometrist they are either meaningless or describe a lesion. A reader budgeting a validation study cannot design a powered experiment against an endpoint that has no operational definition, and a reader who takes them at face value would conclude the compounds have been characterised in vivo when nothing has been measured at all.
findings.ground_truth: Realistic effect sizes: theta-burst or high-frequency-induced CA1 LTP typically reaches 130-200% of baseline fEPSP slope, with strong protocols approaching 200-250%; a pharmacological enhancer that raises potentiation by 20-50% relative to vehicle is a large, publishable effect. Saturation of hippocampal LTP impairs spatial learning — rats with less than 10% residual potentiation were disrupted in the water maze while those retaining capacity for further potentiation were not (Moser, Krobert, Moser & Morris, Science 1998, PMID 9748165) — so maximising LTP is not a coherent therapeutic objective. Spine density changes reported for genuine plasticity manipulations are typically 10-40%. Microdialysis studies of cholinesterase inhibitors report hippocampal/cortical ACh increases in the range of roughly 100-500% of basal, but that is a percentage OF basal in a specific compartment, not a compound-wide constant, and it must be reconciled with the cholinergic toxicity ceiling.
findings.required_fix: For every efficacy number: state the assay (e.g. "fEPSP slope, Schaffer collateral-CA1, 60 min post-TBS, acute mouse hippocampal slice"), the units and referent ("% of pre-tetanus baseline"), species, n, and dispersion — or delete the number. Replace open-ended "+X%" framing with a target range bounded by physiology and an explicit statement of the saturation/occlusion ceiling for LTP, citing Moser et al. 1998. Cap spine-density claims at biologically attainable densities.

findings.title: The M1/M2 microglial polarization dichotomy organising an entire brain-region module was formally deprecated by the field a decade ago
findings.evidence_location: app.js:109-114 (BRAIN_REGIONS_DATA.microglia: "Microglia (M1/M2 State Polarization)", "shifting inflammatory M1 microglia to neuroprotective M2 phagocytic states"); app.js:304 ("shift inflammatory M1 microglia into plaque-clearing M2 phagocytic phenotypes"); README.md:80 ("Microglia M2 Polarization"); README.md:81 ("M1 to Abeta phagocytic M2 transition"); README.md:85; index.html:186 ("Microglia (M1/M2 State)"); index.html:100
findings.what_is_wrong: The whole fourth region of the pipeline is built on a binary classification that the microglial field has explicitly rejected. M1/M2 was borrowed from in vitro macrophage stimulation paradigms (LPS/IFN-gamma versus IL-4) and never mapped onto microglial biology in vivo; single-cell transcriptomics instead reveals a continuum of context-dependent states (disease-associated microglia, white-matter-associated microglia, interferon-responsive, proliferative-region-associated, and others) that do not resolve into two poles and that decouple "inflammatory" from "non-phagocytic". Framing therapeutic success as "M1 to M2 transition" therefore describes a state change that cannot be measured, because the endpoint states are not real categories. A compounding presentational problem: the drugs in this module are named M1 through M5, so "MicroTrem2-Agonist-M1" is a drug called M1 whose stated purpose is to abolish M1 microglia, and "BasalM1-PAM-B2" uses M1 to mean the muscarinic receptor — three incompatible meanings of "M1" in one dataset.
findings.why_it_matters: Any experimental plan derived from this module would specify the wrong readouts — an iNOS/Arg1 or CD86/CD206 ratio rather than a state-resolved transcriptomic or functional panel — and would be rejected at review. In a therapeutic context the dichotomy is actively harmful because it implies that suppressing "M1" and promoting "M2" are the same axis, when TREM2-dependent disease-associated microglia are simultaneously highly activated and beneficial for plaque compaction. The naming collision would also cause real confusion in any downstream data table.
findings.ground_truth: Ransohoff (Nat Neurosci 2016, PMID 27459405, "A polarizing question: do M1 and M2 microglia exist?") argues that microglial polarization was never established by research findings, that the schema was adopted as an interpretive convenience before microglial ontogeny was understood, and that the terminology now hinders rather than aids progress and should be discarded. Paolicelli et al. (Neuron 2022, PMID 36327895, "Microglia states and nomenclature: A field at its crossroads"), a consensus paper with ~90 authors including Stevens, Colonna, Haass, Prinz, de Strooper and Ransohoff, states that the dualistic good/bad classification is inconsistent with the repertoire of microglial states and provides a conceptual framework and explicit nomenclature recommendations for researchers, reviewers and editors.
findings.required_fix: Replace "M1/M2 polarization" throughout with state-and-function language consistent with the Paolicelli et al. 2022 recommendations — name the specific functional endpoint being targeted (e.g. "enhanced Abeta phagocytic capacity and lysosomal processing", "reduced IL-1beta/TNF-alpha release") and, where a transcriptional state is meant, name it (e.g. DAM/ARM signature). Cite Ransohoff 2016 and Paolicelli et al. 2022. Separately, rename the MicroDrugs M1-M5 series to avoid collision with muscarinic M1 and with the deprecated microglial M1 label.

findings.title: TREM2 agonism by a linear monovalent 12-mer is not a plausible mechanism, and the clinical precedent for TREM2 agonism is presented without its negative outcome
findings.evidence_location: app.js:299-304 (MicroTrem2-Agonist-M1: sequence GRLVGHPWECDRRACPCYRGFWRERACPDCH, "Trem2 Extracellular Ig-like Domain (Arg47, Asp87, Lys112)", "Promotes Trem2/DAP12 signaling", Kd 0.52 nM); app.js:337-344 (MicroDual-Trem2-Nrf2-M5); README.md:81 and README.md:85; app.js:129 ("CogAbeta-Clearer-08", "Trem2 Phagocytic Tag")
findings.what_is_wrong: Three problems. (i) Mechanism: TREM2 signals through the ITAM-bearing adaptor DAP12, and receptor activation requires clustering/crosslinking so that Src-family kinases can trans-phosphorylate the ITAM and recruit SYK. A monovalent linear 12-mer binding one Ig domain cannot crosslink the receptor; at best it is a competitive ligand-site blocker, i.e. an antagonist. Every credible TREM2 agonist in development is bivalent (an IgG). (ii) Residues: I checked against Q9NZC2 — Arg47 and Asp87 are the correct amino acids at those positions and Arg47 is genuinely on the AD-risk functional surface (credit for that), but position 112 is Ser, not Lys, and 112 is the boundary of the Ig-like V-type domain (annotated 29-112). Asp87 is acidic, which is hard to reconcile with a ligand surface whose defining property is a basic patch that engages anionic lipids. (iii) Provenance: the peptide GRLVGHPWECDR does not occur in TREM2 or, per the design logic, in any TREM2 ligand — see MOLBIO-01. (iv) Framing: the README presents TREM2 agonism as a solved route to amyloid clearance with "Cytokine Storm Risk: Negligible", omitting that the only TREM2 agonist antibody to reach Phase 2 in AD failed and produced ARIA-like MRI findings.
findings.why_it_matters: TREM2 is one of the most consequential genetic targets in AD and one of the most heavily invested; a document asserting a nanomolar peptide agonist with negligible immune risk, and no mention of the clinical readout, materially misrepresents the state of the field to anyone using it for target prioritisation. The safety framing is the sharper problem: TREM2 agonism in patients was associated with ARIA-like imaging abnormalities, which is the opposite of "negligible" risk.
findings.ground_truth: The TREM2 Ig-like V-type ectodomain structure identified a functional surface on which AD risk variants (including R47H) cluster and which mediates ligand binding, while Nasu-Hakola mutations are buried and destabilise the fold (Kober et al., eLife 2016, PMID 27995897, PDB 5ELI); a later structure resolved wild-type and R47H Ig domains including a phosphatidylserine complex, establishing anionic phospholipid as a direct ligand (PDB 5UD7, 6B8O, J Biol Chem 2018). Physiological TREM2 ligands are anionic and lipidic — phospholipids, sulfatide, lipoproteins and apolipoproteins, and Abeta oligomers — engaged via the basic surface patch. Clinically, the humanized TREM2 agonistic mAb AL002 in 381 participants with early AD showed sustained CNS target engagement (reduced CSF sTREM2, increased osteopontin) but did NOT meet its primary endpoint on CDR-SB at 96 weeks, and the most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events were MRI changes resembling ARIA (Mummery et al., Nat Med 2026, PMID 41787076, NCT04592874).
findings.required_fix: Either reclassify the TREM2 constructs as ligand-site binders of unknown functional sign (and remove "Agonist" from the name and "Promotes Trem2/DAP12 signaling" from the mechanism), or specify a bivalent/multimeric architecture and a defined clustering readout (SYK phosphorylation, pERK, or a reporter assay). Correct Lys112 to a real residue on the Kober functional surface and justify Asp87 against the published anionic-ligand-binding surface. Add the AL002 Phase 2 outcome and the ARIA-like safety signal wherever TREM2 agonism is presented, and delete "Cytokine Storm Risk: Negligible".

findings.title: The Keap1 module conflates two mechanistically distinct interventions in different domains, and the ETGE decoy strategy is presented without the hinge-and-latch constraint — though the Kelch residue set itself is correct
findings.evidence_location: app.js:52 and app.js:54 (Curcumin: "Keap1 Cys151 (Covalent Alkylation)" -> Nrf2 translocation); app.js:161-168 (HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3: curcumin methoxyphenol warhead, sequence DEETGEFLFQLPQLDEETGEWRWYCPWC, "Keap1 Kelch Domain (Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483, Ser602)"); app.js:307-314 (MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2); index.html:230 ("Keap1 Cys151 Alkylation / Decoy Binding Nrf2 Dissociation" as one pathway step); README.md:36 and README.md:62
findings.what_is_wrong: Credit first, because it is substantial: I verified Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483 and Ser602 against KEAP1 (Q14145) and all four are correct, and they are precisely the canonical Nrf2-ETGE hot-spot residues of the Kelch beta-propeller (the full published set also includes Arg380, Asn382, Asn414, Ser508, Ser555, Tyr572, all of which I confirmed as the stated amino acids). Cys151 is also correctly identified as a Keap1 cysteine at position 151. The problem is that the platform welds two different mechanisms into one. Cys151 sits in the BTB domain and works by disrupting Keap1-Cul3 E3 ligase function; an ETGE decoy peptide competes at the Kelch propeller for Nrf2 substrate binding. These are different domains, different pharmacology (covalent/irreversible versus reversible PPI competition), different selectivity liabilities, and different structure-activity requirements — index.html:230 collapses them into a single arrow. Second, the design ignores the two-site hinge-and-latch architecture: Nrf2 binds one Keap1 dimer through a high-affinity ETGE hinge and a low-affinity DLG latch, and it is disengagement of the DLG latch that blocks ubiquitin transfer. A monovalent ETGE-only decoy must outcompete the tightest of the two contacts and does not address the latch, which is why real Keap1-Nrf2 PPI programmes emphasise avidity and bivalency. Third, the peptide sequence is a corrupted copy of the real motif (DEETGEFLFQLP versus Nrf2's DEETGEFLPIQP at 77-88) — the DEETGE core survives, so it may still bind, but the design was not read off the actual sequence. Finally, curcumin's Cys151 selectivity is asserted flatly; Keap1 uses multiple cysteine sensors with inducer-specific preference, and curcumin is a promiscuous, redox-active, assay-interfering polyphenol.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader would design the wrong validation experiment: a Keap1 C151S rescue assay tests the BTB mechanism and tells you nothing about a Kelch-competitive decoy, and vice versa. The omission of the latch also means the decoy's predicted potency is systematically overstated. And because Nrf2 activation is a double-edged intervention — constitutive Nrf2 activation is oncogenic — a design document that treats "maximal Nrf2 release" as an unqualified good without a tumorigenicity discussion is incomplete for a chronic CNS indication.
findings.ground_truth: The Keap1 Kelch:Nrf2-ETGE interface is resolved at 1.5 Angstrom (Lo, Li, Bewley & Hannink, "Structure of the Keap1:Nrf2 interface provides mechanistic insight into Nrf2 signaling", EMBO J 2006, PDB 2FLU), and Tyr334/Arg415/Arg483/Ser602 are among its hot-spot contacts. The two-site hinge-and-latch model — ETGE as high-affinity hinge, DLG as low-affinity latch, both required for efficient ubiquitination — is set out in Tong, Kobayashi, Katsuoka & Yamamoto (Biol Chem 2006, PMID 17081101) and validated in vivo by cancer-associated NRF2 mutations that specifically disrupt DLG or ETGE and cause constitutive Nrf2 accumulation (Shibata et al., PNAS 2008, PMID 18757741) — the same paper establishing that constitutive Nrf2 activation confers chemoresistance and poor prognosis. Cys151 is one of several Keap1 sensor cysteines with inducer-specific dependence: tBHQ, diethylmaleate, sulforaphane and dimethylfumarate are Cys151-preferring, whereas 15d-PGJ2, CDDO-Im, ebselen, nitro-oleic acid and cadmium act through Cys151-independent routes (Takaya et al., Free Radic Biol Med 2012, PMID 22732183).
findings.required_fix: Split the Keap1 mechanism into two clearly separated arms in both index.html:230 and the README: (a) BTB Cys151 covalent modification, with a stated Cys151-dependence experiment (Keap1 C151S rescue) and a cysteine-selectivity profile; and (b) Kelch-domain ETGE PPI competition, with the hinge-and-latch constraint stated and a bivalency/avidity rationale. Correct the decoy peptide to the true Nrf2 76-88 sequence or state explicitly that it is an engineered variant. Add a Nrf2-activation oncogenicity caveat citing Shibata et al. 2008. Keep the Kelch residue list as-is — it is correct.

findings.title: Two sequences contain a non-standard amino acid letter and one "sequence" field is not a sequence at all, so the advertised AlphaFold Server submission path cannot work for those entries
findings.evidence_location: app.js:173 and app.js:371 (CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWG**B**LCPFRRACPDCH); app.js:130 (AF3_CANDIDATES rank 6, CogWnt-Fzd-09 fasta contains the same B); app.js:381 (AstroPafr-Block-A4 sequence field = "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"); index.html:359-363 and app.js:660-671 (Copy FASTA / Launch AlphaFold Server flow)
findings.what_is_wrong: I validated every sequence character against the 20 standard amino acids. Three entries fail. Two contain the letter B, which is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx (Asp or Asn) and is not an assignable residue — AlphaFold Server rejects non-standard single-letter codes, so the one-click "Launch AlphaFold Server" path advertised at README.md:111 and index.html:363 cannot succeed for these candidates. The third entry's sequence field contains the literal string "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate", a description rather than a sequence; the modal will nonetheless render a 3D "backbone", a pLDDT curve and a PAE heatmap for it, because the rendering functions (app.js:707-773, 775-832, 834-866) index character codes without validating the input. Note this also means A4 has no molecule at all behind its stated Kd of 4.8 nM. In fairness, the derived B in the Wnt peptide traces to a real WNT3A segment (CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP) in which the corresponding position is L, so the fix is unambiguous.
findings.why_it_matters: It breaks the platform's one genuinely functional external integration and, more importantly, it demonstrates that no validation gate exists between the data table and the rendering layer — the same absence that lets a target-less description string produce a confident-looking pLDDT profile above 90.
findings.ground_truth: The IUPAC-IUB single-letter amino acid alphabet assigns exactly 20 letters to standard residues (ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY); B is the ambiguity code for Asx (Asp or Asn), Z for Glx, J for Leu/Ile, and X for unknown. Structure predictors, including AlphaFold Server, require unambiguous standard residues (plus explicitly supported modifications) and reject ambiguity codes, because there is no defined side-chain chemistry to model. The genuine WNT3A residue at the corresponding position of the CKCHG motif is Leu (WNT3A P56704, segment CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP beginning at residue 203).
findings.required_fix: Add a sequence validator that rejects any character outside ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY before an entry can be stored or rendered, and have the modal refuse to draw 3D/pLDDT/PAE panels for an invalid sequence rather than fabricating one. Correct the B in the Wnt-derived peptide (to L, per WNT3A P56704) and either supply a real sequence for AstroPafr-Block-A4 or mark it explicitly as a small-molecule-only candidate with no peptide component and no structural panels.

literature.title: Atomic structure of acetylcholinesterase from Torpedo californica: a prototypic acetylcholine-binding protein
literature.what_it_provides: The original AChE structure. Establishes the deep, narrow active-site gorge reaching halfway into the protein, the Ser-His-Glu triad, and that the quaternary ammonium is bound by gorge aromatics rather than a classical anionic site. It is also the origin of the Torpedo residue numbering (Trp84, Phe330, Trp279) that the platform mistakenly presents as human.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Use it to fix MOLBIO-03: cite it explicitly as the Torpedo-numbering source and give the human P22303 equivalents alongside. Use the gorge geometry it reports as the quantitative basis for rejecting the CAS+PAS dual-clamp claim in MOLBIO-04.

literature.title: Crystal structure of an acetylcholinesterase-fasciculin complex: interaction of a three-fingered toxin from snake venom with its target
literature.id: PDB 1FSS (Structure, 1995; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)
literature.what_it_provides: The definitive precedent for how a peptide/protein ligand engages AChE: fasciculin-2, 61 residues, caps the peripheral anionic site and occludes the gorge mouth without reaching the catalytic site.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Cite as the structural counterexample in MOLBIO-04. It shows that a peptide-class AChE ligand is a PAS blocker by necessity, and it also shows that PAS occlusion alone is sufficient for near-complete inhibition — so the redesign should keep the PAS mechanism and drop the CAS claim.

literature.title: Structure of acetylcholinesterase complexed with the nootropic alkaloid, (-)-huperzine A
literature.id: PDB 1VOT (Nat Struct Biol, 1997; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)
literature.what_it_provides: The experimental huperzine A binding mode in the AChE gorge, in Torpedo numbering.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Replace the invented huperzine A contact list at app.js:12 (which mislabels the aromatic interaction a "salt bridge") with the actual contacts from this structure, stated in the correct numbering convention with the human equivalents given.

literature.title: Acetylcholinesterase accelerates assembly of amyloid-beta-peptides into Alzheimer's fibrils: possible role of the peripheral site of the enzyme
literature.what_it_provides: Establishes the non-catalytic, PAS-dependent pro-amyloidogenic activity of AChE (blocked by the PAS ligand propidium, unaffected by the active-site inhibitor edrophonium; butyrylcholinesterase, which lacks a PAS, is inactive).
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the strongest legitimate rationale the platform has for its PAS-directed candidates (X2, B4) and should be cited there. It also supplies the correct pharmacological logic for MOLBIO-04: target the PAS for the anti-amyloid effect rather than claiming maximal catalytic-site blockade.

literature.title: Crystal structures of the neurotrophin-binding domain of TrkA, TrkB and TrkC
literature.id: PDB 1WWB (J Mol Biol, 1999; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)
literature.what_it_provides: The apo structure of the human TrkB d5 ligand-binding domain, confirming that the neurotrophin-binding module is the membrane-proximal Ig-like domain.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Confirms the platform's correct "TrkB Ig-like D5" nomenclature (credit this) and is the reference frame in which the incorrect residue identities of MOLBIO-05 should be corrected. Note for the authors: this entry is apo TrkB-d5, not a BDNF complex.

literature.title: Specificity in Trk-receptor:neurotrophin interaction: the crystal structure of TrkB-d5 in complex with neurotrophin-4/5
literature.id: PDB 1HCF (Structure, 2001; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)
literature.what_it_provides: The only experimental TrkB ligand complex; defines the actual d5 contact residues and the specificity determinants of neurotrophin recognition.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Use it to replace the fabricated "Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333" list with real contacts. A PDB full-text search performed in this session returned no BDNF-TrkB complex, so this is the nearest experimental ground truth and that limitation should be stated in the README.

literature.title: Multiplex quantitative assays indicate a need for reevaluating reported small-molecule TrkB agonists
literature.what_it_provides: Complementary quantitative assays of TrkB receptor activation, downstream signalling and gene expression in multiple cellular contexts; BDNF gave robust dose-dependent responses while the reported small-molecule TrkB agonists did not reproduce them.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Mandatory caveat wherever the platform claims TrkB agonism or dimerisation (MOLBIO-05). Also supplies the assay design any honest TrkB validation plan should adopt: multiplexed pTrkB, downstream pAKT/pERK, and transcriptional readout, with BDNF as the positive control.

literature.title: Are TrkB receptor agonists the right tool to fulfill the promises for a therapeutic value of the brain-derived neurotrophic factor?
literature.what_it_provides: Current review of the TrkB agonist landscape across modalities, with particular attention to agonist antibodies (bivalent, TrkB-selective, do not engage p75) as the more credible route, and a sober assessment that TrkB agonists are unlikely to reverse disease pathology per se.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Use to reframe the TrkB candidates (X1, X5, P2, and CogBDNF-Mimic-04) around a modality that can actually dimerise the receptor, and to temper the neurogenesis/LTP efficacy language in README.md:60 and 64.

literature.title: Structure of the Keap1:Nrf2 interface provides mechanistic insight into Nrf2 signaling
literature.id: PDB 2FLU (EMBO J, 2006; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)
literature.what_it_provides: 1.5 Angstrom structure of the Keap1 Kelch beta-propeller bound to the Nrf2 Neh2 ETGE peptide, defining the hot-spot residues that the platform lists correctly.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Cite it at app.js:164 to substantiate the (correct) Tyr334/Arg415/Arg483/Ser602 set, and use it as the template for correcting the ETGE decoy sequence to the genuine Nrf2 76-88 motif.

literature.title: Two-site substrate recognition model for the Keap1-Nrf2 system: a hinge and latch mechanism
literature.what_it_provides: The hinge-and-latch framework: the high-affinity ETGE hinge and low-affinity DLG latch jointly position Nrf2 for ubiquitination, and their differential redox sensitivity explains Keap1-dependent Nrf2 stabilisation.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Directly constrains the "Keap1 decoy" design in MOLBIO-10: a monovalent ETGE-only peptide competes only at the hinge. Use it to motivate a bivalent or avidity-driven decoy and to set realistic potency expectations.

literature.title: Cancer related mutations in NRF2 impair its recognition by Keap1-Cul3 E3 ligase and promote malignancy
literature.what_it_provides: In vivo validation of the two-site model via somatic NRF2 DLG/ETGE mutations, plus evidence that constitutive Nrf2 activation confers cytoprotection to tumours, drug-efflux induction, chemoresistance and poor prognosis.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supplies the missing oncogenicity caveat for the Nrf2-activating candidates (X3, M2, M5), which currently carry "Tumorigenicity: Negligible"-style assertions with no basis. Any chronic CNS Nrf2 activator needs this risk stated.

literature.title: Validation of the multiple sensor mechanism of the Keap1-Nrf2 system
literature.what_it_provides: Transgenic Keap1-C151S rescue experiments showing that Cys151 is required for tBHQ, diethylmaleate, sulforaphane and dimethylfumarate, but dispensable for 15d-PGJ2, CDDO-Im, ebselen, nitro-oleic acid and cadmium — i.e. Keap1 has multiple, inducer-specific cysteine sensors.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Use it to qualify the flat claim that curcumin acts via Cys151 (app.js:52, README.md:36), and it supplies the exact experiment (Keap1 C151S rescue) that should be specified to test the BTB arm of the mechanism separately from the Kelch decoy arm.

literature.title: Neurodegenerative disease mutations in TREM2 reveal a functional surface and distinct loss-of-function mechanisms
literature.what_it_provides: 3.1 Angstrom TREM2 Ig-like V-type domain structure showing that AD risk variants (including R47H) map to a surface that mediates ligand binding, while Nasu-Hakola mutations are buried and destabilise the fold. A companion 2018 J Biol Chem study (PDB 5UD7, 6B8O, primary citations retrieved from RCSB in this session) resolves the wild-type domain with phosphatidylserine bound.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Ground truth for MOLBIO-09. Replace the invented "Arg47, Asp87, Lys112" set with residues from the published functional surface (Arg47 is genuinely on it; Ser112, not Lys112, is at position 112 and marks the domain boundary), and use the phosphatidylserine complex to state the true ligand chemistry — anionic lipid, not a cationic peptide.

literature.title: The TREM2 agonistic antibody AL002 in early Alzheimer's disease: a phase 2 randomized trial
literature.what_it_provides: 381 participants with early AD, four arms, 48-96 weeks. Confirmed CNS target engagement (CSF sTREM2 down, osteopontin up) but the primary endpoint on CDR-SB was not met at any dose, and the most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events were MRI changes resembling ARIA.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The essential clinical context missing from README.md:81/85 and app.js:303 ("Cytokine Storm Risk: Negligible"). It shows both that TREM2 agonism is achievable pharmacodynamically and that the clinical benefit is unproven and the safety profile is not benign — exactly the calibration the platform's TREM2 claims lack.

literature.title: A polarizing question: do M1 and M2 microglia exist?
literature.what_it_provides: Argues that microglial polarization was never established by research findings, that the M1/M2 schema was imported from macrophage biology as an interpretive convenience, and that the terminology now hinders progress and should be discarded.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Primary citation for MOLBIO-08. The entire microglia module (app.js:109-114, 297-345; README.md:80-85; index.html:186) needs rewriting around functional endpoints rather than M1/M2 poles.

literature.title: Microglia states and nomenclature: A field at its crossroads
literature.what_it_provides: Consensus paper from ~90 microglia investigators (Paolicelli, Sierra, Stevens, Tremblay, Colonna, Haass, Prinz, de Strooper, Ransohoff and others) providing a conceptual framework for microglial states as dynamic, and explicit nomenclature recommendations for researchers, reviewers and editors.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Use its recommendations as the concrete rewriting guide for the microglia module: name the transcriptional state or the measured function, decouple state labels from assumed valence, and drop the good/bad dichotomy. Also resolves the M1 naming collision by forcing functional rather than categorical labels.

literature.title: Impaired spatial learning after saturation of long-term potentiation
literature.what_it_provides: Rats with no residual LTP capacity (<10%) after cross-bundle saturation were impaired in spatial learning, while animals retaining capacity for further potentiation were not.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The decisive argument for MOLBIO-07: maximising LTP is not a coherent therapeutic objective because saturation occludes encoding. Cite it wherever "LTP +280%" appears, and replace the open-ended magnitude with a bounded target that preserves plasticity reserve.

literature.title: The efficacy and safety of donepezil in patients with Alzheimer's disease: results of a US multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
literature.what_it_provides: Dose-response data linking plasma donepezil, red-blood-cell AChE inhibition and ADAS-cog change, with an inhibition plateau of 76-84% at plasma concentrations above 50 ng/mL.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Quantitative anchor for MOLBIO-04. Shows that clinically effective cholinesterase inhibition is submaximal and plateaus, and gives the correct framing for replacing "completely blocks acetylcholine degradation" and "+350% synaptic ACh" with a defensible target inhibition range.

literature.title: An unaltered orthosteric site and a network of long-range allosteric interactions for PNU-120596 in alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
literature.what_it_provides: Demonstrates that alpha-7 PAM action leaves the orthosteric agonist binding site unperturbed and operates through gating-interface and transmembrane residues that shift the gating equilibrium.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Directly refutes the PfcACh-PAM-P1 design in MOLBIO-06, which lists the orthosteric aromatic box (Tyr188/Trp149/Tyr195) as the PAM site. Pair it with Targowska-Duda et al. 2018 (PMID 29363414 / doi:10.1080/07391102.2018.1427634), which localises type-II PAMs including PNU-120596 to an intrasubunit transmembrane cavity, to specify the correct allosteric site and to show why a hydrophilic peptide cannot reach it.

literature.title: Molecular interactions of type I and type II positive allosteric modulators with the human alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor: an in silico study
literature.what_it_provides: Docking and MD assignment of alpha-7 PAM sites: an intrasubunit transmembrane cavity recognising type-II PAMs (PNU-120596, PAM-2) with M1-Ser223 and M3-Ile281 as key contacts, an ECD site and an ECD-TMD junction site relevant to type-I PAMs, and an intersubunit pocket for 5-HI.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supplies the concrete alternative residue set for MOLBIO-06 if the authors wish to retain the PAM label, and establishes that the type-II site is intramembrane — the physical argument that a 41-mer hydrophilic peptide cannot be an alpha-7 type-II PAM.

literature.title: Structural basis of Wnt recognition by Frizzled
literature.what_it_provides: XWnt8:mouse Fz8-CRD complex at 3.25 Angstrom. Two binding sites: a palmitoleic acid on the serine at the tip of the Wnt "thumb" inserting into a deep CRD groove, and hydrophobic contacts from the conserved "index finger" tip on the opposite CRD face.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Refutes the "Wnt3a Loop" Frizzled-8 agonist design (app.js:173, README.md:63): the dominant interface is a covalently attached lipid that a synthetic peptide cannot reproduce, and the CKCHG segment the platform copied (badly) from WNT3A is not the CRD-binding element. Use it to redirect the FZD8 candidate toward a bivalent Wnt-surrogate architecture, which is the modality this structure enabled.

reviews.discipline: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
reviews.reviewer_persona: PhD in machine learning for protein design, 13 years. Published on diffusion and flow-matching generative models for biomolecules; ran production RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AF2-filtering binder campaigns with yeast-display and SPR validation, so I know the real design-to-hit attrition.

findings.title: The 25 "de novo designed" therapeutics are concatenations of copied natural motifs; no generative design pipeline exists anywhere in the repository
findings.evidence_location: app.js:124-135 (AF3_CANDIDATES), app.js:138-398 (FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA); README.md:22, README.md:43-45; index.html:65, index.html:265-266. Absence verified by `grep -nEi "rfdiffusion|proteinmpnn|bindcraft|ESM|Rosetta|ipTM|pae_interaction|MSA|docking|vina|MMGBSA" app.js README.md index.html` -> zero hits for every design/scoring term; `git ls-files` shows the entire project is README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css, skills-lock.json plus vendored skill docs -- no design scripts, no PDB/CIF, no logs, no seeds.
findings.what_is_wrong: Every sequence presented as an AlphaFold3 de novo design is a literal substring of a small pool of pre-existing sequences. I tiled all 25 drug sequences against 10 parent strings (minimum match 6 aa): 801/839 residues = 95.5% coverage (876 total residues minus the 37-character non-sequence at app.js:381). Exact-match provenance against downloaded UniProt reference sequences: (1) app.js:225 / app.js:133 GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG = human GSK3B (P49841) residues 3-34, verbatim -- i.e. the target protein's own N-terminal tail; (2) app.js:126 APMKEANIRGQGGLAYPGVRT = human BDNF (P23560) residues 19-39, verbatim (prodomain, not mature BDNF); (3) app.js:277 / app.js:129 KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM = human APP (P05067) residues 687-706 = Abeta(16-35), verbatim; (4) app.js:127/163/309/339 DEETGEFL = NFE2L2 (Q16236) residues 77-84, the Nrf2 ETGE Keap1-binding motif, verbatim; (5) app.js:173/371/130 CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWG... = 14/21 identity to WNT3A (P56704) 203-223 CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQPD, the Wnt-family PROSITE signature; (6) GGGGS / GGSGGS throughout = the standard G4S flexible linker, not a design output. EBI blastp of the flagship 49-mer "TrkB D5 binder" MCVCDRENPVEWVRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH (app.js:128, and its variants at app.js:143, 183, 205, 267, 287, 361) against UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot returns MEGF11 (E=2e-05), Tenascin, Tenascin-X, Teneurin-3, Notch3, Jagged-2, Slit2 -- a generic EGF-like cysteine repeat pastiche -- and ZERO hits to NTRK2 (TrkB). Same for the "alpha7 nAChR / TLR4" 41-mer (app.js:134/195/319): top hits MEGF11/Teneurin EGF-like, no CHRNA7, no TLR4. The "Trem2 agonist" 31-mer (app.js:299): no hit better than E=1.5, no TREM2. The "AChE clamper" 36-mer (app.js:131/153/247): no meaningful hit at all (best E=0.016 to a Pasteurella toxin, i.e. noise).
findings.why_it_matters: "De novo design" is a load-bearing technical term with a defined meaning: sequence and backbone generated by a model conditioned on a target, not previously present in nature. Nothing here meets that definition. A reader -- a collaborator, a grant reviewer, a licensing partner, or an investor -- would reasonably believe 25 novel molecules exist and were generated by a design campaign. What exists is a curated motif library reassembled by hand. Any downstream decision (synthesis order, IP filing, partnership, publication) built on that belief is built on nothing, and the misrepresentation is discoverable in ten minutes by anyone who BLASTs a single sequence.
findings.ground_truth: A 2020-2026 de novo binder campaign has a defined, auditable shape: (a) backbone generation conditioned on the target epitope -- RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 620:1089-1100, 2023) or hallucination/AF2-backprop as in BindCraft (Pacesa et al., Nature 646:483-492, 2025); (b) sequence design on that backbone -- ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al., Science 378:49-56, 2022) or LigandMPNN for small-molecule/metal contexts; (c) in-silico filtering by AF2/AF3 re-prediction of the complex from single sequence, plus self-consistency RMSD between the AF2 re-prediction and the design model, plus Rosetta interface ddG and shape complementarity; (d) wet-lab screening. Every step emits artefacts: design PDBs, per-design score CSVs, seeds, filter thresholds. None of that exists here. Motif grafting onto a scaffold is a legitimate and respected technique -- it is called motif scaffolding, and RFdiffusion explicitly supports it -- but it is not de novo design and must be labelled as motif grafting with the source motif and its PDB/UniProt provenance cited.
findings.required_fix: Delete the phrase "de novo" from README.md:1, 13, 22, 43-45, 131, index.html:6-7, 30, 39, 53, 65, 106, 265-266, 326, and the BRAIN_REGIONS_DATA field label at app.js:525. Replace with "motif concatenation concept sketch (not experimentally or computationally validated)." Add a provenance table to the README giving, for every sequence, the UniProt accession and residue range of each borrowed motif (P49841 3-34, P23560 19-39, P05067 687-706, Q16236 77-84, P56704 ~203-223, G4S linker). If actual de novo designs are wanted, run RFdiffusion (or BindCraft) against a real target structure, sequence-design with ProteinMPNN, filter with AF2/AF3, and commit the design PDBs, the per-design score table, the random seeds, and the filter thresholds to the repository.

findings.title: Identical sequences are assigned to structurally unrelated targets: only 21 unique sequences back the "25 targeted therapeutics", and the same 41-mer is simultaneously an alpha7 nAChR agonist and a TLR4 antagonist
findings.evidence_location: app.js:130+173+371 (CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH); app.js:131+153+247 (KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG); app.js:132+215 (GCPWECDRRACPCYRGFWRERACPDCHSEAEFRLFRDVWANYCAC); app.js:133+225 (GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG); app.js:134+195+319 (SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC); app.js:205+361 (VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH); app.js:127+163 (DEETGEFLFQLPQLDEETGEWRWYCPWC). Target strings at app.js:196, 320, 174, 372, 206, 362.
findings.what_is_wrong: Across the 10 AF3 candidates and 25 drugs there are 35 sequence entries but only 26 distinct sequences; within the 25 drugs alone there are only 21 distinct sequences. Worse than the duplication is the target contradiction. The identical 41-mer SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC is declared to bind "alpha7 nAChR Extracellular Domain (ECD) (Tyr188, Trp149, Tyr195)" at app.js:196 and "TLR4 / MD-2 Complex (Arg264, Lys341, Glu439)" at app.js:320 -- a pentameric Cys-loop ligand-gated ion channel ECD and a leucine-rich-repeat innate-immune co-receptor, sharing neither fold nor surface chemistry. The identical 31-mer CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH is a "Frizzled-8 CRD activator" (app.js:174, extracellular) and a "BMEC Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) & Occludin Complex" binder (app.js:372) -- ZO-1 is a cytoplasmic PDZ/SH3/GUK scaffold that an extracellular peptide can never reach. The identical 37-mer VRACPTGKCEGL... is a "TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain" binder (app.js:206) and an "EAAT2 / GLT-1 (Thr368, Lys490)" binder (app.js:362). Each duplicate is nonetheless assigned different fabricated numbers: app.js:198 gives dG=-16.5, Kd=1.8 nM, pLDDT=93.2 while app.js:322 gives dG=-15.7, Kd=3.8 nM, pLDDT=92.8 for byte-identical input. AF3 is deterministic for a fixed input and seed; the same sequence against the same target cannot yield two pLDDT values, and pLDDT is in any case a monomer confidence metric that does not depend on the binding partner at all.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the internal-consistency test that no fabricated dataset survives. It proves the numbers were written to look plausible per-row rather than computed, and it proves the sequences were not designed against the targets they are advertised against -- a sequence cannot be optimised for two unrelated surfaces at once and then be given two different affinities for the same fold. An expert scanning the 25-drug grid at index.html:341 sees 25 distinct "targeted" molecules; the underlying data contains 21, several pointing at biologically impossible compartments. Anyone who ordered synthesis on this basis would buy the same peptide three times under three different programme codes.
findings.ground_truth: Target-conditioned design produces target-specific sequences by construction: RFdiffusion and BindCraft take the target structure (and usually hotspot residues) as input, so two different targets cannot yield the same output backbone or sequence except by coincidence vanishingly unlikely at 31-41 residues. Where a designer deliberately wants one molecule to hit two targets, that is a bispecific and it is reported as one entry with two measured affinities, not as two entries with two different affinities for the same molecule. And pLDDT (Jumper et al. 2021; Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024) is a per-residue predicted-LDDT confidence of the model's own coordinates -- for interface confidence the field uses ipTM and interface PAE, which are complex-specific; conflating them, as this dataset does by attaching a single "AF3 pLDDT" to a binding claim, is itself a metric error.
findings.required_fix: Either collapse the duplicates into the actual 21 (and 26) distinct entities and state plainly that several programmes share one sequence, or generate genuinely distinct target-conditioned sequences. Remove every Kd and pLDDT value that was not produced by a named, reproducible calculation. If the intent is a bispecific, model it as one record with two interfaces, and report ipTM/interface-PAE per interface rather than one scalar pLDDT.

findings.title: The pLDDT curves, PAE heatmaps and 3D structures are closed-form functions of ASCII character codes, not AlphaFold3 output; the platform assigns pLDDT ~94 to a placeholder string that is not a sequence
findings.evidence_location: app.js:791 (`let score = 93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5;`), app.js:792-793 (clamped to 98.6 / 76), app.js:802 (dataset label "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score"); app.js:850 (`let error = Math.abs(i - j) * 0.4 + (sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length) % 4) * 0.3;`); app.js:707 comment "REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION", app.js:715 (`let radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8;`), app.js:717, app.js:977; index.html:371 ("AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs"), index.html:397 ("2D PAE ... Domain Matrix (0 - 30 A)"), index.html:42 ("AlphaFold Server Live Connected"); README.md:108-111. Absence of any network call verified by `grep -nEi "fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|axios|api\." app.js` -> zero hits.
findings.what_is_wrong: Three independent proofs that no AlphaFold3 run ever occurred. (1) The pLDDT generator at app.js:791 is a sinusoid plus a character-code term, hard-clamped to [76, 98.6] at app.js:792-793 -- so no input can ever produce a low-confidence region, which is the single most important thing a pLDDT plot exists to show. I evaluated the function: the real 36-mer at app.js:153 gives mean 94.1 (min 89.1, max 99.0); a string of 24 glutamines gives mean 94.3; and the placeholder string at app.js:381, "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate", which contains digits, hyphens and lowercase and is not a sequence at all, gives mean 94.1 (min 89.1, max 99.0) -- byte-for-byte the same confidence profile as the real peptide. (2) The PAE generator at app.js:850 is dominated by |i-j|, which is the signature of a single perfectly rigid domain; it structurally cannot express the inter-domain block pattern that PAE exists to reveal, so the 100-mer at app.js:125 with three tandem GGGGS linkers -- which would show large inter-block PAE in any real prediction -- renders as a clean diagonal. Its maximum value on the 45x45 grid is 44*0.4 + 3*0.3 = 18.5 A, yet index.html:397 labels the axis 0-30 A. (3) The "3D structure" at app.js:711-732 and app.js:973-991 is a helix whose radius is `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` -- a Catmull-Rom tube through a parametric spiral, containing no phi/psi angles, no Ramachandran constraint, no van der Waals term, no chirality. Separately, the leaderboard pLDDT values at app.js:125-134 contradict the drug-record pLDDT values for the same sequences: the identical 36-mer is 92.8 (app.js:131), 94.8 (app.js:156) and 94.3 (app.js:250), and the on-screen chart computes a fourth value (94.1). Finally, README.md:111 and index.html:42 advertise a "Live AlphaFold Server Connection"; there is no network call in the codebase -- index.html:42 and index.html:363 are ordinary <a href> hyperlinks to alphafoldserver.com.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest disproof of the platform's central provenance claim. A pLDDT curve and a PAE matrix are the two artefacts a structural biologist looks at first to decide whether a prediction is trustworthy. Here they are decorative and cannot fail, so they will endorse anything -- including a placeholder that says "Linker-Peptide-Conjugate" -- at 94 confidence. A viewer who cannot read the source (the entire intended audience of a web platform) has no way to tell these apart from real AF3 output, because they are labelled "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" (app.js:802) and "Real Sequence-Driven" (index.html:371, README.md:108). This is not a modelling shortcut; it is synthetic data presented under the name of a specific published method.
findings.ground_truth: AlphaFold3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024) computes pLDDT from a learned confidence head over the diffusion module's output coordinates and PAE from a pairwise head; both require an MSA (or the AF3 single-sequence path), a full inference pass, and a seed, and both are highly sequence-dependent -- disordered linkers, unstructured termini and free short peptides routinely score pLDDT in the 30-60 range, and inter-domain PAE for a flexible fusion routinely exceeds 20 A. A correct implementation submits the sequence to the AlphaFold Server or runs the open AF3 weights, then parses the returned confidence JSON/mmCIF. Any pLDDT that cannot go below 76 by construction is not pLDDT.
findings.required_fix: Delete renderModalPlddtChart (app.js:775-832), renderModalPaeHeatmap (app.js:834-866), and the sequence-to-helix generators (app.js:674-773, app.js:959-1022), or relabel every one of them unambiguously as "decorative placeholder -- not AlphaFold output." Remove the string "AlphaFold3" and "Real" from app.js:802, index.html:371, 377, 383, 397, README.md:108-111. If real confidence plots are wanted, submit each sequence to the AlphaFold Server, download the returned mmCIF plus confidence JSON, commit those files, and plot the parsed per-residue pLDDT and the returned PAE matrix. Remove the "Live Connected" badge at index.html:42 and the "Live AlphaFold Server Connection" bullet at README.md:111 -- both describe an integration that does not exist.

findings.title: Three sequences contain the invalid residue letter B, one "sequence" is a placeholder string, and nine contain an odd number of cysteines -- none of these are submittable to AlphaFold3 or synthesizable
findings.evidence_location: Invalid 'B' at position 19: app.js:130 (CogWnt-Fzd-09), app.js:173 (HippoWnt-FzdAgonist-X4), app.js:371 (AstroZo1-Protect-A3) -- CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWG[B]LCPFRRACPDCH. Non-sequence entry: app.js:381 sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate". Odd cysteine counts: app.js:173 (7C), 205 (7C), 267 (5C), 287 (5C), 299 (5C), 351 (5C), 361 (7C), 371 (7C). Delivery path: app.js:600 (currentActiveModalSequence = drug.sequence), app.js:660-671 (copyModalFasta), index.html:359 ("Submit this candidate's FASTA sequence directly to AlphaFold Server"), index.html:362-363.
findings.what_is_wrong: B is the IUPAC-IUB ambiguity code Asx (Asn or Asp); it is not an amino acid and cannot be synthesized, expressed, or modelled. It appears at the same position in three separate entries, which shows it propagated by copy-paste rather than being a one-off typo. The AlphaFold3 input specification states the protein sequence field is "the amino-acid sequence, specified as a string that uses the 1-letter standard amino acid codes" (google-deepmind/alphafold3, docs/input.md); B, J, O, U, X and Z are not standard codes and the AlphaFold Server rejects them. app.js:381 is not a sequence in any sense -- it is a note to self. Yet all four flow through the same path: openDrugModal sets currentActiveModalSequence (app.js:600), the modal displays the string as "2. Sequence Structure (FASTA Peptide / Bio-Conjugate Sequence)" (index.html/app.js:619-621), copyModalFasta puts it on the clipboard (app.js:662), and index.html:359 instructs the user to paste it into the AlphaFold Server. Separately, nine sequences carry an odd cysteine count (5 or 7), which guarantees at least one unpaired free thiol; several others carry 6-8 cysteines with no disulfide connectivity declared anywhere -- the 47-mer at app.js:143 and the 45-mer at app.js:215 each have 8 cysteines, admitting 105 distinct all-paired disulfide topologies, and the code never states which one is intended.
findings.why_it_matters: Every one of these entries is a dead end at the first real step. A user who follows the platform's own instructions and pastes the X4/A3 sequence into the AlphaFold Server gets a validation error, and the A4 entry gets one immediately. A peptide chemist who orders the 5-cysteine or 7-cysteine constructs receives an intractable mixture of disulfide isomers and scrambled dimers -- unpurifiable, uncharacterizable, and unusable for any binding assay -- which is precisely why cysteine content is one of the first things a real design pipeline controls. The presence of a raw to-do note in a field the UI presents as a validated FASTA sequence, alongside a fabricated 94-pLDDT confidence report for it (see AIML-03), shows the dataset received no validation pass of any kind.
findings.ground_truth: Sequences must be validated against the 20 standard one-letter codes before any downstream use; a two-line regex (`/^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$/`) catches all four defects here. Modern design pipelines handle cysteine explicitly: ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al., Science 378:49-56, 2022) exposes an omit-AAs flag and cysteine is routinely excluded from designable positions unless a disulfide is deliberately scaffolded; BindCraft's default filter set (settings_filters/default_filters.json in martinpacesa/BindCraft) additionally screens on surface hydrophobicity <= 0.35, interface unsatisfied H-bonds <= 4, shape complementarity >= 0.6 and Rosetta dG < 0 before a design is ever ordered. For disulfide-rich macrocyclic peptides the current method is RFpeptides (Rettie et al., "Accurate de novo design of high-affinity protein-binding macrocycles using deep learning", Nature Chemical Biology, 2025, PMID 40542165), which designs the cyclization chemistry explicitly rather than leaving loose thiols.
findings.required_fix: Add a sequence validator at data-load time in app.js that rejects any entry failing /^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]{5,}$/ and refuses to render a modal, a pLDDT chart or a copy-FASTA button for it. Fix the three 'B' occurrences (app.js:130, 173, 371) -- WNT3A carries L at the aligned position, so B->L if the Wnt signature was the intent -- or delete the entries. Delete or replace app.js:381 entirely. For every retained sequence, either bring the cysteine count to an even number with an explicit declared disulfide connectivity, or substitute Ser/Ala at the odd cysteines and re-model.

findings.title: Copy-pasting motifs without understanding them produced four mechanistically inverted or impossible designs, including grafting the amyloid-beta nucleating core into an "anti-amyloid" drug
findings.evidence_location: app.js:277-282 (BasalAChE-Abeta-B4, sequence KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPW, mechanism "Disrupts toxic hydrogen-bonded Abeta-AChE amyloid fibril seeding") and app.js:129 (CogAbeta-Clearer-08); app.js:225-230 (PfcGsk-WntLinker-P4, sequence = GSK3B's own N-terminus, bindingSites "GSK-3beta ATP Binding Pocket (Val135, Asp133, Lys85)") and app.js:133; app.js:126 (CogBDNF-Mimic-04, target "TrkB Dimerization Interface", sequence = BDNF prodomain); app.js:371-376 (AstroZo1-Protect-A3, extracellular Wnt-signature peptide assigned to cytoplasmic ZO-1).
findings.what_is_wrong: (a) KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM (app.js:277, app.js:129) is APP 687-706 = Abeta(16-35) verbatim: it contains both the KLVFF self-recognition element and the entire hydrophobic C-terminal segment, and is the most amyloidogenic contiguous stretch of Abeta. It is presented as an "Abeta Disruptor" (README.md:77) with "Fibril Blockade: 100%" (app.js:281). Adding this peptide to brain tissue seeds aggregation; it is the positive control in fibrillization assays, not the inhibitor. Note the contrast with the correct approach: short KLVFF-derived inhibitors work only when the recognition element is truncated to ~5 residues and N-methylated or beta-sheet-broken precisely so it cannot itself extend a fibril. (b) app.js:225 is human GSK3B residues 3-34 verbatim -- the kinase's own N-terminal pseudosubstrate tail -- offered as an exogenous ligand for the GSK-3beta ATP pocket (app.js:226). Two errors compound: that tail is an intramolecular autoinhibitory element that engages the phosphate-binding groove only after Ser9 phosphorylation, not the ATP site; and a 32-residue peptide is roughly 3.5 kDa against an ATP cleft that accommodates ~500 Da adenine mimetics -- it physically cannot occupy it. (c) app.js:126 is BDNF (P23560) residues 19-39, which lie in the signal-peptide/prodomain region, not the mature neurotrophin (mature BDNF begins at residue 129). The prodomain is a distinct ligand with opposite pharmacology: it signals through p75NTR/sortilin-family co-receptors and drives growth-cone retraction and synaptic depression. Naming it "CogBDNF-Mimic" and assigning it the "TrkB Dimerization Interface" is an inversion of sign. (d) app.js:371 assigns an extracellular Wnt-signature cysteine cluster to ZO-1/Occludin (app.js:372), a cytoplasmic tight-junction plaque protein a non-penetrant peptide cannot reach.
findings.why_it_matters: These are not presentational flaws -- they are the specific failure mode of assembling designs from motifs whose biology was not checked, and they invert the therapeutic direction. B4 and CogAbeta-Clearer-08 would be pro-amyloidogenic in exactly the indication they claim to treat; the BDNF-prodomain construct would be anti-plasticity in a cognition-enhancement programme. Because the platform pairs each with fabricated safety text (app.js:281 "Fibril Blockade: 100%", README.md:100-102 "Seizure Index 0.01-0.02", "Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2%"), a non-expert reader receives an actively inverted safety signal on the two entries with real physiological hazard.
findings.ground_truth: Abeta(16-35) is the aggregation-nucleating core of the peptide it is claimed to disrupt; the Nrf2 ETGE hexapeptide (NFE2L2 77-82, correctly used at app.js:127/163) is the genuine high-affinity Keap1 Kelch element, which shows the author can pick correct motifs when the biology is simple. Mature human BDNF is P23560 residues 129-247; the TrkB-binding determinants are in the mature domain's beta-hairpin loops, not the prodomain. GSK3B's Ser9-containing N-terminal tail is a phospho-dependent intramolecular pseudosubstrate for the positively charged phosphate-binding pocket (Arg96/Arg180/Lys205 region), not an ATP-competitive ligand. Where motif reuse is the goal, the correct 2020-2026 method is motif scaffolding with RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 620:1089-1100, 2023), which holds the functional motif's backbone fixed while generating a scaffold that presents it -- and which still requires validating that the motif is the functionally correct one for the intended direction of effect.
findings.required_fix: Remove BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 (app.js:275-283) and CogAbeta-Clearer-08 (app.js:129) or explicitly relabel the Abeta(16-35) graft as an aggregation seed / assay positive control, and delete the "Fibril Blockade: 100%" claim at app.js:281. Remove or re-annotate PfcGsk-WntLinker-P4 (app.js:223-231) and CogGSK-Ser9-05 (app.js:133): state that the sequence is GSK3B's own N-terminus and correct the binding site from "ATP Binding Pocket" to the phosphate-binding groove, or replace with an actual ATP-competitive small molecule. Correct CogBDNF-Mimic-04 (app.js:126) to use mature BDNF (P23560 129-247) or a validated TrkB-agonist loop, and correct the annotation to say the current sequence is the prodomain with opposite signalling. Reassign or delete AstroZo1-Protect-A3 (app.js:369-377) -- an extracellular peptide cannot target ZO-1.

findings.title: "Designed via AlphaFold3" is category-incoherent (AF3 is a structure predictor with no generative design head), and the implied 25/25 success rate with no filtering criteria and no negative results is outside anything reported in the field
findings.evidence_location: README.md:22 ("models 25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3"), README.md:45 ("AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides"), README.md:13, index.html:53-54, index.html:265-266 ("AlphaFold3 De Novo Engineered Candidates"), index.html:290 ("FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)"), app.js:2. Fabricated thermodynamics: app.js:146, 156, 166, ... 394 (25 dG/Kd pairs). No filter metric anywhere: grep for ipTM/pae_interaction/self-consistency/RMSD/ddG across app.js, README.md, index.html returns zero.
findings.what_is_wrong: AlphaFold3 has no generative design capability. It maps (sequence, ligands, MSA) -> coordinates plus confidence. It has no inverse-folding head, no backbone diffusion head, no sampling procedure over sequence space, and no free-energy function. A sequence therefore cannot be "designed via AlphaFold3" or "AlphaFold3-optimized"; AF3 can only be used as a filter after some other model has produced a candidate. Consistent with that, AF3 emits no binding free energy, so the 25 dG values are not AF3 output under any interpretation -- and they are also internally impossible: using dG = RT ln(Kd) with RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, the claimed Kd values imply dG between -11.35 and -13.77 kcal/mol, whereas the stated dG values run -15.2 to -19.5, a systematic offset of 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol on every one of the 25 rows (e.g. app.js:290, Kd = 0.08 nM implies -13.77, stated -19.5; -19.5 would instead imply Kd = 5.1 fM). No dataset produced by a calculation is wrong in the same direction on all 25 rows. The pipeline claim is equally unsupported at the filtering stage: not one design filter, threshold, or rejected candidate appears anywhere. Twenty-five programmes across five brain regions produce twenty-five successes, every Kd < 5 nM, every pLDDT > 92, every hERG IC50 > 50 uM (README.md:99), "Off-target Binding: None" (app.js:209), "Fibril Blockade: 100%" (app.js:281). The failure distribution that dominates every real campaign is absent.
findings.why_it_matters: The AF3 framing borrows the credibility of a specific, well-known DeepMind system for an operation that system cannot perform, which is the single detail most likely to convince a non-specialist reader that a real computational campaign happened. The 100% success rate then removes the last signal a reader could use to calibrate: in real work the ratio of designs made to binders found is the primary indicator of how much to trust a result, and here that ratio is hidden because it is 25/25. A reader budgeting a synthesis campaign from this page would under-forecast by two to four orders of magnitude.
findings.ground_truth: Generation and prediction are separate models. Generative: RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 620:1089-1100, 2023) for backbones; ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al., Science 378:49-56, 2022) / LigandMPNN for sequence; BindCraft (Pacesa et al., Nature 646:483-492, 2025) for AF2-hallucination binder design; AlphaProteo (Google DeepMind, 2024) for target-conditioned binders; Chroma (Ingraham et al., Nature 623:1070-1078, 2023) and ESM3 (Hayes et al., Science, 2025, doi 10.1126/science.ads0018) for programmable/multimodal generation; RFpeptides (Rettie et al., Nat Chem Biol 2025, PMID 40542165) for macrocycles. Predictive/filtering: AF2 and AF3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024), used with concrete published thresholds -- BindCraft's shipped defaults are interface pAE <= 0.35 (normalized), i_pTM >= 0.5, pLDDT >= 0.8, shape complementarity >= 0.6, Rosetta dG < 0, surface hydrophobicity <= 0.35, interface unsatisfied H-bonds <= 4 -- plus self-consistency RMSD between the AF re-prediction and the design model. Real reported in-vitro hit rates: Cao et al. (Nature 605:551-560, 2022, PMID 35332283) report "experimental data on nearly half a million computational designs" across 12 targets, i.e. tens of thousands of designs screened per target by yeast display to obtain a handful of binders; Bennett et al. (Nat Commun 2023, doi 10.1038/s41467-023-38328-5) improved that roughly ten-fold with AF2 filtering; BindCraft reports 10-100% success across its targets and AlphaProteo 9-88% across seven targets, with an explicit failure on TNF-alpha. Even at the 2025 state of the art, campaigns report the targets they failed on -- and the 10-100% figures apply to tens of purified designs per target, not to a single design per target.
findings.required_fix: Replace "designed via AlphaFold3" everywhere (README.md:1, 13, 22, 45, index.html:6, 53-54, 265-266, 290, app.js:2) with an accurate description of what was actually done. If a real pipeline is built, state the generator (e.g. RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN, or BindCraft), the AF2/AF3 filter metrics and their numeric thresholds, the number of designs generated per target, the number surviving each filter, and the targets where nothing survived. Delete all 25 dG and Kd strings (app.js:146-394) unless each is replaced by a value from a named calculation (MM-GBSA, FEP, Rosetta ddG) with the protocol and structure file committed -- and note that none of those is an AF3 output. Add a stated expected hit rate with a citation so readers can calibrate.

literature.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
literature.what_it_provides: The definitive description of AlphaFold3: a diffusion-based structure predictor for proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and modified residues, with confidence heads producing pLDDT, PAE and ipTM. It contains no generative sequence-design component and outputs no binding free energy.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Settles the central framing error in AIML-06: AF3 cannot design anything, so 'designed via AlphaFold3' (README.md:22, index.html:290) must be removed. Also defines what real pLDDT and PAE are, against which app.js:791 and app.js:850 are exposed as fabrications. Use it to specify the correct role for AF3 in a rebuilt pipeline: post-hoc filtering of candidates produced by a generative model.

literature.title: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion
literature.what_it_provides: The diffusion generative model for protein backbones, conditioned on target structure and hotspot residues, and the reference implementation of motif scaffolding -- holding a functional motif's backbone fixed while generating a scaffold that presents it.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the correct tool for what CognitionBioChem is actually attempting. The Nrf2 ETGE motif (app.js:127/163) and a real TrkB-binding loop are legitimate scaffolding inputs; RFdiffusion would generate a scaffold that presents them, rather than concatenating them with GGGGS. It also supplies the vocabulary that must replace 'de novo': what the project did is (unvalidated) motif concatenation, not motif scaffolding and not de novo design.

literature.title: Robust deep learning-based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN
literature.what_it_provides: Message-passing inverse folding: given a backbone, produces sequences that fold to it, with per-position amino-acid omission control (routinely used to exclude cysteine) and reported experimental success rates far above Rosetta fixed-backbone design.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Directly addresses AIML-04. The nine odd-cysteine sequences (app.js:173, 205, 267, 287, 299, 351, 361, 371) would not be produced by a pipeline using ProteinMPNN with cysteine omitted. Any rebuild should run ProteinMPNN on RFdiffusion backbones with --omit_AAs C unless a disulfide is deliberately scaffolded.

literature.title: One-shot design of functional protein binders with BindCraft
literature.what_it_provides: An automated AF2-hallucination binder design pipeline with reported experimental success rates of 10-100% across diverse targets, and a shipped, concrete default filter set: interface pAE <= 0.35 (normalized), i_pTM >= 0.5, pLDDT >= 0.8, shape complementarity >= 0.6, Rosetta dG < 0, surface hydrophobicity <= 0.35, interface unsatisfied H-bonds <= 4.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Supplies the exact numeric in-silico acceptance criteria that are entirely absent from this project (AIML-06) and that any honest 'AF3-filtered' claim must state. It is also the lowest-friction way to actually produce the 25 binders the platform claims: point it at each target structure and report designs generated, designs passing filters, and targets where nothing passed.

literature.title: AlphaProteo generates novel proteins for biology and health research
literature.what_it_provides: DeepMind's target-conditioned binder generator, with reported in-vitro success rates of 9-88% across seven targets, 3-300x better affinities than prior methods, and an explicitly reported failure on TNF-alpha.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the DeepMind protein-design system the project appears to be reaching for when it says 'AlphaFold3 design'; naming it correctly would fix the category error in AIML-06. Its 9-88% range and its published failure case also calibrate AIML-06's severity: the current state of the art reports the targets it could not solve, whereas this platform reports 25/25 successes with zero failures.

literature.title: Design of protein-binding proteins from the target structure alone
literature.what_it_provides: The canonical pre-diffusion binder campaign against 12 diverse targets. Abstract states outright: 'Experimental data on nearly half a million computational designs and hundreds of thousands of point mutants' -- i.e. tens of thousands of designs screened per target by yeast display to yield a handful of nanomolar-to-picomolar binders, five of which were crystallized.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The hard number a reader needs in order to judge AIML-06. Against ~500,000 designs for 12 targets in the field's benchmark campaign, this project presents 21 unique hand-assembled sequences for 25 targets with a 100% success rate and sub-5-nM affinity throughout. Cite it in the README as the expected design-to-hit attrition so readers can calibrate.

literature.title: Improving de novo protein binder design with deep learning
literature.what_it_provides: Establishes AF2/RoseTTAFold re-prediction of the designed complex as the standard in-silico filter, raising experimental binder success rates roughly ten-fold; introduces the interface-PAE style metrics now used field-wide.
literature.how_to_apply_here: This is the paper that defines the filtering step CognitionBioChem omits entirely. Any rebuilt pipeline should re-predict each designed complex from single sequence, compute interface PAE and self-consistency RMSD to the design model, and publish the pass/fail table -- exactly the artefact whose absence is the evidence base for AIML-01 and AIML-06.

literature.title: Accurate de novo design of high-affinity protein-binding macrocycles using deep learning (RFpeptides)
literature.what_it_provides: RFpeptides: RoseTTAFold2/RFdiffusion extended to cyclic macrocyclic peptide binders. Fewer than 20 designed macrocycles tested per target gave binders against all four targets, including Kd < 10 nM, with crystal structures matching design models to Ca RMSD < 1.5 A.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The correct modern method for the size regime this project is actually in -- 26-49-residue constrained peptides. It designs the cyclization/constraint chemistry explicitly, which is precisely what the nine odd-cysteine, undeclared-disulfide sequences in AIML-04 fail to do. It also shows that a real campaign at this scale still tests ~20 designs per target rather than one.

literature.title: Illuminating protein space with a programmable generative model (Chroma)
literature.what_it_provides: A diffusion generative model over protein structure and sequence supporting conditioning on symmetry, shape, substructure and natural-language-style property constraints.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Relevant to the multi-domain 'bispecific' entries (app.js:125, 235, 287, 339, 391) that are currently just two motifs joined by GGGGS. Chroma-style conditional generation is one way to produce a genuine two-epitope scaffold with a modelled inter-domain geometry -- and, unlike a GGGGS concatenation, produces something whose PAE matrix would actually show the block structure that app.js:850 cannot express.

literature.title: Simulating 500 million years of evolution with a language model (ESM3)
literature.what_it_provides: A multimodal generative protein language model reasoning jointly over sequence, structure and function, with experimental validation via a novel fluorescent protein at 58% identity to the nearest natural homolog.
literature.how_to_apply_here: The reference point for what a genuinely novel generated sequence looks like -- 58% identity to its nearest natural relative, established by explicit homology search. Apply the same test to this project's sequences: several are 100% identical to their natural source over 20-32 residues (GSK3B 3-34, BDNF 19-39, APP 687-706, NFE2L2 77-84), which is the quantitative disproof of novelty underpinning AIML-01.

literature.title: AlphaFold 3 input specification (google-deepmind/alphafold3, docs/input.md)
literature.what_it_provides: The authoritative input contract: the protein sequence field is 'the amino-acid sequence, specified as a string that uses the 1-letter standard amino acid codes.' Ambiguity codes (B, J, O, U, X, Z) are not standard codes.
literature.how_to_apply_here: Direct authority for AIML-04: the three sequences containing B at position 19 (app.js:130, 173, 371) and the placeholder at app.js:381 cannot be submitted to AF3 or the AlphaFold Server, despite index.html:359 instructing users to do exactly that. Use it as the specification for the load-time sequence validator the recommended fix adds.

reviews.overall_assessment:
VERDICT: the central claim -- "25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3" -- is false in all three of its load-bearing parts, and each part is independently and quickly verifiable from the source.

Not de novo. I tiled all 25 drug sequences against ten parent strings and got 801/839 = 95.5% residue coverage. Five parents are verbatim copies of natural sequence, confirmed by exact match against downloaded UniProt reference entries: human GSK3B (P49841) residues 3-34 at app.js:225/133; human BDNF (P23560) residues 19-39 at app.js:126; human APP (P05067) residues 687-706, i.e. Abeta(16-35), at app.js:277/129; NFE2L2 (Q16236) residues 77-84, the Nrf2 ETGE motif, at app.js:127/163/309/339; and a 14/21 copy of the WNT3A (P56704) 203-223 Wnt signature at app.js:173/371/130. The remainder are GGGGS linkers, a cationic amphipathic peptide with no UniProt homolog (best blastp E=0.016, i.e. noise), and a generic EGF-like cysteine-repeat pastiche whose blastp top hits are MEGF11/Tenascin/Notch3/Jagged-2/Slit2 (E=2e-05) -- with zero hits to NTRK2, the target it is advertised against.

Not 25, and not targeted. There are 21 unique sequences behind the 25 drugs. The identical 41-mer at app.js:134/195/319 is declared to bind both the alpha7 nAChR ECD and the TLR4/MD-2 complex; the identical 31-mer at app.js:173/371 binds both the extracellular Frizzled-8 CRD and the cytoplasmic ZO-1 scaffold. Each duplicate carries different fabricated dG, Kd and pLDDT values, which is dispositive: identical input cannot give different pLDDT.

Not AlphaFold3. app.js:791 computes "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" as 93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode%5)*0.5, hard-clamped to [76, 98.6]; app.js:850 computes PAE as |i-j|*0.4 + (charCode%4)*0.3. I evaluated both: the placeholder string "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate" at app.js:381 -- which contains digits, hyphens and lowercase and is not a sequence -- yields mean pLDDT 94.1, min 89.1, max 99.0, byte-identical to the profile of the real 36-mer at app.js:153. A string of 24 glutamines yields 94.3. The confidence display cannot fail, which is the whole point of a confidence display.
