There is no network call anywhere in the codebase (grep for fetch(/XMLHttpRequest/axios: zero hits), so "AlphaFold Server Live Connected" at index.html:42 is a static hyperlink. And the 25 dG/Kd pairs are internally impossible: with RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, every stated dG exceeds RT*ln(Kd) by 3.85-5.73 kcal/mol, in the same direction, on all 25 rows.

WHAT IS DONE WELL, and it is not nothing. The motif choices, where copied, are the right motifs: NFE2L2 ETGE genuinely is the highest-affinity Keap1 Kelch element and KLVFF genuinely is the Abeta self-recognition element used in aggregation-inhibitor design -- someone read the primary literature to find these. The natural-product pharmacology in NATURAL_PRODUCTS_DATA (app.js:6-87) is largely accurate synthesis: Huperzine A at the AChE CAS via cation-pi, baicalein at the GSK-3beta hinge (Val135), curcumin's covalent Keap1 Cys151 alkylation, salvianolic acid B pi-stacking at the AChE PAS. The bispecific architecture -- warhead + binder + G4S linker + second binder -- is the correct architecture in the abstract. The front-end engineering is competent and clean, including chart lifecycle management at app.js:779-781 to avoid Chart.js leaks. And one part of the UI is already honest: index.html:359 and the "Launch AlphaFold Server" button correctly acknowledge that prediction has not been run and must be done externally. That is the seed of the honest version of this project.

THE PATH FORWARD, in order. (1) Strip the false provenance: remove "de novo," "AlphaFold3-designed," "Live Connected," and all 25 dG/Kd/pLDDT strings; relabel the pLDDT/PAE/3D renderers as decorative placeholders or delete them. This is a one-afternoon change and it converts the project from a misrepresentation into a defensible design-concept sketch. (2) Add a load-time validator on /^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]{5,}$/ -- this catches the three B-containing sequences and the placeholder entry immediately. (3) Publish a provenance table giving the UniProt accession and residue range for every borrowed motif. (4) If real designs are wanted: pick two targets with good experimental structures (TrkB D5 and Keap1 Kelch are both well-served in the PDB), run BindCraft or RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN against them, filter with the published BindCraft thresholds (i_pAE <= 0.35, i_pTM >= 0.5, pLDDT >= 0.8, SC >= 0.6, Rosetta dG < 0), and commit the design PDBs, the per-design score table, the seeds, and the count of designs that failed. Twenty designs against two targets, honestly reported with their failures, is worth infinitely more than 25 fabricated ones. For the constrained-peptide size regime this project actually occupies, RFpeptides is the right tool and needs fewer than 20 designs per target. (5) Fix the four mechanistic inversions in AIML-05 before anything is synthesized -- grafting Abeta(16-35) into an anti-amyloid agent is the one finding here with a physical hazard attached.

The reviewer's conclusion is right but the premise as written is wrong and a domain reader will catch it. verdicts.reasoning: The arithmetic converting dG to Kd is exact (-18.2 -> 45.6 fM, -18.4 -> 32.6, -18.7 -> 19.6, -18.9 -> 14.0, -19.1 -> 10.0, -19.5 -> 5.09 fM; the remaining values span -15.2 -> 7.2 pM to -17.8 -> 90 fM; LE = 19.5/295 = 0.066). But the finding's headline -- an 'empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding' at ~-18 kcal/mol that 6 of 25 candidates 'exceed' -- does not survive three independent checks. (a) THE COUNT IS WRONG. At the reviewer's own calibration Kd = 4e-14 M -> dG = -18.28, only FIVE candidates are more negative (-18.4, -18.7, -18.9, -19.1, -19.5). The reviewer lists app.js:394 (-18.2) among the six, but -18.2 > -18.28, so it does not exceed. (b) THE CITED SOURCE SAYS SOMETHING ELSE. I retrieved Delgadillo et al., PLoS ONE 2019;14(2):e0204194 (PMID 30818336, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0204194) -- the paper the reviewer cites for the biotin calibration. Its abstract states 'The high affinity (KD ~ 10-15 M) of biotin for avidin and streptavidin'. At KD = 1e-15 M, dG = -20.46 kcal/mol and ZERO of the 25 candidates exceed it. The 4e-14 figure is defensible from Kuntz's Table 1 (I confirmed it lists biotin-streptavidin at -log K1 = 13.43, i.e. Kd = 3.7e-14 -> dG = -18.32) but it is not what the cited paper reports, and the reviewer selected the loosest value in a range that spans 1e-15 to 4e-14, which maximizes the count. (c) THE PHYSICS FRAMING IS DOMAIN OVERREACH. I retrieved Kuntz et al., PNAS 1999;96(18):9997-10002 (PMID 10468550, doi 10.1073/pnas.96.18.9997) and the full text: the plateau it reports is '~-15 kcal/mol (i.e., picomolar dissociation constants)', NOT '-18 kcal/mol' as the reviewer's ground_truth states, and the analysis is per-non-hydrogen-atom for SMALL-MOLECULE ligands -- it does not define a ceiling for protein/peptide interfaces. There is no such ceiling: barnase-barstar, a natural non-covalent protein-protein complex, has Kd ~ 1.3e-14 M and dG0 ~ -19 kcal/mol, essentially equal to the platform's most extreme claim. So '-19.5 kcal/mol is beyond the empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding' is false as stated. What IS true and survives is the modality argument: Cao et al., Nature 2022;605:551-560 (PMID 35332283, doi 10.1038/s41586-022-04654-9) -- abstract verified -- reports binders 'smaller than 65 amino acids' that are 'hyperstable' and reach 'nanomolar to picomolar affinities' only 'following experimental optimization'. The platform claims 5-45 fM to 7 pM, uniformly, for unoptimized flexible LINEAR 26-47-mers with unspecified disulfides, across six unrelated target classes, with no experimental data. That is the real finding.
verdicts.corrections: Rewrite the finding as an achievability argument, not a ceiling argument. (PNAS 1999) place the plateau for tight ligands at ~-15 kcal/mol; 25 of 25 candidates exceed that plateau and 5 approach barnase-barstar (dG0 ~ -19 kcal/mol), the tightest natural protein-protein complex known.' One correction to the REMEDIATION, not the finding (see fix_is_sound): the fix recommends PRODIGY as 'the correct tool class for this project's actual modality'. verdicts.corrections: Two corrections. Also add, as the practical consequence of the fix: with a 1.9 kcal/mol error bar and a 6.1 kcal/mol total spread, the ten candidates collapse to roughly three indistinguishable bands -- so 'suppress orderings whose gaps fall inside the stated error' means deleting the 1-10 leaderboard, and the report should say so rather than leave it as an exercise.

verdicts.reasoning: The substance is correct and I confirm every structural claim: CEI is a hardcoded literal at app.js:125-134 with no formula, inputs, units, weights, validation set or reference anywhere in the repository; it is rendered as a gold-badged leaderboard column (app.js:886, index.html:306) under the heading 'TOP 10 Candidate Computational Benchmark' (index.html:316); and the chart at app.js:1057-1078 puts CEI (dimensionless, 0-100) and |dG| (kcal/mol) in two bar datasets with no `yAxisID` on either -- I grepped, there are zero occurrences of yAxisID in app.js -- so Chart.js renders both against a single shared y-axis, exactly as described. I reproduce the reviewer's correlations to the digit: r(CEI, rank) = -0.9845, r(CEI, dG) = -0.9389, r(pLDDT, dG) = -0.3798. The point that no in silico pipeline outputs a cognition score, and that a benchmark column nobody can reproduce is unfalsifiable, is correct and well within discipline.
verdicts.corrections: One factual error to fix before issue. The claim 'They are strictly monotone with the assigned rank' is FALSE: the CEI series is 98.4, 95.2, 92.1, 93.8, 90.5, 89.0, 87.6, 85.4, 83.9, 82.5 -- rank 3 (92.1) is LOWER than rank 4 (93.8). A correlation of -0.985 is not strict monotonicity, and the inference the reviewer draws from it ('this shows the leaderboard is ordered by CEI, i.e. by the undefined quantity') is therefore unsupported. Replace it with the stronger and verifiable statement: the rank column is an independent hardcoded literal that NO displayed metric reproduces -- CEI has 1 inversion, dG has 3, pLDDT has 4 -- so the 'TOP 10' ordering is not a ranking by anything present in the table, and CEI is merely its closest correlate. Also broaden the scope: CEI is not the only undefined index. The same defect appears 21 times as 'Seizure Index' (app.js:147-395 and README.md:100), plus 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291), 'Safety Index: 99.1 / 100' and '99.3 / 100' (app.js:343, 395), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (app.js:281), 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (app.js:323) and 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%' (app.js:157) -- undefined composites reported as probabilities of exactly zero or one, a stronger claim than CEI ever makes. Any remediation that deletes only `cei` leaves the larger instance of the same defect in place.

missed_by_reviewer: NO CHEMICAL DEFINITION OF ANY MOLECULE EXISTS -- a more fundamental blocker than CT-02. Every candidate is a bio-conjugate of a natural-product warhead plus a peptide, but the warhead is given only as prose plus a molecular formula ('Ginsenoside Rg1 Dammarane-12,20-diol (C42H72O14) + C-20 Linker', app.js:142; 'Huperzine A Pyridone Core (C15H18N2O) + Cys-Lys Amide Coupling', app.js:152; 'Onjisaponin V Presenegenin Aglycone (C30H46O6) + 1,2,3-Triazole Linker', app.js:182) and the `sequence` field carries only the peptide half. No SMILES, no CCD code, no attachment atom, no linker topology, no stereocentres, no protonation state, no disulfide connectivity. Even a reviewer who accepted the intent could not compute these numbers: 25 of 25 records are chemically underdetermined. Note also that a full SMILES exists for the free natural products at app.js:10-80 -- so the omission is specifically at the conjugate, the thing whose dG is claimed. (Two of those SMILES are also invalid: app.js:50 curcumin contains the literal token 'OCH3', which is not valid SMILES; app.js:60 and 70 contain molecular formulas, not SMILES.)

A BISPECIFIC OR TRI-FUNCTIONAL CONJUGATE CANNOT HAVE A SINGLE dG OR Kd -- an unflagged thermodynamic category error, and the mechanism by which the most extreme values are generated. app.js:238 reports one dG/Kd for a molecule binding both alpha7 nAChR ECD and GluN2A NTD; app.js:290 reports one for AChE plus TrkA plus M1 mAChR; app.js:342 for Trem2 plus Keap1; app.js:394 for ER-beta plus EAAT2. These are separate equilibria with separate constants. A single number exists only for a defined ternary complex and only with an explicit effective-concentration/avidity term, which is never stated. Note the four 'Dual/Super/Bispecific' entries hold four of the five most negative values in the dataset -- the marketing tier is doing the thermodynamics.

THE IMPLIED KINETICS ARE ABSURD AND ARE NEVER STATED. No kon, koff or residence time appears anywhere in the repository. At the flagship Kd = 5.09 fM (app.js:290) and a realistic peptide association rate of 1e5-1e7 M-1 s-1, koff = 5.1e-10 to 5.1e-8 s-1, i.e. a dissociation half-life of 0.4 to 43 years. This is quantitatively irreconcilable with README.md:102 ('Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days'), with README.md:100 ('Allosteric NMDAR tuners feature capped Emax'), and with app.js:15's own description of huperzine A as a 'potent REVERSIBLE acetylcholinesterase inhibitor'. CT-03 gestures at 'effectively irreversible' but never computes it; the computed half-life is the single most legible way to show a non-specialist that the number is impossible.

README.md AND app.js DISAGREE ABOUT WHICH MOLECULE EACH dG BELONGS TO -- an independent, cross-file proof of fabrication that the review does not use. README.md:60 assigns HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 the peptide CVDRENPVEWVRAC (14 residues) with dG = -18.4; app.js:143 assigns the same drug a 47-residue sequence with the identical dG = -18.4. README.md:61 gives X2 the 8-mer KWWKFLRR at -16.2 while app.js:153 gives a 36-mer at -16.2. README.md:62 gives X3 the 12-mer DEETGEFLFQLP at -15.8 while app.js:163 gives a 28-mer at -15.8. The reported free energy is invariant to a three-fold change in the length of the molecule. No estimator -- physical or learned -- is invariant to that. This is cleaner evidence than the duplicate-sequence argument because it requires no assumption about what was run.

THE PEPTIDES ARE PHYSICOCHEMICALLY IMPLAUSIBLE AS THERAPEUTICS AND NOBODY CHECKED. KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:153 and 247, the highest-valued AChE binder) is a 36-mer with 13 Lys/Arg and 4 Glu/Asp -- net charge +9, 36% cationic, 4 Trp -- the canonical cationic-amphipathic profile of a membrane-lytic / cell-penetrating peptide, not of a CNS therapeutic. This directly contradicts README.md:99, which claims 'hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656': highly charged amphipathic peptides are associated with nonspecific membrane and channel perturbation, not protection from it, and a peptide of this class would not be assayed against hERG in the first place because the stated 'IC50 > 50 uM' is a small-molecule endpoint applied to the wrong modality. Separately, 14 of the 35 distinct sequences carry an ODD number of cysteines (up to 9, at app.js:125 and 128) with disulfide pairing never specified -- both a missing required input for any structure or energy calculation and a first-order determinant of the conformational-entropy penalty CT-03 invokes.

THE PAE PANEL IS WRONG ON ITS OWN TERMS, BEYOND BEING SYNTHETIC. app.js:844 caps the matrix at gridSize = min(length, 45), so any candidate longer than 45 residues is silently truncated (the 100-residue rank-1 candidate at app.js:125 would display 45% of itself with no indication). The maximum value the generator can reach at gridSize 45 is 45*0.4 + 0.9 = 18.9 A, so the axis label '0 - 30 A' at index.html:397 is unreachable by construction. And the alpha ramp at app.js:862, `1 - error/35`, renders HIGH predicted error as nearly transparent, i.e. the lowest-confidence regions read as background -- the inverse of the AF3 convention, where high PAE is the visually dominant off-diagonal block. A reader comparing this panel to a real AF3 output is being shown a reversed colour semantic.

NO CONTROLS, NO RETROSPECTIVE VALIDATION, NO APPLICABILITY DOMAIN. A credible affinity layer is judged on controls before it is judged on predictions: redock a solved complex and report RMSD, score a known binder against a known non-binder on the same target, report enrichment on a decoy set. Nothing here scores a single reference ligand -- huperzine A against AChE is the obvious positive control with experimental Ki/IC50 available in ChEMBL, and the repository already contains its SMILES at app.js:10. Without one scored control there is no evidence the pipeline could rank even a case whose answer is known, which is the precondition for any of the reviewer's proposed remediation tiers to be worth adding.

THE AChE BINDING-SITE RESIDUE LISTS MIX TWO INCOMPATIBLE NUMBERING CONVENTIONS -- and the review's overall_assessment explicitly praises them as 'correct textbook structural pharmacology', which overstates. app.js:154 lists 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)' and app.js:248 lists 'Trp84, Phe330, Trp286, Tyr341': Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica numbering, while Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341 are human AChE numbering (the Torpedo equivalents are Trp279/Tyr70/Tyr334; the human equivalents of Trp84/Phe330 are Trp86/Phe338). app.js:12 uses Trp279 for the PAS while app.js:154 uses Trp286 for the same site. This matters directly to this discipline because these residue lists are precisely the input to the per-residue decomposition the review proposes under the gmx_MMPBSA remediation -- a decomposition keyed to a mixed-species numbering scheme cannot be mapped onto any prepared receptor.

THE ONE FEATURE THE REVIEW PRAISES AS HONEST IS BROKEN FOR 4 OF 25 RECORDS. copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) copies `drug.sequence` raw, with no '>' header line, so what lands on the clipboard is not FASTA despite the button label 'Copy FASTA Sequence' and the modal heading at index.html:290. For app.js:381 it copies the string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' for submission to AlphaFold Server, and for app.js:173, 371 and 130 it copies sequences containing B, which the server rejects. The 'copy-and-hand-off' pattern is genuinely the right design, but it should be validated before it is held up as the honest part of the platform.

THE PROPOSED FIXES ARE NOT SAFE TO IMPLEMENT IN THE ORDER GIVEN. CT-01's remediation -- store kd_M, compute dg = RT*ln(kd_M) at render time, add a unit test asserting |dG - RT ln Kd| < 0.01 -- is arithmetically correct (I verified RT = 0.0019872041*298.15 = 0.592485 and the sign convention) but if implemented ALONE it makes 25 fabricated numbers thermodynamically self-consistent, removing the single most legible external signal that the dataset is invented and making the platform strictly more convincing to a non-specialist. It must be gated behind CT-02's remediation (remove the values or mark them 'not computed'), and the report should say so explicitly, because a downstream implementer reading these findings in order will do CT-01 first since it is the smallest patch. The unit test as specified is also either vacuous (if only kd_M is persisted there is no second value to compare) or brittle (a 0.01 kcal/mol tolerance is tighter than the 0.1 kcal/mol display rounding); it should assert over any persisted pair with a tolerance derived from the display precision.

NO TIER IN THE PROPOSED REMEDIATION ACTUALLY PRODUCES A NUMBER FOR THIS MODALITY, AND THE REVIEW DOES NOT SAY SO PLAINLY. CT-04's fix lists Vina/gnina (small molecules, poses not kcal/mol), gmx_MMPBSA (relative ranking within a congeneric series), PRODIGY (folded protein-protein complexes, cannot see the covalent warhead), Boltz-2 (small-molecule potency), and ABFE (which the reviewer concedes 'for 30-50-mer flexible peptides is not a solved problem'). Every entry is either the wrong chemistry or the wrong modality for a peptide-small-molecule bio-conjugate binding a receptor ectodomain. The honest conclusion the review stops one step short of: for this modality there is currently no computational method that legitimately returns a kcal/mol, so the correct remediation is to display no affinity at all until experimental SPR/ITC data exist -- not to substitute a differently-labelled prediction with an error bar.

verdicts.corrections: (1) "The leaderboard is actually sorted by CEI" is not exactly true and should be restated. rho(rank,CEI) = -0.988, not -1: ranks 3 and 4 are inverted (CEI 92.1 at rank 3 sits above CEI 93.8 at rank 4). rho(rank,dG) = +0.964, close behind. (2) The Bennett et al. characterisation is slightly over-sharpened. I pulled the abstract from PubMed (PMID 37149653, Nat Commun 14:2625, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-38328-5): the ~10-fold gain comes from using AF2/RoseTTAFold to assess BOTH "the probability that a designed sequence adopts the designed monomer structure" AND "the probability that this structure binds the target as designed". pae_interaction is the decisive interface term, but the filter is a conjunction that includes monomer self-consistency, so "not monomer confidence" should read "monomer confidence alone is insufficient; the interface term is what carries the gain". This does not weaken the finding -- the platform has neither term, since it never predicts a complex. (3) Karelina et al. is real and correctly summarised (PMID 38131311, eLife 12, DOI 10.7554/eLife.89386); the reviewed-preprint id RP89386 is fine, PubMed records e89386.

missed_by_reviewer: THE STRONGEST AVAILABLE PROOF OF FABRICATION WAS MISSED: identical sequences carry different 'AF3' numbers. Four sequences appear twice in the 25-drug set with contradictory metrics -- KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG is both HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (app.js:153, dG -16.2, Kd 2.1 nM, pLDDT 94.8) and BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 (app.js:247, dG -17.5, Kd 0.65 nM, pLDDT 94.3); SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC is both PfcACh-PAM-P1 (app.js:195, pLDDT 93.2) and MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3 (app.js:319, pLDDT 92.8); CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH is X4 (app.js:173, 95.1) and A3 (app.js:371, 93.8); VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH is P2 (app.js:205, 95.8) and A2 (app.js:361, 94.1). Seven more collisions exist between drug sequences and leaderboard FASTAs with different pLDDT (e.g. X2 == CogAChE-PAS-02, 94.8 vs 92.8; P1 == CognACh-Mod-06, 93.2 vs 90.7). A deterministic model given identical input cannot return different confidences. This needs no formula reverse-engineering, no arithmetic and no external ground truth -- it is visible by sorting the array. Worse, the same peptide is claimed to bind unrelated receptors (alpha7 nAChR ECD vs TLR4/MD-2; FZD8 CRD vs ZO-1/occludin; TrkB D5 vs the EAAT2 transporter), which is a target-assignment fabrication independent of the numbers. And because the generators are deterministic, those four card pairs render byte-identical pLDDT curves, PAE heatmaps and 3D models -- 8 of the 25 modals are visually indistinguishable in pairs.

AF3 IS NOT A DESIGN MODEL -- the headline claim is a category error, not merely unimplemented. README.md:22 and README.md:45 say the 25 therapeutics were 'designed via AlphaFold3' and 'AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides'; index.html:290 labels the field 'FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)'. AF3 is a structure predictor: it consumes a sequence and emits coordinates and confidences. It has no generative sequence head and cannot propose, optimise or mutate a binder. De novo binder design requires a separate generative stack (RFdiffusion / ProteinMPNN / BindCraft / hallucination), none of which is named anywhere. The reviewer argues at length that AF3 was never RUN; the deeper point is that even a perfect AF3 run could not have produced these sequences. Relatedly, 'de novo' is false on its own terms: the peptides are concatenations of known natural motifs the review itself identifies as authentic (KLVFFAED = Abeta16-23, DEETGE = the Nrf2 Neh2 ETGE motif, GRPRTTSFAESC = the GSK-3beta Ser9 substrate motif, GGGGS spacers). Copied motifs joined by linkers are a fusion construct, not a de novo design.

ZERO REPRODUCIBILITY METADATA, which is the first thing a Nature Methods reviewer checks. There is no seed, no sample index, no model version, no run date, no software version and no error bar anywhere in the repository (`grep -niE 'seed|model_version|sample|version'` over app.js and README.md returns only the unrelated word 'seeding' in two mechanism strings). AF3 by default runs multiple seeds x multiple diffusion samples and ranks across them via ranking_scores.csv; pLDDT varies materially between samples. Quoting 35 pLDDT values to 0.1 with no seed, no sample count and no spread is by itself grounds for rejection even if a model had been run, and it should be a named requirement of the AIML-01 fix: persist seed, sample, model version and the per-sample spread alongside every number surfaced.

NO CALIBRATION, NO CONTROLS, AND AN IMPLIED 100% HIT RATE. The discipline here is 'confidence calibration' and the review never asks the calibration question. There is no held-out set, no reliability diagram, no negative control, no scrambled-sequence or shuffled-linker baseline, no decoy targets, and no experimental validation path. All 25 candidates are reported as successes with sub-10 nM Kd and 15 of 25 below 2 nM. Against the literature baseline the review itself cites (Bennett et al. 2023, PMID 37149653), AF-filtered de novo binder campaigns run at single-digit percent experimental success. A pipeline reporting 25/25 is reporting an impossibility, and that is checkable without reading a line of code -- it should be its own finding, because it is the one a funder or collaborator can evaluate.

THE FABRICATION POINTS THE WRONG WAY FOR THIS INPUT CLASS, which is the specifically ML observation. Short de novo peptides have essentially no MSA depth; AF2/AF3-class models give isolated 28-47mer peptides with no receptor and no homologs LOW and poorly calibrated pLDDT, frequently 40-70 with wide seed-to-seed variance, not the 89.0-99.0 band the generator produces. So a domain reader is not merely seeing invented numbers, they are seeing numbers whose central tendency is inverted relative to what this exact input class produces. The same inversion applies at the linkers (which the review does catch) and at the termini. Any relabelling fix should say so explicitly, because 'placeholder data' understates it -- the placeholder is anti-correlated with reality.

THE PAE PANEL IS BROKEN AS A VISUALISATION INDEPENDENT OF ITS CONTENTS. index.html:399 sizes the canvas 540x220 while app.js:845-846 compute cellW = width/gridSize and cellH = height/gridSize, so a square token x token matrix is drawn stretched 2.45:1 horizontally for every single drug (12.00 x 4.89 px cells at gridSize 45). A PAE matrix that is not square is unreadable as a PAE matrix -- the diagonal is not a diagonal. On top of that, app.js:853-862 encode error with a three-step hard-switched hue AND an alpha ramp of 1 - error/35, so high-error cells fade to the page background: the encoding is non-monotonic in perceived lightness, has no colourbar, and has no axis ticks or chain dividers. Even after a real confidences.json is wired in, this renderer would misdisplay it. The AIML-02 fix should require a square canvas, a monotonic sequential colormap, a labelled colourbar in Angstroms, and chain-boundary rules.

THE pLDDT CHART AXIS GUARANTEES A FLAT LINE. app.js:824-825 pin the y-axis to [50, 100] while the data are confined to [89.0, 99.0]. Every one of the 25 curves therefore renders as a nearly flat trace pressed against the ceiling, occupying the top fifth of the plot, under a four-band legend (index.html:388-391) whose lower two bands can never be reached. The visual message 'uniformly maximal confidence, no variation worth reading' is manufactured by the axis choice as much as by the generator, and the fix list should say to derive the axis from the data or use the standard 0-100 with band shading.

NO PROVENANCE OR AUDIT TRAIL AS A GENERAL REQUIREMENT. The review frames the problem correctly as a provenance failure but stops at deletion and relabelling. The structural fix is a provenance contract: every displayed number should carry the artifact path it was read from, the model and version that produced it, and the run timestamp, and the UI should be incapable of displaying a metric that has no such backing. Without that, the same class of defect reappears the first time someone hand-edits a value. This should be stated as an acceptance criterion for the AIML-01 remediation, not left implicit.

verdicts.corrections: Three. (1) The ground-truth paragraph says app.js:850 'makes the second term depend only on the row index i, so it is a per-row constant offset carrying no pairwise information.' The clause is imprecise about the whole expression: the |i-j|*0.4 term IS pairwise (trivially, in sequence separation); only the ASCII term is the per-row offset, and its effect is to break symmetry — I computed PAE[0][5]=2.90 vs PAE[5][0]=2.00 for the drug-2 sequence. (2) A stronger tell was missed: the generated diagonal is nonzero, PAE[i][i] taking values {0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9} Å, whereas a real PAE matrix is identically zero on the diagonal by construction. That single check is the cheapest possible disproof of the 'PAE' label. The 'same molecule, same receptor, different ΔG' point for drugs 2 and 11 (both AChE) is correct and is the strongest single argument in the finding. Thermodynamics re-derived with R=1.987204259e-3, T=298.15: RT=0.59248 (reviewer 0.5925, correct); ΔG=-18.4 implies Kd=3.256e-5 nM = 32.6 fM (reviewer 3.3e-5 nM, 33 fM, correct); Kd=0.32 nM implies ΔG=-12.95 (correct); 1 nM implies -12.28 (reviewer -12.27, correct to rounding). verdicts.corrections: Four numerical errors and one substantive upgrade. (1) 'the pipeline contains 28 unique sequences across 35 records' — actual count is 26 unique across 35 (7 collisions absorbing 16 records, i.e. 9 excess). (2) 'pLDDT differs by up to 4.4 points' is wrong: the maximum spread on byte-identical input is 2.50 (drug 6 = 93.2, drug 18 = 92.8, candidate 10 = 90.7). The argument survives — 2.5 points is still far outside seed noise — but the figure must be corrected before issue. (3) 'ΔG by up to 4.4 kcal/mol' understates: the maximum is 4.90 (drug 2 -16.2, drug 11 -17.5, candidate 7 -12.6). (4) 'The discrepancy across all 25 records ranges from 3.45 to 5.73' — the true range is 3.85 to 5.73. (5) Substantive: the reviewer's inference that the numbers 'were written by hand' is under-argued and slightly wrong. I regressed ΔG on ln(Kd in M) across all 25 records: ΔG = 1.0495·ln(Kd_M) + 4.682 with R² = 0.994. They were not entered independently — they were generated by a single smooth rule with an effective RT of 1.05 kcal/mol (RT at ~528 K) plus a spurious +4.68 kcal/mol intercept. That is far stronger evidence than 'the offset is not constant' and it should replace that sentence.

verdicts.reasoning: The mechanism is real and I confirmed every link in it. `grep -n "dispose\|cancelAnimationFrame" app.js` returns exit 1 — neither token appears in the file. `grep -n "modalThreeRenderer"` shows the variable is declared at :410, assigned only at :688, and never set to null or undefined anywhere, so the guard `if (!modalThreeRenderer) return;` at :764 is permanently satisfied after the first modal open and no animation loop can ever terminate. closeDrugModal (app.js:655-658) is three lines and does only `modal.classList.remove('active')`. Because animateModal3D closes over module-level globals rather than its own renderer, N surviving loops each mutate the same modalThreeMeshGroup, so rotation advances N × 0.006 rad/frame and render() is called N times per frame — the 2x-after-second-open prediction is correct. (2) The finding misses the second, identical leak site: update3DProteinStructure (app.js:959-1022) empties proteinMeshGroup at :962-965 with remove() and no dispose(), then allocates a fresh TubeGeometry at :994 plus up to ceil(len/2) SphereGeometry meshes and MeshPhongMaterials at :1003-1010 on every leaderboard row click. verdicts.reasoning: Facts all verified. No LICENSE, LICENSE.md or COPYING at root (git ls-files confirms). README.md:3 is the shields.io badge with `logo=google` reading 'AlphaFold3 | DeepMind Server'. index.html:30 subtitle is 'DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform'; :410 reads 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling'; :42 is the hyperlink-only 'Live Connected' pill. `grep -ri abramson` across all files returns nothing; no third-party attributions exist. I retrieved google-deepmind/alphafold3 OUTPUT_TERMS_OF_USE.md directly and every quoted clause is verbatim and correctly numbered: §1 non-commercial/permitted-organizations, §2 'To misinform, misrepresent or mislead' including 'misrepresenting your relationship with Google' and 'misrepresenting the origin of Output', §5 conspicuous notice, §6 the Abramson citation requirement, and the 'theoretical modeling only... not intended, validated, or approved for clinical use' disclaimer. Critically, the reviewer was careful and correct in attributing the automated-binding-prediction prohibition to the AlphaFold Server terms rather than to the GitHub Output terms — I confirmed it is absent from the GitHub file and present verbatim in the Server Output Terms via an independent mirror: 'IN CONNECTION WITH ANY AUTOMATED SYSTEM that predicts the binding or interaction of the protein with ligands or peptides, including, but not limited to, Glide or AutoDock.' The same source shows the misrepresentation clause expressly covers 'using Google's trademarks, trade names, logos or suggesting endorsement by Google', which lands squarely on the logo=google badge.
verdicts.corrections: One substantive reasoning error. The AlphaFold 3 Output Terms of Use govern Output. This project has produced, received and distributes zero AF3 Output, so §2, §5 and §6 do not attach to it, and the sentence '§6 requires citing Abramson; this project claims AlphaFold3 findings throughout and cites nothing' is not a breach of §6 — the defect is falsely claiming AF3 provenance, which is a different wrong. The claim that the conduct is 'aggravated, not mitigated, by the fact that no AlphaFold output is present at all' inverts the instrument: absence of Output removes the contract, it does not intensify it. Re-route the argument to what actually applies now: (i) ordinary trademark and passing-off exposure from placing 'DeepMind' and the Google logo in the masthead and badge of a third-party product, for which the Terms' own wording is strong evidence of how Google characterises the conduct rather than the operative prohibition; and (ii) a genuine §2/§5/§6 breach that becomes live the instant real Output enters the pipeline — which is why the fix's sequencing (resolve before building the compute layer) is right. Also: neither the reviewer nor I is counsel, and the finding should recommend counsel review rather than assert a violation. Severity stays CRITICAL on the independent grounds that the missing LICENSE makes lawful sharing impossible and that 'Live Connected' is a false statement of fact regardless of any contract.

verdicts.corrections: Two additions that are stronger than anything currently in the finding and should be folded in. (1) The generated PAE diagonal is nonzero: PAE[i][i] takes values {0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9} Å depending on the residue's ASCII code, whereas a real PAE matrix is identically zero on the diagonal by definition. That is a one-line check and it is the single most conclusive internal proof that this is not a PAE matrix. (2) The matrix is asymmetric in a way no PAE generator produces — PAE[0][5]=2.90 vs PAE[5][0]=2.00 for the drug-2 sequence — because the ASCII term keys on the row index only. Severity MINOR is correct given SWE-01 subsumes the panels, but the finding's real value is as the cheapest available evidence that nobody ever compared these figures against a genuine AlphaFold output, and that framing should lead it.

missed_by_reviewer: Raw LaTeX renders literally on the landing page. No MathJax or KaTeX is loaded anywhere — I grepped both index.html and app.js for mathjax|katex and got zero hits — yet index.html:75, :285, :305 and app.js:635 emit `$\Delta G$`. A visitor's first screen therefore reads 'Peak Binding Energy ($\Delta G$)' in the hero stat card, the leaderboard column header reads '$\Delta G$ (kcal/mol)', and the 3D viewer overlay reads '$\Delta G$: -17.9 kcal/mol'. The reviewer read all 415 lines of index.html and characterised the front end as 'a competent prototype' and 'well-built' while missing a defect visible without scrolling.

'CEI' is never defined anywhere and the reviewer never mentions it. The Cognitive Enhancement Index is the leaderboard's headline column (index.html:306), the primary series of the benchmark chart (app.js:1063), and a hardcoded field on all ten candidates ranging 82.5–98.4. It has no formula, no units, no range justification, and zero occurrences in README.md. It is the one quantity in the artifact that cannot even be checked for internal consistency, because there is nothing to check it against — which makes it strictly worse than the ΔG/Kd mismatch that got a BLOCKER. The same applies to 'Seizure Index', 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291) and 'Safety Index: 99.1 / 100' (app.js:343). Nine findings, no mention of any of them.

The leaderboard is not a ranking. I tested monotonicity of ranks 1–10 against all three displayed metrics: CEI inverts at rank 3→4 (92.1 → 93.8), pLDDT inverts four times (93.2→94.0, 94.0→96.1, 92.1→94.8, 92.8→93.6), and |ΔG| inverts three times. No code sorts AF3_CANDIDATES; `rank` is a hardcoded literal. A leaderboard whose order cannot be reproduced from any column it displays is the same defect family as SWE-02, is checkable in one line, and was not found.

Two of the 'de novo designed' molecules are verbatim wild-type sequence. Drug 14 BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 (app.js:277) and candidate rank 5 CogAbeta-Clearer-08 (app.js:129) both begin KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM, which is exactly Aβ(16-35) of human amyloid-beta (Aβ42 = DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA; positions 16–35 match character for character). KLVFFAE is the amyloidogenic nucleation core. So an 'Aβ fibril disruptor' and an 'Aβ clearer' are each built on the aggregation nucleus of the peptide they claim to clear, presented without comment. More generally the sequences are known literature motifs (Nrf2 ETGE as DEETGE, Wnt/Fzd and Trk fragments) concatenated with GGGGS linkers — which contradicts 'designed via AlphaFold3' independently of whether AF3 was ever run, and needs no structure prediction to establish. SWE-02 sorted these sequences for duplication and never asked what they were.

The README ADMET claims flagged in the brief are never addressed on their substance. README:96-102 and the per-drug safety strings assert things no in silico method can emit: 'IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)' — no predictor outputs a zero risk; 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' — a 30-day longitudinal receptor-regulation endpoint is an in vivo measurement, not a static-model output, and nothing in this codebase computes anything over time; and 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (app.js:323), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (:281), 'BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%' (:375). SWE-03 touches app.js:147 only as a string-formatting problem. Absolute 0% and 100% safety claims on a self-described drug discovery platform are the numbers most likely to be quoted out of the artifact and they deserved their own finding.

The remediation is far cheaper than the review's 'rewrite along a three-layer boundary' implies, because the tooling is already committed to this repository. `git ls-files` shows .agents/skills/alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze/scripts/ containing fetch_structure.py — which pulls real mmCIF and PAE JSON from https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/api/prediction/{uniprot_id} — plus analyze_plddt.py and analyze_pae.py, Apache-2.0, sourced from google-deepmind/science-skills and hash-pinned in the tracked skills-lock.json. The reviewer both asserted AlphaFold is 'never even contacted' anywhere and declared 'no lockfile' while this was in the index. A reviewer who misses what is already in the tree mis-scopes the effort estimate, and effort estimates are what determine whether an author acts on a report or discards it.

The benchmark chart plots two incommensurate units on one shared axis. app.js:1057-1102 renders a dimensionless 0–100 index (CEI) and |ΔG| in kcal/mol as two bar series against a single untitled linear y-axis, so the ΔG bars are compressed to roughly a fifth of the CEI bars purely by unit choice while the chart invites direct visual comparison between them. For a review whose declared discipline covers scientific data presentation, a two-unit single-axis bar chart on the artifact's only summary figure is a standard finding.

None of the ten named natural products is on that list. app.js:660-671 does copy only drug.sequence; index.html:362-363 is a clipboard button plus a bare anchor to alphafoldserver.com. The GSK-3beta claim checks out precisely: UniProt P49841 begins MSGRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG..., residues 3-34 are exactly GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG = app.js:225 byte for byte, and Ser9 sits at peptide position 7 with no SEP modification specified anywhere (0 grep hits). AF3 emits pLDDT/PAE/pTM/ipTM/ranking score and no free energy, so the dG values cannot have come from it.
verdicts.corrections: One sub-claim overreaches. 'The sequences at app.js:173 and app.js:371 contain B ... and would be rejected by both the Server and the local parser.' The Server half is safe. The LOCAL parser half I could not confirm: docs/input.md says only 'a string that uses the 1-letter standard amino acid codes' and is silent on B/Z/J/X handling, and I did not read the parser source. Restate as 'rejected by the Server; local behaviour unverified — at minimum B (Asx) does not map to a defined residue.' Also, the reviewer missed a third occurrence of B: app.js:130, the CogWnt-Fzd-09 fasta in AF3_CANDIDATES, which is the string rendered in the main 3D viewer and shown in the leaderboard panel. verdicts.reasoning: I extracted all 25 entries programmatically rather than trusting the citation. All four pairs are byte-identical at the cited lines with the cited metrics: app.js:153/247 (36-mer, pLDDT 94.8/94.3, dG -16.2/-17.5), app.js:173/371 (31-mer, 95.1/93.8, -16.9/-16.1), app.js:195/319 (41-mer, 93.2/92.8, -16.5/-15.7), app.js:205/361 (37-mer, 95.8/94.1, -17.2/-15.8). The determinism argument is correct, and the observation that the app's own renderer will draw pixel-identical structures and identical pLDDT curves beside contradictory summary numbers is correct because both generators are pure functions of the string. The ground-truth caveat (peptide pLDDT may legitimately differ in different complexes, but then the receptor must be an input entity with separate jobs and ipTM) is properly stated.
verdicts.corrections: THE FINDING IS MATERIALLY UNDERSTATED — it stops at the 25-drug array. Across all 35 sequence-bearing entries (25 drugs + 10 AF3_CANDIDATES) there are only 26 distinct sequences, and 5 of the 10 leaderboard fastas are byte-identical to 25-drug sequences with a different reported pLDDT, producing two THREE-WAY contradictions: KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG carries 94.8 (X2, app.js:153), 94.3 (B1, app.js:247) and 92.8 (CogAChE-PAS-02, app.js:131); SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC carries 93.2 (P1), 92.8 (M3) and 90.7 (CognACh-Mod-06, app.js:134). Three further cross-array pairs: app.js:163 vs :127 (97.0/96.1), app.js:215 vs :132 (93.9/93.6), app.js:225 vs :133 (92.5/91.9). So the correct statement is '9 of 35 entries are sequence duplicates and every duplicate group carries a different pLDDT', and '26 distinct sequences across 35 entries', not 'four pairs' and '21 distinct designs'. The build-time assertion in the fix must span both arrays. Separately, this finding is missing its strongest evidence — see missed_by_reviewer item 1, the thermodynamic inconsistency of every dG/Kd pair.

verdicts.reasoning: I recomputed every count from the file. Total Cys = 103; designs with >=4 Cys = 16; maximum 8, in HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (app.js:143) and PfcGluN2A-LTP-P3 (app.js:215); 11 designs with an odd count, and the reviewer's per-design list (X4:7, P2:7, P4:1, B3:5, B5:5, M1:5, M5:3, A1:5, A2:7, A3:7, A4:1) matches mine exactly. The X2 contradiction is real: app.js:152 specifies 'Cys-Lys Amide Coupling' and app.js:153 contains zero cysteine. Combinatorics verified (8 Cys -> 7!! = 105; 6 -> 15; 4 -> 3). Disulfide geometry ground truth is accurate (S-S 2.05 A, Cb-S-S ~104 deg, chi3 ~ +/-87 deg with left-handed-spiral preference) and these are exactly the quantities MolProbity/OneDep flag. Zero grep hits for disulfide, SSBOND, cystine, bondedAtomPairs. The free-thiol chemistry (scrambling, dimerisation, mixed disulfides with albumin Cys34 and glutathione) is correct, as is the point that FZD8 CRD (app.js:174) and TrkB Ig-like D5 (app.js:144) are cystine-framework-defined folds.
verdicts.corrections: Two counting caveats a reader will find. (1) A4 (app.js:381) appears in the odd-Cys list with C=1 only because its 'sequence' field is the prose string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' — the C comes from 'Conjugate'. It is not a design with a free thiol. The honest figure is 10 odd-Cys designs among 24 real sequences. (2) The 11 odd-count entries collapse to 8 distinct molecules, because X4/A3 are the same 7-Cys sequence and P2/A2 are the same 7-Cys sequence (per SB-04). Neither correction weakens the finding, but both should be stated so the numbers survive checking. On the fix: gating chi3 at +/-(75-105) deg is a reasonable flag but should not be a reject — real chi3 distributions are bimodal with substantial spread, and legitimate disulfides fall outside that window. The reviewer says 'flag', which is right; keep that wording.

verdicts.reasoning: I ran the greps myself over README.md, app.js, index.html and styles.css: 0 hits for each of molprobity, ramachandran, clashscore, posebusters, rdkit, openmm, mmcif, .cif, b-factor, resolution. Confirmed that the only quality-like numbers in the platform are the synthetic curve at app.js:791 and the hardcoded strings at app.js:146/156/166/... and README.md:96-102. All four literature anchors are real and cited correctly, which I verified independently: MolProbity, Williams et al., Protein Sci 27(1):293-315, DOI 10.1002/pro.3330 (PMID 29067766); wwPDB validation, Gore et al., Structure 25(12):1916-1927, DOI 10.1016/j.str.2017.10.009 (PMID 29174494); PoseBusters, Buttenschoen/Morris/Deane, Chem Sci 15(9):3130-3139, DOI 10.1039/D3SC04185A; Engh & Huber, Acta Cryst A47:392-400, DOI 10.1107/S0108767391001071 (confirmed via Crossref). The AF3 self-reported failure modes are quoted verbatim from the paper: 'The model outputs do not always respect chirality... we still observe a chirality violation rate of 4.4% in the benchmark' and 'a tendency of the model to occasionally produce overlapping (clashing) atoms'. The argument that AF3's own documented failure modes are precisely the ones only post-hoc validation catches is sound and well-supported.
verdicts.corrections: No factual error. One scoping point the reviewer should make explicit, because he concedes it in the overall assessment but not in the finding: this is not an independently actionable defect today, since there are no coordinates to validate. It is a required precondition on the SB-01/SB-03 remediation, not a standing gap that can be closed on its own. As written at MAJOR alongside the others it reads as a fifth independent problem when it is a conditional sixth. Minor factual note: RDKit 2026.03.5 IS installed in the repository's own .venv — it is simply never used by the platform, which if anything sharpens the point.

verdicts.reasoning: All four defects verified directly. (1) app.js:381 is literally sequence: 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. I ran it through the three generators: 37 characters; the pLDDT chart labels are H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8 exactly as claimed; the '14' point evaluates to 99.0 exactly; and copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) writes this string to the clipboard beneath a button offering AlphaFold Server submission. (2) I fetched the three.js r128 CatmullRomCurve3 source and the mapping is 'const p = ( l - ( this.closed ? 0 : 1 ) ) * t;' — so getPoint(i/L) returns control index i*(L-1)/L, and the displacement reaches 0.944 residues at i=L-2 for L=36 and 0.957 for L=47. Confirmed. (3) The i += 2 stride is at app.js:743 and app.js:1004. (4) SphereGeometry(2.2) at app.js:757 and SphereGeometry(2.5) labelled bindingSite at app.js:1012, both .position.set(0, 0, 0), with no relation to the bindingSites strings rendered in the same modal. The ground-truth statement (validate against the 20 standard codes, reject B/Z/J/X, key annotations to label_seq_id/auth_seq_id, define pockets from actual coordinates) is correct.
verdicts.corrections: Defect (3) is loosely attributed. The four-band legend at index.html:387-392 belongs to graph-box 2 (the pLDDT chart), not the 3D box, and the chart itself does plot every residue (app.js:787 loops 1..seqLen). The 'only half the residues' problem is confined to the 3D spheres, and the legend mismatch is an adjacency inference from the 3D panel's title at index.html:377, not a direct contradiction. Weaken the wording accordingly. Also, as in SB-03, the third 'B' at app.js:130 is missed. On the fix: 'reject any character outside the 20 standard codes' is too blunt for a pipeline that will later need modified residues — the validator should carry an explicit allow-list of permitted AF3 modification CCD codes alongside the 20. Finally, note that defects (2) and (3) evaporate the moment SB-01's fix lands; only (1) and (4) are independently actionable, which is why MAJOR rather than CRITICAL is the right level.

missed_by_reviewer: THERMODYNAMIC INCONSISTENCY OF EVERY dG/Kd PAIR — the single strongest arithmetic proof of fabrication in the repository, and the review never performs it. dG(deg) = RT ln(Kd); at 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol. The 25 reported Kd values (app.js:146,156,166,...) imply dG of -11.35 to -13.77 kcal/mol, but the dG reported in the SAME string runs -15.2 to -19.5. Every one of the 25 is too negative, by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol. Critically the offset is NOT constant (1.88 kcal/mol spread), so it cannot be rescued by a different standard state, temperature, or unit convention — if both numbers came from one calculation they would satisfy the relation exactly. The pairs are, however, almost perfectly rank-monotonic (1 inversion in 24), the signature of someone writing 'bigger dG implies smaller Kd' by hand. This is checkable by any reader in one line of Python and belongs in SB-04 as its primary evidence.

HALF THE NATURAL-PRODUCT SMILES ARE NOT MOLECULES, AND NONE CARRIES STEREOCHEMISTRY. index.html:118 advertises 'SMILES formulation, pharmacophoric moieties, receptor binding residue coordinates, and stereochemistry' and app.js:477 renders the field as 'SMILES Formulation'. Run through RDKit 2026.03.5 (already installed in the repo's own .venv): app.js:10 Huperzine A fails to parse at the grammar level; app.js:50 Curcumin fails to parse ('OCH3' is not SMILES — it must be OC); app.js:60 Onjisaponin V is the string 'C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)', a molecular formula not a SMILES; app.js:70 Salvianolic Acid B likewise 'C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)'. Of the four that do parse, two are the wrong compound: app.js:20 Ginsenoside Rg1 parses to C38H64O14 / MW 744.9 when the real compound is C42H72O14 / MW 801.0 — and the app's own chemStruct at app.js:142 states C42H72O14, so the SMILES contradicts the formula in the same repository; app.js:30 Ginkgolide B parses to C18H22O8 / MW 366.4 when ginkgolide B is C20H24O11 / MW 424.4 (app.js:370 states C20H24O10, also wrong). And every parseable SMILES has ZERO assigned stereocentres: Rg1 has 21 unassigned, ginkgolide B 12, asiatic acid 12. A SMILES with 21 unassigned centres denotes ~2 million stereoisomers. For a platform whose warheads are dammarane and ursane triterpenoids and a cage diterpene — molecules defined by their stereochemistry — this is a first-order error, and it makes SB-06's discussion of AF3's 4.4% chirality-violation rate moot: there is no chirality in the input to violate. This deserves its own finding at BLOCKER/CRITICAL and sits squarely in the discipline (SB-06 even names RDKit as the missing tool but never runs it on the data that IS present).

AChE ACTIVE-SITE RESIDUE NUMBERING CONFLATES TWO DIFFERENT PROTEINS, AND THE REVIEWER CREDITS IT AS CORRECT. app.js:154 reads 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)' — Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica AChE numbering while Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341 are human AChE numbering (the human equivalents of the first three are Trp86/Tyr337/Tyr124). No single structure exists in which all six numbers are correct. The repo is also internally inconsistent for the same compound: app.js:12 calls the PAS tryptophan 'Trp279' (Torpedo) while README.md:32 calls it 'Trp286' (human). The overall assessment explicitly praises 'the AChE CAS (Trp84/Phe330) and PAS (Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341) assignments' as correct and non-obvious — that credit is misplaced and should be withdrawn.

ZERO STRUCTURAL PROVENANCE ANYWHERE IN THE PLATFORM. Not one PDB accession, UniProt accession, resolution, method, or chain/auth-numbering convention appears in README.md, app.js or index.html, yet the platform asserts residue-level binding epitopes for TrkB, AChE, Keap1, FZD8, alpha7 nAChR, GluN2A, TLR4/MD-2, Trem2, TrkA, M1 mAChR, ER-beta and EAAT2. Every residue number in the app is therefore unverifiable by construction — a reader cannot tell whether 'Keap1 Tyr334, Arg415' (app.js:164) refers to the Kelch beta-propeller of any deposited structure or to nothing. Citing the source structure and its numbering scheme is the most basic provenance requirement in structural pharmacology and the review never raises it; it should be a MAJOR finding with the fix 'every residue-level claim carries a PDB ID (or UniProt accession) and states auth vs label numbering'.

THE LEADERBOARD IS RANKED BY AN UNDEFINED METRIC, AND IT IS NOT EVEN SORTED BY IT. Ranks 1-10 at app.js:125-134 are ordered by 'cei', surfaced as a table column at index.html:306 and as 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI / 100)' at app.js:1063. CEI has no formula, units, or provenance anywhere in the code, and appears 0 times in README.md. Worse, the ranking violates its own metric: rank 3 (CogNrf-KeapDis-03) has CEI 92.1 while rank 4 (CogTrk-DeNovo-01) has CEI 93.8. SB-04 correctly says the ranking is 'ordered on invented quantities' but never notes that the ordering quantity is undefined and self-inconsistent — which is a cleaner, purely internal demonstration than any of the pLDDT arguments.

THE PRIMARY 3D VIEWER IMPLEMENTS NO pLDDT COLOURING AT ALL. SB-01 and SB-02 both analyse only the modal viewer's letter-based colour rule (app.js:747-749). In update3DProteinStructure — the viewer behind the whole 'AF3 TOP 10 Candidates' tab — the residue spheres are hardcoded white at app.js:1006 (MeshPhongMaterial({ color: 0xffffff })). README.md:108 promises a 'residue-specific pLDDT color spectrum' for the '3D WebGL Molecular Engine'; in the main engine there is no colour mapping of any kind. This is a more direct README-to-code contradiction than the one the review actually cites.

NO ASSESSMENT OF WHETHER THE DESIGNED SEQUENCES ARE PLAUSIBLE FOLDED ENTITIES AT ALL. Several 'binders' are highly cationic amphipathic 30-40mers — KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:153/247) and FLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:329) — which is the canonical cell-penetrating / antimicrobial amphipathic-helix motif, not an AChE gorge or LC3 binder, and is a well-known source of nonspecific membrane lysis and false-positive binding. Others are GGGGS-linked two-domain fusions (app.js:183, 235, 287, 339, 391) for which any single reported pLDDT and single Kd is meaningless because the linker is by design disordered. A structural biologist assessing designed peptides would raise both: the first as a specificity/artefact concern that invalidates the stated mechanism, the second as a reason a chain-averaged confidence number cannot be reported at all. Neither appears in the review.

verifications.discipline: AI/ML for ADMET and toxicity property prediction — cheminformatics, computational safety pharmacology, model calibration and applicability domain
verifications.verifier_persona: Full professor / distinguished industry scientist, 20+ years post-PhD in computational safety pharmacology and cheminformatics; built and validated regulatory-facing hERG, seizure-liability and peptide-developability models; routine reviewer for Toxicol Sci and J Chem Inf Model. Independently re-read every cited line, re-ran every calculation in Python/RDKit, and resolved every PMID against PubMed before signing.

verdicts.reasoning: I re-derived every quantitative claim independently. `grep -n 'safety:' app.js` returns exactly 25 hits at the 25 lines cited (147,157,167,177,187,199,209,219,229,239,251,261,271,281,291,303,313,323,333,343,355,365,375,385,395). The sole read is app.js:640 (`${drug.safety}` inside the openDrugModal template literal, app.js:606-643); nothing parses, derives or validates it. `git ls-files` confirms the platform is README.md + app.js + index.html + styles.css only; no model, no manifest, no output JSON, no HTTP call, no descriptor code. The distributional forensics are exact, not approximate: 24 rows carry the byte-identical string 'hERG IC50 > 50 μM' and 1 (app.js:147) the same value with '(0% Cardiotoxicity)' appended; Seizure Index appears in 21/25 rows with exactly {0.00: 9, 0.01: 8, 0.02: 4}; and a Python extraction of the third pipe-delimited slot returns exactly 22 distinct labels. Every count the reviewer asserts reproduces. BLOCKER is the right call: README.md:98 ('All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening') has no referent whatsoever.
verdicts.corrections: Two factual imprecisions, neither altering the finding. (1) The file inventory is wrong: the repo also tracks skills-lock.json and a ~200-file .agents/skills/ library that includes chembl-database and alphafold-database skills with real analyze_plddt.py / analyze_pae.py scripts. None is wired to the platform, so the conclusion stands, but an absence-claim in a fabrication review must be exact. (2) The claimed 'zero hits' grep is overstated — 'clearance' matches at app.js:64, 112, 333, 359 and README.md:89. The defensible statement is 'no pharmacokinetic clearance anywhere; the only clearance hits are efficacy language about lysosomal and glutamate clearance.'

verdicts.reasoning: README.md:99 reads verbatim 'IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)' and app.js:147 '(0% Cardiotoxicity)'; both verified in situ. All three margin computations reproduce exactly in Python: 50/30 = 1.67 μM, 50/37 = 1.35 μM, 50/50 = 1.00 μM, and at the peptide MW I computed independently (4943.0 Da, average residue masses + water) those are 8.24, 6.68 and 4.94 mg/L. The Leishman citation is real and says precisely what is claimed — PMID 32768644, J Pharmacol Toxicol Methods 105:106900, n=367, CredibleMeds means 4.8/28/71/339, and the abstract states verbatim that ROC-optimal thresholds were '37- and 50-fold, respectively.' Lehmann PMID 29380488 likewise gives 0.312 (95% CI 0.205-0.476, p<0.0001) and a negligible-risk ratio of 80. The three-part critique is correct: a 0% claim is unfalsifiable, risk is a ratio whose denominator is absent, and a byte-identical single-significant-figure value across 25 chemically distinct entities is not a measurement or a prediction.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Same absence-grep overstatement as AIML-01: 'clearance' does appear, as efficacy language. Rephrase to 'no pharmacokinetic or exposure parameter of any kind.' (2) The reviewer enumerates the zero-risk claims but misses a fourth: app.js:375 asserts 'BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%', which belongs in the same deletion list as '0% Risk', '0% Cardiotoxicity' and 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%'.

verdicts.reasoning: The premise-falsification is airtight. I read every cited linker: app.js:183 (GGGGS), 235 (GGGGS), 277 (GGGSGGS), 287 (two GGGGS), 339 (GGGGS), 391 (GGGGS), 125 (GGGGSGGGGSGGGGS), 126 (GGSGGSGGSGGSGGS), 129 (GGGSGGS). Every peptide linker in the platform is Gly-Ser. Kyte-Doolittle G = -0.4 and S = -0.8 are correct. My own physicochemistry on the 36-mer reproduces the reviewer's to three decimals: GRAVY -1.09 (exact), Eisenberg hydrophobic moment 0.615 (exact), MW 4943.0, 13 Lys+Arg vs 4 Asp+Glu (exact). Both supporting papers are real and say what is claimed: Pardo-Lopez PMID 11864985 identifies Trp-585, Gly-590, Ile-593 (S5-P) and Pro-632 (P-S6) as the outer-vestibule determinants of ErgTx binding; Zavarzina PMID 38563123 shows BeKm-1 Arg20 forming a salt bridge plus hydrogen bonds with the vestibule and R20K dramatically reducing activity. The mechanistic sentence at README.md:99 is false against the repo's own sequence data and names a site the modality cannot reach.
verdicts.corrections: (1) 'There are no hydrophobic linkers in this platform' is too broad — app.js:182 declares a '1,2,3-Triazole Linker', app.js:194 a 'Trans-Cinnamoyl Linker', app.js:298 an 'Azide Linker'. None is a peptide linker, so README.md:99's specific phrase 'hydrophobic peptide linkers' remains false, but narrow the sentence to peptide linkers or the author refutes it in one line. (2) My net-charge calculation gives +8.79 at pH 7.4 rather than +8.98; the ~0.19 offset is a pKa-set difference (N-terminus) and is immaterial, but quote a pKa set. (3) The Tyr652/Phe656 attribution is given only as 'Ala-scanning of S6 and the pore helix; see e.g. Mitcheson-type SAR literature' — that is a gesture, not a citation, and I could not verify it as written. In a report whose thesis is unsourced numbers, replace it with a specific reference or delete the parenthetical.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified line by line: README.md:100 states 'Seizure Index = 0.01 - 0.02 / 1.0 (Negligible)' with 'capped Emax (135%)'; app.js:219 carries '(Capped Emax 135%)'; 21 of 25 rows carry a Seizure Index taking only {0.00, 0.01, 0.02}. The target classes are as cited: GluN2A NTD modulation (app.js:215-220), α7 nAChR ECD PAM (app.js:195-200), M1 mAChR PAM with explicit M-current suppression and increased burst firing (app.js:257-262), AChE gorge block raising synaptic ACh +350% (app.js:246-252). Cholinergic overdrive and M-current suppression are textbook proconvulsant mechanisms; the reported values invert the true risk direction. Cohen PMID 39661496 is real and the key numbers are exact: the integrated 11-target panel gives sensitivity 68%, specificity 56%, accuracy 65%, with Cav2.1 the highest-importance single target. Bradley PMID 29432603 is real: MEA on cryopreserved rat cortical neurons, 12 spike-train parameters, 20 chemicals, 16/17 seizurogenic/neurotoxic compounds detected. No standardized 0-1 seizure index exists; the metric is invented.
verdicts.corrections: (1) The Cohen evaluation set is misstated. The abstract says the 11-target panel was assessed against 34 preclinical compounds and 10 approved drugs; an *additional* 35 approved drugs were run in the Cav2.1 assay alone. 'against 34 preclinical compounds and 45 approved drugs' overstates the panel's evidence base. Also note the 68/56/65 figures are specifically for predicting convulsion in nonclinical species from the preclinical compound set. (2) Bradley used rat cortical neurons only; the reviewer's 'rodent cortical or hiPSC-derived' generalizes beyond the cited paper. (3) A stronger adjacent point is left on the table: app.js:251 pairs the most seizurogenic candidate in the portfolio (ACh +350%) with 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' — see missed_by_reviewer.

verdicts.reasoning: The core claim survives fully. README.md:102 reads verbatim 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days. Biased agonist signaling redirects receptors to recycling endosomes'; app.js:147 '< 3.5%', app.js:157 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%', app.js:187 '< 3.8%', app.js:199 'Receptor Desensitization: Low', app.js:261 'Desensitization: Safe'. A 30-day receptor-downregulation percentage is a chronic in vivo pharmacodynamic endpoint requiring repeat dosing plus Bmax/surface-biotinylation/immunoblot quantification and a vehicle arm; the repo contains no dose, route, species or PK model. No in-silico method outputs it. The bias rationale is equally unsupported — no operational-model fit, no ΔΔlog(τ/K_A), no β-arrestin readout, no Rab11-vs-Rab7 trafficking data.
verdicts.corrections: One sub-claim is factually wrong and must be struck. The reviewer writes that HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (app.js:157) has 'no receptor for it to downregulate, so the endpoint is not merely unmeasured, it is inapplicable.' That inverts the pharmacology. Chronic cholinesterase inhibition is the classical cause of muscarinic receptor downregulation and pharmacodynamic tolerance: Costa, Schwab & Murphy (Biochem Pharmacol 1982;31:3407-3413, PMID 7150362) showed 2 weeks of anticholinesterase dosing reduced forebrain muscarinic Bmax by 40% with cross-tolerance to oxotremorine. Tolerance is therefore *more* pertinent to the AChE-inhibitor candidates, not inapplicable — which makes 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%' at app.js:157 the single most inverted string in the file rather than a category error. Separately, the biased-signalling ground truth is supported only by bare 'PMC6620903' and 'PMC3952036' with no title, author, year or journal; I did not retrieve either and they cannot be checked as given. Replace with full citations or drop them.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified. README.md:101 and app.js:167, 271, 303, 323, 343 read as quoted. Grep over README.md, app.js and index.html for MHC|epitope|NetMHC|EpiMatrix|ADA|anti-drug returns zero — no immunogenicity analysis of any kind exists. My own frame enumeration reproduces the reviewer's counts exactly: the 36-mer yields 22 15-mer frames (22 with F/W/Y/L/I/V/M in positions 1-6) and the 100-mer at app.js:125 yields 86 frames (53 with such a residue). The innate/adaptive conflation at README.md:101 is a real category error — TLR4/MD2 antagonism cannot reduce MHC-II presentation of the construct's own sequence. Both methodology citations are real (NetMHCIIpan-4.3, PMID 38000035; ISPRI/EpiMatrix/JanusMatrix, PMID 38536724), and the AN1792 6% meningoencephalitis figure is confirmed independently in PMID 25860060 and PMID 21592055.
verdicts.corrections: (1) The P1-anchor screen flags 22 of 22 frames — a filter with a 100% hit rate conveys no information and should be presented as an illustration of unscored scale, not as evidence of epitope content. The reviewer's own 'candidate' hedge is right; the surrounding framing ('are therefore candidate P1-anchored MHC-II binders') overstates it. (2) The AN1792 analogy needs a caveat and is then stronger than stated. AN1792's meningoencephalitis is attributed to Th1 responses against T-cell epitopes in the mid/C-terminal region of Aβ delivered with QS-21 adjuvant — which is exactly why the second-generation vaccines named in PMID 25860060 (CAD106, ACC-001, AFFITOPE) restricted the antigen to the Aβ1-6 B-cell epitope. The repo's payload is Aβ16-35, squarely inside the region those programs deliberately excluded. An unadjuvanted conjugate is not the same exposure as an adjuvanted vaccine, so the 6% rate is not transferable — but the epitope-selection argument is more precise and more damaging than the raw incidence figure.

verdicts.reasoning: The physicochemistry is fully reproducible and I confirm it to three decimals on independent code using the Eisenberg consensus scale at 100°/residue: KWWKFLRRFWRR μH 0.989, MW 1865.3; FLRRFWRR μH 1.068, MW 1236.5; the 36-mer μH 0.615, GRAVY -1.09, MW 4943.0; melittin 0.353; LL-37 0.559. Every value matches the reviewer's. Grep confirms zero occurrences of hemoly/cytotox/aggregat/protease/proteoly outside the one efficacy hit at app.js:334. The substantive point is correct and important: the panel reports a small-molecule CNS liability set for peptides while omitting every peptide-specific liability. The reviewer's calibrated refusal to over-claim toxicity — citing Deslouches PMID 27046192, where WK12/WR12 showed negligible haemolysis and cytotoxicity up to 10× MIC — is exactly right and is the most scientifically disciplined passage in the review.
verdicts.corrections: (1) 'Trp/Arg-rich cationic 8-12-mers of exactly this composition are a well-characterized engineered-AMP series' is wrong on 'exactly'. The Deslouches eCAP series is composed *exclusively* of Trp plus Arg or Trp plus Lys; KWWKFLRRFWRR also contains Phe and Leu. Analogous chemotype, not identical composition. (2) 'peptides of 4-5 kDa with strongly negative GRAVY do not cross the blood-brain barrier' is stated too absolutely — brain-penetrant peptide shuttles and Arg-rich CPPs achieve measurable CNS uptake. The defensible form is that unmodified polycationic 4-5 kDa peptides have negligible passive BBB permeability and require an explicit delivery strategy, which the repo does not have. (3) Severity: lower to MAJOR. This is a missing-capability finding that asserts no false fact of its own and is largely subsumed by AIML-01; labelling five separate items CRITICAL beneath a BLOCKER parent is severity inflation that dilutes AIML-02/03/04/08, which each assert something affirmatively false.

verdicts.reasoning: The alignment is exact and I reproduced it against Aβ42 (DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA): KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM = Aβ16-35, KLVFFAED = Aβ16-23, KLVFFA = Aβ16-21, GAIIGLM = Aβ29-35. app.js:275 does label it 'AChE-Aβ Fibril Disruptor' and app.js:281 does read 'Fibril Blockade: 100%'. My physicochemistry on the app.js:277 construct reproduces the reviewer's GRAVY of +0.26 exactly (net charge +0.84 vs their +1.03, a pKa-set offset) — a near-neutral hydrophobic peptide, uniquely so in this portfolio. Balbach PMID 11076514 is real and states verbatim that Aβ16-22 is among the shortest fibril-forming fragments of full-length β-amyloid reported to date, with an antiparallel β-sheet organization and β-strand conformation extending from Leu17 through Ala21. 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' is a fabricated completeness claim on top of a directionally inverted design.
verdicts.corrections: The conclusion is right but the reasoning is one-sided and refutable as written. KLVFF is the canonical *recognition* motif for Aβ-targeting inhibitor design: Tjernberg et al. (J Biol Chem 1996;271:8545-8548, PMID 8621479) showed that peptides incorporating KLVFF (Aβ16-20) bind full-length Aβ and prevent its assembly into fibrils, and that work founded the whole KLVFF-based inhibitor class. So 'a wild-type copy of the CHC is a seed, not a breaker' is too strong as a general proposition and hands the author a one-move rebuttal. The precise version: (a) KLVFF as a recognition element is legitimate and precedented; (b) the hazard is the *extension* to Aβ16-35, which appends the second hydrophobic segment GAIIGLM (Aβ29-35) and yields an unmodified 20-mer spanning both aggregation-driving regions at near-neutral charge and positive GRAVY; (c) Balbach establishes that even the shorter Aβ16-22 self-assembles into ordered amyloid; (d) no register-disrupting modification (Pro, N-methyl, D-residue) is present anywhere in the construct. Also, the supporting 'PMID 21309606, PMID 35134456' are given bare with no titles and I did not verify them — supply full citations or remove.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified by extraction rather than inspection. Parsing the third pipe-delimited slot across all 25 records returns exactly 22 distinct labels, confirming the count; the second slot returns only 3 (Seizure Index, Cytokine Storm Risk, BBB Disruption Risk), so no two candidates share a full endpoint set and cross-candidate safety ranking is genuinely impossible. Every efficacy-flavoured field cited is real and sits under the heading 'ADMET Safety Profile & Side Effects' at app.js:639: Lysosomal Clearance +420% (app.js:333), Inflammatory Cytokine Suppression 98% (app.js:313), Vasodilation Rate +45% (app.js:355), Tau Hyperphosphorylation Suppressed (app.js:229), Fibril Blockade 100% (app.js:281). No interval, coverage level, probability, model identity, version, training set, AD verdict, timestamp or git SHA appears anywhere. The conformal-prediction, Chemprop and ADMET-AI citations (PMIDs 33075380, 38147829, 38913862) all resolve to real papers with the stated titles and venues.
verdicts.corrections: (1) The enumerated label list contains 23 items, one of which ('Cytokine Storm Risk') belongs to the second slot, not the third. The count of 22 is right; the list is not. Trim it. (2) A missed opportunity rather than an error: this is the one finding where the reviewer looks directly at the `affinity:` literals (app.js:146-394) and concludes only that they lack uncertainty. They are also internally impossible — ΔG and Kd cannot both be true for any of the 25 records, and the same sequence is assigned three different pLDDT values. That is a stronger, fully objective falsification and belongs here. See missed_by_reviewer items 1-3.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified verbatim. app.js:381 reads `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` and app.js:385 gives it a full ADMET profile ('hERG IC50 > 50 μM | Seizure Index: 0.00 | Cerebral Edema: Prevented'). The character B — the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx, rejected by AlphaFold Server for protein chains — appears in app.js:173, app.js:371 and app.js:130. All three of these plus the prose string flow unchecked through app.js:648-652 into initModal3DCanvas (app.js:708-729), renderModalPlddtChart (app.js:787-795) and renderModalPaeHeatmap (app.js:844-865). The reviewer is right that this is the cleanest single proof for AIML-01: no cached upstream computation can have existed if a prose string and an invalid residue code both render a safety profile and a confidence curve.
verdicts.corrections: (1) The copy-button count is wrong. copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) reads `currentActiveModalSequence`, which is set only from FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA at app.js:600. Exactly three copyable entries are invalid (app.js:173, 371, 381); the AF3 rank-6 fasta at app.js:130 is rendered at index.html:291 with no copy control. Three, not 'at least four'. (2) Severity: raise to MAJOR. The reviewer under-weights its own best evidence. This is not merely a missing guard — renderModalPlddtChart will emit and plot a per-'residue' AlphaFold3 confidence profile labelled L1 i2 n3 k4 e5 r6 for the letters of the English word 'Linker', under a heading that reads 'AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs' (index.html:371). That is affirmatively misleading rendered output, not an engineering hygiene gap, and it sits in the same class as the fabricated safety strings.

missed_by_reviewer: THE SINGLE LARGEST MISS — ΔG and Kd are thermodynamically impossible for all 25 candidates, and the reviewer read these exact strings (AIML-09 cites app.js:146-394) without checking them. ΔG = RT·ln(Kd); at 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol. Every pair is irreconcilable: X1 reports ΔG -18.4 kcal/mol with Kd 0.32 nM, but -18.4 implies Kd = 3.3e-5 nM (off by 9,828×); B5 reports -19.5 with 0.08 nM against an implied 5.1e-6 nM (15,730×). Across all 25 the discrepancy is 3.85-5.73 kcal/mol, i.e. 665-15,730× in Kd. Yet Pearson r(ΔG, ln Kd) = 0.997, so the two columns were generated from one another by a wrong formula; regressing gives an implied RT of 1.056 kcal/mol, i.e. a binding temperature of 531 K (258 °C). This is a two-line arithmetic falsification requiring no domain judgement and no literature, it is more objective than the distributional argument in AIML-01, and it independently destroys the 'affinity' half of the platform. It belongs in the report as a BLOCKER alongside AIML-01.

pLDDT is a deterministic function of the input sequence, and the platform assigns the same sequence three different values. KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears verbatim at app.js:153 (pLDDT 94.8, ΔG -16.2, Kd 2.1 nM), app.js:247 (94.3, -17.5, 0.65 nM) and app.js:131 as AF3 rank 7 (92.8, -12.6). Four further collisions: app.js:173 vs 371; app.js:195 vs 319; app.js:205 vs 361; and app.js:163 vs the AF3 rank-3 fasta at app.js:127 (97.0 vs 96.1). One molecule cannot have three AlphaFold3 confidences or three binding free energies. The reviewer cited app.js:153/247/131 as the same peptide (AIML-07) and did not notice the metrics conflict — a cleaner proof of fabrication than any statistical argument in the review.

The duplicate sequences directly falsify a specific safety string the reviewer never tested. The identical 41-mer at app.js:195 and app.js:319 is claimed to bind α7 nAChR ECD (Tyr188/Trp149/Tyr195) and TLR4/MD-2 (Arg264/Lys341/Glu439); the identical 37-mer at app.js:205 and app.js:361 is claimed to bind TrkB D5 and the EAAT2 transporter; the identical 31-mer at app.js:173 and app.js:371 to bind Frizzled-8 CRD and the ZO-1/occludin complex. app.js:209 — on one of those very rows — asserts 'Off-target Binding: None'. Demonstrated intra-repo promiscuity across four unrelated receptor families refutes the platform's only selectivity claim from its own data, which is exactly the off-target polypharmacology competence AIML-07 invokes but does not exercise.

SEVEN OF EIGHT SMILES STRINGS ARE UNUSABLE, WHICH MAKES THE REVIEW'S PRIMARY REMEDIATION IMPOSSIBLE AS WRITTEN. I parsed all eight in RDKit 2026.03.5. Four do not parse at all: Huperzine A (app.js:10), Curcumin (app.js:50 — the terminal 'OCH3' is an illegal token outside brackets and ring-closure 3 is unmatched), Onjisaponin V (app.js:60) and Salvianolic Acid B (app.js:70), the latter two being bare molecular formulas typed into a field the UI renders as 'SMILES Formulation' (app.js:477). Two parse but encode the wrong molecule: Ginsenoside Rg1 gives C38H64O14 not C42H72O14, and Ginkgolide B gives C18H22O8 not C20H24O10. Baicalein parses to the correct formula but the wrong regioisomer — InChIKey SXZJEWVPXPKGJG-UHFFFAOYSA-N, which is 6,7,8-trihydroxyflavone, not baicalein/5,6,7-trihydroxyflavone (FXNFHKRTJBSTCS-UHFFFAOYSA-N). Only Asiatic Acid is constitutionally correct, and it carries zero stereochemistry despite ~9 stereocentres. The reviewer instead praised this module as 'largely correct, checkable literature pharmacology... the strongest part of the repo,' and then proposed in AIML-01 step (2) to 'run ADMET-AI or Chemprop v2 over the warhead SMILES' — which cannot execute, because half the inputs are not molecules. Structure repair and RDKit round-trip validation must be step zero of any remediation plan.

The rendered 'pLDDT' is provably incapable of expressing the confidence bands the UI advertises, and the code contains dead guards that prove it. app.js:791 computes score = 93 + sin(i·0.4)·4 + (charCode % 5)·0.5, whose analytic range is 89.0 to 99.0. The guards at app.js:792-793 (`if (score > 100)` and `if (score < 70)`) are therefore unreachable dead code, and the legend at index.html:390-391 declaring 'Low (50-70)' and 'Very Low (<50)' bands can never be exercised. Worse, the 3D 'pLDDT Color Spectrum' at index.html:377 is coloured at app.js:747-749 by amino-acid identity (G/S green, P/D amber) — a lookup on the letter, not on any confidence value. Since AlphaFold reliably assigns low pLDDT to poly-GS linkers and disordered cationic peptides, the one region guaranteed to score low is the one this code paints green. This is a concrete, self-contained falsification of README.md:108-109 and Section 4.

A section titled 'In Silico ADMET' contains no A, D, M or E. Across README.md:96-102 and all 25 rows the only endpoints are hERG, a fabricated seizure index, and one rotating third slot. Entirely absent: absorption/permeability (Caco-2, PAMPA), plasma protein binding, BBB permeability, CYP inhibition and induction, DDI risk, metabolic stability, clearance, half-life, DILI/hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, Ames/genotoxicity, phototoxicity, and the ICH S7A secondary-pharmacology panel. A senior reviewer must publish the missing-endpoint inventory, because 'the T is fabricated' understates the problem — the ADME is not fabricated, it was never contemplated, and the section name is itself a misrepresentation.

'Peripheral Side Effects: None' (app.js:251) is the most directly falsifiable safety string in the file and goes unmentioned. It is attached to BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, whose stated mechanism at app.js:252 is elevating synaptic acetylcholine by +350%. The approved cholinesterase inhibitors — donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine — carry labelled nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, anorexia, bradycardia, syncope and AV block. This also exposes a conceptual gap in AIML-02: for a cholinomimetic, cardiac risk is not principally a hERG question at all — vagotonic bradyarrhythmia is mediated through muscarinic tone and would be invisible to any hERG assay, so even a genuine 'hERG IC50 > 50 μM' would not clear these candidates cardiologically.

The natural-product warheads are dominated by frequent-hitter chemotypes, and the review praises them instead.
