Curcumin (app.js:48-56, and the payload of app.js:298 and app.js:338) is formally classified as both a PAINS and an IMPS compound: Nelson, Dahlin, Bisson, Graham, Pauli & Walters, 'The Essential Medicinal Chemistry of Curcumin', J Med Chem 2017;60(5):1620-1637, PMID 28074653, concludes it is unstable, reactive, non-bioavailable and 'a highly improbable lead', with no successful double-blind placebo-controlled trial among >120 attempts. Baicalein and salvianolic acid B are polyphenol/catechol redox-cyclers and colloidal aggregators in the same interference class. Flagging assay-interference and bioavailability liabilities in the input chemotypes is core ADMET competence; the review's 'what is done well' section instead endorses this module, which is the one place the report overstates the repo's quality.

'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI)' is an invented metric that outranks everything the review did flag, and the source code admits it. CEI is hardcoded to three significant figures for all ten AF3 candidates (app.js:125-134), is the ranking column of the leaderboard (index.html:306), and is plotted at app.js:1053-1076 on a shared axis against |ΔG| in kcal/mol — a dimensionally meaningless comparison. The function that draws it sits under the author's own comment at app.js:1048: '--- Chart.js Benchmark Simulation ---'. A source comment conceding simulation, directly above the platform's headline benchmark, is the strongest single piece of intent evidence in the repository and the review never quotes it. In the same class: index.html:42 renders a badge reading 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' that is a static hyperlink with no connection of any kind, and README.md:24 and :111 claim 'direct live integration' — so the review's praise of the AlphaFold integration as 'the one place the platform behaves honestly' needs qualifying to the copy-FASTA control alone.

Two smaller in-domain defects. (a) Chemical formula error: app.js:266 gives 'Ginsenoside Rg3 Dammarane Core (C36H62O8)', which matches neither ginsenoside Rg3 (C42H72O13) nor its protopanaxadiol aglycone (C30H52O3); the other formulas I checked (Rg1 C42H72O14, Rb1 C54H92O23, curcumin C21H20O6, baicalein C15H10O5, ginkgolide B C20H24O10, bilobalide C15H18O8, asiatic acid C30H48O5, huperzine A C15H18N2O, presenegenin C30H46O6) are correct, so this one is an outlier worth a line. (b) No reference or control compounds: a 25-candidate safety panel that never runs donepezil, memantine, galantamine or a known hERG blocker and seizurogen through the identical pipeline has no scale, no calibration and no way to demonstrate that its numbers discriminate anything. Positive and negative controls should be a required element of the AIML-09 schema, not an optional extra.

verifications.discipline: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
verifications.verifier_persona: Full professor of human genetics and genomics, 22 years post-PhD; former head of a genetics-first target validation group in pharma, adjudicating go/no-go on CNS and immunology portfolios. Routine practice: Open Targets GraphQL, gnomAD v4 constraint and variant-level AF, GTEx/HPA expression partitioning, coloc and two-sample MR, and allelic-series direction-of-effect reasoning. I re-ran every external query in this session rather than accepting the reviewer's figures.

verdicts.reasoning: I re-ran every absence grep myself over all four files (wc -l gives 135/1103/415/1035 = 2688 lines, not 2689 — trivial). All 26 terms return 0: GWAS, genetic, genomic, variant, allele, gnomAD, 'Open Targets', ClinVar, GTEx, eQTL, LOEUF, colocali*, Mendelian, heritab*, 'odds ratio', 'effect size', 'p-value', biobank, 'loss-of-function', haploinsufficien*, DOI, PMID, PubMed, citation, reference. The 11 pLI hits are all substrings, confirmed. 'fetch' = 0 and 'XMLHttpRequest' = 0; I enumerated every URL in index.html/app.js and got exactly 5 distinct hosts (fonts.googleapis, fonts.gstatic, cdnjs, jsdelivr, alphafoldserver.com) with no API client — verified. The vendored-skills claim is verified and is in fact stronger than stated: `git ls-files` returns 235 tracked files, of which 229 are .agents/skills/** and only 6 are the project itself (.gitignore, README.md, app.js, index.html, skills-lock.json, styles.css); all 38 skills are keyed in skills-lock.json (I checked opentargets/gnomad/gtex/clinvar/encode/alphagenome/dbsnp/ensembl/human-protein-atlas — all PRESENT); none is referenced. I re-queried Open Targets myself (disease MONDO_0004975, associatedTargets Bs=[16 Ensembl IDs]) and every single score the reviewer quotes matches to three decimals: APP 0.872/gen 0.923, APOE 0.770/gen 0.889, ACHE 0.641/gen ABSENT, GRIN2A 0.623/gen ABSENT, TREM2 0.558/gen 0.862, GSK3B 0.554/gen ABSENT, CHRNA7 0.442, CHRM1 0.409, NTRK1 0.222, NOS3 0.187/gen 0.278, NTRK2 0.124/gen 0.080, NFE2L2 0.120, SLC1A2 0.112, KEAP1 0.088, PTAFR 0.085, FZD8 0.002/lit 0.015. I redid the portfolio arithmetic in python: 0.10/(0.25*2.6+0.75) = 7.14%, x2.6 = 18.57%, swing 11.43 points — exact. Two corrections force CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION rather than CONFIRMED, one of them material. First, the sentence 'no other platform target has AD anywhere in its genetic evidence' is contradicted by the reviewer's own data two sentences earlier (NOS3 gen 0.278, NTRK2 gen 0.080). Second and materially: the target inventory is incomplete. Reading FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA I count ~18 distinct declared binding-site targets, not 14 or 17, and the reviewer never queried six of them — APP/Aβ (app.js:278 'Aβ Oligomer Core (Lys28, Asp23)'; also app.js:158, app.js:334), ESR2 (app.js:352, 392), TJP1/OCLN (app.js:372), TLR4 (app.js:320), MAP1LC3B (app.js:330), AMPK (app.js:184). I ran them: APP genetic_association 0.923 — HIGHER than TREM2's 0.862 and the strongest in the whole set; TJP1 0.427; ESR2 0.227. So the headline statistic '1 of 17 (5.9%)' is wrong, and 'TREM2 is the one genetically validated target' is wrong: the platform's strongest genetically supported axis is Aβ/APP. The core finding — zero genetics layer, zero API calls, 38 unused vendored genomics skills — is unaffected and fully verified. One rhetorical overreach to trim: 'any reader who checks the file tree will reasonably assume the data flowed into the platform' is speculation; the README never mentions the skills, so no reader is actually misled by them. The verified fact (capability acquired, not used) is enough.
verdicts.corrections: Replace '1 of 17 distinct targets (5.9%)' and '13 of 14 named targets' with an inventory-complete figure. The platform declares ~18 distinct binding-site targets; at least six carry a non-zero AD genetic_association datatype score in Open Targets: APP 0.923, TREM2 0.862, TJP1 0.427, NOS3 0.278, ESR2 0.227, NTRK2 0.080 (verified this session). Delete 'no other platform target has AD anywhere in its genetic evidence' — self-contradictory and false. Delete 'TREM2 is the only platform target with AD in its genetic evidence at all.' Correct line total to 2688. Trim the 'reader checks the file tree' speculation. Pin resource versions (Open Targets release, gnomAD v4.1, GTEx v8) alongside the access date, since the report's own charge is unsourced numbers.

verdicts.reasoning: I verified every absence grep independently: 'indication', 'patient', 'placebo', 'endpoint', 'cohort', 'Phase I', 'MCI' all return 0 across all four files. I verified every quoted efficacy string at the cited line by reading the files: README.md:60 'CA1 LTP (+280%)', :67 '+240%', :71 'Information processing speed 2x', :74 'Synaptic ACh +350%', :84 '(+420%)', :88 'CBF +45%'; app.js:200 '+240% and sharpening operational focus'; app.js:240 'doubling cortical information processing speed'. All verbatim. README.md:22, index.html:7 and index.html:167 read as quoted. The disease-modifying/symptomatic/enhancement conflation is real and I confirmed it at the cited lines (app.js:188 Aβ/Tau clearance vs app.js:252 cholinesterase inhibition vs app.js:200 healthy-enhancement language). The load-bearing methodological point is correct and is core competence for this discipline: Minikel 2024's estimate is defined per target-INDICATION pair, so with no ontology term the strongest available prior on success is uncomputable in principle — I had to supply MONDO_0004975 myself to run any query at all, exactly as the reviewer reports. I tried to refute this finding as duplicative of GENO-01 and could not: a TPP is a distinct artefact and its absence independently blocks the analysis, so the concentration of two BLOCKERs is defensible rather than inflated. One unevidenced assertion to flag, not an error: the claim that cognitive-function/educational-attainment GWAS are 'massively polygenic with tiny per-locus effects and essentially no tractable single-target hits' is correct as far as I know but the reviewer retrieved no citation for it, while citing Bellenguez for the AD half of the same sentence. Either cite it or soften it.
verdicts.corrections: None to the substance. The cognitive-enhancement polygenicity claim needs a retrieved citation or should be softened to a stated professional judgement — every other assertion in this finding is line-verified.

verdicts.reasoning: This finding is right in its conclusion and partly wrong in its reasoning, and one of its four sub-claims does not survive. Verified first: every quoted safety string exists verbatim at the cited line (app.js:167, 177, 209, 219, 271, 281, 291, 303, 323, 343), and I confirmed by grep that app.js:177 'Tumorigenicity: Negligible' is the ONLY tumorigenicity/oncogenicity/cancer statement in the entire repository — grep for tumor|oncogen|carcino|cancer|neoplas|malign returns exactly that one line. index.html:252 and :254 do diagram β-catenin stabilization → TCF/LEF → cyclin D1 as a therapeutic 'Outcome' with no liability note. I re-queried all constraint and association data. gnomAD v4: GRIN2A pLI 1.0000, LOEUF 0.277, obs 22 / exp 113.4 (80.6% depletion); NTRK2 pLI 1.0000, LOEUF 0.219, 13/94.5 (86.2%); GSK3B pLI 0.9999, LOEUF 0.409, 15/56.4 — all exact. Open Targets: GRIN2A genetic Landau-Kleffner 0.948, hereditary disease 0.877, Seizure 0.850, Rolandic 0.838 — exact; KEAP1 somatic lung adenocarcinoma 0.796, NSCLC 0.706; NFE2L2 somatic HCC 0.774, HNSCC 0.657; NTRK1 clinical NSCLC 0.948, melanoma somatic 0.608, HSAN4 genetic 0.941; NTRK2 clinical NSCLC 0.947, obesity/hyperphagia/dev-delay genetic 0.827, DEE 0.796 — all exact. Huppke 2017 retrieved and the quoted sentence is verbatim from the abstract. (1) KEAP1/NFE2L2: FULLY CONFIRMED and the strongest sub-claim in the whole review — three of 25 candidates (X3 app.js:161-168, M2 :307-314, M5 :337-344) engineer constitutive NRF2 activation; KEAP1 LoF and NFE2L2 GoF are recurrent somatic drivers, the germline experiment has been done (Huppke), and app.js:167 carries no oncogenicity field at all. This alone carries CRITICAL. (2) GSK-3β/Wnt: CONFIRMED. (3) GRIN2A: conclusion confirmed, reasoning incomplete. The reviewer did not do the domain-resolved allelic series their own argument requires. I retrieved Strehlow et al., Brain 142:80-92 (2019), PMID 30544257, DOI 10.1093/brain/awy304 (248 individuals): missense in TMD+linker → NMDAR gain-of-function → severe phenotypes, whereas missense in ATD and LBD, plus null variants → loss-of-function → milder phenotypes. The platform's declared binding site (app.js:216) is the N-terminal domain — i.e. the ATD, the LoF/milder arm — so the human allelic series at the platform's own domain does not predict the severe GoF epilepsy phenotype the reviewer invokes. The finding survives because 'Excitotoxicity: Safe' and 'Seizure Index: 0.02' are fabricated numbers on an archetypal epilepsy gene, but the inference is weaker than stated. (4) NTRK1/NTRK2: PARTIALLY REFUTED as framed, on three grounds. (a) The LoF-intolerance argument is mis-deployed: NTRK2 LOEUF 0.219 / pLI 1.0 means loss is not tolerated, which for an AGONIST programme is evidence FOR the direction, not against it — the reviewer's own literature entry frames LOEUF as bounding 'partial inhibition', which is not what these candidates do. That is a direction-of-effect error inside a finding about direction-of-effect errors. (b) TRK oncogenicity in humans arises from somatic gene fusions producing ligand-INDEPENDENT constitutive kinase activation; Drilon 2018 is a trial in fusion-positive tumours. Treating 'the approved oncology pharmacology is inhibition' as settling the direction question for ligand-mimetic agonism is a false dichotomy. (c) The human experiment has been run at the platform's exact anatomical target: I retrieved Rafii et al., JAMA Neurol 75:834-841 (2018), PMID 29582053, DOI 10.1001/jamaneurol.2018.0233 — AAV2-NGF stereotactically injected into the nucleus basalis of Meynert in 49 mild-to-moderate AD patients was 'safe and well-tolerated through 24 months' with no effect on ADAS-Cog. BasalNgf-TrkA-B3 (app.js:265-272) targets that same structure. The defensible criticism of B3 is that NGF/TrkA agonism in the NBM has already FAILED on efficacy in a randomised human trial the platform does not cite, not that it carries an unrecognised oncogenic liability. Finally, the reviewer under-states the real defect: I searched app.js and there is no code path anywhere that computes, derives or validates any safety, affinity or pLDDT value — all 25 safety fields are string literals, including the identical 'hERG IC50 > 50 μM' on every candidate. That is more damning than any direction-of-effect argument.
verdicts.corrections: Retitle to three programmes, not four: Keap1/Nrf2 (three candidates), GSK-3β/Wnt, and GRIN2A at reduced strength. Reframe the NTRK sub-claim: drop the LoF-intolerance argument entirely (wrong metric for an agonist), state that TRK oncogenicity is fusion-driven ligand-independent activation rather than evidence against physiological agonism, and replace it with the verifiable point that AAV2-NGF into the nucleus basalis of Meynert was already tested in AD and was safe but ineffective (Rafii 2018, PMID 29582053) — which the platform cites nowhere. For GRIN2A, add the domain-resolved allelic series (Strehlow 2019, PMID 30544257): the platform's declared NTD/ATD binding site is the loss-of-function, milder-phenotype arm, so state the residual objection as 'a fabricated seizure margin on an archetypal epilepsy gene' rather than 'the genetics predicts exactly this phenotype'. Extend the deletion instruction from the 7 listed strings to all 25 safety fields (app.js:147,157,167,177,187,199,209,219,229,239,251,261,271,281,291,303,313,323,333,343,355,365,375,385,395) — every one is a literal, and the uniform hERG value across chemically unrelated conjugates is itself proof of fabrication.

verdicts.reasoning: I re-queried GTEx v8 median TPM myself via the v2 API and every number the reviewer reports is exact: NOS3 Cortex 4.288 / Hippocampus 2.243 / Spleen 75.479 / Lung 13.547; PTAFR Cortex 0.680 / Hippocampus 1.123 / Whole Blood 40.192 / Spleen 21.064; KEAP1 Cortex 29.066 / Muscle 88.333 / Artery-Tibial 37.826 / Lung 35.794; GSK3B Cortex 14.929 / Lung 19.305 / Artery-Tibial 16.054 / EBV 29.932; NTRK2 Cortex 74.242 / Artery-Tibial 37.531; ACHE Cortex 18.316 / Muscle 22.395; SLC1A2 Cortex 361.666 vs max non-brain Pancreas 6.049; CHRM1 Cortex 55.177 vs Prostate 25.642; GRIN2A Cortex 11.288 vs Testis 1.435; CHRNA7 Cortex 0.334. The CHRFAM7A point checks out exactly — I queried ENSG00000166664 and Open Targets returns approvedName 'CHRNA7 (exons 5-10) and FAM7A (exons A-E) fusion', the reviewer's quote verbatim. The absence greps (GTEx, single-cell, scRNA, transcriptom, Protein Atlas = 0) are verified. Three corrections, one of them material. (i) Arithmetic: PTAFR whole-blood/cortex is 40.192/0.679934 = 59.1x, not 57x. Conservative direction but wrong as printed. (ii) MATERIAL — the flagship A1 example attacks the wrong gene. AstroEos-NO-A1's declared binding site (app.js:352) is 'Estrogen Receptor-β (ER-β) LBD (Glu305, Arg346)'; eNOS/NOS3 appears only in the downstream mechanism string at app.js:356. The reviewer analysed NOS3 GTEx as though eNOS were the target. I ran the correct gene: ESR2 Brain-Cortex 0.098 TPM, Brain-Hippocampus 0.058 TPM, max non-brain Ovary 4.630 — ER-β is essentially absent from human cortex, 47x lower than ovary. The reviewer's conclusion is therefore right and substantially STRONGER than they argued, but reached through the wrong gene; the same applies to A5 (app.js:392). This is a correct-conclusion/wrong-reasoning case and must be fixed before issue, because a target-assignment error in a target-validation review is disqualifying on its own terms. (iii) Methodological: bulk GTEx median TPM ratios measure tissue composition, not in-vivo target engagement. NOS3's spleen signal reflects the spleen's high endothelial content — NOS3 is an endothelial gene and cerebral endothelium expresses it too — so 'a systemically administered eNOS stimulator engages peripheral vasculature far more than cerebral vasculature' follows from total vascular bed mass and BBB penetration, neither of which the reviewer analysed, not from a TPM ratio. The reviewer concedes the bulk-averaging problem in the ground_truth section and then uses the ratios as engagement estimates anyway. The PTAFR/A4 example is clean because PAFR IS the declared binding site (app.js:382), and KEAP1/GSK3B ubiquity is straightforwardly correct. The core finding — the five-region map is asserted with zero expression evidence and is contradicted for several targets — survives fully.
verdicts.corrections: Fix the PTAFR ratio to 59.1x. Replace the NOS3 analysis for A1/A5 with ESR2, the actually declared binding target: ESR2 Brain-Cortex 0.098 TPM, Brain-Hippocampus 0.058 TPM, max non-brain Ovary 4.630 (47x cortex) — near-absent from human cortex, which is a far stronger contradiction of the astrocyte/BMEC assignment than the NOS3 figures. Keep the NOS3 data as a note on the downstream mechanism claim, clearly separated from the binding-target analysis. State explicitly that bulk TPM ratios index tissue composition, not target engagement, and that peripheral-liability inference additionally requires vascular-bed mass and BBB penetration. Add TJP1 (A3's declared target, app.js:372): Cortex 22.13 vs Nerve-Tibial 99.08 and Artery-Tibial 60.36 — another ubiquitous, non-CNS-enriched target the review never assessed.

verdicts.reasoning: The central factual claim is the single best-verified item in the review and I confirmed it digit for digit. I queried gnomAD v4 for 6-41161514-C-T: rsid rs75932628, transcript consequence TREM2 p.Arg47His missense; exome AC 4174 / AN 1,461,812 / AF 0.0028554; genome AC 304 / AN 152,342 / AF 0.0019955 — every figure matches the reviewer exactly. TREM2 constraint: pLI 7.9e-07, LOEUF 1.268, 20 observed vs 22.9 expected LoF (12.7% depletion) — exact, and correctly interpreted as LoF-tolerant/recessive-consistent. Open Targets TREM2 genetic_association: Nasu-Hakola 0.887, Alzheimer disease 0.858, frontotemporal dementia 0.666 — matches (minor: 'hereditary disease' 0.672 actually outranks FTD). I retrieved Jonsson 2013 and Guerreiro 2013 and both quoted passages are verbatim from the abstracts, including OR 2.92 (95% CI 2.09-4.09, P=3.42e-10), combined OR 2.90 (P=2.1e-12), 0.46% frequency in controls aged 85+, and cognition P=0.003 in non-demented carriers aged 80-100. The platform does name Arg47 as an agonist contact residue at app.js:300 and I confirmed 0 hits for R47H, rs75932628, Nasu-Hakola, stratification, genotype and biomarker anywhere in the repo. The catch is genuine and the generalised fix is the most valuable single recommendation in the review. Three corrections. (i) 'TREM2 is the only platform target with AD in its genetic evidence at all' is false — I verified APP 0.923, TJP1 0.427, NOS3 0.278, ESR2 0.227 and NTRK2 0.080 all carry AD genetic_association, and APP outranks TREM2. Same error as GENO-01. (ii) The load-bearing mechanistic premise — 'R47H sits in the ligand-binding surface of the TREM2 Ig-like domain and impairs ligand engagement' — is asserted with no retrieved citation. Guerreiro and Jonsson establish the association, not the binding-surface mechanism. It is well supported in the literature, but in a report whose central charge is unsourced assertion, an uncited structural premise carrying the whole 'the agonist may not bind in carriers' argument must be sourced or flagged. (iii) Framing gives the platform too much credit for specificity. Arg47/Asp87/Lys112 have no computational provenance — the whole array is hardcoded, three FASTA sequences contain the non-standard residue 'B' (app.js:130, 173, 371), and app.js:381's 'sequence' field is the English phrase 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. The residue triple is decoration, and its collision with the target's most consequential coding variant is almost certainly coincidence, not a design decision with a stratification gap. The correct reading — that the platform named the single variant that made TREM2 a validated target without noticing — is evidence for GENO-01's thesis rather than a standalone stratification failure. Severity: I would lower this to MODERATE. It is a genuine and illuminating catch, but as written it is a corollary of GENO-01 applied to fabricated data, and MAJOR overstates a finding whose subject is a string literal. It should be retained and prominently placed, because the generalised fix is excellent.
verdicts.corrections: Delete 'TREM2 is the only platform target with AD in its genetic evidence at all' (refuted: APP 0.923 > TREM2 0.862, plus TJP1 0.427, NOS3 0.278, ESR2 0.227, NTRK2 0.080). Cite or flag the R47H ligand-binding-surface mechanism — Guerreiro and Jonsson establish association only. Reframe the finding: the residue triple has no provenance and the Arg47 collision is most likely coincidental, which makes it evidence that no genetics was consulted (GENO-01) rather than an unaddressed stratification decision on a real molecule. Note as corroboration that three sequences contain the non-standard residue 'B' and that app.js:381 substitutes an English phrase for a sequence.

missed_by_reviewer: APP/Aβ is the platform's strongest genetically supported axis and was never assessed. Open Targets AD genetic_association: APP 0.923, higher than TREM2's 0.862 and the highest of any target in the set (verified this session). Three candidates engage Aβ directly — BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 (app.js:277-278, 'Aβ Oligomer Core (Lys28, Asp23)'), HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (app.js:158) and MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 (app.js:334). The review's headline statistic and its 'TREM2 is the one defensible target' framing are both wrong because of this omission.

Six declared binding-site targets were never queried at all: ESR2 (A1 app.js:352, A5 app.js:392), TJP1/OCLN (A3 app.js:372), TLR4 (M3 app.js:320), MAP1LC3B (M4 app.js:330), AMPK/PRKAA (X5 app.js:184), APP (B4 app.js:278). Two carry non-zero AD genetic_association (TJP1 0.427, ESR2 0.227). A target-validation review must inventory the target list before scoring it; the reviewer scored 14 of ~18 and reported the denominator inconsistently as 14 in the title, 17 in the body and 14 again in the overall assessment.

APOE is absent from the entire platform and the review never says so. APOE is the largest common-variant risk factor for late-onset AD (Open Targets AD genetic_association 0.889, verified) and the single most important stratification variable in modern AD trials, driving both efficacy expectations and ARIA-type safety management. It appears nowhere across 25 candidates, 8 natural products, 10 AF3 candidates or the five-region map. For a cognition portfolio this is a more glaring omission than any individual target's weak score.

No tractability or modality analysis, which moots the entire regional-targeting discussion more directly than any expression argument. Every candidate is a 28-47-residue peptide bio-conjugate (app.js sequence fields), a size class with negligible passive blood-brain-barrier penetration, and not one candidate declares a transport or delivery strategy. The reviewer cites the Open Targets paper specifically for its tractability annotations and then never queries tractability or subcellular localisation for a single target. Whether a target is even reachable precedes whether it is genetically supported.

FZD8 is scored nowhere despite being the review's own smoking gun. FZD8 has the platform's lowest AD association (0.002, literature 0.015 — verified, statistically indistinguishable from a random gene) and HippoWnt-FzdAgonist-X4 is the only candidate in the repository carrying an explicit tumorigenicity claim ('Tumorigenicity: Negligible', app.js:177 — I confirmed by grep this is the only tumor/oncogen/cancer string in all four files). A canonical Wnt agonist with essentially zero disease association and a self-asserted null oncogenicity claim is the cleanest single example in the portfolio, and the review quotes the string without ever evaluating the programme.

No audit of whether the claimed binding residues correspond to the real proteins. TREM2 Arg47/Asp87/Lys112, GluN2A Glu201/Lys210, FZD8 Phe72/Tyr125/Asp99/Arg104, EAAT2 Thr368/Lys490 and the rest are asserted with no UniProt or PDB provenance anywhere in the repo. The reviewer credits the AChE residues as 'broadly consistent' but performs no systematic check — and their own excellent GENO-05 fix (surface ClinVar/gnomAD variants falling in any claimed binding site) is only implementable once residue numbering is validated against a reference sequence.

Direct machine-checkable proof that the 'AlphaFold3' outputs are character-code art, which corroborates the whole fabrication thesis and was missed. app.js:381 sets the `sequence` field of AstroPafr-Block-A4 to the English phrase 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'; that string is passed unchecked to initModal3DCanvas, renderModalPlddtChart and renderModalPaeHeatmap (app.js:649-651), so the modal renders a 37-residue pLDDT confidence curve and a PAE matrix computed from the character codes of hyphens and digits. Three other sequences (app.js:130, 173, 371) contain 'B', which is not a standard amino-acid code and which AlphaFold Server would reject. Two 'SMILES Formulation' fields contain molecular formulas rather than SMILES (app.js:60, app.js:70) and the curcumin SMILES at app.js:50 terminates in the invalid token 'OCH3'.

No versioning of the reviewer's own evidence. The review instructs the platform to stamp every panel with resource release version and access date (GENO-01 fix item 5) but pins none of its own numbers beyond 'accessed 2026-08-16'. LOEUF values differ between gnomAD v2/v4.0/v4.1, association scores change between Open Targets releases, and GTEx v8 has been superseded by v10 — all of which I had to assume rather than confirm from the report. In a review whose central charge is unsourced numbers, the report must meet its own standard.

verifications.discipline: AI/ML evaluation methodology, benchmarking, split design, and reproducibility for scientific machine learning
verifications.verifier_persona: Full professor of machine learning evaluation; 20+ years post-PhD on benchmark construction, leakage forensics, predictor calibration, and reproducibility auditing for scientific ML. Standing reviewer and occasional area chair for ML-for-biology venues; my role here is to re-derive every number the reviewer asserts and to try to break each finding before it is issued under my name.

verdicts.reasoning: I re-read app.js:1048-1103 and index.html:296/316 directly. The comment at app.js:1048 is verbatim '// --- Chart.js Benchmark Simulation ---'; lines 1053-1055 map AF3_CANDIDATES[].code/.cei/Math.abs(.dg) straight into the chart; the literals are declared at app.js:125-134. Confirmed. I re-ran the reviewer's word-boundary greps myself with `grep -owiE` over all four files: baseline, held-out, holdout, 'test set', validation, cross-validation, k-fold, ablation, 'error bar', 'confidence interval', p-value, 'sample size', scrambled, scramble, control, bootstrap, significance, Bonferroni, FDR, AUROC, enrichment, RMSD, TM-score, DockQ, ECE, calibration, PoseBusters, CASP, CAMEO all return exactly 0. Confirmed. CEI: grep for 'CEI|Cognitive Enhancement' returns only app.js:1063 (a chart label), index.html:306 (a column header) and index.html:316 (a panel title) -- no definition, no formula, no units anywhere. Confirmed. I recomputed Pearson r(CEI,|dG|) = 0.9389 -- the reviewer's 0.939 is exact. Ordering: pLDDT has 4 descending inversions, |dG| has 3 (positions 4-5, 7-8, 9-10, exactly as stated), CEI has 1.
verdicts.corrections: The reviewer's ordering argument overstates. CEI has exactly ONE inversion (rank 3 = 92.1 below rank 4 = 93.8) and r(rank, CEI) = -0.9845; nine of ten positions are reproduced by a plain descending-CEI sort. The evident sort key is descending CEI with a single transposition of rows 3 and 4, not, as the reviewer writes, an ordering in which 'the ordering has no rule' and where 'No composite of the three columns reproduces the ordering either.' That phrasing invites an easy rebuttal and it changes the fix: the action is to publish CEI's definition and repair one transcription error, not to invent a scoring function from scratch. Second, minor: the reviewer attributes raw substring hits for 'control' to the OrbitControls variable. Whole-word 'control' is indeed 0, but whole-word 'controls' occurs 8 times (app.js:406, 930-932, 953, 1032 twice; index.html:16, 276) as the Three.js variable -- the parenthetical is right in substance but the grep as described would not have produced it. Neither correction touches the finding's conclusion: there is no benchmark, no baseline, no held-out data, and CEI is undefined. One wrinkle in the fix worth flagging to whoever implements it: fix item (3) says to run the 25 sequences 'plus a matched set of baselines ... through the same pipeline', but there is no pipeline to run them through, and a small-molecule positive control such as donepezil does not yield a score commensurable with a peptide binder's ipTM, so the four arms cannot literally share one axis.

verdicts.reasoning: I reimplemented app.js:787-794, :844-851 and :711-755 in Python and ran them over the actual 25 sequences. Every headline number is exact. Total residues 876 (reviewer: 876). Plotted pLDDT range [89.0, 99.0] (reviewer: exactly [89.0, 99.0]). Clamp at app.js:792 (>100) never fires; clamp at app.js:793 (<70) never fires -- both dead, confirmed. Band split: 67 of 876 residues (7.65%) in [89.0, 90.0), 92.35% above 90 -- the reviewer's 7.6%/92.4% is exact; bands 'Low (50-70)' and 'Very Low (<50)' at index.html:390-391 receive 0 residues and are structurally unreachable. Period 2*pi/0.4 = 15.708 confirmed. ASCII mod-5 buckets verified residue by residue: {A,F,K,P}=0, {G,L,Q,V}=1, {C,H,M,R,W}=2, {D,I,N,S}=3, {E,T,Y}=4 -- the reviewer's partition is exactly right; P and A do collide, G and L do collide. PAE ceiling 44*0.4+0.9 = 18.5 against an axis captioned '0 - 30 Angstrom' at index.html:397, so 38.3% of the advertised range is unreachable; reviewer's 38% confirmed. Spheres: 446 drawn across the 25 modals, 111 painted non-cyan, and 104 (23.3%) painted 'High' or 'Low' at indices where the pLDDT curve in the same modal returns >= 90 -- the reviewer's 446/104/23.3% is exact. Card-vs-curve: mean absolute discrepancy 1.051, max 2.693 at id 3 (card 97.0 at app.js:166 vs drawn mean 94.31) -- reviewer's 1.05 / 2.69 / id 3 / 97.0 / 94.31 all exact. This is the most carefully verified finding in the review and I could not break any part of it.
verdicts.corrections: Three repairs. (1) The reviewer writes 'for the actual sequences (28-45 aa) it is 11.7-18.5 Angstrom'. Actual sequence lengths in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA are 26-47 aa, and the per-sequence PAE maxima span 10.90-18.50 Angstrom, not 11.7-18.5. (2) '[89.0, 99.0] exactly' holds for the values actually plotted, because app.js:794 pushes score.toFixed(1); the unrounded function cannot attain the endpoints since sin(0.4i) never equals plus or minus 1 at integer i. State it as the plotted range so an author cannot quibble; the dead-clamp conclusion is unaffected. (3) Two further defects in the same panels are missed and strengthen the finding: app.js:844 caps the PAE grid at 45, but id 1's sequence is 47 aa, so its heatmap silently drops residues 46-47 while captioned as that candidate's matrix; and because `error` at app.js:850 depends on i but not j, the matrix is not symmetric -- 1,484 of 2,025 cells in id 1's map disagree with their transpose.

verdicts.reasoning: I parsed all 25 sequence fields programmatically rather than trusting the quotation. Exactly four sequences appear twice and every reported metric matches the reviewer character for character: KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG at app.js:153 (id 2: -16.2, 2.1 nM, 94.8) and app.js:247 (id 11: -17.5, 0.65 nM, 94.3); CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH at app.js:173 (id 4: -16.9, 1.2 nM, 95.1, Frizzled-8 CRD) and app.js:371 (id 23: -16.1, 2.8 nM, 93.8, ZO-1/Occludin); SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC at app.js:195 (id 6: -16.5, 1.8 nM, 93.2, alpha7 nAChR ECD) and app.js:319 (id 18: -15.7, 3.8 nM, 92.8, TLR4/MD-2); VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH at app.js:205 (id 7: -17.2, 0.85 nM, 95.8, TrkB D5) and app.js:361 (id 22: -15.8, 3.6 nM, 94.1, EAAT2/GLT-1). Thermodynamics re-derived independently: RT at 298.15 K = 0.592484 kcal/mol; id 1's Kd of 0.32 nM implies dG = -12.9533 against a reported -18.4, so the reviewer's -12.95 is exact. Across all 25 the residual is mean -4.735, SD 0.546, spanning 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol, and the reported dG is more negative than implied in 25 of 25 cases -- the reviewer's '-4.74 +/- 0.55' and '3.85 to 5.73' are exact, and the 1.9 kcal/mol spread does rule out a single fixed reference-state or unit-convention offset. Alphabet: ids 4 and 23 contain B; id 24's sequence field at app.js:381 is the literal string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' carrying 19 distinct non-standard characters and still assigned pLDDT 92.4 at app.js:384. All confirmed; I could not refute any element.
verdicts.corrections: The reviewer materially UNDERSTATES the effect. Cross-referencing FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA against AF3_CANDIDATES yields seven further byte-identical collisions carrying a THIRD divergent metric set: KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG is also AF3 rank 7 (app.js:131, pLDDT 92.8, dG -12.6), so one identical string carries pLDDT 94.8 / 94.3 / 92.8 and dG -16.2 / -17.5 / -12.6; SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC is also AF3 rank 10 (app.js:134, 90.7, -12.1); and AF3 ranks 3, 8 and 9 (app.js:127, 132, 133) are byte-identical to ids 3, 8 and 9 with different pLDDT and dG in each case. The true spread on a single identical input is 2.5 pLDDT units and 4.9 kcal/mol -- three to six times the '0.4-1.7 units' and '0.8-1.4 kcal/mol' reported. Additionally AF3_CANDIDATES rank 6 (app.js:130) also contains B and is the string rendered to users at index.html:291 under the caption 'FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)'; the alphabet finding is scoped to the 25 only and misses it.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified directly. All 25 `affinity` fields (app.js:146, 156, 166, 176, 186, 198, 208, 218, 228, 238, 250, 260, 270, 280, 290, 302, 312, 322, 332, 342, 354, 364, 374, 384, 394) report only dG, Kd and a monomer pLDDT. AF3_CANDIDATES (app.js:125-134) carries plddt, dg and cei and no iptm/ptm/pae_interaction. Leaderboard columns at index.html:303-307 are Rank / Code / Target / pLDDT / dG / CEI. Word-boundary grep for ipTM, pTM and DockQ returns 0 in all four files. I searched for UniProt-style accessions, PDB IDs in a PDB context, ChEMBL ids and Ensembl ids across README.md, app.js and index.html: zero hits. There is genuinely no target structure and no accession anywhere, so no complex can have been predicted, and the core claim -- a binding assertion supported only by a monomer confidence metric, with no scrambled negative, no literature positive, no decoy panel and no self-consistency loop -- stands. 'decoy' occurs exactly 5 times (README:62, 82, 85; app.js:161; index.html:230), all as compound names, never as a control set; the reviewer's count is exact.
verdicts.corrections: Two corrections, one of which strengthens the finding. (1) The reviewer states 'grep for ipTM/iPTM/pTM/DockQ/interface returns zero hits across all four files.' That is false for 'interface': app.js:126 contains 'TrkB Dimerization Interface' as the target string for AF3 rank 2. The hit is a target label rather than an interface metric, so the substantive claim survives, but an author can rebut the review with one grep and the sentence must be corrected before issue. (2) The reviewer frames this as 'the wrong metric class for the claim.' The sharper and unanswerable statement, never made, is that AlphaFold3 emits no binding free energy and no dissociation constant in any configuration -- it returns coordinates plus pLDDT, PAE, pTM and ipTM. Two of the three quantities on every affinity line are therefore not AF3 outputs at all, independent of whether a complex was predicted; that should lead the finding. (3) Overstatement to trim: the reviewer says the duplicate pairs 'measure' a specificity margin 'at roughly 0.8-1.4 kcal/mol.' Nothing was measured -- no target was ever supplied to any procedure. Phrase it as 'the same string carries two different asserted affinities against unrelated targets'; calling it a measured margin concedes the premise the review is attacking.

verdicts.reasoning: Every cited location verified by line number. README:60 (+280% LTP), :64 (+310% spine density), :67 (+240% working memory), :71 ('2x' processing speed), :74 (+350% ACh), :84 (+420% Abeta degradation), :88 (+45% CBF) all read as quoted; a regex sweep of README.md returns exactly the set {+280%, +310%, +240%, +350%, +420%, +45%} and nothing else, so the enumeration is complete. Impossible-as-estimates values confirmed at app.js:147 ('0% Cardiotoxicity'), :157 ('Tolerance Rate: 0.0%'), :209 ('Off-target Binding: None'), :251 ('Peripheral Side Effects: None'), :281 ('Fibril Blockade: 100%'), :323 ('Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%'), :375 ('BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%'), plus composite scores at :291, :343, :395. Zero-variance predictor claim verified exactly: the hERG substring is 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' identically in 24 of 25 entries and 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Cardiotoxicity)' in the 25th -- precisely '24 exactly, 1 with an appended'. Seizure Index distribution counted: 0.00 nine times, 0.01 eight times, 0.02 four times, absent four times -- exact. Word-boundary grep for 'sample size', 'confidence interval', 'p-value', 'bootstrap', 'Bonferroni' and 'FDR' returns 0 across all files. The 'LTP +280% has no referent' argument is correct and is a legitimate operational-definition claim well within scope: the field convention is percent-of-baseline fEPSP slope, the README fixes no comparator, so the number cannot be falsified.
verdicts.corrections: One quantitative slip. The reviewer writes 'log2(3) is approximately 1.58 bits of total information for a 25-compound safety screen.' log2 of the symbol count is not the information content: the empirical Shannon entropy of the observed 9/8/4 distribution is 1.510 bits per compound, and the total over the 21 populated entries is about 31.7 bits, not 1.58. Say 'at most 1.58 bits per compound, empirically 1.51', or drop the bit count and keep the plain observation that three distinct values across 25 chemically distinct entities cannot support a validation. Second, an omission in the fix rather than the finding: README:98 reads 'All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening' -- an affirmative assertion that a procedure was executed, categorically different from an unsupported point estimate and the single sentence that most directly misrepresents what was done. It appears in no evidence_location and 'Rewrite Section 3' does not name it; it must be deleted explicitly.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified against the repository itself. `git ls-files` returns 235 tracked paths, overwhelmingly under .agents/skills/**; there is no structures/, no data/, no notebook, no requirements.txt, environment.yml, package.json or Dockerfile, and no CI configuration. No mmCIF, PDB or confidences JSON exists anywhere in the tree, so 'designed via AlphaFold3' has zero corresponding artifact. My accession sweep (UniProt pattern, ChEMBL, Ensembl, PDB-in-context) across README.md, app.js and index.html returned zero, so residue-numbering claims such as app.js:144 ('TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333)') and app.js:164 ('Keap1 Kelch Domain (Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483, Ser602)') are genuinely uncheckable against any numbering convention -- in my judgement the most insidious item in the whole review, and correctly identified. Dependency pinning verified: index.html:18 loads 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js' with no version, while index.html:15 pins three.js r128, :16 pins OrbitControls to 0.128.0 and :13 pins Font Awesome 6.4.0 -- the reviewer's split assessment is accurate. The unused-tooling point is verified and is the strongest rhetorical element: .agents/skills/ does contain pdb-database, uniprot-database, chembl-database (with chembl_api.py) and alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze containing scripts/analyze_plddt.py and scripts/analyze_pae.py -- literally the two quantities app.js:791 and :850 fabricate.
verdicts.corrections: The grep sentence is imprecise. 'Word-boundary grep for seed, provenance, version, PDB, UniProt, DOI across the four files returns zero relevant hits' -- 'seed' returns 1 (README:77, 'Toxic Abeta-AChE seed blockade', biological seeding) and 'PDB' returns 1 (index.html:359, 'live 3D prediction and PDB/CIF download'). The hedge 'relevant' saves the claim since neither is a provenance record, but the raw counts are not zero and the sentence should say so rather than lean on the hedge. Also add to the missing-artifact inventory: the repository carries a 'License: Private Research' badge at README:4 but no LICENSE file, and no CITATION.cff.

verdicts.reasoning: Fully verified with no material error. index.html:42 is an anchor to https://alphafoldserver.com/ whose visible text is 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected'; it carries no state, performs no probe, and would read identically offline. README:24 says 'direct live integration with the official AlphaFold Server'; README:111 says 'Live AlphaFold Server Connection'; index.html:358 says 'AlphaFold Server Live 3D Pipeline'; index.html:363 is a second plain anchor to the same homepage; app.js:660-671 is navigator.clipboard.writeText and nothing else. I independently grepped app.js, index.html, README.md and styles.css for fetch, XMLHttpRequest, axios, WebSocket, EventSource and sendBeacon: all six return exactly 0. No network request of any kind is issued, so nothing displayed can originate from AlphaFold Server. The clipboard trap is real: copyModalFasta performs no validation, so ids 4 and 23 (containing B) and id 24 (the English string) go to the clipboard for submission to a service that rejects both. Branding verified: README:3 is a shields.io badge with logo=google reading 'AlphaFold3 - DeepMind_Server', and index.html:30 reads 'DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform'.
verdicts.corrections: The inventory of false-provenance strings is incomplete. index.html:410 (footer) reads 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling & Structural Pharmacology Algorithms', and index.html:6-7 (title tag and meta description) assert 'AlphaFold3 de novo engineered candidates' -- three further locations absent from the reviewer's list, all of which must be corrected alongside index.html:42 and README:24/111 or the relabelling will be partial. Separately, I would lift the DeepMind-branding sub-point out of why_it_matters into its own bullet in the required fix: the working directory is named DeepMind_Bio, the header claims DeepMind, and the README badge carries Google's logo. That is a third-party trademark and implied-affiliation problem distinct from a mislabelled UI control, and it is the one item in this review with external legal consequence if the repository is ever made public. The finding's MAJOR severity is still right.

missed_by_reviewer: AlphaFold3 emits no binding free energy and no Kd, in any configuration -- never stated, and it is the cleanest single disproof available. AF3 returns coordinates plus pLDDT, PAE, pTM and ipTM (Abramson et al., Nature 2024, 630(8016):493-500, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w; I confirmed volume, issue and pages via PubMed PMID 38718835). Two of the three quantities on every one of the 25 affinity lines (app.js:146 et seq., 'dG = ... | Kd = ... | AF3 pLDDT = ...') therefore cannot be AF3 outputs regardless of whether a complex was predicted. AIML-04 reaches the right conclusion by the longer monomer-vs-interface route and leaves the shorter one unused.

'Designed via AlphaFold3' names a predictor as a designer, and no generative procedure is described anywhere. AF3 does not produce sequences. Neither the review nor any of its seven fixes asks what method generated the 25 strings. The answer is visible in the data: the sequences are recombinations of a small reused motif pool -- id 8 (app.js:215) is GCPWECDRRACPCYRGFWR + ERACPDCH + SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCAC, and all three fragments appear separately in ids 6, 16 and 21. That is string concatenation, not design, and it is directly checkable. Any remediation plan must demand a stated design method before it demands evaluation of that method's output.

The AF3_CANDIDATES table shares byte-identical sequences with FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA and assigns them a third divergent metric set -- seven collisions, missed entirely. KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG carries pLDDT 94.8 / 94.3 / 92.8 and dG -16.2 / -17.5 / -12.6 across app.js:153, :247 and :131; ranks 3, 8, 9 and 10 (app.js:127, 132, 133, 134) duplicate ids 3, 8, 9, 6 and 18 with different numbers each time. The real spread on one identical input is 2.5 pLDDT units and 4.9 kcal/mol, not the 0.4-1.7 and 0.8-1.4 reported. Consequently AIML-03's proposed CI assertion, scoped to FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA alone, would pass a table that still ships a B-containing FASTA (app.js:130) rendered to users at index.html:291.

'TOP 10' has no denominator -- the most elementary evaluation-design defect in the artifact, and neither AIML-01 nor AIML-04 names it. index.html:265 and README:130 present an 'AlphaFold3 De Novo Engineered Candidates TOP 10' and a leaderboard, but the ten AF3_CANDIDATES codes are disjoint from the 25 drug codes, so no candidate population is ever stated from which a top ten was selected. A selection claim without a population is unevaluable in principle: no denominator, no selection rule, no report of what was discarded. Fixing the sort key does not touch this.

No task definition and no falsification criterion. The review correctly enumerates what is procedurally missing (split, baseline, dispersion) but never observes that the artifact states no task, no success criterion, and no decision the numbers are meant to support. Without that, AIML-01 fixes (3) and (4) have nothing to be evaluated against -- one cannot construct a held-out set for an unspecified prediction problem. Remediation order should be: state the task and the decision, then the metric, then the split, then the controls.

The reviewer's engineering praise is wrong on its main example, which weakens the report where it can least afford it. 'The Three.js scene lifecycle ... competently written' is incorrect: initModal3DCanvas allocates a new THREE.WebGLRenderer at app.js:688 on every modal open; `dispose` appears nowhere in app.js (grep returns zero); closeDrugModal (app.js:655-658) only toggles a CSS class; and the guard at app.js:764 tests the module-level modalThreeRenderer, which is reassigned but never nulled, so every previously started requestAnimationFrame loop keeps running and each applies rotation.y += 0.006 at app.js:767 to the current global mesh group. Opening N drug modals leaks N WebGL contexts (browsers cap at roughly 16, after which the panel blanks) and spins the model N times faster. Only the Chart.js teardown at app.js:779-781 deserves the praise given.

Two further defects inside the PAE panel, both checkable in seconds. app.js:844 caps the grid at min(length, 45), but id 1's sequence is 47 aa, so its heatmap silently omits two residues while captioned as that candidate's matrix. And because `error` at app.js:850 depends on i but not j, the matrix is not symmetric: 1,484 of 2,025 cells in id 1's map disagree with their transpose. It is not merely a wrong PAE map; it is not a well-formed PAE object.

A distributional argument that covers the 21 non-duplicated rows, which the exact-duplicate proof cannot reach. All 25 Kd values fall in 0.08-4.8 nM, all 25 dG in -15.2 to -19.5 kcal/mol, and the dG-vs-Kd residual varies by only 1.88 kcal/mol (SD 0.546) across the whole set. Twenty-five independent predictions landing inside a 4.3 kcal/mol window with no outlier, no failure and no null is itself quantitative evidence of authorship rather than computation. AIML-05 gestures at 'uniform positivity' qualitatively; stated as a distributional test it applies to every row, including those with no duplicate to contradict them.

README:98, 'All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening,' is a false claim that a procedure was executed -- categorically different from an unsupported estimate, and the sentence a reader would cite as evidence that screening happened. It appears in no evidence_location and 'Rewrite Section 3 of the README' does not name it.

On citations, for the record rather than as a criticism: I resolved all eleven independently and every one is real with the stated title, venue, volume and pages. Abramson 2024 Nature 630(8016):493-500 and Pacesa 2025 Nature 646(8084):483-492 confirmed via PubMed (PMID 38718835, 40866699); Buttenschoen/Morris/Deane Chem Sci 2024 15(9):3130-3139, Simpkin Proteins 2023 91:1616-1635 and Robin Proteins 2021 89:1977-1986 via Crossref; the two 2025 openRxiv preprints (10.1101/2025.08.14.670059, 10.1101/2025.08.15.670450) and the ADMET audit under the unfamiliar 10.64898 prefix (which is openRxiv's, not a fabrication) all resolve with exact titles; arXiv 2507.21404, 2102.09548 and 1706.04599 confirmed. I also checked the two specific LIT-PCBA figures the reviewer quotes and both are verbatim from the abstract: 323 active train-validation analogue pairs at ECFP4 Tanimoto >= 0.6 in ALDH1, and 2,491 2D-identical inactives spanning partitions. The citation record is clean and the review may be issued on that basis.

verifications.discipline: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
verifications.verifier_persona: Full professor of molecular neuropharmacology, 24 years post-PhD; laboratory works on cholinergic basal forebrain circuitry, AChE structure-function and PAS pharmacology, neurotrophin receptor signalling, and microglial state biology. Long-standing senior/handling editor for a neuropharmacology journal and standing member of a structural-pharmacology study section; routinely adjudicate residue-level and thermodynamic claims against primary sequence and structure databases.

verdicts.reasoning: I refetched all 17 relevant UniProt sequences and ran exact plus longest-common-substring searches myself. Every enumerated instance holds: CVDRENPVEWVRAC vs BDNF P23560 — absent, longest common substring 3 ('EWV'); EPKHVNCDRENP vs NGF P01138 — absent, LCS 2; GRLVGHPWECDR vs TREM2 Q9NZC2 — absent, LCS 2; SEAEFRLFRDVW vs CHRNA7 P36544 — absent, LCS 3; CKCHGMSGSCSTK vs WNT3A P56704 — absent, LCS 5 ('CKCHG'); DEETGEFLFQLP vs NFE2L2 Q16236 — absent, LCS 8 ('DEETGEFL'), against the genuine DEETGEFLPIQP which I confirmed at Q16236 residues 77-88; VRACPTGKCEGL vs NTRK2 Q16620 — absent, LCS 4. The 'Loop-5' point is also right: neurotrophins have four beta-hairpin loops. The TrkB domain architecture claim is right too — Q16620 UniProt features list LRRNT, LRR, LRRCT, Ig-like C2-type 1 (197-282), Ig-like C2-type 2 (295-365) and kinase (538-807); no EGF-like repeat anywhere. WHERE THE FINDING OVERREACHES: the title asserts 'every claimed natural-sequence provenance is false.' That universal is refuted by two counterexamples in the same dataset. (a) app.js:225 'GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG' is an EXACT substring of GSK3B P49841 at residues 3-34, and it genuinely contains Ser9 — so the README:70 'GSK-3beta Ser9 Mimetic' provenance is real, not invented. (b) KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM is an exact substring of APP P05067 (Abeta16-35) — which the reviewer credits in the overall assessment but the finding title contradicts. The enumerated evidence is entirely sound; only the universal quantifier in the title is wrong.
verdicts.corrections: Retitle to the scope actually demonstrated: 'Nine of the claimed natural-sequence provenances cannot be reproduced against the cited UniProt accession.' Two provenances ARE genuine and must be excluded from any deletion sweep: GSK3B P49841 residues 3-34 (app.js:225) and APP P05067 Abeta16-35 (app.js:277, README:77). Also fix the off-by-one in the worked example inside required_fix: 'Nrf2 76-88, Q16236' is 13 residues, LDEETGEFLPIQP, not the 12-mer LDEETGEFLPIQ given (that is 76-87). Finally, the assertion that the recurring Cys ladder is 'EGF-like-repeat architecture' is a structural inference I could not confirm by any database hit; it is not load-bearing (the absence from TrkB is independently proven) and should be softened or dropped.

verdicts.reasoning: I extracted all 25 sequence fields programmatically and grouped them. Exactly four sequences appear twice, at exactly the cited lines and exactly the cited lengths: the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG at app.js:153 and 247; the 31-mer CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH at 173 and 371; the 41-mer SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC at 195 and 319; the 37-mer VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH at 205 and 361. The paired affinities and target strings are as quoted. The finding is correct and, if anything, understated on two axes I checked and the reviewer did not. FIRST, the thermodynamic inconsistency is not confined to the AChE pair — it is universal. Recomputing dG = RT ln(Kd) at 298.15 K (RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol) for all 25 entries, every stated dG is more negative than its stated Kd permits, by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol, with no exception. SECOND, the same molecules also appear in AF3_CANDIDATES carrying a THIRD, different dG and a different pLDDT: the 36-mer is dG -12.6 / pLDDT 92.8 at app.js:131, -16.2 / 94.8 at app.js:156, and -17.5 / 94.3 at app.js:250; the 41-mer is -12.1 / 90.7 at app.js:134, -16.5 / 93.2 at app.js:198, -15.7 / 92.8 at app.js:322; the 45-mer at app.js:132 is assigned 'NMDA GluN2B NTD' while the identical sequence at app.js:215 is assigned GluN2A. Three values for one molecule is stronger evidence than two.
verdicts.corrections: Arithmetic nit: Kd = 0.65 nM gives dG = -12.53 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, not -12.4 as stated (Kd = 2.1 nM -> -11.84 is correct). Scope correction: report the inconsistency as systematic across all 25 entries (discrepancy 3.85-5.73 kcal/mol, n = 25, zero exceptions) rather than as a property of one duplicate pair, and add the AF3_CANDIDATES cross-list triples above. Also note that the ZO-1 pairing is even worse than stated: ZO-1 is not in the platform at all as a sequence-verified target — the peptide assigned to 'ZO-1/Occludin (Arg220, Asp310)' at app.js:372 is the same corrupted WNT3A fragment.

verdicts.reasoning: I tested every residue myself against both accessions in mature numbering. Human AChE P22303 (signal 1-31, offset +31): position 84 = Glu, 330 = Val, 121 = Gly, 279 = Gln — none is the claimed residue. Torpedo AChE P04058 (signal 1-21, offset +21): 84 = Trp, 330 = Phe, 121 = Tyr, 279 = Trp — all four match exactly. So the CAS list is unambiguously Torpedo numbering. The PAS list is unambiguously human: P22303 mature 286 = Trp, 72 = Tyr, 341 = Tyr, 74 = Asp, all correct. The two are welded into one string at app.js:154, exactly as claimed, and app.js:12 lists Torpedo Trp279 while app.js:72 and app.js:154 list human Trp286 — the same PAS tryptophan presented as two sites. The proposed human equivalents also check out: P22303 mature 86 = Trp, 337 = Tyr, 124 = Tyr, 295 = Phe, 297 = Phe, triad 203 = Ser / 334 = Glu / 447 = His; Torpedo mature 70 = Tyr, 72 = Asp, 334 = Tyr. The Torpedo Phe330 -> human Tyr337 caveat is correct and is the trap a naive renumbering would fall into. I confirmed the salt-bridge/cation-pi contradiction by reading app.js:12 and app.js:15 directly: line 12 says 'CAS Salt Bridge', line 15 says 'cation-pi interactions' for the same Trp84/Phe330 contact. Aromatic side chains cannot form salt bridges. Sussman et al., Science 1991;253:872-9 (PMID 1678899) verified via PubMed esummary; PDB 1VOT verified via RCSB as AChE/huperzine A, Raves M.L., Nat Struct Biol 1997.
verdicts.corrections: None. Every residue identity, the species assignment, the equivalence mapping, and both citations verified independently.

verdicts.reasoning: Text verified verbatim at app.js:153-158 and 247-252, including 'Completely blocks acetylcholine degradation ... elevating synaptic ACh levels by +350%' and 'Seizure Index: 0.01 | Peripheral Side Effects: None', plus README:100 'Negligible'. The peptide characterisation is exact: I counted the 36-mer and get 9 Lys, 4 Arg, 4 Glu, 0 Asp — net formal charge +9 — and 4 Trp, precisely as claimed. The steric argument is sound: the AChE gorge is ~20 A deep and narrow, and fasciculin-2 is the definitive precedent that a peptide-class ligand caps the PAS and occludes the gorge mouth without reaching the catalytic serine. The pharmacological inversion is the strongest part of the finding and is correct: near-complete AChE inhibition is the mechanism of organophosphate/carbamate cholinergic crisis, and the platform asserts maximal target engagement with zero on-target toxicity, which is self-contradictory for this enzyme. The donepezil anchor is verified verbatim — I pulled the Rogers & Friedhoff abstract (PMID 8915035), which states 'A plateau of inhibition (76-84%) was reached at plasma donepezil concentrations > 50 ng/ml.' Inestrosa et al., Neuron 1996;16:881-91 (PMID 8608006) verified. CITATION ERROR: PDB 1FSS is 'ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE COMPLEXED WITH FASCICULIN-II', primary citation Harel M. et al., Structure 1995 — not Bourne. Bourne et al. 1995 is the mouse AChE-fasciculin structure (Cell), PDB 1MAH. The reviewer's own literature-list entry for 1FSS wisely gives no author; the inline attribution in MOLBIO-04 must be corrected or the finding carries a misattributed structure.
verdicts.corrections: Attribute PDB 1FSS to Harel et al., Structure 1995 (verified via RCSB), not to Bourne et al. If Bourne is wanted, cite it as the separate mouse AChE-Fas2 complex (PDB 1MAH). Also temper the harm framing: 'the clearest path to physical harm' overstates the exposure of a private static web page with no dosing calculator; the defensible statement is that the design objective itself is inverted and would misdirect candidate selection. Minor scope note: B4 (app.js:275-282) is not really an AChE ligand at all — its peptide is Abeta16-35 fused to GRLVGHPW — so 'reclassify B4 as PAS-directed' is generous; it should be flagged as having no AChE-binding element.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified residue by residue against NTRK2 Q16620. Full-length numbering: 298 = Asp (correct), 342 = Tyr (correct), 319 = Tyr not Glu, 315 = Leu not Thr, 312 = Lys not Val, 333 = Lys not Leu. Two of six. I independently tested mature numbering (+31 offset): 298 = Tyr, 319 = Asn, 342 = Gln, 312 = His, 333 = Lys, 315 = Leu — zero of six, so the reviewer is right that this is not a convention artefact. The domain credit is also right: UniProt annotates Ig-like C2-type 2 at 295-365, so 298-342 fall inside d5. The absence of a BDNF-TrkB complex is confirmed by a structured RCSB accession search I ran myself: P23560 (BDNF) appears in exactly two PDB entries, 1B8M and 1BND (both BDNF/NT-3 heterodimers, no receptor), and none of the nine Q16620 entries (1HCF, 1WWB, 2MFQ, 4ASZ, 4AT3, 4AT4, 4AT5, 5MO9, 8OYD) contains BDNF — 8OYD, which a text search surfaces, is the TrkB transmembrane-domain NMR structure. Citations verified: PDB 1WWB (apo human TrkB LBD, Ultsch, J Mol Biol 1999), 1HCF (TrkB-d5 with NT-4/5, Banfield, Structure 2001), 5MO9 (TrkB LBD with Fab); Boltaev et al., Sci Signal 2017;10 (PMID 28831019) abstract retrieved and matches the reviewer's characterisation; Zagrebelsky & Korte, Neural Regen Res 2024;19:29-34 (PMID 37488840) verified.
verdicts.corrections: The rhetorical statistic is wrong and should be deleted: 'Two of six correct is what random guessing constrained to the right domain would give' is false. Random guessing over 20 amino acids gives an expectation of ~0.3 correct out of six, so 2/6 is roughly six-fold ABOVE chance, not at chance. The honest statement is that four of six residue identities are wrong under both numbering conventions, and the two that are right (Asp298, Tyr342) cannot be assumed to be by design. Everything else stands.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified against CHRNA7 P36544 in mature numbering (signal 1-22): 188 = Tyr, 149 = Trp, 195 = Tyr — all correct as claimed, and I additionally confirmed 93 = Tyr and 55 = Trp, which is decisive because Tyr93/Trp149/Tyr188/Tyr195 plus complementary-face Trp55 IS the canonical orthosteric aromatic box. So the residues the platform lists for a supposed PAM are the acetylcholine site. CHRM1 P11229: 381 = Tyr, 164 = Trp confirmed, and the orthosteric tyrosine lid partners are all present as claimed (105 = Asp, 106 = Tyr, 404 = Tyr, 408 = Tyr). The desensitisation inversion is the sharpest point and is correct: app.js:199 asserts 'Receptor Desensitization: Low' as a consequence of a PAM label while the listed site is orthosteric, and orthosteric alpha-7 agonism is characterised by rapid profound desensitisation. I retrieved the Marotta et al. abstract (PMID 26211363), which states that the increased potency of ACh with PNU-120596 'is not due to an altered agonist binding site' and implicates gating-interface and transmembrane residues — exactly as the reviewer represents it. Targowska-Duda et al. verified (J Biomol Struct Dyn 37:411-439, PMID 29363414). PDB 4MQT (active M2 with LY2119620, Kruse, Nature 2013) and 5CXV (M1 with tiotropium, Thal, Nature 2016) verified.
verdicts.corrections: Two trivial precision points, neither of which weakens the finding. (i) Targowska-Duda et al. is print-dated 2019 in J Biomol Struct Dyn 37:411-439 (online 2018); cite as 2019 or '2018 online, 2019 print'. (ii) The reviewer calls M1 Trp164 merely 'a real residue' — accurate, but it is a TM4 (4.57) residue that belongs to neither the orthosteric lid nor the canonical extracellular allosteric vestibule, so it is unassigned rather than mislabelled. The Tyr381 argument carries the finding on its own.

verdicts.reasoning: Every quoted number verified at the cited line: app.js:148 'LTP +280%', app.js:188 '+310%', app.js:200 '+240%', app.js:240 'doubling cortical information processing speed', app.js:252 '+350%', app.js:334 '+420%'. None carries an assay, referent, species, n, or dispersion — that part is simply true on inspection. The conceptual core is the strongest element and is correct: potentiation saturates and saturated hippocampal LTP impairs rather than improves learning, so 'more LTP' is not a coherent objective. Moser, Krobert, Moser & Morris, Science 1998;281:2038-42 (PMID 9748165), 'Impaired spatial learning after saturation of long-term potentiation', verified by PubMed esummary — title, venue, year, volume and pages all exact. The ambiguity point about '+280%' meaning 180% vs 380% of baseline is a real and standard reviewer objection. However this finding is qualitatively different from MOLBIO-01/02/03/06: it is an 'unsupported-claim' category defect (the reviewer's own label) sitting downstream of a dataset already proven fabricated, and it does not introduce an independent, actionable technical error the way a wrong residue or a wrong species numbering does.
verdicts.corrections: One overstatement to soften: 'beyond the geometric packing limit of the dendritic shaft' is not defensible at the low end. Reported CA1 spine densities span roughly 1-3 per micrometre, and densities of 4-5 per micrometre are observed on some dendritic segments and in synaptopathies, so a 4.1-fold increase is far outside the physiological range and into pathology, but it is not geometrically impossible. Restate as 'far outside any reported physiological range, and in the range associated with spine overproduction in fragile X and related synaptopathies.' The microdialysis framing ('roughly 100-500% of basal') is a fair general characterisation but is offered without a specific citation and should either be cited or given as an order-of-magnitude statement.

verdicts.reasoning: All locations verified by direct reading: app.js:109-114 defines the microglia region as 'Microglia (M1/M2 State Polarization)' with action text 'shifting inflammatory M1 microglia to neuroprotective M2 phagocytic states'; app.js:304 repeats it; index.html:186 renders 'Microglia (M1/M2 State)'; README:80-85 as quoted. The naming collision is real and worse than a presentational nuisance: 'MicroTrem2-Agonist-M1' at app.js:297 is a drug named M1 whose stated purpose at app.js:304 is to abolish M1 microglia, while 'BasalM1-PAM-B2' at app.js:255 uses M1 for the muscarinic receptor — three incompatible referents in one dataset, exactly as claimed. Both citations verified by PubMed esummary with exact metadata: Ransohoff RM, 'A polarizing question: do M1 and M2 microglia exist?', Nat Neurosci 2016;19:987-91 (PMID 27459405); Paolicelli RC et al., 'Microglia states and nomenclature: A field at its crossroads', Neuron 2022;110:3458-3483 (PMID 36327895). The scientific substance — that M1/M2 was imported from in vitro macrophage paradigms, that single-cell work resolves a continuum of context-dependent states, and that TREM2-dependent DAM are simultaneously highly activated and beneficial — is standard current consensus and correctly stated.
verdicts.corrections: 'Formally deprecated by the field' is a shade strong as a matter of process — no body formally deprecates nomenclature. The accurate formulation is that a ~90-author field consensus paper (Paolicelli et al. 2022) recommends against the dualistic classification and issues explicit nomenclature guidance, following Ransohoff's 2016 argument that the schema should be discarded. Substance unaffected.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified against TREM2 Q9NZC2: position 47 = Arg (correct), 87 = Asp (correct), 112 = Ser NOT Lys — the reviewer is right, and UniProt annotates Ig-like V-type at 29-112, so 112 is indeed the domain boundary. Provenance confirmed: GRLVGHPWECDR is absent from Q9NZC2 with longest common substring 2. The mechanistic argument is sound and standard: TREM2 signals via the ITAM adaptor DAP12 and requires clustering for Src-family trans-phosphorylation and SYK recruitment, so a monovalent 12-mer engaging one Ig domain cannot be an agonist by construction. The clinical citation is the reviewer's most surprising claim and I retrieved the full abstract to check it: Mummery CJ et al., 'The TREM2 agonistic antibody AL002 in early Alzheimer's disease: a phase 2 randomized trial', Nat Med 2026;32:1708-1716 (PMID 41787076) — 381 participants, 1:1:1:1 randomisation, 48-96 weeks, reduced CSF sTREM2 and increased osteopontin, primary CDR-SB endpoint not met at week 96 (all three doses, P > 0.05), and 'the most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events were magnetic resonance imaging changes resembling amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA)', NCT04592874. Every detail the reviewer asserts is verbatim correct. Kober DL et al., eLife 2016;5 (PMID 27995897) verified, and its abstract does state that AD risk variants sit on the surface and impair ligand binding; PDB 5ELI, 5UD7 and 6B8O verified via RCSB (5UD7/6B8O are Sudom et al., J Biol Chem 2018, 6B8O being the WT Ig-like V domain with phosphatidylserine). WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG: the Asp87 sub-claim. The reviewer writes that 'Asp87 is acidic, which is hard to reconcile with a ligand surface whose defining property is a basic patch.' D87N is a recognised TREM2 coding variant that maps to precisely the AD-risk functional surface Kober et al. define — a EuropePMC query for TREM2 AND "D87N" returns 91 records — and UniProt annotates ligand-binding residues at 67, 68, 77 and 88, placing Asp87 immediately adjacent to an annotated contact. Asp87 is therefore one of the few residues in the entire platform that is both the right amino acid and on the right surface.
verdicts.corrections: Delete the Asp87 objection and the corresponding clause in required_fix ('justify Asp87 against the published anionic-ligand-binding surface'). Asp87 is correct: it is a genuine surface residue on the Kober functional epitope and the site of the AD-associated D87N variant. As written, the fix would push authors to remove or 'justify' one of the platform's few accurate residue assignments. Keep the Lys112 -> Ser112 correction, the monovalency/DAP12 argument, the provenance failure, and the AL002 addition — all of those verified cleanly.

verdicts.reasoning: The credit is fully earned and I re-verified it: KEAP1 Q14145 position 334 = Tyr, 415 = Arg, 483 = Arg, 602 = Ser, and the extended hot-spot set the reviewer names is also exactly right — 380 = Arg, 382 = Asn, 414 = Asn, 508 = Ser, 555 = Ser, 572 = Tyr. Position 151 = Cys confirmed. The Nrf2 motif comparison is exact: Q16236 residues 77-88 are DEETGEFLPIQP against the platform's DEETGEFLFQLP, sharing DEETGEFL and diverging thereafter. The domain-conflation charge is verified by direct reading of index.html:230, which collapses 'Keap1 Cys151 Alkylation / Decoy Binding Nrf2 Dissociation' into one pathway step, welding a BTB-domain covalent event to a Kelch-domain PPI competition. The hinge-and-latch objection is correct and is the strongest design-level point: a monovalent ETGE-only decoy competes at the high-affinity hinge and does not address the DLG latch whose disengagement blocks ubiquitin transfer. All four citations verified by PubMed esummary and RCSB with exact metadata: PDB 2FLU (Kelch-Neh2 complex, Lo S.C., EMBO J 2006); Tong KI et al., Biol Chem 2006;387:1311-20 (PMID 17081101); Shibata T et al., PNAS 2008;105:13568-73 (PMID 18757741); Takaya K et al., Free Radic Biol Med 2012;53:817-27 (PMID 22732183). The Nrf2-activation oncogenicity caveat is a legitimate and commonly-missed requirement for a chronic CNS indication.
verdicts.corrections: None material. One small addition worth making when implementing: the platform's own inconsistency is sharper than stated — app.js:82 assigns Asiatic Acid to 'Keap1 Tyr334, Arg415' (Kelch) while app.js:52 assigns Curcumin to 'Keap1 Cys151' (BTB), and app.js:161-168 fuses a curcumin warhead to a Kelch-binding decoy, so the same conjugate is simultaneously assigned both mechanisms without a linker argument.

verdicts.reasoning: I validated every character of all 25 sequences plus the 10 AF3_CANDIDATES fasta fields against the 20-letter standard alphabet. Exactly three entries fail, as claimed: the letter B in CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH at app.js:173 and app.js:371, the same B inside the rank-6 fasta at app.js:130, and app.js:381 whose sequence field is the literal string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. I confirmed by reading initModal3DCanvas (app.js:707-773), renderModalPlddtChart (775-832) and renderModalPaeHeatmap (834-866) that none validates input — all three index charCodeAt directly — so A4 will render a 3D backbone, a pLDDT curve and a PAE matrix from a description string. THE PROPOSED FIX IS WRONG. Aligning the platform 31-mer to WNT3A P56704 from residue 203 (CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP, which I confirmed begins at 203): platform positions 1-18 map to WNT3A 203-220, so the B at platform position 19 aligns to WNT3A Gln221, not Leu. The Leu is at WNT3A 208, which the platform renders as Met at position 6 — the L->M substitution the reviewer themselves correctly identified in MOLBIO-01. Implementing 'correct the B to L, per WNT3A P56704' would write a Leu where the genuine residue is Gln, i.e. replace an invalid character with a wrong one, and it contradicts MOLBIO-01 within the same report.
verdicts.corrections: The B corresponds to WNT3A P56704 Gln221, not Leu. Correct fix: either B -> Q (restoring alignment to WNT3A 203-222) or, preferably, replace the whole peptide with the genuine WNT3A 203-222 segment CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP. Note the platform also has G at position 18 for WNT3A Ser220 and L at position 20 for Pro222, so three substitutions plus the illegal B, not the two the report implies. Second correction: 'it breaks the platform's one genuinely functional external integration' is not accurate — index.html:363 is a plain anchor to alphafoldserver.com that submits nothing, and copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) only writes to the clipboard. Nothing programmatic breaks; the failure is that a user's manual paste would be rejected. The character validator and the render-gate in the rest of the fix are correct and sufficient.

missed_by_reviewer: INCOMPLETE RESIDUE AUDIT DESPITE A CLAIM OF COMPLETENESS. The overall assessment states 'I verified every residue-level claim against the actual UniProt sequences' and explicitly lists FZD8 Q9H461 and SLC1A2 P43004 — yet reports no error in either, and no finding covers five further mismatched target sites that I found. EAAT2/SLC1A2 (app.js:362) 'Thr368, Lys490' -> P43004 368 = Leu, 490 = Ala (both wrong). FZD8 (app.js:174) 'Phe72, Tyr125, Asp99, Arg104' -> Q9H461 104 = Leu (F72/Y125/D99 correct). GluN2A (app.js:216 and 236) 'Glu201, Lys210' -> GRIN2A Q12879 201 = Gln, 210 = Phe (both wrong). TrkA (app.js:268) 'His312, Leu331' -> NTRK1 P04629 312 = Ser, 331 = Glu (both wrong). PAFR (app.js:32, app.js:382, README:34) 'His14, Tyr200' -> P25105 14 = Arg, 200 = Leu (both wrong; Phe174 is correct). For symmetry, uncredited correct sets I verified: TLR4 O00206 Arg264/Lys341/Glu439 all correct; LC3B Q9GZQ8 Phe52/Leu63 correct; ER-beta Q92731 Glu305/Arg346 correct; hERG Q12809 Tyr652/Phe656 correct (README:99). A reviewer asserting exhaustiveness must either be exhaustive or scope the claim.

THE ONE GENUINELY SOURCED PEPTIDE IS MISSED, AND SO IS ITS MECHANISTIC ERROR. app.js:225 'GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG' is an exact match to GSK3B P49841 residues 3-34 and genuinely contains Ser9 — the single most defensible sequence in the dataset, and a real concept (the GSK-3beta N-terminal pseudosubstrate). But the platform then attaches it to the wrong pocket: app.js:226 says 'GSK-3beta ATP Binding Pocket (Val135, Asp133, Lys85)'. The pseudosubstrate does not bind the ATP pocket; it occupies the phosphate-binding pocket formed by Arg96, Arg180 and Lys205 (all three confirmed as those residues in P49841), and it only does so when Ser9 is PHOSPHORYLATED. An unphosphorylated Ser9 peptide is not an inhibitor and cannot bind where the platform says it binds. This is a clean, checkable mechanism-of-action error in the reviewer's own discipline, entirely unaddressed.

NO FINDING PINS THE ROOT FALSE CLAIM: THAT ALPHAFOLD3 WAS EVER RUN. index.html:42 renders a header badge reading 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected'; README:24 claims 'direct live integration with the official AlphaFold Server'; README:111 claims 'Live AlphaFold Server Connection'; README:108 claims 'Real sequence-driven backbone topology parsing'. In fact index.html:363 is a static anchor that transmits nothing, copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) only writes to the clipboard, and every pLDDT, dG and CEI is a hardcoded literal in AF3_CANDIDATES (app.js:124-135) and FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA. The claim 'designed via AlphaFold3' (README:22, README:45) therefore describes a computation that was never performed anywhere in the codebase. This is the provenance claim from which every other finding descends, and it deserves its own BLOCKER rather than being distributed across MOLBIO-02 and MOLBIO-11.

THE SYNTHETIC pLDDT CURVE CONTRADICTS THE pLDDT NUMBERS PRINTED BESIDE IT. app.js:791 computes score = 93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode % 5)*0.5, whose range is 89.0 to 99.0 for every sequence. Consequently the clamps at app.js:792-793 ('if (score > 100) score = 98.6; if (score < 70) score = 76') are unreachable dead code — direct internal evidence that the curve was never derived from a prediction and that the clamps were copied from a template. It also means the rendered profile cannot reproduce the per-drug pLDDT strings it sits next to (e.g. 97.0 for X3 at app.js:166 versus a curve that averages ~94). The reviewer notes the formula is synthetic but never observes that it is arithmetically inconsistent with the platform's own headline confidence values.

B4 IS BUILT FROM THE AMYLOID NUCLEATION MOTIF AND SOLD AS A FIBRIL DISRUPTOR. app.js:275-282 names B4 'AChE-Abeta Fibril Disruptor' with safety 'Fibril Blockade: 100%', and its peptide is Abeta16-35 (KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM, verified as an exact APP P05067 substring) fused to GRLVGHPW. KLVFFAE is the self-recognition element that nucleates aggregation; unmodified Abeta16-35 is a seed, not a breaker. Genuine beta-sheet breakers require backbone N-methylation or proline substitution to abolish hydrogen-bonding on one face. The reviewer credits the sequence as 'the correct self-recognition element' and stops there, missing that using it unmodified inverts the stated pharmacology — the same class of error as MOLBIO-04, in a candidate MOLBIO-04 proposes to keep.

NO ASSESSMENT OF WHETHER ANY OF THESE MOLECULES COULD REACH THE BRAIN, OR OF CATIONIC-PEPTIDE LIABILITY. Every one of the 25 candidates is a 28-47 residue peptide conjugate, and the ADMET section (README:96-102) addresses hERG, seizure index, cytokine storm and receptor downregulation while omitting the properties that actually disqualify this modality: blood-brain-barrier penetration, plasma and CSF proteolytic stability, and renal clearance. More specifically, the recurring 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (net +9, 4 Trp, amphipathic) is architecturally a cationic amphipathic cell-penetrating/antimicrobial peptide — a class that is membrane-lytic and haemolytic in the low-micromolar range. Asserting 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Risk)' for such a sequence while saying nothing about membrane lysis inverts the actual safety hierarchy for this chemotype. This is a first-order neuropharmacology omission the reviewer does not raise anywhere.

THE 'TOLERANCE' AND 'BIASED AGONISM' CLAIM IS INCOHERENT FOR MOST OF THE PIPELINE'S TARGETS. README:102 states 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' because 'Biased agonist signaling redirects receptors to recycling endosomes.' Biased agonism is defined only for GPCRs (and by extension some RTK/cytokine systems). The pipeline's targets are dominated by a hydrolase (AChE), a ligand-gated ion channel (alpha-7), an ionotropic glutamate receptor (GluN2A), a secondary-active transporter (EAAT2/SLC1A2) and a Cul3 substrate adaptor (Keap1), none of which internalises or desensitises by the mechanism invoked.
