The reviewer flags desensitisation only for P1 in MOLBIO-06 and does not challenge the platform-wide mechanistic claim behind the number.

HUPERZINE A'S NMDA-CHANNEL TARGET ASSIGNMENT IS ASSERTED WITHOUT ANY RESIDUE OR EVIDENCE. app.js:11 lists the target as 'AChE Catalytic Anionic Site (CAS) & NMDA Channel' and README:32 propagates it, but no NMDA subunit, no accession and no residue is given anywhere, and the mechanism string at app.js:14 never returns to it. Huperzine A's reported NMDA activity is weak, non-competitive and contested; presenting it in a target line beside a residue-level AChE claim implies an equivalence of evidence that does not exist. MOLBIO-03 corrects the AChE half of that same string and leaves the NMDA half untouched.

verifications.discipline: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
verifications.verifier_persona: Full professor of pharmaceutics and distinguished industry DMPK scientist, 22 years post-PhD in CNS drug delivery and peptide/biologic developability; ran brain-penetration and Kp,uu,brain platforms for two large-pharma neuroscience portfolios, took two BBB-shuttle biologics and one intrathecal peptide through IND-enabling tox, and served on journal editorial boards where fabricated citations and unreproducible in-silico calibrations are a standing concern.

verdicts.reasoning: I re-ran the reviewer's vocabulary grep myself across all four files. Every string they list returns zero: dose, dosing, dosage, route, administ*, intravenous, subcutaneous, intrathecal, intranasal, infusion, bolus, half-life, bioavailab*, exposure, plasma, serum, CSF, cerebrospinal, microdialysis, efflux, P-gp, MDR1, MDCK, BCRP, transcytosis, permeab*, Papp, protease, peptidase, proteolysis, aggregation, solubility, excipient, lyophil, hemolysis, anti-drug, transferrin, TfR, unbound. Word-boundary greps for Kp, fu, Vd, PK and ADA also return exactly 0 in all four files, which closes the substring loophole the reviewer flagged. I confirmed each claimed artifact individually: 'clearance' occurs 6 times and is glutamate/autophagic/lysosomal/phagocytic clearance every time (README.md:89; app.js:64,65,112,333,359); 'vial' occurs 3 times and is the FontAwesome class fa-flask-vial every time (index.html:35,89,117); 'oral' matches only inside querySelectorAll. 'therapeutic' occurs exactly 14 times, as claimed. I read openDrugModal (app.js:596-653) and confirmed the innerHTML block at 606-643 renders exactly six numbered fields -- chemStruct, sequence, bindingSites, targets, affinity, safety -- none pharmacokinetic. index.html:326 reads '25 De Novo Targeted Therapeutics Precision Center' verbatim, and README.md:45 reads 'We engineered 25 targeted bio-conjugate therapeutics'. The reasoning is also correct: the leaderboard (app.js:869-895) ranks on pLDDT, dG and CEI with no exposure term, so the platform's prioritisation is affinity-only. Nothing in this finding is overstated.
verdicts.corrections: None on the facts. Two notes on the proposed fix rather than the finding. (1) Instruction (3) -- 'a predicted Kp,uu,brain with an explicit credible interval' -- directly contradicts DMPK-07's own (correct) instruction to render 'OUT OF DOMAIN' for a 4 kDa hydrophilic polypeptide. Implemented as written, DMPK-01 replaces one set of invented numbers with a newer, better-dressed set. DMPK-07's instruction must govern, and DMPK-01 should be reworded to require route, target compartment and an explicit out-of-domain flag rather than a predicted Kp,uu value. (2) index.html:39 is cited as evidence but reads '25 De Novo Drug Center', not 'Therapeutics'; index.html:326 and README.md:45 carry the claim, and the citation should rest on those.

verdicts.reasoning: I parsed all 25 sequence fields out of app.js myself and recomputed every descriptor independently (average residue masses, EMBOSS pKa set, Kyte-Doolittle, sliding-window Eisenberg). The reviewer's physicochemistry reproduces almost exactly: length 26-47 (median 35.5 vs their 35); MW 2877-5436 Da (median 4112 vs their 4094); net charge at pH 7.4 spanning -7.20 to +8.93, identical to the digit; pI 3.45-10.95 vs their 3.44-10.95; GRAVY -1.12 to +0.26, median -0.92, identical. Their three spot-checked rows reproduce: X1 at app.js:143 = 47 aa, 5340 Da, GRAVY -0.94 (charge -0.61 vs their -0.54, a trivial pKa-set difference); X2 at app.js:153 = 36 aa, 4943 Da, q +8.93, pI 10.95, GRAVY -1.09, 36.1% Arg+Lys, all exact; X3 at app.js:163 = 28 aa, 3508 Da, q -7.20, pI 3.45, exact. I confirmed no candidate carries an RMT shuttle, Fc, TfR1/CD98hc binder or transporter ligand. I re-derived their dose arithmetic for X2 from scratch: 3xKd = 6.3 nM unbound brain, Kp,uu 0.01, fu 0.05, Vd 0.1 L/kg, t1/2 27 min gives CL 10.8 L/h and 16.1 g/day by continuous infusion, and 0.109 g/day under their generous parameter set -- their 16 g/day and 0.11 g/day are correct, as is the >3-log spread. I verified the Pardridge calibration numbers directly in the Europe PMC full text (PMC10426772): '0.07% ID/Gram' for the murine precursor of bapineuzumab, '0.028% ID/Gram' for mAb158, and 'the level of IgG in primate brain following IV administration is <0.01% of the plasma concentration' all appear verbatim. Pardridge 2020 (PMID 33207605) states verbatim that 98% of small molecules and ~100% of biologics do not cross the BBB and that <1% of AD projects used a BBB delivery technology. The core conclusion stands.
verdicts.corrections: Three corrections. (1) The stated ground truth 'roughly 8-10 hydrogen-bond donors' is wrong. Pajouhesh & Lenz give HBD < 3 and HBA < 7, with total H-bonds < 8.8; the reviewer has conflated the total-H-bond ceiling with the donor ceiling, making the quoted limit roughly threefold too permissive. Correcting it strengthens the finding: on my count (44-90 donors, median 72) the candidates exceed an HBD<3 limit by ~15-30x, not the 5-13x claimed. My donor counts also differ from theirs (they report 52-106, median 80) purely by counting convention; the conclusion is convention-independent. (2) 'Nothing in these 25 designs does better than an IgG at crossing' is an overstatement and is the one sentence in this review a motivated author could rebut. Adsorptive-mediated transcytosis is an established, if crude, BBB route for polycationic peptides and CPPs, with published 6-30x enhancements of conjugated payload brain uptake for SynB and penetratin conjugates. The four candidates at net charge +4.8 to +8.9 with 27-36% Arg+Lys are precisely that chemotype and would be expected to exceed IgG's 0.028-0.07 %ID/g. AMT is low-efficiency, non-saturable, non-selective and carries heavy peripheral and renal uptake, so it does not rescue the designs -- but the claim should be narrowed to 'no candidate carries a specific, saturable receptor-mediated transport mechanism; the only plausible route is non-selective AMT, which is not a delivery strategy'. (3) 'glomerular charge trapping' is backwards: the glomerular basement membrane is anionic, so charge selectivity favours filtration of polycations rather than trapping them. The real renal liability, which the review omits entirely, is proximal-tubule reabsorption and accumulation -- the mechanism behind polymyxin and aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity.

verdicts.reasoning: I implemented the Eisenberg normalized-consensus hydrophobic moment with a sliding 18-residue, 100-degree window independently and reproduced the candidate values to three decimals: X2/B1 (app.js:153, 247) muH = 0.893 at q +8.93, 36.1% Arg+Lys; M4 (app.js:329) muH = 0.883 at q +6.93, 34.4% Arg+Lys; X5 (app.js:183) muH = 0.883 at q +4.79, 27.3% Arg+Lys. Their maximally amphipathic window for X2/B1, KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFE, is the window my scan also selects, and it is textbook pore-forming architecture. Three of their four calibration points reproduce on my identical implementation: melittin 0.550 (they said 0.55), pexiganan/MSI-78 0.746 (0.75), (KLAKLAK)2 0.690 (0.69), polyalanine 0.000 (0.00). I confirmed via grep that hemolysis, HC50, MRGPRX2 and complement appear zero times in the codebase, that no infusion-reaction statement exists, and that README.md:99 states verbatim that 'Hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656 residues' for all 25 candidates. Wieprecht 1997 (PMID 9166783) supports the mechanistic rebuttal precisely: the abstract states the analogues were designed with 'retained hydrophobic moment, peptide charge, and angle subtended by the hydrophilic helix region', that PC-rich (mammalian) permeabilisation 'increases drastically with enhanced peptide hydrophobicity', and that 'the antibacterial and hemolytic activity of the peptides increases with enhanced hydrophobicity' with 'a strong correlation ... between the hemolytic effect and the bilayer-permeabilizing activity against PC-rich vesicles'. Maturana 2017 (PMID 28236791) likewise confirms P6 (no antimicrobial, high hemolytic) had 'the highest affinity toward erythrocyte membranes'. The chemotype identification and the safety-gap conclusion are correct. Their proposed flag threshold works: muH > 0.5 and net charge > +3 catches exactly ids 2, 5, 11 and 19 on my numbers and nothing else.
verdicts.corrections: Two corrections, one of which matters. (1) The LL-37 calibration does not reproduce. On the identical Eisenberg scale and identical 18-residue window, full-length LL-37 (LLGDFFRKSKEKIGKEFKRIVQRIKDFLRNLVPRTES) gives muH = 0.894 -- equal to, marginally above, X2/B1's 0.893, not the 0.78 the reviewer reports. The reviewer writes 'LL-37 core', i.e. an unspecified fragment, so the comparison is not reproducible from the stated method. The headline claim 'exceeds LL-37' must be withdrawn and replaced with 'matches LL-37, the best-characterised human membranolytic peptide, and exceeds melittin, pexiganan and (KLAKLAK)2'. That is still a damning statement and is defensible; 'exceeds LL-37' is not. Their 'idealized Leu/Lys amphipathic helix 0.63' is likewise unreproducible -- my LKKLLKLLKKLLKLLKKLLKLL gives 0.807, and an idealised amphipath should sit near the theoretical maximum, so 0.63 suggests a different, unstated sequence. Any calibration table published in this report must ship the exact reference sequences. (2) The quoted safety string is mis-anchored. 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Cardiotoxicity)' appears only at app.js:147, which is HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 -- not one of the four flagged candidates. The four flagged records say only 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' (app.js:157, 251, 333) plus 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%' and 'Peripheral Side Effects: None', which I verified verbatim. The blanket '0% Risk' claim covering all 25 is at README.md:99. Re-anchor the quotation there. Separately, the review would be stronger if it acknowledged that this architecture may be a deliberate CPP/AMT motif rather than an accident -- the finding is that a known dose-limiting liability of the chemotype is unassessed, not that the designers blundered.

verdicts.reasoning: I verified the residue mapping myself rather than trusting it. Against canonical Abeta42 (DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA), the string KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM is an exact contiguous match to residues 16-35, beginning at Lys16 and ending at Met35; KLVFF maps to Abeta 16-20 and GAIIGLM to Abeta 29-35, exactly as claimed. In APP770/UniProt P05067 numbering, with Abeta1 = APP672, this is residues 687-706 -- the reviewer's range is correct to the residue. I confirmed the fragment is the literal prefix of the candidate-14 sequence at app.js:277 and is contained in the AF3 rank-5 fasta at app.js:129. I independently computed GRAVY for all 25 and confirmed candidate 14 is the sole positive value at +0.26, with every other candidate negative -- the uniqueness claim is exactly right. 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' at app.js:281 and 'Salvianolic Acid B + Abeta Disruptor (KLVFFAED)' at README.md:77 are verbatim, as is the basal-forebrain target string at app.js:279. Greps confirm zero occurrences of aggregation, solubility, thioflavin, seeding, ARIA or oligomer-content anywhere. The pharmacological argument is correct and is the standard position in the field: KLVFF is the self-recognition element of Abeta self-assembly, and beta-sheet-breaker designs deliberately truncate to the minimal motif and abolish self-assembly competence by N-methylation, D-substitution or proline insertion; extending to residue 35 restores the full nucleating unit rather than blocking it.
verdicts.corrections: Two small ones, neither affecting the verdict. (1) The reviewer says the other 24 candidates fall 'between -0.30 and -1.12'; the actual range is -0.34 to -1.12. (2) Calling GRAVY +0.26 'the computational signature of its aggregation propensity' overreaches -- GRAVY is a crude bulk hydropathy average and is not an aggregation predictor. The evidence that carries this finding is the verbatim identity of the amyloidogenic core, which is sufficient on its own; the GRAVY value should be presented as corroborating context, not as a signature. The recommendation to add a TANGO/AGGRESCAN/Waltz-style predictor in the fix is the right instrument for that job.

verdicts.reasoning: I extracted all 25 sequence fields programmatically and confirmed exactly four byte-identical pairs, at exactly the lines cited: 153/247 (36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG), 173/371 (31-mer CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH), 195/319 (41-mer SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC), 205/361 (37-mer VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH). Distinct-sequence count is 21, as claimed. Every conflicting metadata pair checks out: Kd 2.1 vs 0.65 nM and pLDDT 94.8 vs 94.3 for the same 36-mer, sent to hippocampal CA1 cholinergic terminals and to the nucleus basalis of Meynert respectively; Kd 1.2 vs 2.8 nM (FZD8 agonist in DG SGZ vs ZO-1 protector at BBB endothelium); Kd 1.8 vs 3.8 nM (alpha7 nAChR PAM in PFC vs TLR4/MD-2 antagonist on microglia); Kd 0.85 vs 3.6 nM (TrkB ERK enhancer vs astrocytic EAAT2 upregulator). I also confirmed the reviewer's substantive point about mechanism: no candidate carries a cell-type-restricted ligand, capsid, promoter or locally activated prodrug, and the distribution argument for a freely diffusing peptide in brain ISF is correct. The cited literature is real and says what is claimed -- Huang 2024 (PMID 38753766) states verbatim '40 to 50 times greater reporter expression in the CNS of human [TfR1] knockin mice' and that 'the enhanced tropism was CNS-specific and absent in wild-type mice'; Rezai 2024 (PMID 38169490) states the Abeta reduction 'was numerically greater in regions treated with focused ultrasound than in the homologous regions in the contralateral hemisphere'.
verdicts.corrections: The conclusion is right but the central argument is wrong and must be replaced before this ships. The reviewer writes that a different pLDDT for the same input string 'is not possible for a deterministic model'. That is false twice. First, AlphaFold3 is not deterministic: its structure module is a seeded diffusion model, multiple samples are drawn per seed, and AlphaFold Server returns an ensemble, so identical input legitimately yields different pLDDT across runs. An author could rebut the finding on exactly this point. Second, and decisively, none of these numbers came from AlphaFold at all. app.js:791 computes the displayed pLDDT as `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5` and app.js:850 computes PAE as `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (charCodeAt(i%len) % 4)*0.3` -- closed-form functions of residue index and ASCII code, bounded to roughly 89-99 for any input whatsoever. The correct argument is therefore not 'the model is deterministic so the numbers conflict' but 'no pLDDT anywhere in this platform is an AlphaFold output, so all of them, conflicting or not, are fabricated'. Also: the same 36-mer carries a third, different value (92.8) as AF3 candidate CogAChE-PAS-02 at app.js:131, which the reviewer missed and which makes the point unanswerable. Finally, a citation error: 'conflicting metadata at app.js:145/146' should read 155/156 -- lines 145/146 belong to HippoTrk-Saponin-X1, an unrelated record. And 'at most 21 distinct sequences' should note that one of the 21 (app.js:381) is not a sequence at all, leaving 20 real peptides.

verdicts.reasoning: This is the most rigorously supported finding in the review and it holds under direct replication. I retrieved the Cavaco 2021 full text from Europe PMC (PMC8301568) and the regression appears verbatim: 'ln t1/2 = 2.226 + 0.053 x NP residues % - 1.515 x W[0,1] + 1.290 x Y[0,1] - 1.052 x pI[0,1]', with NP = presence of nonpolar residues (%), W = absence/presence of at least one Trp, Y = presence of just one Tyr (0) or at least two Tyr (1), pI = pI less than 10 (0) or greater than 10 (1). The validation library range is also verbatim: 'The ln[t1/2] of the 16 peptides in human serum ranged from 2 to 6 (i.e., 7.4 to 403.4 min)'. I then implemented the model myself and applied it to all 24 letter-parseable sequences (mapping B to Asn, as the reviewer evidently did to reach n=24) with nonpolar = AVLIPFMWG. My output matches theirs to the digit: 22 of 24 contain Trp; minimum 7.9 min for HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 (they said 8); maximum 99.7 min for AstroSuper-CBF-EAAT2-A5 (they said 100); median 26.4 min (they said 26); 18 of 24 below 60 min; 24 of 24 below 120 min. I independently confirmed that no sequence carries cyclisation, D-residue, N-methyl, PEG, lipid, albumin-binder or Fc notation, that the chemStruct fields describe only warhead attachment chemistry, and that README.md:102 states 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' and app.js:157 states 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%'. The 30-day-pharmacology-versus-minutes-scale-residence contradiction is real. Lau & Dunn (PMID 28720325) confirms '>60 peptide drugs are approved' and 'over 150 peptides in active development'.
verdicts.corrections: Two refinements. (1) The predicted half-lives are more sensitive to an undefined term than the review admits. Cavaco does not fix the membership of 'nonpolar residues'; with AVLIPFMWG I reproduce median 26 min, but including Cys gives median 43 min and excluding Gly and Trp gives median 8 min. The point estimate should be published as a set-dependent range, which is what the reviewer's own fix demands elsewhere and should demand here. (2) The pI term is pI > 10, not pI >= 10 as written; immaterial for these sequences. Substantively I would add that the proteolysis estimate is an upper bound, not the answer, because renal filtration is the parallel clearance pathway the review never quantifies -- see my missed-issues list.

verdicts.reasoning: I recomputed the thermodynamic consistency for all 25 records rather than the reviewer's five. At 298 K with RT = 0.5921 kcal/mol, dG = -18.4 kcal/mol implies Kd = 3.195e-5 nM against the stated 0.32 nM, a factor of 10,014 -- the reviewer's 3.2e-5 nM and ~9,900x are correct. Across all 25 records the discrepancy runs from 676x (app.js:384) to 16,046x (app.js:290), bracketing the reviewer's spot-checked 670x-15,800x, and in every single case the stated Kd is weaker than the stated dG implies. That unidirectional bias is itself strong evidence the two numbers were assigned independently rather than derived, exactly as the reviewer infers. Word-boundary greps confirm zero occurrences of Kp, fu, unbound, MDCK, MDR1, P-gp, efflux and Papp in all four files. I read renderLeaderboardTable (app.js:869-895) and renderBenchmarkChart (app.js:1049-1103) and confirmed the ranking columns are pLDDT, dG and CEI only, with the chart plotting CEI against |dG| at app.js:1053-1055. 'Cognitive Enhancement Index' is indeed never defined anywhere in the codebase -- it appears only as a data field (app.js:124-135), a chart label (app.js:1063) and a table header (index.html:306). Loryan 2022 (PMID 35411506) supports the ground truth verbatim: 'the majority of the companies (93%) has established a common understanding across disciplines of the concept and utility of K[p,uu]', '79% of all responders describe the portfolio impact of K[p,uu] implementation in their companies as game-changing', and '74% consider the current toolbox ... satisfactory'.
verdicts.corrections: None on the facts; one on grading. I would raise this from MAJOR to CRITICAL. The dG/Kd inconsistency is presented as a secondary point inside a methodology finding, but it is not a methodological preference -- it is arithmetic proof that the two headline numbers on every one of the 25 cards and the leaderboard were fabricated independently of each other. That is the same class of evidence, and the same degree of certainty, as the duplicate-sequence finding graded CRITICAL at DMPK-05, and it covers 25 records rather than 8. It should either be split into its own CRITICAL fabricated-data finding alongside DMPK-05 or this finding should be regraded. One caution on the fix: 'replace the affinity-only ranking with a composite that requires an exposure term' cannot be implemented honestly on these molecules, because the same finding correctly concludes the exposure predictors are out of domain for 3-5 kDa polypeptides. The implementable instruction is to remove the ranking entirely rather than to reweight it.

verdicts.reasoning: The three headline defects are real and I verified each. app.js:381 literally sets sequence to 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'; I traced it through openDrugModal (app.js:600, 648-652) and confirmed all three renderers execute on it unconditionally without crashing, and that copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) will place that English phrase on the clipboard. The letter B appears at app.js:173, app.js:371 and app.js:130, and I confirmed independently that AlphaFold Server accepts only the 20 standard single-letter codes and rejects B, J, O, U and X -- so the Copy-FASTA-and-launch workflow genuinely emits input the server will refuse for those records. On cysteines, I counted them programmatically: 7 Cys in the 31-mer at app.js:173/371 (correct), 7 Cys in the 37-mer at app.js:205/361 (correct), 8 in the 47-mer at app.js:143 and 8 in the 45-mer at app.js:215 (correct). Greps confirm no disulfide connectivity is specified anywhere, and no oxidative folding, scrambling or thiol-mediated dimerisation discussion exists. The 'Immunogenicity: Low/Very Low' strings are at app.js:167, 271 and 303 exactly as cited. The free-thiol developability argument is sound and standard.
verdicts.corrections: The cysteine census is wrong and must be fixed before publication, because a reviewer who miscounts the thing they are counting loses the room. The actual number of records with an odd cysteine count is 10, not 11, and the id list given (3,4,7,9,12,13,15,16,17,20,22,23) is wrong on four entries: id 3 has 2 Cys (even), id 12 has 6 (even), id 17 has 4 (even), and id 21 -- 5 Cys in a 34-mer at app.js:351 -- is odd and was omitted. The correct set is ids 4, 7, 9, 13, 15, 16, 20, 21, 22, 23 (app.js lines 173, 205, 225, 267, 287, 299, 339, 351, 361, 371). The two 8-Cys records cited as evidence (ids 1 and 8) have even counts and belong to the separate 'high cysteine density' argument, not the free-thiol argument; the reviewer merged the two under the phrase 'odd or high counts', which is what produced the error. Second, the illustrative pLDDT axis labels are wrong: the reviewer writes 'H1 i2 s3 -4 15 44', the actual output is H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8. Substance unaffected but do not print a wrong quotation. Third, one defect the reviewer missed in this same finding: copyModalFasta writes the bare sequence with no '>' header (app.js:662), so the button labelled 'Copy FASTA Sequence' never produces FASTA for any of the 25 records, not just the broken one.

missed_by_reviewer: THE CENTRAL FABRICATION IS NEVER NAMED. The reviewer treats pLDDT and PAE as though they were real AlphaFold outputs (DMPK-05 argues about determinism; DMPK-07 lists pLDDT as a ranking input). They are not outputs at all. app.js:791 computes every displayed pLDDT as `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5`, which returns 89-99 for literally any input string including 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' (I checked: 89.1-99.0). app.js:850 computes every PAE cell as `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (charCodeAt % 4)*0.3`, a trivial diagonal ramp with no structural content. app.js:674-773 builds the 3D 'backbone' as a Catmull-Rom tube through a helix whose radius is `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` -- geometry from ASCII arithmetic, not coordinates. Against this, app.js:707 comments 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION', index.html:371 titles the panel 'AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs', index.html:377 labels the viewer 'Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)', and README.md:108-110 describes 'Real sequence-driven backbone topology parsing' and 'residue-by-residue confidence profile'. No AlphaFold prediction exists anywhere in this repository. This is the single most serious integrity finding available and the review omits it, which also leaves DMPK-05's argument resting on the refutable claim that AF3 is deterministic.

THE SECOND BARRIER -- THE PLASMA MEMBRANE -- IS NEVER MENTIONED. The review is entirely about the BBB and stops there. Roughly a third of the 25 candidates name targets that are intracellular, so even a molecule that crossed the BBB perfectly would still be in the wrong compartment: Keap1 Kelch domain (app.js:164, 310, 340), AMPK alpha-subunit kinase domain (app.js:184), GSK-3beta ATP pocket (app.js:226), LC3-II on the autophagosomal membrane (app.js:330), and ER-beta ligand-binding domain (app.js:352, 392). A 3-5 kDa hydrophilic, largely anionic polypeptide cannot reach the cytosol or nucleus; it requires uptake plus endosomal escape, which is the harder of the two delivery problems and for which none of the proposed fixes (TfR1 RMT, CD98hc, intrathecal, FUS, AAV for a peptide payload) provides a solution. Omitting this understates the delivery gap by one entire barrier and makes the recommended remediation look more achievable than it is.

RENAL CLEARANCE IS ABSENT, WHICH MAKES THE HALF-LIFE ESTIMATE AN UPPER BOUND. Every candidate is 2877-5436 Da, an order of magnitude below the glomerular sieving threshold, so filtration alone drives clearance toward GFR and caps plasma half-life at minutes regardless of proteolysis. The Cavaco proteolytic prediction in DMPK-06 is therefore a ceiling, not an estimate, and the true dose requirement in DMPK-02 and DMPK-06 is understated. Separately, and more importantly for safety: cationic peptides are reabsorbed and accumulate in the proximal tubule, which is the established nephrotoxicity mechanism for polymyxins and aminoglycosides. For the four candidates at net charge +4.8 to +8.9 that would be dosed at gram-per-day scale, renal tubular injury is at least as probable a dose-limiting toxicity as the hemolysis the review does flag, and the kidney appears nowhere in the report.

THE MOLECULE ANALYSED IS NOT THE MOLECULE CLAIMED. Every record is described as a bio-conjugate, and the chemStruct fields specify large natural-product warheads: ginsenoside Rg1 C42H72O14 (app.js:142), ginsenoside Rb1 C54H92O23 (app.js:204, 360), salvianolic acid B C36H30O16 (app.js:276, 350), curcumin C21H20O6 (app.js:162, 298). The reviewer computed MW, GRAVY, net charge, hydrogen-bond donors and hydrophobic moment for the peptide alone and reported them as the candidate's properties. An Rb1 conjugate adds roughly 930 Da and about eleven further hydrogen-bond donors; salvianolic acid B adds a polyanionic tetracatechol. These warheads are themselves textbook poor CNS penetrants. The physicochemical table needs an explicit caveat that it describes the peptide moiety only and that the actual claimed entity is larger, more polar and worse.

THE RECOMMENDED FIXES ARE PRESCRIBED WITHOUT THEIR OWN LIMITATIONS. (a) Intrathecal/ICV is offered four times as an alternative route, but CSF-administered macromolecules penetrate brain parenchyma only on the order of hundreds of microns to a couple of millimetres from ependymal and pial surfaces, and human CSF turns over several times per day. IT/ICV will not deliver a 4 kDa peptide to hippocampal CA1 or the nucleus basalis of Meynert -- precisely the deep structures this platform targets -- so as written the recommendation sends the author down a route that fails for the stated indications. (b) TfR1 RMT is prescribed across four findings, with its liabilities relegated to a single clause in a literature note. High-affinity or bivalent TfR engagement causes reticulocyte depletion and acute clinical-chemistry changes; monovalency, affinity tuning and effector-function silencing are prerequisites of the format, not implementation details. A fix reading 'attach a TfR1 shuttle' can reproduce a known safety failure.

FABRICATED EFFICACY NUMBERS GET A PASS WHILE FABRICATED SAFETY NUMBERS ARE ATTACKED. The review demands 'NOT ASSESSED' for all 25 safety strings but leaves the equally unsupported efficacy point estimates in the same records untouched: 'LTP +280%' (README.md:60, app.js:148), 'dendritic spine density +310%' (README.md:64, app.js:188), 'synaptic ACh +350%' (README.md:74, app.js:252), 'lysosomal degradation +420%' (app.js:333-334), 'CBF +45%' (app.js:355-356), 'working memory span +240%' (app.js:200), 'information processing speed 2x' (README.md:71). These carry no model, no n, no dose and no error bar, and they are the numbers a reader will actually act on. Correcting only one side of the ledger is an asymmetry an author can exploit.

TWO OF THE SCORED METRICS DO NOT EXIST AS ENDPOINTS. The review treats 'Seizure Index: 0.01-0.02 / 1.0' as an unassessed value that should be relabelled. There is no such normalised in-silico endpoint; like 'Cognitive Enhancement Index' (which the review does correctly flag), it is an invented scale. The same applies to 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291) and 'Safety Index: 99.1 / 100' (app.js:343). Inventing a metric and then scoring against it is a distinct and more serious defect than failing to measure a real one, and these strings should be deleted rather than populated with 'NOT ASSESSED', which would imply the endpoint is real and merely unrun.

NO VALIDATION IS DEMANDED OF THE PREDICTORS THE FIXES WOULD INSTALL. The review prescribes a substantial new in-silico DMPK layer -- Kp,uu,brain, fu,plasma, fu,brain, MDCK-MDR1 efflux ratio, Papp, aggregation propensity, serum t1/2 -- but never requires the platform to demonstrate that any of it recovers known answers. The minimum standard before any of these numbers is displayed is a positive-control set: run several marketed CNS small molecules and at least one marketed peptide with published Kp,uu and human t1/2 through the identical pipeline and show the predictions bracket the measured values, with the out-of-domain flag firing on the peptide. Without that, the remediation risks replacing a visibly fabricated dataset with an invisibly fabricated one, which is worse.

verdicts.corrections: (1) FACTUALLY WRONG: 'the PAE matrix is symmetric by construction'. The ASCII term at app.js:850 indexes only i (`sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length)`), never j, so PAE(i,j) != PAE(j,i). I computed 936 of 1296 cells asymmetric for a 36-mer. This is also self-contradictory with the reviewer's own ground_truth ('PAE is not symmetric'). Delete the sub-claim; the surviving true statement is that the matrix is |i-j|*0.4 plus a row-constant ASCII offset. (2) OVERSTATED: the curve 'can never enter the High (70-90) bin'. Analytic range is [89.0, 99.0], so 89.0-90.0 IS reachable; across all 25 sequences 77 of 876 residue points (8.8%) fall below 90. Only 'Low (50-70)' and 'Very Low (<50)' are unreachable. The sharper true defect is that the legend at index.html:388-391 is purely decorative: the line is a fixed cyan (`borderColor: '#00f2fe'`, app.js:804) and no binning is applied to anything. (3) ARITHMETIC NIT: '1208% bond-length variation' should be 1203% ((15.77-1.21)/1.21); pooled across sequences the spread is wider still (1.04-19.08). (4) git ls-files also returns .gitignore, omitted from the reviewer's list; immaterial.

verdicts.reasoning: I extracted all 25 affinity strings from app.js and redid every calculation in python3 with R = 1.9872041e-3 kcal/mol/K. Every figure the reviewer states reproduces to the digit: at 298.15 K the stated dG is more negative than the stated Kd permits by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol; the Kd/dG ratio spans 665x to 15,729x; HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (-18.4 | 0.32 nM) gives dG_from_Kd = -12.95 and Kd_from_dG = 3.256e-14 M, a 9,828-fold gap; BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (-19.5 | 0.08 nM) is off by 15,729x with an implied Kd of 5.086e-15 M. My OLS of dG on ln(Kd) returns slope 1.0495, intercept 4.6817, R^2 = 0.99391 - identical to the reviewer's 1.0495 / 4.682 / 0.9939 - and slope/R = 528.1 K = 255.0 C. At 310 K the discrepancy narrows to 3.40-5.18 kcal/mol but never closes. The categorical claim that AlphaFold 3 emits no energetic quantity is confirmed against the Nature paper. This finding is the strongest in the review because it is checkable with a calculator and needs no reading of the rendering code.
verdicts.corrections: The biotin-streptavidin anchor is internally inconsistent, which is unfortunate in a finding about dG/Kd consistency: '~10 fM, dG ~ -18.3 kcal/mol' cannot both hold, since 1e-14 M gives -19.10 kcal/mol at 298.15 K and -18.3 kcal/mol gives 3.9e-14 M (39 fM). Pick one anchor and state it self-consistently (Green's Ka = 2.5e13 M^-1 gives Kd 4e-14 M and dG -18.3 kcal/mol). The conclusion is unaffected and if anything sharpened: -19.5 kcal/mol corresponds to 5.1 fM, i.e. roughly 8-fold tighter than the tightest well-characterised non-covalent protein-ligand complex, and all 25 candidates are claimed at or beyond that regime.

verdicts.reasoning: Provenance and expressibility are confirmed outright. README.md:98 asserts screening was performed; there is no ADMET code, no descriptor calculation, no result file (git ls-files). I verified every absolute string cited: 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' (app.js:251), 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (app.js:323), 'Off-target Binding: None' (app.js:209), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (app.js:281), 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291), plus 'BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%' (app.js:375) and 'Cytokine Storm Risk: None' (app.js:343) which the reviewer did not list. I recomputed the physicochemistry: X2/B1 (app.js:153/247) carry 13 K+R and 4 D+E for net ~+9 at pH 7.4 with 30.6% W/F/Y; M4 (app.js:329) is +7 with 28.1% aromatic - the reviewer's numbers are right. I fetched the Mitcheson et al. PNAS 2000 abstract (PMID 11005845 verified): Y652 and F656 sit on S6 and 'face the cavity of the channel', with block by structurally diverse small lipophilic compounds. The README's steric-shielding rationale is indeed unsupported. But the reviewer's stated reason overreaches (see corrections).
verdicts.corrections: Point (3) 'Direction' is domain overreach as written. 'Cationic, aromatic-rich, amphipathic sequences are the canonical hERG-blocker pharmacophore' imports a small-molecule SAR (basic nitrogen + lipophilic aromatic, reaching the inner cavity from the cytosolic side) onto a 30-45mer polycation that cannot physically access Y652/F656 at all. The correct and stronger criticism is a category error, not an inverted direction: the site named in README.md:99 is inaccessible to a peptide of this size, so neither 'steric prevention' nor 'blockade' is assertable, and the genuine peptide liabilities are membrane lysis/haemolysis, immunogenicity (ADA/MHC-II) and protease instability - exactly what the reviewer's own required_fix says, which contradicts their point (3). Rewrite the finding to match the fix. Additionally, the reviewer missed the single fastest tell: all 25 records carry the byte-identical string 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' (app.js:147 through 395) - one value applied to 25 chemically distinct entities is prima facie proof that no per-compound calculation occurred, and it is checkable in one grep.

verdicts.reasoning: I checked every cited line verbatim in README.md: :60 'Neurogenesis & CA1 LTP (+280%)', :64 'Dendritic spine density (+310%)', :67 '(+240%)', :71 'Information processing speed 2x', :74 'Synaptic ACh +350%', :84 '(+420%)', :88 'CBF +45%', :100 'capped Emax (135%)', :102 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days'; and the app.js mirrors at 148, 188, 200, 240, 252, 334, 356. Every CID the reviewer cites is correct with the stated formula and MW: Huperzine A 854026 C15H18N2O 242.32; Curcumin 969516 C21H20O6 368.4 (and the isomeric SMILES they quote matches PubChem byte-for-byte); Ginkgolide B 11973122 C20H24O10 424.4; Ginsenoside Rg1 441923 C42H72O14 801.0; Baicalein 5281605 C15H10O5; Asiatic acid 119034 C30H48O5. verdicts.corrections: (1) WRONG REASON, RIGHT CONCLUSION: Huperzine A (app.js:10) does not 'encode 14 carbons' - it does not parse at all. RDKit returns 'SMILES Parse Error: unclosed ring for input: CC1=CC2C(=C)C3C(=O)NC(=C2CC3(C)N)C' (ring-closure label 1 is opened and never closed) and PubChem PUG-REST returns PUGREST.BadRequest 'Standardization failed'. So three of eight fields are hard syntax failures, not one. Fix the reasoning; the finding gets stronger. (2) UNDERSTATED: Baicalein is not merely 'worth a separate chemistry check'. I submitted the repo string to PubChem and it resolves to CID 14372623 = 6,7,8-trihydroxy-2-phenylchromen-4-one - a different regioisomer, not baicalein (5,6,7-, CID 5281605). It is definitively the wrong molecule, and should be stated as such. Asiatic acid resolves to CID 296191, the stereochemistry-stripped parent rather than CID 119034, consistent with the reviewer's stereochemistry point. Net tally: 6 of 8 fields defective. (3) FIX IS INSUFFICIENT: the proposed CI gate - 'RDKit MolFromSmiles non-null and formula match against the recorded CID' - would PASS the baicalein error, because the wrong regioisomer has the identical formula C15H10O5. I demonstrated this empirically. The gate must compare InChIKey (or at minimum canonical connectivity SMILES) against the recorded CID, never the molecular formula.

verdicts.reasoning: My own grep for 'cei|cognitive enhancement' across all four files returns only the data literals (app.js:125-134), the leaderboard cell (app.js:886), the chart dataset label (app.js:1063-1064) and the two index.html render sites (:306 th, :316 'Computational Benchmark'). There is no formula, no input list, no normalisation, no validation set and no citation. The absence-claim holds exactly as stated, and the objection - that 'benchmark' asserts a defined reproducible quantity - is correct and proportionately rated.
verdicts.corrections: 'The values also track the rank order almost perfectly' is slightly wrong and should be replaced by a stronger, exactly true statement. CEI is not monotone in rank: rank 4 (CogTrk-DeNovo-01, CEI 93.8, app.js:128) exceeds rank 3 (CogNrf-KeapDis-03, CEI 92.1, app.js:127). |dG| is monotone in rank either (rank 4 is -14.2, rank 5 is -14.8). The defensible finding is therefore sharper: the leaderboard ranking is not reproducible from ANY column the page displays - it follows neither CEI nor binding energy - so the ordering has no stated derivation at all, not merely an undefined one. Drop the inference that the score was 'written to match a pre-decided ranking'; the inversion undercuts it and it is not needed.

missed_by_reviewer: LEAD FINDING MISSED - AlphaFold 3 cannot design sequences at all, so the platform's central capability claim is impossible in principle, not merely unperformed. README.md:22 says the 25 therapeutics were 'designed via AlphaFold3'; README.md:45 says they fuse warheads with 'AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides'; index.html:290 labels the sequence box 'FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)'; index.html:53 says 'AlphaFold3 Sequence-Driven Drug Discovery'. AF3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w, verified via PMC11168924) is a structure predictor conditioned on a supplied sequence; it has no generative or design head and cannot propose, optimise or score a de novo sequence. Every one of the nine findings treats AF3 as a tool that could have been run but wasn't. None states that even a flawless AF3 run could not have produced these sequences - which is the more fundamental error and should lead the report, above the pLDDT labelling. Sequence design requires an RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN-class pipeline, which the reviewer cites for reporting style but never invokes on this point.

SECOND LEAD FINDING MISSED - fragment recombination is pervasive, not four duplicate pairs. I enumerated all 8-mers across the 24 peptide records: 169 of 321 distinct 8-mers (53%) appear in two or more candidates, and 16 of the 24 sequences have 100% of their residues inside a motif shared with another candidate. Concretely: X1 (app.js:143, 'TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain') and B3 (app.js:267, 'TrkA Extracellular Ig-like Domain') share a contiguous 28-residue block; X1, P2 and A2 (app.js:143/205/361) share a contiguous 37-residue block spanning targets 'TrkB D5', 'TrkB D5' and 'EAAT2/GLT-1' - the last being a 12-transmembrane solute carrier with no Ig fold whatsoever; X2 (app.js:153, 'AChE catalytic gorge') and M4 (app.js:329, 'autophagosomal membrane LC3-II') share a contiguous 32-residue block; M1 (app.js:299, 'Trem2 Ig domain') and P3 (app.js:215, 'GluN2A NTD') share 25 residues. The pipeline is roughly six fragments recombined and assigned to targets post hoc. This is a broader and more damning integrity signal than the four exact duplicates, it is quantitative and reproducible in ten lines of python, and it is the specific reason I raised INTEG-07 to CRITICAL.

No pharmacokinetics, no route of administration, no blood-brain-barrier story anywhere. Every record asserts delivery specificity in its targets field - e.g. app.js:145 'CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1/CA3 Pyramidal Neurons & DG SGZ Neural Stem Cells)' - for 26-47mer polycationic peptides conjugated to triterpenoid saponins. Peptides of this size and charge have essentially no oral bioavailability and negligible passive BBB permeability, and no targeting or delivery moiety appears anywhere (no TfR/LRP1 shuttle, no CPP rationale beyond incidental cationicity, no intranasal or intrathecal route, no serum-stability statement). The reviewer mentions BBB penetration once, buried in a remediation bullet under INTEG-03. It warrants its own finding, because it is the load-bearing assumption behind every brain-region claim in the document, and it is unaffected by any labelling fix.

The claimed binding modes are geometrically implausible even as hypotheses, which the review never assesses. app.js:154/158 and README.md:61 assert that a 36-mer 'dual-clamps the AChE gorge entrance (PAS) and catalytic site (CAS)'. The AChE active-site gorge is roughly 20 A deep with a narrow bottleneck; simultaneous CAS+PAS occupancy is achieved by small bivalent ligands (bis-tacrines, donepezil-tacrine hybrids), not by a 36-residue polycation that cannot enter the gorge. The same class of objection applies to the Keap1 Kelch 'decoy' and the a7 nAChR ECD contacts. A structural pharmacology review must say that the residue lists are not merely uncited but sterically incompatible with the stated ligand size - otherwise the remediation ('mark as HYPOTHESIS') licenses hypotheses that are physically impossible.

Mixed and self-contradictory AChE residue numbering, in the very material the review credits as 'largely sound'. app.js:154 reads 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)': Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica numbering while Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341 are human - two organisms' numbering inside one string. Separately app.js:12 gives 'Trp279 (PAS)' (Torpedo) for Huperzine A while README.md:32 gives 'PAS (Trp286)' (human) for the same compound. No organism or numbering convention is declared anywhere in the repository. Additionally app.js:12 calls the Trp84/Phe330 contact a 'CAS Salt Bridge' while README.md:32 correctly calls it cation-pi; a salt bridge between two neutral aromatics is chemically impossible. These are uncontroversial, individually checkable domain errors.

The bio-conjugate - the thing every number is nominally about - is never represented in machine-readable form. All 25 are described as warhead + linker + peptide, with named chemistry: '1,2,3-Triazole Linker' (app.js:182), 'Azide Linker' (app.js:298), 'Cys-Lys Amide Coupling' (app.js:152). But the only structure stored is the peptide FASTA: no SMILES, no conjugation site, no attachment residue, no stoichiometry, no molecular weight for any of the 25. Consequently even the one honest feature the reviewer praises - copy FASTA, run it on AlphaFold Server - would model a chemically different entity from the one the page claims, and every dG, Kd and safety value refers to a molecule whose structure does not exist anywhere in the repository. (Note also that an azide is the reagent in CuAAC click chemistry, not the resulting linker.)

The uniform hERG string is the single fastest demonstration and the review does not use it. All 25 safety fields carry the byte-identical substring 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' (app.js:147 through app.js:395). One identical value across 25 chemically distinct entities is direct positive evidence that no per-compound calculation was performed, which is stronger and cheaper to verify than INTEG-03's argument from the absence of tooling. It is one grep, and it survives any objection of the form 'the tool ran elsewhere and only the results were pasted in'.

Headline pLDDT and plotted pLDDT are two unconnected numbers shown in the same panel and are never reconciled. Each modal renders a hardcoded string such as 'AF3 pLDDT = 97.0 / 100' (app.js:166) directly beside a chart generated independently by app.js:791, whose values across all 25 sequences span 89.0-99.0 with a mean near 94 and can never reach 97.0 as a mean. Two different values for the same quantity, from two unrelated sources, in one view. Related and equally unflagged: app.js:903 hardcodes '(AF3 Confidence: Very High)' for every candidate regardless of the value shown, including rank 10 at 90.7.

A rendering bug that falsifies the 'residue-specific' claim independently of any labelling question. Residue spheres are positioned with curve.getPoint(i / seqLength) (app.js:744 and app.js:1005), but a Catmull-Rom curve through n control points parameterises control point i at approximately i/(n-1), not i/n. Every sphere is therefore displaced from the residue it nominally marks, with the error growing along the chain. So even the sequence-driven decoration does not index the residue it claims to - the 'pLDDT color spectrum' spheres are both coloured by residue letter (app.js:747-749, which the reviewer notes only in the ledger and never elevates to a finding) and positioned off-residue.

Reproducibility and archival hygiene, which the reviewer's own provenance scheme depends on. README.md:4 advertises 'License: Private Research' but git ls-files shows no LICENSE file exists. index.html:15-16 load Three.js r128 and an OrbitControls build from a different release (three@0.128.0 examples) from two separate CDNs with no subresource-integrity hashes, so README.md:119-124's instruction to 'open index.html directly in any web browser' fails offline and the rendering stack is unpinned and unverifiable. There is no version number, no DOI, no changelog and no data dictionary. The proposed provenance field and CI gates cannot be enforced or audited without these. (For completeness: I read styles.css in full; it contains layout only and carries no scientific claim, so no finding is hiding there.)

verifications.discipline: Machine learning for protein / peptide binder design (generative models, inverse folding, in-silico filtering)
verifications.verifier_persona: Full professor of computational protein design, 22 years post-PhD. I run a lab that ships RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN/BindCraft campaigns with SPR and yeast-display readout, and I have refereed for Nature, Science and Nat Chem Biol on binder-design manuscripts. My name goes on this report, so every number in it was recomputed here: I re-derived the pLDDT/PAE generators from source, re-ran the dG/Kd thermodynamics in python3, pulled the UniProt reference sequences over the network and re-did the substring provenance, ran my own Smith-Waterman-with-shuffled-null homology test in place of the reviewer's unreproducible BLAST, and resolved every citation against Crossref/PubMed and the actual GitHub files.

verdicts.reasoning: Absence of a design pipeline: CONFIRMED. My own `grep -nEi "rfdiffusion|proteinmpnn|bindcraft|Rosetta|ipTM|pae_interaction|docking|vina|MMGBSA|MSA"` and a separate grep for ESM returned zero hits across app.js, README.md, index.html. `git ls-files` returns exactly .gitignore, README.md, app.js, index.html, skills-lock.json, styles.css plus ~230 vendored .agents/skills/** files -- no design script, no PDB/CIF, no score table, no seed. Provenance: I downloaded the UniProt reference entries and confirmed all four exact-match claims to the residue: GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG = P49841 (GSK3B) 3-34 verbatim; APMKEANIRGQGGLAYPGVRT = P23560 (BDNF) 19-39 verbatim; KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM = P05067 (APP) 687-706 verbatim; DEETGEFL = Q16236 (NFE2L2) 77-84 verbatim. WNT3A: P56704 203-223 is CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQPD and the drug motif is CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLC -- I counted 14/21 identity, exactly as claimed. Tiling: my greedy maximal-substring tiling (min 6 aa) of the 25 drug sequences against the 10 AF3_CANDIDATES fastas gives 805/839 = 95.9% (reviewer: 801/839 = 95.5%); total residues 876 and 876-37 = 839 both reproduce exactly, so the small delta is tiling-algorithm choice, not error. BLAST: I could NOT reproduce the reviewer's specific blastp hit list (MEGF11 E=2e-05, Tenascin, Notch3, Jagged-2, Slit2) -- no BLAST was run in my session. I substituted an independent test: Smith-Waterman (BLOSUM62, gap 11/1) of each flagship sequence against its advertised target, calibrated against 30 shuffled-sequence nulls. Results fully support the reviewer's conclusion: 49-mer 'TrkB D5 binder' vs NTRK2 SW=35, z=2.3, below the shuffled maximum of 36; 41-mer vs CHRNA7 SW=33 (z=1.8) and vs TLR4 not in top 6; 31-mer 'Trem2 agonist' vs TREM2 not in top 6; 36-mer 'AChE clamper' vs ACHE indistinguishable from noise. By contrast the three genuine grafts light up unmistakably: GSK3B fragment z=44.5, APP fragment z=19.8, WNT3A fragment z=26.7. The substantive claim -- these are copied natural motifs, and the sequences bear no relation to their advertised targets -- is independently established.
verdicts.corrections: (1) The evidence line 'app.js:130 ... CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH' is imprecise: app.js:130 is a 40-mer, CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCHGMSGSCSTK, not the 31-mer at 173/371. (2) The BLAST hit list must be re-run and logged before issue, or downgraded to 'no significant similarity to the advertised target (verified by Smith-Waterman vs shuffled null)'; a specific E-value that the report cannot reproduce is the one thing that would let the author dismiss the whole review. (3) The tiling figure should read 805/839 = 95.9% or be stated as ~96%. (4) The NFE2L2 verbatim stretch is 8 residues (DEETGEFL, 77-84), not 12: the drug's DEETGEFLFQLP does not exist in NFE2L2, which has DEETGEFLPIQPAQ -- so even the correctly-chosen motif is garbled past residue 8, and README.md:62 presents the non-existent 12-mer as 'Nrf2 ETGE'. (5) The fix's line list is incomplete: README.md:45 contains no 'De Novo' (it says 'AlphaFold3-optimized'); index.html:54, 262 and 323 also carry 'De Novo' and are omitted; app.js:137 is omitted; and index.html:410, the footer reading 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling & Structural Pharmacology Algorithms', is the most explicit false-provenance line on the page and appears in no fix list in this review.

verdicts.reasoning: Counts reproduce exactly: I parsed 25 `sequence:` entries yielding 21 distinct, and 25+10 = 35 entries yielding 26 distinct. The four intra-drug duplicate pairs are exactly those named. Target contradictions verified verbatim from source: SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC appears at app.js:195 against 'alpha7 nAChR Extracellular Domain (ECD) (Tyr188, Trp149, Tyr195)' and byte-identically at app.js:319 against 'TLR4 / MD-2 Complex (Arg264, Lys341, Glu439)'. CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH appears at app.js:173 against 'Frizzled-8 (FZD8) CRD Domain' and at app.js:371 against 'BMEC Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) & Occludin Complex'. TJP1/ZO-1 is a cytoplasmic MAGUK scaffold; an extracellular Cys-rich peptide cannot reach it -- that sub-point is unassailable and is the strongest part of this finding. VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH at 205 (TrkB D5) and 361 (EAAT2) confirmed. Divergent numbers for identical input confirmed: 196/198 gives dG -16.5, Kd 1.8 nM, pLDDT 93.2 while 320/322 gives -15.7, 3.8 nM, 92.8.
verdicts.corrections: Two reasoning errors that must be fixed before issue. (1) 'pLDDT ... is in any case a monomer confidence metric that does not depend on the binding partner at all' is FALSE as written. When AF3 predicts a complex, the per-residue pLDDT of the binder chain is computed on the complex coordinates and is influenced by the partner; a binder disordered alone and ordered at an interface genuinely scores differently. The reviewer states the correct version in their own ground_truth (pLDDT is a local-confidence metric, not an interface metric; ipTM and interface PAE are the interface metrics) -- the what_is_wrong text must be brought into line with it. (2) Following from (1), 'AF3 is deterministic for a fixed input and seed; the same sequence against the same target cannot yield two pLDDT values' does not actually apply here, because 196 and 320 are nominally two DIFFERENT complexes (alpha7 vs TLR4); real complex predictions would legitimately give two different pLDDTs. The dispositive argument is different and stronger: no target appears anywhere in the pipeline (AIML-01/03 establish that no complex was ever predicted), so a partner-dependent number cannot have been computed; and no target-conditioned generator can emit one 41-mer optimised for a Cys-loop receptor ECD and an LRR innate-immune co-receptor. As written, a knowledgeable author could refute the stated reason and, by association, dismiss a correct finding. (3) The reviewer missed the sharper internal contradiction: the SAME 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG carries THREE different binding free energies -- dG -12.6 (app.js:131), -16.2 (app.js:156), -17.5 (app.js:250) -- and the 32-mer GSK3B graft carries -11.8 (app.js:133) vs -16.0 (app.js:228). dG, unlike pLDDT, has no partner-dependence escape hatch once you also accept that no partner structure exists. That belongs in this finding.

verdicts.reasoning: Source quotations are exact. app.js:791 is verbatim `let score = 93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5;`, app.js:850 is verbatim `let error = Math.abs(i - j) * 0.4 + (sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length) % 4) * 0.3;`, app.js:707 carries the 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING' comment, app.js:715 is `let radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8;`, app.js:802 labels the dataset 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score'. I re-implemented the pLDDT generator in python3 and reproduced every reported statistic: real 36-mer mean 94.11, min 89.1, max 99.0; placeholder 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' mean 94.09, min 89.1, max 99.0; poly-Q24 mean 94.31. PAE maximum on a 45x45 grid = 44*0.4 + 3*0.3 = 18.5 against an axis labelled '0 - 30 A' at index.html:397 -- confirmed. No fetch/XMLHttpRequest/axios in app.js -- confirmed, zero hits. index.html:42 and :363 are ordinary anchors to alphafoldserver.com -- confirmed by reading. Leaderboard/drug pLDDT contradictions 92.8 (131) / 94.8 (156) / 94.3 (250) -- confirmed exactly. The 3D generator at 711-732 and 973-991 has no phi/psi, no Ramachandran term, no vdW, no chirality -- confirmed by reading.
verdicts.corrections: Three factual corrections, one of which strengthens the finding. (1) 'hard-clamped to [76, 98.6]' is wrong. Those clamps at app.js:792-793 are unreachable dead code: the expression's algebraic range is 93 +/- 4 plus 0..2, i.e. [89.0, 99.0], so `score > 100` and `score < 70` never fire. The true floor is 89.0, not 76 -- the display is even less capable of expressing low confidence than the reviewer claims. State the range as [89.0, 99.0] and drop the reference to the clamps as the mechanism. (2) 'byte-for-byte the same confidence profile as the real peptide' is REFUTED. The two strings differ in length (36 vs 37) and in every per-residue value (real starts 94.6, 96.9, 97.7, 97.0; placeholder starts 95.6, 95.9, 96.7, 99.0). What is true, and is still damning, is that the rounded summary statistics are identical: mean 94.1, min 89.1, max 99.0 for both. Rewrite to 'the same mean, minimum and maximum to one decimal place'. (3) 'the 100-mer at app.js:125 ... renders as a clean diagonal' is wrong: app.js:125 is an AF3_CANDIDATES fasta and never reaches renderModalPaeHeatmap, which is called only from openDrugModal (app.js:651) with drug.sequence. The correct examples are the GGGGS-containing drug sequences at app.js:183, 235, 287, 339 and 391. (4) Minor: 'there is no network call in the codebase' overstates -- index.html:9-18 load Google Fonts, FontAwesome, three.js and Chart.js from CDNs. The precise claim is 'no AlphaFold API call anywhere in the codebase', which is what matters. (5) The fix list omits index.html:296, 347, 368 and, most importantly, the footer at index.html:410.

verdicts.reasoning: B at 1-based position 19 in all three entries -- confirmed (app.js:130, 173, 371). app.js:381 `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` -- confirmed. The AF3 input contract is verified verbatim: I fetched google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/input.md and line 222 reads 'the 1-letter standard amino acid codes.' The delivery path is real: app.js:600 sets currentActiveModalSequence, app.js:619-621 renders it as 'FASTA Peptide / Bio-Conjugate Sequence', app.js:662 writes it to the clipboard, index.html:359 tells the user to submit it to the AlphaFold Server. The disulfide-ambiguity arithmetic checks out: app.js:143 (47-mer) and app.js:215 (45-mer) each carry exactly 8 cysteines, and 7!! = 7*5*3*1 = 105 perfect matchings.
verdicts.corrections: (1) The cysteine count is UNDERSTATED. I enumerated all 25 drug sequences: ten genuine peptide entries carry an odd cysteine count, not nine, and the evidence block lists only eight. The reviewer missed app.js:225 GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG (1 Cys) and app.js:339 GRLVGHPWECDRGGGGSDEETGEWRWYCPWC (3 Cys). Correct list: 173 (7), 205 (7), 225 (1), 267 (5), 287 (5), 299 (5), 339 (3), 351 (5), 361 (7), 371 (7). (2) The quoted string for app.js:130 is wrong -- that line holds the 40-mer ...ACPDCHGMSGSCSTK, not the 31-mer. (3) The fix contains a concrete error that would be implemented as written: 'WNT3A carries L at the aligned position, so B->L' is FALSE. B sits at motif position 19, which aligns to WNT3A Gln221 (P56704 203-223 = CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQPD; position 19 is Q, position 6 is the L the reviewer appears to have read off). B->L would install a residue that is wrong at that position and would change the cysteine-independent character of the C-terminal segment. Either B->Q with the WNT3A alignment stated, or -- better, given AIML-01 -- delete the entries.

verdicts.reasoning: All four sub-claims verified against downloaded UniProt entries. (a) app.js:277 KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPW -- I located KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM at P05067 687-706 exactly, i.e. Abeta(16-35) given Abeta1 = APP672; app.js:282 does describe it as disrupting 'Abeta-AChE amyloid fibril seeding', README.md:77 calls it an 'Abeta Disruptor' and app.js:281 asserts 'Fibril Blockade: 100%'. Abeta16-35 contains KLVFF plus the entire hydrophobic C-terminal stretch and is the nucleating core; presenting it as the inhibitor inverts the direction of effect. This is the one finding in the report with a physical hazard attached. (b) app.js:225 is P49841 3-34 verbatim, and I confirmed it contains Ser9 (GSK3B = M-S-G-R-P-R-T-T-S...). The mechanistic objection is correct: the phospho-Ser9 N-terminal tail is an intramolecular pseudosubstrate for the primed-phosphate groove, not an ATP-competitive ligand, and a 32-mer (~3.5 kDa) cannot occupy an adenine cleft that accommodates ~500 Da. (c) P23560 residues 19-39 = APMKEANIRGQGGLAYPGVRT confirmed; I also confirmed the mature chain begins at 129 (P23560 129- = HSDPARRGELSVCDSISEWVTA). (d) TJP1/ZO-1 is cytoplasmic -- an extracellular Cys-rich peptide cannot engage it. My Smith-Waterman screen independently supports the grafts being what the reviewer says they are (APP z=19.8, GSK3B z=44.5, WNT3A z=26.7 against a shuffled null).
verdicts.corrections: (1) P23560 1-18 is the signal peptide and 19-128 the propeptide, so residues 19-39 lie wholly within the prodomain; 'signal-peptide/prodomain region' is loose and should read 'prodomain (propeptide 19-128)'. The substantive point -- not mature BDNF, opposite pharmacology via p75NTR/sortilin-family co-receptors -- stands, but note the review offers no retrieved citation for the prodomain-signalling claim; either add one or state it as established textbook pharmacology. (2) The reviewer's aside that the Nrf2 ETGE at app.js:127/163 shows 'the author can pick correct motifs when the biology is simple' needs qualifying: only DEETGEFL (NFE2L2 77-84) is verbatim. The construct's DEETGEFLFQLP does not occur in NFE2L2 (the natural sequence continues DEETGEFLPIQPAQ), and README.md:62 presents that non-existent 12-mer as the 'Nrf2 ETGE'. The one motif held up as correctly handled is itself wrong past residue 8.

verdicts.reasoning: The category error is correct on the merits: AF3 maps (sequence, ligands, MSA) to coordinates plus confidence heads, with no inverse-folding head, no backbone diffusion over sequence space and no free-energy function, so nothing can be 'designed via AlphaFold3' or 'AlphaFold3-optimized'. I verified the framing text at README.md:22 and :45, index.html:265-266 and :290, and the page title at index.html:6. The thermodynamics reproduce EXACTLY, digit for digit. With RT = 0.0019872041 * 298.15 = 0.5925 kcal/mol and dG = RT ln(Kd), all 25 rows parsed cleanly: implied dG spans -11.35 to -13.77 against stated -15.2 to -19.5; the offset spans 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol; every one of the 25 offsets has the same sign; and the -19.5 row (app.js:290, Kd 0.08 nM) implies -13.77 while -19.5 would imply Kd = 5.09 fM. The reviewer's numbers are precise. Absence of filter metrics confirmed by grep (zero hits for ipTM, pae_interaction, RMSD, ddG). The 25/25 success pattern confirmed: every Kd < 5 nM (max 4.8), every pLDDT > 92 (min 92.4 at app.js:384), 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' on all 25 safety strings, 'Off-target Binding: None' at app.js:209, 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' at app.js:281. Literature: I verified Cao et al. via PubMed efetch and the abstract contains the reviewer's quotation verbatim -- 'Experimental data on nearly half a million computational designs and hundreds of thousands of point mutants' -- plus '12 diverse protein targets' and crystal structures of five complexes. I verified the AlphaProteo blog by fetching it: 'seven target proteins we tested', '3 to 300 times better binding affinities', 88% for BHRF1, and the explicit TNF-alpha failure as the 8th target. I fetched martinpacesa/BindCraft settings_filters/default_filters.json and every threshold the reviewer quotes is exact: Average_i_pAE 0.35 (lower-is-better), Average_i_pTM 0.5, Average_pLDDT 0.8, Average_ShapeComplementarity 0.6, Average_dG 0, Average_Surface_Hydrophobicity 0.35, Average_n_InterfaceUnsatHbonds 4.
verdicts.corrections: Two sub-claims I could not verify in this session and which should be marked or dropped: the '9%' lower bound of AlphaProteo's 9-88% range does not appear on the cited blog URL (88%, seven targets, 3-300x and the TNF-alpha failure all do), and Bennett et al.'s 'roughly ten-fold' improvement was not confirmed against the paper text. Both are almost certainly right, but a report whose thesis is fabricated numbers cannot carry an unverified number. Also: the reviewer's 'the 25 dG values are not AF3 output under any interpretation' would be sharper paired with the observation that the same sequence carries three different dG values across the dataset (-12.6/-16.2/-17.5 for the 36-mer), which forecloses the 'computed by some other tool' defence.

missed_by_reviewer: SEVERITY MISCALIBRATION: AIML-06 is graded MAJOR while AIML-02 is a BLOCKER. That is backwards. The dG/Kd inconsistency -- a 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol error in the same direction on all 25 rows, which I reproduced exactly -- is the single cleanest, most self-contained proof of fabrication in the whole dataset, and 'designed via AlphaFold3' is the headline claim in the repository title, README.md:1 and README.md:22. It should be a BLOCKER.

THE REPOSITORY LEAKS A WEBGL CONTEXT PER MODAL OPEN, AND THE REVIEW PRAISES THE ENGINEERING INSTEAD. `grep -n 'dispose|forceContextLoss|cancelAnimationFrame' app.js` returns nothing. initModal3DCanvas (app.js:674) calls container.innerHTML = '' and then constructs a fresh THREE.WebGLRenderer (app.js:688) on every openDrugModal, while the previous animateModal3D loop keeps running because its only guard, `if (!modalThreeRenderer) return;` (app.js:764), reads a global that is never nulled. Opening ~16 drug cards exhausts the browser's WebGL context limit and the 3D panel goes blank. The overall_assessment specifically commends 'competent and clean' front-end engineering 'including chart lifecycle management at app.js:779-781 to avoid Chart.js leaks' -- the cheap Chart.js instance is destroyed, the expensive GL contexts are not. Praising the engineering while this is present is the kind of error that costs the report credibility with the author.

CEI -- THE LEADERBOARD'S ACTUAL RANKING KEY -- IS NEVER MENTIONED IN THE REVIEW AND IS DEFINED NOWHERE IN THE PROJECT. 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI / 100)' is the primary series of the benchmark chart (app.js:1063), a leaderboard column (index.html:306) and the chart's headline (index.html:316), with hardcoded values 82.5-98.4 at app.js:125-134. There is no formula, no units, no citation, no code that computes it anywhere in the repository. An invented 0-100 score presented as a 'Computational Benchmark' axis is a fabricated metric of exactly the class the review is otherwise cataloguing, and it is the field by which the 'TOP 10' is ranked -- note that rank does not track pLDDT (rank 1 = 93.2, rank 3 = 96.1) or dG (rank 1 = -17.9, rank 4 = -14.2).

HALF THE 'SMILES' STRINGS DO NOT PARSE, WHICH IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS AIML-04 IN A DIFFERENT FIELD. I ran RDKit over all eight entries in NATURAL_PRODUCTS_DATA: four fail. app.js:60 is 'C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)' and app.js:70 is 'C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)' -- molecular formulas with prose, not SMILES, rendered by app.js:477 under the label 'SMILES Formulation', exactly the 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' failure mode the review catches only for peptides. app.js:50 (curcumin) contains 'OCH3', which is not valid SMILES, and app.js:10 (Huperzine A) also fails to sanitize. AIML-04's proposed validator therefore needs a chemistry arm (RDKit MolFromSmiles) alongside the peptide regex, or the fix leaves half the same bug in place.

BINDING-SITE RESIDUE NUMBERING MIXES TWO ORGANISMS INSIDE A SINGLE STRING. app.js:154 reads 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)'; app.js:248 repeats the pattern. I checked these against human ACHE (P22303, 614 aa, signal peptide 1-31): in mature human numbering position 84 is Glu, 330 is Val and 121 is Gly, whereas 286 is Trp, 72 is Tyr and 341 is Tyr. Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica numbering (human equivalents Trp86/Phe338/Tyr124, which I confirmed are W/F/Y). So the catalytic-site residues are Torpedo and the peripheral-site residues in the same parenthesis are human. The project is internally inconsistent too: app.js:12 gives 'Trp279 (PAS)' (Torpedo) while README.md:32 gives 'PAS (Trp286)' (human). Any of the residue-level annotations across all 25 entries should be presumed unchecked until re-verified against a stated reference numbering.

THE 3D VIEWER COLOURS RESIDUES BY AMINO-ACID LETTER WHILE THE UI LABELS THE LEGEND 'pLDDT COLOR SPECTRUM'. app.js:747-749 assigns cyan by default, green if the residue is G or S, amber if it is P or D. index.html:377 titles that panel 'Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)' and index.html:388-391 supplies a legend reading 'Very High (>90) / High (70-90) / Low (50-70) / Very Low (<50)'. So every glycine is displayed as '70-90 confidence' and every proline as '50-70' -- and both are flatly contradicted by the same modal's own pLDDT chart, which cannot emit anything below 89.0. This is a third fabricated confidence display beyond the two AIML-03 catalogues.

NO TARGET STRUCTURE EXISTS ANYWHERE, WHICH IS THE PRECONDITION THE WHOLE DISCIPLINE TURNS ON. There is not one PDB ID, mmCIF, hotspot-residue set derived from a structure, or epitope definition in the repository. Target-conditioned design (RFdiffusion, BindCraft, AlphaProteo) begins with target coordinates plus hotspots; without them there is nothing to condition on, so the absence is not merely undocumented provenance -- it makes the claimed activity impossible in principle rather than merely unevidenced. The review argues from the absence of outputs (design PDBs, score CSVs, seeds); the absence of the required input is the stronger and more easily explained argument.

ZERO DEVELOPABILITY OR LIABILITY FILTERING, ON A SET WHERE THE LIABILITIES ARE VISIBLE FROM THE SEQUENCE. The 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:131/153/247) has 13 K/R against 4 D/E, net charge about +9, with 4 Trp, 4 Phe and 6 Leu -- a textbook cationic amphipathic architecture of the cell-penetrating/membrane-lytic class, not a selective enzyme binder. It is shipped with 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Cardiotoxicity)' and 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' (app.js:251). No aggregation propensity, no MHC-II immunogenicity prediction, no hemolysis or membrane-lysis assessment, no protease-stability consideration appears anywhere, yet README.md:101 asserts 'Low Immunogenicity'. For a reviewer whose stated speciality is in-silico filtering, the complete absence of a developability filter set -- and a safety claim that is plausibly inverted for the most-reused sequence in the dataset -- is the omission a referee would notice first.

NO CNS-EXPOSURE ANALYSIS FOR 26-49-RESIDUE PEPTIDES SOLD AS BRAIN-REGION-TARGETED. Every one of the 25 entries is a multi-kilodalton, often highly charged peptide conjugate assigned to a specific brain region and cell type, and not one line of the repository addresses blood-brain-barrier penetration, route of administration, or CNS PK -- while README.md:90 and app.js:369-377 go so far as to name a BBB tight-junction target. The platform's entire organising principle (5 brain regions) presupposes the one property it never examines.

THE PAE GENERATOR HAS TWO FURTHER DEFECTS WORTH NAMING IN THE FIX. app.js:850 indexes the character term by row only -- charCodeAt(i % len), never j -- so PAE(i,j) != PAE(j,i) by construction and the 'sequence-driven' contribution is a constant per row, not a pairwise quantity at all. Separately, app.js:844 caps the grid at Math.min(len, 45), so the 47-mer at app.js:143 silently renders only its first 45 residues, and neither axis is labelled with residue indices. If the panel is retained in any form these must be fixed alongside the relabelling.

NO SEED, NO VERSION, NO DETERMINISM STATEMENT. Even taken at face value, nothing in the repository records an AF3 model version, an inference seed, a date, or a compute environment. The review asks for these in the rebuild but does not list their absence as a present-tense reproducibility defect in the artefact under review.

verifications.discipline: Medicinal chemistry / natural product chemistry / cheminformatics and assay interference assessment
verifications.verifier_persona: Distinguished medicinal chemist, 24 years post-PhD across natural-product lead discovery and structure-based design; former head of a pharma compound-integrity function responsible for structure curation and assay-interference triage across a 2M-compound collection. All verification below was performed in this session in a fresh venv with RDKit 2026.03.5, against PubChem PUG-REST, UniProt REST (P05067, P22303, P25105, P49841, Q14145, P36544, Q16620, P04629, Q9NZC2), and PDB coordinate files 1VOT and 4EY7 downloaded from RCSB; literature verified against PubMed (per PubMed terms, DOIs are linked in the reasoning fields below).

verdicts.reasoning: I re-parsed all eight smiles fields myself. Chem.MolFromSmiles returns None for exactly the four cited (app.js:10, 50, 60, 70) and returns None with sanitize=False as well, confirming these are tokenizer/graph-construction failures, not valence sanitization failures. Applying s/OCH3/OC/ to the curcumin string at app.js:50 yields C21H20O6 with InChIKey VFLDPWHFBUODDF-UHFFFAOYSA-N, whose skeleton block matches PubChem curcumin CID 969516 (VFLDPWHFBUODDF-FCXRPNKRSA-N) exactly. The huperzine A string opens ring-closure label 1 at 'CC1=' and never closes it. app.js:60 and app.js:70 literally contain 'C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)' and 'C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)'. Every PubChem reference the reviewer states I retrieved independently and all match to the character: huperzine A CID 854026 C15H18N2O 242.32 ZRJBHWIHUMBLCN-YQEJDHNASA-N; curcumin CID 969516 C21H20O6 368.4; salvianolic acid B CID 6451084 C36H30O16 718.6 SNKFFCBZYFGCQN-VWUOOIFGSA-N; onjisaponin V CID 177827987 C82H122O41 1763.8 MYKOTWPDDUNUJG-VNBMPPIYSA-N. I confirmed by grep that app.js:477 is the only consumer of the field: `smiles` appears exactly nine times in the codebase, eight definitions plus one innerHTML interpolation.
verdicts.corrections: Two small factual slips that do not touch the conclusion. (1) The absence-grep is literally false as written: 'canonicalization' is absent but the substring 'canonical' matches app.js:178 ('canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling'). The reviewer should scope the grep to library/API tokens rather than claiming zero hits for word stems that occur in prose. (2) 'The app.js string ... has no pyridone ring fusion' is imprecise; the string does encode a C(=O)N-C= lactam fragment. The accurate statement is that ring-closure label 1 is never closed, so the bridged tricyclic framework is never formed and no molecule is produced at all.

verdicts.reasoning: The identity error is certain and I reproduced every step. The app.js:40 string parses to C15H10O5, MW 270.24, InChIKey SXZJEWVPXPKGJG-UHFFFAOYSA-N. A PubChem InChIKey lookup on that key returns CID 14372623, IUPAC name '6,7,8-trihydroxy-2-phenylchromen-4-one'. Real baicalein by name lookup is CID 5281605, C15H10O5, MW 270.24, FXNFHKRTJBSTCS-UHFFFAOYSA-N, '5,6,7-trihydroxy-2-phenylchromen-4-one'. I also confirmed the reviewer's proposed replacement string parses to FXNFHKRTJBSTCS. An independent 5-hydroxy-4-keto-chromone SMARTS test returns False for the app.js structure and True for real baicalein. This is exactly the silent-failure class the reviewer describes: identical formula, identical mass, different substance.
verdicts.corrections: The mechanistic consequence is stated too absolutely. 6,7,8-trihydroxyflavone retains a pyrogallol A-ring, so it still has an ortho-dihydroxy pair capable of chelating Fe; what it loses is specifically the 5-OH/4-keto bidentate chelate, not all iron chelation. Likewise for GSK-3beta, loss of the C5-OH degrades but does not categorically abolish flavone hinge binding, which is also served by the 4-keto and the 7-OH. Rewrite as 'removes the 5-OH/4-keto motif the stated rationale is written around' rather than 'cannot form that chelate'. Also note 6,7,8-trihydroxyflavone is not a nonsense structure but a real registered compound with its own literature, which the reviewer does correctly flag in the fix.

verdicts.reasoning: Every headline number reproduces exactly. app.js:20 parses to C38H64O14, MW 744.92, skeleton DYTIXWQVBPQHKX, versus PubChem Rg1 CID 441923 C42H72O14 MW 801.0 skeleton YURJSTAIMNSZAE; a ring-quaternary-carbon-bearing-two-methyls SMARTS returns 0 matches for the app string and 1 for the reference, and methyl counts are 5 versus 8. app.js:30 parses to C18H22O8, MW 366.37, 8 SSSR rings, 1 lactone, 1 ketone, skeleton KRGCYOMVCDUGIP, versus ginkgolide B CID 11973122 C20H24O10 MW 424.4, 6 rings, 3 lactones, 0 ketones, skeleton SQOJOAFXDQDRGF. Both app-string skeletons return PUGREST.NotFound on PubChem, i.e. they correspond to no registered substance. Constitutional comparison after stereo stripping: Rg1 False, ginkgolide B False, asiatic acid True. The internal contradictions are real: app.js:142 states C42H72O14 and app.js:370 states C20H24O10, both correct, both contradicting the SMILES. Rg3 at app.js:266 is C36H62O8 against PubChem CID 9918693 C42H72O13 MW 785.0; presenegenin at app.js:182 and 328 is C30H46O6 against CID 21594224 C30H46O7 MW 518.7.
verdicts.corrections: Three corrections. (1) The anomeric census is garbled. My SMARTS gives 1 O-glycosidic anomeric carbon in the app string versus 2 in real Rg1; real Rg1 has zero C-glycosides, so the reviewer's 'versus 2 and 2 in real Rg1' is wrong. The substantive claim, that the C20 sugar in the app string is attached through a C-C bond rather than a glycosidic oxygen, is correct and is what matters. (2) 'Ginsenoside Rg3 Dammarane Core' arguably names a fragment rather than the intact glycoside, which softens the framing, though C36H62O8 matches neither Rg3 nor its protopanaxadiol aglycone (C30H52O3), so it is wrong under any reading. (3) The reviewer understates the ginkgolide B defect. RDKit ETKDG cannot embed the app.js:30 constitution at all (EmbedMolecule returns -1 after 200 attempts, and ETKDGv3 with random coordinates over 50 conformers did not terminate), while the true ginkgolide B stereoisomer embeds on the first attempt. The app.js ginkgolide B is not merely the wrong molecule; on this evidence its ring fusion appears not to be three-dimensionally realizable at all.

verdicts.reasoning: The factual core is exact. I extracted all eight smiles fields by regex and confirmed not one contains '@', '/' or backslash. FindPotentialStereo gives, for specified/unspecified: app Rg1 0/22 (reference 21/0), app ginkgolide B 0/12 (reference 11/0), app asiatic acid 0/12 (reference 12/0), app baicalein 0/0, repaired curcumin 0/2. 2^22 = 4194304 and 2^12 = 4096 check out arithmetically. index.html:118 does advertise 'and stereochemistry', so the contradicted-claim element is solid. The InChIKey second-block point is correct and I reproduced it: the flat app asiatic acid gives JXSVIVRDWWRQRT-UHFFFAOYSA-N while PubChem CID 119034 gives JXSVIVRDWWRQRT-UYDOISQJSA-N, identical on the first block.
verdicts.corrections: The stereoisomer arithmetic is inflated in two of three cases. 2^n is an upper bound on graph-level stereoisomers, not a count of chemically realizable diastereomers.
